title: 2016 nUSA–United Kingdom war
text: 2016 nUSA–United Kingdom war Date July–3 August 2016 Exact opening date uncertain Result British victory; peace agreement acknowledged a 5–0 result for the United Kingdom [ 1 ] Belligerents United States United Kingdom Settlement Peace Agreement of the United States and the United Kingdom, 3 August 2016 [ 1 ] The 2016 nUSA–United Kingdom war was a conflict between nUSA and the United Kingdom during the presidency of SuddenRush12G . Fighting took place in the summer of 2016 and ended with a peace agreement dated 3 August. The agreement acknowledged a British victory with a score of 5–0, provided for a mutual cessation of hostilities, and required American recognition of Hawaii's independence. SuddenRush12G and Secretary of State Lumidas were listed as the American signatories, alongside British Prime Minister SidousThePwnda. [ 1 ] The war also produced a diplomatic crisis involving the United Nations and prompted SuddenRush12G to propose changes to military organization and training. The peace arrangement later became the subject of a congressional dispute, followed by renewed hostilities under President TheySinned in January 2017. [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] Declaration and diplomatic crisis On 21 July 2016, Vice President TimGeithner published a joint resolution titled Declaration of War on the United Kingdom . It proposed authorizing a full military campaign and immediately revoking the alliance between the two countries upon passage. Apteria offered to sponsor and present the resolution in a reply to the proposal. The date of its formal legislative approval is uncertain. [ 5 ] The conflict coincided with a deterioration in relations with the United Nations. In a November account, Geithner, who had served as Vice President during the war and participated in backchannel negotiations, described nUSA's suspension from the organization and the loss of its permanent Security Council status. He attributed the diplomatic rupture to the conduct of an American ambassador, whom he said was subsequently dismissed. [ 2 ] Geithner also described an attempt by EUSA to obtain international recognition in nUSA's place during the war. He stated that the United Kingdom and other UN members continued to defend nUSA's recognition despite the conflict. His later argument for remaining in the UN presented that support as a reason to preserve membership. [ 2 ] Fighting and outcome American and British forces engaged in combat. In his October report to the National Security Council, SuddenRush12G referred to the recent UK conflict as evidence that large military memberships had not produced cohesive or effective fighting units. He criticized the ability of American forces to operate together against the enemy. [ 3 ] The 3 August peace agreement recorded a 5–0 result in favor of the United Kingdom and stated that the United States would submit to the United Kingdom and King James I and lower its arms. The dates and locations of the individual engagements are uncertain. [ 1 ] Peace agreement The agreement required the United States Military and British Armed Forces to cease hostilities against one another. It also called for an end to attacks that infringed international law and principles. In exchange for the settlement, Britain was to work toward normalizing relations, support the United States in international organizations including the United Nations, and seek the removal of sanctions against the United States. [ 1 ] The American commitments included: Recognizing Hawaii's independence. A formal apology by Vice President TimGeithner to Tentacools for his actions and remarks. Maintaining open and responsive communication channels to prevent another conflict. Working to normalize relations and strengthen diplomatic cooperation. [ 1 ] The document listed Lumidas and SuddenRush12G as the United States delegation and SidousThePwnda as the United Kingdom delegation. These provisions established the terms of the settlement; the extent to which every commitment was implemented is uncertain. [ 1 ] Aftermath Military reform proposals On 23 October 2016, SuddenRush12G used the UK conflict as the basis for proposed military reforms. He advocated smaller, cohesive combat units and criticized training that emphasized formations and obstacle courses over fighting. His recommendations included membership caps of 150 for the Army, 75 for the Marine Corps, and 300 each for the Navy and Air Force, together with a common two-day basic-training program. The report set out recommendations rather than announcing their implementation. [ 3 ] Renewed conflict in 2017 In an address dated 28 January 2017, President TheySinned credited SuddenRush12G, TimGeithner, and Lumidas with negotiating the earlier peace plan. He stated that Congress had overridden SuddenRush12G's veto of the Sovereignty Act on 22 January, nullifying the arrangement. TheySinned reported that Britain had subsequently declared war and begun assembling troops and a coalition. He announced military preparations and negotiations over war terms. This renewed conflict occurred under TheySinned's presidency. title: 2019 presidential elections (nUSA)
text: The 2019 presidential elections in nUSA comprised several separate presidential contests announced as the Winter, Summer, and Fall 2019 elections. Archived records preserve ballots and results for the Summer and Fall races and announcements for the Winter ballot and voting phase. Their outcomes and eligibility decisions differed, so they are best treated as a cycle of separate elections rather than one race. [ 1 ] Winter election An announcement on 28 January introduced the Winter 2019 election for President. The ballot released on 18 February listed Dralian as the Republican candidate and devGralius as an independent; voting was announced open for a 24-hour period on 23 February. The reviewed announcement record establishes the ballot and voting window, but the sources cited here do not establish the Winter election's final result. [ 2 ] Summer election The FEC released its Summer 2019 presidential plan in May, followed by a ballot on 7 June listing Kind_Yada, Blastatack, SpeakerJosh, devGralius, and Reset3634643. The result letter, delivered to congressional leaders in June, reported two candidate hearings and 753 votes, of which 362 were disqualified. It reported SpeakerJosh as the winner and President-elect, with ClutchAntonioVII as vice-President-elect. [ 3 ] Fall election The Fall 2019 plan specified registration from 15 September to 15 October and a 24-hour voting period on 19–20 October, with results expected on 21 October after filtering and any hearings. Its ballot included AntonioTRoosevelt, 24craft, Aerium, JamesMontagu, Lordsightss, Wetheliwars, CrownedShaggy, and noobsandguestskiller. [ 4 ] The results letter reported 653 votes received and 30 disqualified for being alternate accounts. It recorded a hearing concerning JamesMontagu, who was “not disqualified, but declared ineligible.” The letter then certified him as the election winner but said an injunction meant that he did not qualify for office; applying the cited constitutional provision, it declared vice-President-elect TomFoley to be the acting President-elect until a President qualified. This account reflects the result letter's statements and does not resolve any later constitutional or judicial history. title: 2020 nUSA–United Kingdom war
text: The 2020 nUSA–United Kingdom war was a brief conflict represented within the Roblox nUSA roleplay community and a United Kingdom roleplay group. A retrospective published by the nUSA military's Military Times in October 2025 dates the start to 2 April 2020 and describes a peace agreement nine days later. A contemporary 11 April post by nUSA President Reset4K says he had spoken with a king and that a treaty declaring a stalemate would be released shortly. The account and outcome concern the Roblox communities, not the real governments of the United States or United Kingdom. [ 1 ] Background and fighting The military retrospective says that a United Kingdom group associated with Sovereign gave nUSA an ultimatum in early 2020. It portrays that ultimatum as unreasonable and says the United States side did not accept it. It dates the outbreak of the roleplay war to 2 April. The same account claims that the nUSA military won the first battle, but also says that the United Nations voided that battle. This is the later Pentagon press office's description, rather than a surviving contemporary battle report or a neutral account from the other group. [ 2 ] The reviewed nUSA announcement archive records Reset4K's March 2020 inauguration and other April government notices, but it does not contain a contemporaneous formal declaration of this war or battle results. This limits how precisely the battles, participants, and military result can be reconstructed. The 2025 retrospective is also a heritage and recruitment item for the nUSA military, giving it an evident institutional perspective. [ 3 ] Peace talks and outcome On 11 April 2020, Reset4K wrote that he had spoken with “the King” and expected the release of a treaty declaring a stalemate. He credited nUSA troops for enabling the negotiations. His post included images, one of which shows two Roblox avatars outside a large building. The visible image does not identify the other avatar or reproduce the treaty. [ 4 ] The later Military Times account calls the settlement the Hillsborough Accords and says it secured American sovereignty. That is its retrospective characterization; the reviewed sources do not supply the 2020 agreement's signed text, a ratification record, or an independent United Kingdom account. Reset4K's contemporary wording supports the more limited conclusion that a stalemate treaty was anticipated on 11 April. A separate 2018 document titled The Hillsborough Pact appears in a congressional Trello record, but its date and terms concern an earlier agreement and it should not be confused with the purported 2020 accords. title: 2022 government reconstruction (nUSA)
text: Reorganization of government and preparations for Boulder County in 2022 The 2022 government reconstruction was a broad reorganization of national institutions, legislation and public administration. Announced in January under pauljkl and a new management leadership including Libres, it sought to rebuild a government facing low participation and prepare it for a renewed national life centered on Boulder County . The program extended across constitutional discussions, congressional elections, public employment and legal practice. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] Reconstruction was a sequence of reforms rather than a single enactment. Government continued to conduct business while institutions were being reconsidered. By the autumn, temporary elections had renewed Congress, the House had adopted new standing rules, and President TacticalRock101 was consolidating agencies in preparation for Boulder's opening. [ 3 ] [ 4 ] [ 5 ] The January program On 19 January, Speaker MasonRockefeller announced a plan assembled by pauljkl to undertake extensive reconstruction. Departments and agencies would close or change, legislation would be removed from the governing body of law, and the administration would pursue a clean-slate approach. Citizens were invited to contribute proposals and criticism. The announcement described the intended direction without itself enacting every agency closure or repeal. [ 6 ] The promise of a fresh start did not extend to every sanction. In March, Rockefeller explained that many office bars and blacklists would be reset, while exclusions for destructive attacks on official institutions and assets would remain. Reconstruction therefore combined relief from older restrictions with the retention of penalties protecting the government's operating infrastructure. [ 7 ] Constitutional discussions The Speaker and President pro tempore convened a joint town hall on 4 February to discuss Congress, reconstruction and constitutional rewriting. On 25 April, Rockefeller announced that Congress had adopted H. Con. Res. 1 and S. Con. Res. 1, obtained the Supreme Court's consent and entered a constitutional convention scheduled to last until 31 May. The convention placed revision of the governing framework alongside the practical rebuilding of public offices. [ 8 ] [ 9 ] Staffing a diminished government The House sought staff for its leadership and committees in April. Rockefeller appealed to citizens to participate while activity was low, arguing that the government needed people to rebuild institutions before a larger return of public participation. This recruitment effort made administrative capacity a central part of reconstruction: laws and revised structures required officials able to operate them. [ 10 ] In November, TacticalRock101 addressed the same problem from the executive side. Limited personnel and resources led him to furlough agencies whose responsibilities could be absorbed elsewhere. He left open their future return as needs and activity changed. The measure concentrated personnel rather than promising to maintain every existing institution at its previous size. [ 11 ] [ 12 ] Citizenship and legal practice The Domestic Protection Act of 2022 became an important legislative product of reconstruction. Introduced by Rockefeller on 12 July and announced as signed on 13 July, it distinguished citizenship in another American nation from holding civil office there. It removed discrimination based solely on foreign citizenship while retaining office-ineligibility provisions and a congressional process for imposing or lifting bars. [ 13 ] [ 14 ] The judiciary prepared its own reforms. On 14 July, Chief Justice RummyLeroux outlined a Federal Bar Association subordinate to the Supreme Court. The plan provided for licensing, ethical standards, paid legal services and law firms in Boulder County. Legal practice was being treated as a profession with a route toward clerkships and judicial appointments, rather than simply admission to individual cases. [ 15 ] Interim elections and parliamentary reform The Federal Election Commission's August schedule called for the replacement of both chambers through temporary elections: sixteen representatives and ten senators. House voting was scheduled for 20–21 August and Senate voting for 27–28 August. The temporary arrangement anticipated a later election system associated with Boulder's opening. [ 16 ] Further House reforms followed under Rockefeller. In October he proposed tighter limits on absences and proxies, emphasizing that elected representatives should ordinarily perform their own duties. On 9 November the chamber adopted a new set of standing rules covering committees, leadership responsibilities, legislative procedure, conduct, activity and possible educational programs. By this stage, reconstruction involved not only filling seats but also defining how their occupants were expected to serve. [ 17 ] [ 18 ] Boulder and the next institutional era Boulder County opened on 26 November 2022. Its arrival brought reconstruction's preparations into a new setting for municipal government, law enforcement and professional activity. It also generated external tensions: Rockefeller introduced H.R. 25 in response to Ridgeway's restrictions on participation, proposing protections against discrimination based on membership there. The announcement introduced a bill and sought support; it did not by itself establish enactment. [ 19 ] [ 20 ] The reconstruction preceded the separate 2023 legal reset . The two belong to successive phases of institutional change and should not be collapsed into a single event: the 2022 program rebuilt offices, procedures and participation over many months, while the later reset formally voided existing legal materials. title: 2023 nUSA legal reset
text: The 2023 nUSA legal reset was a Group Management action that declared specified federal roleplay records void effective 6 p.m. Eastern time on 15 July 2023. The announcement covered federal laws, case law and precedent, and congressional resolutions, motions and awards. A new Constitution and related governance and archival framework followed on 17 July. The reset concerned nUSA's Roblox roleplay and had no real-world legal effect. [ 1 ] Announcement and scope The reset announcement identified the affected material as federal laws, case law or precedent, and congressional resolutions, motions and awards. It gave an effective time rather than describing a vote or amendment procedure. The article therefore treats the event as an announced Group Management rule; the available announcement does not provide a detailed instrument listing each voided record or a separate adjudication of every prior measure. [ 2 ] The next phase introduced a new Constitution and a suite of Group Management directives, including #001-03 on NARA and #001-04 on legislative archival requirements. The accompanying announcement also referred to new NARA and Congress Trello boards. This establishes a new administrative framework after the reset, rather than proving that every former roleplay record was physically deleted from archives. [ 3 ] New archival framework The Constitution published and instituted on 17 July 2023 places NARA under Group Management control, assigns it storage and maintenance of public records for Congress, the Judiciary and the Executive, and authorizes retention schedules and archival processes. Memorandum #001 describes NARA as autonomous from the player government, while also stating that GM empowered and oversaw the agency. [ 4 ] For legislative records, the memo set filing and format requirements and allowed NARA to decline archival acceptance when a passed bill did not comply. The document says a rejected item would not become active law and that revised text had to be proposed again as a new bill. These were operational rules in the July 2023 roleplay package, distinct from the broader voiding action that preceded them by two days. [ 5 ] Limits and later continuity The announcement's phrase “null and void” records GM's stated status rule for the enumerated classes of material. It does not establish that old records disappeared from Trello or other archives, and the surviving source set does not include a complete inventory of affected enactments. Subsequent NARA materials preserve older documents alongside later instruments, so archival survival should not be confused with continuing legal effect in the roleplay. [ 6 ] Later constitutions complicate any claim that the 2023 framework governed continuously. A new Constitution was announced as passed in November 2024, and NARA announced a readoption of an earlier Constitution in May 2025. The sources do not explain every transitional rule between these versions. See Constitutions of nUSA , 2024 Constitution of nUSA and 2025 constitutional readoption in nUSA . title: 2024 Constitution of nUSA
text: The 2024 Constitution of nUSA is the constitutional text that Group Management announced as passed on 6 November 2024 after review by the roleplay Senate, House, District Courts and Supreme Court. The announcement described its two-column presentation and said Group Management would own and maintain the PDF. The linked document could not be retrieved in the reviewed source archive, so the text's substantive articles and exact effective provisions remain unverified here. [ 1 ] Approval announcement The announcement reported approval from four institutions: the Senate, House, District Courts and Supreme Court. It described the document as a new Constitution that “has passed” and noted a two-column format inspired by the National Constitution Center's presentation. This is a contemporaneous Group Management report of the approval sequence; no individual votes or convention record are included in the accessible announcement excerpt. [ 2 ] Group Management was identified as the owner and maintainer of the PDF. That custody statement differs from the May 2025 NARA-linked copy's cover, which identifies the Archivist's document as a readopted version; it does not by itself settle the broader division of archival and constitutional authority between GM and NARA. [ 3 ] Surviving status evidence The original 2024 Constitution attachment was linked as “Constitution2024.pdf,” but the source review recorded a permission failure and did not preserve a readable copy. The NARA Hub later listed “GobiesCons 11-6-24” and marked it inactive. The available records therefore support the reported passage and later inactive label, but do not support paraphrasing specific rights, branches, terms or amendment rules in the missing text. [ 4 ] In May 2025, NARA announced the readoption of a Constitution associated with Timothy F. Geithner, and the Hub's TimCons card identifies its copy as re-adopted on 12 May 2025. This later record does not describe the 2024 text's provisions or fully explain whether the 2024 version was repealed, superseded or otherwise displaced; the Hub's inactive label is the clearest surviving status marker. [ 5 ] Context The Constitution announced in 2024 followed the July 2023 Constitution, which had been published and instituted after Group Management's legal reset. The 2023 copy explicitly defines NARA's records role; because the 2024 copy is unavailable, that mandate cannot be assumed to have persisted unchanged into the 2024 text. [ 6 ] This article concerns the constitution of the nUSA roleplay on Roblox. It does not refer to the Constitution of the real United States. For the broader sequence and conflicting version dates, see Constitutions of nUSA and nUSA (Roblox group) . title: 2024 Group Management restructuring (nUSA)
text: The 2024 Group Management restructuring (nUSA) refers to a series of leadership and organizational changes announced in the Roblox nUSA community during 2024. On 28 April, Senior Group Management members Dilliuss and Hayden said they would leave that role and become Notable Figures, citing differences in management style and a desire for one leadership vision. Owner UKR41NIAN then described the change as a shift toward streamlined decisions and announced a management team and plans for development and roleplay oversight. [ 1 ] On 8 June, the owner announced that the Group Management liaison positions for the Judicial, Executive, and Legislative branches would be combined in a Government GM post, while NARA remained separate. [ 2 ] A further August statement promised a review and simplification of Group Management; it listed goals rather than documenting each resulting policy change. [ 3 ] Ownership and senior leadership On 28 April, Hayden said that both he and Dilliuss would step down from Senior Group Management effective that evening and move to Notable Figures. He described the reason as different management styles, goals, and visions from UKR41NIAN, and said neither departing member would retain an ownership stake or Group Manager influence. This account documents their announced departure and explanation; it does not independently establish the participants' motives beyond their public statement. [ 4 ] In a separate message later that day, UKR41NIAN thanked the departing managers and said the single-vision shift was intended to streamline decision-making and align development with community needs. The owner listed TacticalRummy for Government Liaison, Josh for Legal, a then unnamed account for Public Outreach, CephalGPT for Trust & Safety, and Benda587 for Development Affairs. These titles describe the announced team at that moment; the notice did not provide a new charter or fixed tenure terms. [ 5 ] Consolidation of government liaison roles On 8 June, UKR41NIAN announced a more specific organizational change: the Judicial, Executive, and Legislative liaison GM positions would merge into one Government GM post. The announcement appointed AdamStratton to that position and said TacticalRummy would remain NARA GM. It described the Government GM's scope as Group Management entities that touched the roleplay environment, while leaving the listed acronyms FRB and FBA unexplained in that notice. [ 6 ] The separation mattered institutionally: the notice placed the consolidated liaison role and NARA GM role alongside one another as distinct positions. It did not say that NARA itself merged into Government GM or that its archival function was transferred. See National Archives and Records Administration (nUSA) . [ 7 ] August review announcement On 31 August, the owner said the team would re-examine the GM structure, policies, and work with prominent group members over the following 48 hours. The statement listed aims including less intervention in group affairs, more equal moderation, clearer branch authority and checks and balances, improved trust in government, and community growth. It described objectives of a review, not a completed set of structural amendments; the announcement's general language does not identify which changes were subsequently adopted. [ 8 ] The surviving 2024 notices thus document leadership turnover, a concrete merger of three liaison portfolios into one Government GM post, the stated separation of NARA, and a later review announcement. They do not present one consolidated reorganization instrument or establish that every announced goal was realized. The separate 2024 judicial reset (nUSA) concerned the judiciary's personnel and appointments, not this management structure. title: 2024 judicial reset (nUSA)
text: The 2024 judicial reset (nUSA) was a reorganization of the Roblox nUSA roleplay judiciary announced by Group Management on 26 November 2024. The announcement said all sitting judges and justices would be removed and that a seven-member commission would recommend replacements for presidential nomination and Senate confirmation. It presented the action as a response to declining activity and bureaucracy; the announcement also outlined a judicial conference, legal support, and education initiatives as follow-on plans. [ 1 ] The surviving announcement documents the decision and intended process, while making clear that recommendations and the subsequent conference were future steps. It does not itself document the completion of every appointment. [ 2 ] Background and announcement Group Management described a long-term decline in judicial activity and increasing bureaucracy. It said the problem had reached a boiling point during summer 2024, when earlier changes were attempted, and that those measures had not reversed the decline. The owner framed a restart as a final option and compared it with a 2013 congressional restart that some community members called a "Carlos wipe." These were Group Management's explanation and historical comparison in the announcement. [ 3 ] The announced reset applied to "all judges and justices of the judiciary." A seven-member Group Management commission was to prepare recommendations for President Blanket, who would nominate new judges and justices; the Senate would confirm nominees. Group Management asked the President and senators to emphasize merit and competency rather than politics. The announcement records the stated selection framework, but does not list the commission members or name replacement nominees. [ 4 ] Planned reforms and documented scope The announcement said a judicial conference would follow the filling of the judiciary, led by the new Chief Justice and Chief Judge, to analyze and reform the branch. It also cited continued work by the Federal Bar Association under Josh and a planned education effort involving attorneys with real-world education or practice experience. These were prospective initiatives in the same notice; the source does not establish that they were all carried out as announced. [ 5 ] The record is strongest as evidence of Group Management's decision, rationale, and proposed appointment and reform process. The announcement does not say that NARA's judicial records were erased, nor does it describe a destruction of case files; its stated scope was the sitting judicial personnel. For related changes to the governance structure, see 2024 Group Management restructuring (nUSA) and District Court (nUSA) . title: 2024 presidential election (nUSA)
text: November 2024 Presidential Election November 2024 Presidential Election Voting 8–10 November 2024 Result announcement 10 November 2024 Certified or announced winner Teasoups Vice Presidential candidate Rathuzen Valid ballots or voters 308 The November 2024 Presidential Election in nUSA returned Teasoups to the presidency. The Pioneer ticket of Teasoups and Rathuzen received 184 votes, ahead of ApolloKorman and MitsuoMochizuki with 82. The FEC and Group Management certified the result on 10 November. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] Campaign The campaigning period opened on 10 October. FTN News reported that incumbent President Teasoups and Nasanovuh had launched campaigns; the same outlet reported a merger of the Plutocratic and Forward parties, with Forward continuing and former Plutocratic caucus members becoming independents. [ 4 ] An 18 October campaign announcement PDF said Nasanovuh intended to run on a Plutocratic ticket, while an Inside Edition News post on 14 October had said that Nasanovuh's campaign was suspended and that he endorsed ApolloKorman. The campaign announcement and suspension report conflict; the timing of Nasanovuh’s withdrawal is uncertain. [ 5 ] By 1 November, news posts identified three major tickets: Teasoups with Rathuzen, ApolloKorman with MitsuoMochizuki, and Forward nominee TradeNato with Razvanpaul. The FEC’s final notice lists TradeNato among candidates who withdrew on 8 November; the results page lists the remaining candidates and their vote totals. [ 6 ] The ApolloKorman campaign received a warning from the FEC on 15 October after a complaint alleged that a campaign leader used Discord announcement channels in other communities to urge members to join nUSA and vote for ApolloKorman and another candidate. Reuters News described the FEC as finding repeated campaign announcements; the linked FEC/Group Management warning itself is the primary source for the commission’s stated action. [ 7 ] During the campaign, Teasoups’s campaign released a defense and military platform. The document proposed changes to nUSA institutions and agencies, including the Department of Defense and intelligence organizations; the proposals did not establish that those changes were enacted. [ 8 ] Election and candidates The 7 November ballot also listed TradeNato, stratnixon, Sheev_Palpatine with AdremiCross, and Joobz2121 with EmperorXD. It described ApolloKorman as independent, while the result certificate labeled his ticket Forward. The certificate did not explain the changed affiliation or stratnixon’s absence from its final distribution. adamsoups appeared in the certificate but not in that ballot notice. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] Voting The election opened on 8 November, with Reuters News reporting that voting would close on 10 November at 3 p.m. Eastern Time. On election day, outlets posted competing calls before the FEC announcement: Fact Feed Network prematurely called the race for ApolloKorman at 1:17 p.m., while The American Times projected a Teasoups win thirteen minutes later. These were media reports and projections, not the official result. The certificate separately recorded 27 votes for withdrawn TradeNato and six for withdrawn Sheev_PalpatineTGR/AdremiCross, bringing the itemized total to the stated 308 post-filter voters. It reported 18 new voters; pre-filter turnout and invalidations were not stated. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] Certification and transition The certificate scheduled the winning ticket’s inauguration for 23 November. Contemporary news reported that Teasoups and Rathuzen took their oaths that day; the electoral certification and inauguration were distinct events. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] Inauguration The FEC results notice scheduled the inauguration for 23 November 2024, nearly two weeks after the result announcement. The American Times reported that Teasoups and Rathuzen took their oaths that day, describing Teasoups as beginning a second term and the 53rd President in the group’s sequence. The result announcement and the later reported swearing-in were separate events. title: 2025 constitutional crisis (nUSA)
text: The 2025 constitutional crisis (nUSA) was a May 2025 dispute in the Roblox nUSA roleplay government over the impeachment of President Rathuzen and the certification of its result. In a 20 May community statement, nUSA ownership reported that the Chief Justice had been expelled during the impeachment trial, two Associate Justices had been blacklisted, and Supreme Court Justice Leroux had refused to certify the impeachment. Ownership described the resulting situation as constitutional limbo and referred the dispute to a three-judge District Court panel while keeping Rathuzen in office pending a decision. [ 1 ] The statement is ownership's account of the dispute and its proposed resolution; it is not itself a court judgment or an independent finding about the stated causes of the disciplinary actions. [ 2 ] Impeachment and certification dispute Ownership said the crisis began during the President's impeachment trial. Its statement reported that the Chief Justice was expelled during the trial and that two Associate Justices were subsequently blacklisted for violations of the community's terms of service. It then identified Justice Leroux's refusal to certify the President's impeachment as the immediate escalation. Those descriptions are attributed to the ownership announcement; the notice does not reproduce the underlying disciplinary records or explain the constitutional provision governing certification. [ 3 ] Ownership said the impasse required intervention to restore constitutional order and protect roleplay integrity. It chose to defer the question to what it called the only remaining court, the District Court, while the President remained in office under the status quo. The message thus documented a management decision about interim status and jurisdiction during the dispute, rather than a completed impeachment or a ruling on its merits. [ 4 ] District Court referral The announced panel consisted of Waffles, Jtport, and Moneymack. Ownership directed the judges to review the matter in a public trial and issue a final, binding decision within 72 hours after the case began. It also said preliminary injunctions would not be permitted and that Rathuzen would remain President unless the District Court decided otherwise. [ 5 ] The referral followed the 2024 judicial reset (nUSA) , which had separately announced replacement of sitting judges and justices and requested merit-based confirmations. The panel issued an opinion three days after ownership's referral; its holding and remedy are set out below. [ 6 ] District Court decision In Rathuzen v. United States Senate et al. , decided 23 May 2025, the three-judge panel accepted jurisdiction over the challenge. The majority concluded that the presidential impeachment trial was procedurally invalid when an acting Chief Justice designated Justice Leroux to preside even though Leroux was not the next eligible justice in the succession prescribed by the roleplay's cited law. The opinion expressly declined to decide Rathuzen's separate claim that the House had not met the impeachment threshold. This was a ruling about the authority of the presiding officer, not a judgment on the underlying impeachment accusations. [ 7 ] The majority ordered the Senate to reconvene and vote again with a lawfully seated Chief Justice or acting successor. Because the court described all Supreme Court seats as vacant at that time, it stayed execution of the revote order until one of those officers could be seated. Judge Cardozo dissented in part, arguing that the judicial succession statute did not govern a Senate impeachment trial; Judge Mackie also dissented in part from the majority's succession analysis. The reviewed decision does not itself show whether a new Chief Justice was seated or a new Senate vote occurred. title: 2025 constitutional readoption in nUSA
text: A NARA public post dated 16 May 2025 reported that a Constitution associated with Timothy F. Geithner had been readopted and revised through Public Law 105-1 (S.J. Res. 14) on 12 May. The NARA Hub's “TimCons 09-22-18” card links a document whose cover identifies it as authored on 22 September 2018 and re-adopted on 12 May 2025. A separate Public Law Database entry gives the constitutional text an 8 September 2017 origin and an additional 17 January 2024 readoption date; the available sources do not reconcile these versions. [ 1 ] Announcement and document The NARA public announcement attributes the Constitution's development to Timothy F. Geithner in late 2018 and says the text was readopted with revisions by P.L. 105-1, identified as S.J. Res. 14. Zhang Jinping signed the announcement as Archivist. The dated post documents NARA's account of the process; it does not independently establish details absent from the underlying resolution or a complete convention history. [ 2 ] The attached 17-page PDF cover says “TimCons 09-22-18,” gives 22 September 2018 as the authorship date and 12 May 2025 as the readoption date. The NARA Hub marks that card “Active Constitution.” These are document and board status statements; they support identifying the archived copy but do not erase the discrepant 2017 and January 2024 dates found in the separate PLD entry. [ 3 ] Version and status questions The Public Law Database history card describes a constitution adopted on 8 September 2017, readopted on 17 January 2024 and readopted again on 12 May 2025. The Hub, in contrast, names a September 2018 TimCons version. The records may concern a related text lineage or different drafts, but no accessible source here explains the discrepancy. Accordingly, this article reports both attributions rather than treating either origin date as settled. [ 4 ] The July 2023 Constitution is a distinct archived version, published and instituted on 17 July 2023 and labeled inactive on the Hub snapshot. The 2024 “GobiesCons” record is also labeled inactive, while TimCons bears the active label. This pattern suggests the Hub's recorded status at export time, but board labels do not supply a complete legal transition history or explain the exact effect of P.L. 105-1. [ 5 ] Relationship to NARA and prior versions The 2023 Constitution expressly assigns NARA records responsibilities. The 19-page May 2025 Constitution PDF was inspected, but it contains no searchable NARA clause. That absence alone cannot establish that NARA's authority was removed or changed; the documents may address the agency differently, or the PDF text may omit relevant language in a way not captured by extraction. [ 6 ] The 2025 readoption is part of a broader sequence that includes the July 2023 legal reset and a Constitution announced as passed in November 2024. The sources reviewed do not state in one place how the 2024 text transitioned to the 2025 version. See Constitutions of nUSA , 2024 Constitution of nUSA and 2023 nUSA legal reset . title: 2025 presidential elections (nUSA)
text: The 2025 nUSA presidential elections included a March election and later July and November contests. The records distinguish schedules, certified results, and public oath announcements; they do not fully explain every transition or roster ordinal. March election Main article: Elections in nUSA The Federal Election Commission's 13 March ballot notice listed Pioneer Party nominees Rathuzen and snowbleed, Forward Party nominees aConArtist and Frosty_TheSn0wman, and independent candidates FighterHath and warlockings. Voting was scheduled for 14–16 March, with inauguration planned for 23 March. [ 1 ] The 16 March results reported 444 ballots, 44 filtered out, and 400 valid. The Rathuzen–snowbleed ticket received 60.75% (269 ballots; 243 valid); aConArtist–Frosty_theSn0wman received 28.0% (123; 112 valid); and FighterHath–warlockings received 11.25% (52; 45 valid). The FEC declared Rathuzen and snowbleed President-elect and Vice President-elect for a term scheduled to begin 23 March and end 20 July. [ 2 ] On 23 March, an owner-affiliated post advertised Rathuzen's inauguration as happening; later announcements publicly identified Rathuzen as President and snowbleed as Vice President. The inspected posts do not contain oath text. [ 3 ] July election The July presidential schedule changed during the campaign. The initial notice scheduled voting for 11–13 July and described a term beginning 20–26 July, ending 22 November. On 5 July, the National Elections Administrator extended registration, allowed a Forward Party primary, and moved voting to 18–20 July; the 18 July schedule described a term beginning 21 July and ending 21 November. [ 4 ] The 20 July NEA Discord post named @zapz. as President-elect and linked a certificate that instead names aConArtist the 56th President. The accessible one-page certificate lists 99 votes for aConArtist, 72 for Fighterhath, 25 for Saviorjosh, and one each for Rammarchangel and Old_dude47. A separate inaugural notice identifies aConArtist and TacticalRock101 as President-elect and Vice President-elect and schedules their ceremony for 25 July. The owner later announced that aConArtist's inauguration was starting. The inspected July records do not include an oath transcript or explicit completion notice. [ 5 ] November election On 23 October, a public notice named Bathamza as the Pioneer Party nominee and ArmanFoley as the Forward Party nominee; independent candidates could register beginning 7 November. The NEA's 4 November notice scheduled voting for 14–16 November and said the term would begin 21 November and end 21 March 2026. [ 6 ] Mallsoft appeared on the 14 November ballot and was disqualified that day. The announcement does not state the reason. The results document certified Bathamza as President-elect and the 58th President, with 111 votes; it did not name a Vice President. On 22 November, the NEA announced that Bathamza had just been sworn in as President alongside Vice President aConArtist. The published schedule's 21 November start and the reported 22 November oath date differ by one day. [ 7 ] Roster and transition limits NARA's roster lists Rathuzen as 54th, snowbleed as 55th, Mallsoft as 56th, and aConArtist as 57th. The accessible July FEC certificate calls aConArtist the 56th President; November results identify Bathamza as 58th. The checked sources do not explain the ordinal differences or establish a dated Mallsoft accession. The roster labels should be reported as NARA entries rather than treated as a complete succession history. title: 2026 military reorganization (nUSA)
text: Suspension of independent Marine Corps and Air Force operations in July 2026 The 2026 military reorganization was a consolidation of the armed forces ordered by President jsjsjbsd in July 2026. An executive order dated 8 July suspended the independent operations of the Marine Corps and Air Force and directed the transfer of their active personnel into the Army and Navy. The President publicly announced the measure on 9 July as a response to strategic needs discussed with military leadership. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] The order preserved the suspended branches' legal existence. It expressly distinguished suspension from abolition, allowing their reconstitution by a later executive order or an act of Congress. Its immediate focus was personnel, command arrangements and readiness rather than the permanent elimination of Marine and Air Force institutions. [ 3 ] Recruitment and independent operations The order halted recruitment, enlistment, commissioning and accession in both branches upon signing. It also suspended independent training, deployments, promotions and disciplinary proceedings, except where required for orderly transfers of personnel and records. The transition thus affected both the entry of new servicemembers and the continuing administration of those already serving. [ 4 ] The President invoked his constitutional and statutory authority as commander in chief and referred to consultation with the Board of Governors under Article XXXV. His public explanation emphasized strengthening military readiness and optimizing the command structure. The text directed the Department of Defense to preserve the standing of personnel affected by the consolidation. [ 5 ] [ 6 ] Personnel transfers All active Marine Corps personnel were to transfer to the Army. Marine units would be integrated into corresponding Army commands at the discretion of the Army chief of staff and staff. Air Force personnel were to transfer to the Navy's Naval Aviation Forces, with assignments determined by the chief of naval operations and staff. [ 7 ] Air Force Special Operations Command personnel received a separate destination: Naval Special Warfare Command, with integration into SEAL teams determined by its commander and staff. The order therefore provided more specific arrangements than a general move of all air personnel into an undifferentiated naval organization. [ 8 ] Rank and service records Transfers were not to reduce a servicemember's grade, rate or rank. Receiving branches had to recognize existing service records, commendations, decorations and awards in full. No decoration could be revoked or downgraded because of the reorganization. These protections made continuity of individual service a stated condition of the institutional consolidation. [ 9 ] The order also preserved other lawful departmental and agency authority and included a severability provision. Its instructions establish the transfers and safeguards the administration ordered; they do not supply a completion date for every personnel movement. The July announcement presented the measure as an active transition with the suspended branches available for future restoration. title: AConArtist
text: aConArtist 57th President of nUSA (NARA roster) In office 25 July 2025 (inauguration) – 22 November 2025 [ 1 ] Preceded by Mallsoft Succeeded by bathamza NARA Presidential Records roster aConArtist is listed as the 57th President of the Roblox nUSA roleplay government. An inaugural committee announcement identified aConArtist as President-elect with TacticalRock101 as Vice President-elect in July 2025 and scheduled a July 25 oath; a same-day notice announced that the inauguration was starting. NARA later listed aConArtist as the 67th Vice President, reflecting another office after the 57th presidency. The sources reviewed here do not establish the exact time at which either presidential or later vice-presidential service ended. [ 2 ] Judicial service before the presidency Court and congressional archives record several judicial nominations and service periods under the name aConArtist. The nominations board has entries for Associate Justice and Chief District Court Judge. The court roster contains a Justice aConArtist entry and a separate second-term entry, while a district-court archive lists a senior judge. These records show judicial involvement across different periods, but the card titles alone do not establish a continuous tenure or the disposition of any particular lawsuit. The reviewed sources do not provide a verified prior mayoral or congressional term. [ 3 ] Presidential election and term The July 20 announcement congratulated the aConArtist–TacticalRock101 ticket and planned an inauguration on July 25. Its stated theme was “On the Edge of a New American Dawn”. On July 25 the committee called the inauguration to order, while the later NARA roster records aConArtist as the 57th President. The available notices do not include a certified vote total or the text of the oath. NARA places Mallsoft immediately before aConArtist and bathamza after him, but does not give exact transition dates on those profile cards. [ 4 ] A House resolution titled Impeaching aConArtist, President of the United States is preserved in the congressional board's Failed Items list. Its title documents a proposed impeachment, not a finding that the charges were true or that the President was removed. The reviewed Presidential Records board does not include a dated executive order under aConArtist's name, so the surviving records consulted for this article cannot support a detailed account of presidential policy or a reason for departure. [ 5 ] Vice presidency and later court listing People bid farewell to aConArtist beside a presidential helicopter during his later period in office. The supplied screenshot does not establish the date or precise occasion. In November 2025, an inauguration report identified aConArtist as the Vice President sworn in alongside 58th President bathamza. A March 2026 announcement again identified bathamza and aConArtist as President-elect and vice-President-elect and scheduled their next inauguration. This later service is consistent with NARA's 67th vice-presidential listing, though the roster gives no term dates. A Supreme Court card last updated in 2026 also describes aConArtist as a senior associate justice following a nomination by bathamza; the record does not establish how that court role relates chronologically to the vice presidency. [ 6 ] 2025 FEC election records In July 2025, the NEA's linked election certificate named aConArtist the 56th President and listed 99 votes for him. The Discord post linking the certificate instead named @zapz. as President-elect. A separate inaugural notice identified aConArtist and TacticalRock101 as President-elect and Vice President-elect, scheduled their ceremony for 25 July, and the owner later announced that aConArtist's inauguration was starting. The inspected July records do not include an oath transcript or explicit confirmation of completion. In November, the NEA announced that Bathamza had just been sworn in as the 58th President alongside Vice President aConArtist. The reviewed records establish this later VP pairing but do not explain when or how aConArtist moved from the July presidential result to the vice presidency. NARA lists him as 57th, unlike the July certificate. title: AdamStratton
text: AdamStratton is an account recorded in nUSA announcements as a Government Group Manager and participant in institutional oversight in 2024. The June 2024 management restructuring appointed AdamStratton to the Government Group Manager post, assigning it responsibility for Group Management entities connected to the roleplay environment. [ 1 ] Government Group Manager In June 2024, UKR41NIAN announced that the existing Group Manager liaison posts for the judicial, executive, and legislative branches would merge into a single Government Group Manager role; National Archives and Records Administration (nUSA) was to retain a separate manager. The same notice named AdamStratton as appointee and described the position as covering roleplay-facing entities, with FRB and FBA given as examples. [ 2 ] The archived record shows AdamStratton exercising that remit through a constitutional convention notice. In August 2024, a message signed “AdamStratton, Group Oversight and Government Group Manager” certified and bound a convention proposed by the President, stating that the President could begin proceedings under the Constitution. [ 3 ] Role in constitutional governance The two notices place the Government Group Manager between Group Management and the roleplay institutions it oversaw: the appointment announcement defined the remit, and the later convention message applied that authority to a constitutional procedure. These sources establish what the office was said to do in that period, but do not document a complete term or a formal end date for AdamStratton's appointment. title: Aerium
text: Aerium 7th President of nUSA In office 23 September 2014 – 29 November 2014 [ 1 ] Preceded by Lumidas Succeeded by Pathwaysbball Aerium was the seventh President of the United States , serving from 23 September to 29 November 2014. He later served as a Clan Manager and election administrator in 2019, receiving a trial appointment in July and a full appointment in August with responsibility for election, military, and community portfolios. [ 2 ] Clan Management and elections A 9 July 2019 public notice designated Aerium a trial Clan Manager for thirty days, with full appointment to follow at the end of the trial. The accompanying letter described the group's appointment process and the trial's connection to a planned handover of election and military oversight duties. [ 3 ] On 13 August, the announcement said Aerium had fully ascended to Clan Manager and would take over the National Elections Administrator and Military Clan Manager posts, as well as a Community Clan Manager assignment. The linked letter described the National Elections Administrator as the senior overseer or commissioner of the Federal Election Commission (nUSA) , responsible for elections, rules, and procedures. [ 4 ] The election records provide examples of this portfolio in practice: a May 2019 letter certifies Senate Class III results, and a June letter delivers House Class I results to the outgoing Speaker. Both documents bear Aerium's name and are linked from election-result announcements. [ 5 ] Later government service A July 2019 Senate bi-weekly report identified Aerium as a former President selected to serve as Senate President Pro Tempore. The report also summarized Senate activity, including consideration of the National Archives Reformation Act, placing Aerium's later Senate role in the period when the group was discussing archival organization. [ 6 ] Election documentation The Senate results letter reported seven winners in the Class III contest and stated that voters disqualified by the election process would be placed on a voting blacklist. The House Class I letter delivered twelve winners to the outgoing Speaker and likewise described a blacklist for disqualified voters. These are statements within the election documents about their own procedures; the article does not repeat the names or circumstances of individual voters. [ 7 ] The sequence links formal staff appointment with concrete records work: as elections lead, Aerium's letters moved results to the relevant legislative recipients, while the Senate report places Aerium in a separate parliamentary post later that summer. This distinction matters because the Group Manager, National Elections Administrator, Military Clan Manager, Community Clan Manager, and Senate President Pro Tempore were different roleplay positions, each documented in a different type of record. title: Akacoolguy96
text: Akacoolguy96 49th President of nUSA (NARA roster) In office 10 December 2023 – 15 February 2024 [ 1 ] Preceded by UnitedGPT Succeeded by Robbiebeastpro90000 NARA Presidential Records roster Akacoolguy96 (also styled Akacoolguy96GPT in contemporary records) was the 49th President of the United States in the nUSA roleplay community. His administration issued executive orders on Treasury powers, national-security classification, martial law in Colorado and the District of Columbia , and executive-branch oversight. Group Management removed him from office in February 2024 and announced a one-month blacklist; that action was a community-management decision, not an adjudicated finding in the available record. [ 2 ] Election and inauguration The Federal Election Commission announced on December 5, 2023, that Akacoolguy96GPT and Robbiebeastpro90000 had won the Winter 2023 presidential election as President- and vice-President-elect. The announcement said the inauguration would be planned for the following weekend. On December 10, a separate community notice invited members to the presidential inauguration that evening. [ 3 ] Executive orders Executive Order 49-001, dated December 11, 2023, delegated the Treasury Secretary’s powers and duties to the Secretary of Commerce and Labor. It expressly included fiscal policy, public-debt management, and oversight of the monetary system, and directed other executive departments and agencies to assist the receiving department. [ 4 ] Executive Order 49-002, dated December 12, established a classification and declassification framework for national-security information. Its 52-page text set three classification levels; restricted original classification to designated authorities and specified national-security categories; and provided for written delegations and time-limited declassification. The order also called for publication in a Federal Register. [ 5 ] On December 24, Executive Order 49-003 declared martial law in Colorado for no longer than 72 hours. The order said the governor had requested federal assistance, ordered elements of the Colorado National Guard into federal service, placed the deployed forces under General Joshua Nomikos, and authorized military tribunals for matters arising from detention during the period. These are the order’s stated grounds and provisions, not independent findings about the events it described. [ 6 ] An order signed January 22, 2024, created a Bureau of Internal Affairs as a subordinate office of the Executive Office of the President. It assigned the Bureau complaint intake, investigations, agency reviews, and recommendations; authorized suspensions of up to two months and terminations in specified circumstances; and set an executive-branch employment bar for certain conduct. The order provided an appeal first to an appointed appeals attorney and then to the White House Chief of Staff, and required presidential approval for action against Senate-confirmed officers. [ 7 ] The Trello archive indexes a second “Declaration of Martial Law” as Executive Order 49-005. Its attached PDF is dated February 3, 2024, but labels itself Executive Order 49-002. It declared martial law in the District of Columbia in response to what the order called a “Zombie Outbreak,” created a Joint Containment Task Force for the duration of martial law, ordered National Guard forces into federal service, and tied the end of martial law and the task force to containment of the outbreak. [ 8 ] Removal from office On February 14, 2024, Group Management announced that it had voted to ban the serving President under a community guideline and impose a one-month blacklist, removing him from office. Its February 15 public statement described allegations of accepting in-game-rank bribes as the reason for the action; the statement is Group Management’s account of its decision and allegations, not a court judgment. In the same announcement, management said Robbiebeastpro90000 would serve as acting President under the line of succession until the next President was sworn in. A January 28 election notice had set March 16 for the Spring election and March 21 for the inauguration, after management said the earlier election calendar conflicted with the Constitution. [ 9 ] References 2024 FEC election records On 18 June 2024, the Federal Election Commission announced that Akacoolguy96GPT had been removed from the July presidential candidate list and that his campaign was being dissolved into Teasoups’s campaign. The FEC described the merger as accepted by both parties and final. This notice documents the disposition of the campaign; it does not establish a later term in office or a party affiliation for Akacoolguy96. title: AntonioTRoosevelt
text: Antonio T. Roosevelt 28th President of nUSA In office 29 August 2019 – 21 November 2019 [ 1 ] Preceded by SpeakerJosh (JoshMiller in NARA roster) Succeeded by JamesMontagu NARA Presidential Records roster Antonio T. Roosevelt (account name AntonioTRoosevelt ) was identified by the nUSA roleplay community's archives as its 28th President. The records reviewed here concern the simulated government of the Roblox group; they do not describe the real United States government. The Presidential Records board places Roosevelt between JoshMiller, listed as the 27th President, and JamesMontagu, listed as the 29th. A separate presidential-library card also calls him the 28th President. [ 2 ] Presidency and election The Federal Election Commission's plan for the Fall 2019 election described the next presidential term as running from 21 November 2019 through 21 March 2020. Its ballot, published in nUSA's #announcements channel on 17 October, included Roosevelt as the Republican candidate. The contemporaneous election letter reported 653 votes, 30 disqualified as alternate accounts, and 220 votes for Roosevelt, with five of those votes disqualified. JamesMontagu received 322 votes, with 11 disqualified. [ 3 ] The result letter named JamesMontagu the winner and President-elect but also said an injunction meant he did not yet qualify for office. Applying the cited 20th Amendment provision, the National Elections Administrator declared vice-President-elect TomFoley acting President-elect until a President qualified. The announcement record changed later that day: in #announcements , Aerium first congratulated TomFoley after posting the letter, then wrote, “Tom not gon' be President, Jame gon' be President.” This sequence records the initial ruling and its rapid change in public presentation; it does not explain the legal or procedural basis for the change. [ 4 ] Roosevelt was in office during this election period: an Executive Archives card says he nominated AdremiCross as Secretary of Veterans Affairs on 8 October 2019, and that the Senate confirmed the nomination on 13 October. The same card records AdremiCross's resignation on 5 November. On 20 November, the #nusa-updates channel announced that President-elect Montagu would be inaugurated the following night. A message the next day linked to JamesMontagu's presidential inauguration, and Roosevelt posted that it had been a “really good 3 months” and signed off. The post does not by itself identify his role, but the roster sequence and Montagu's inauguration place the end of Roosevelt's presidency on 21 November 2019; he entered office on 29 August 2019. [ 1 ] [ 5 ] The archival numbering was itself corrected. The Executive Archives created Roosevelt's former-President card on 25 October 2019 as “AntonioTRoosevelt, 27th,” then changed its title to “AntonioTRoosevelt, 28th” on 18 November. The Presidential Records roster and the library card likewise give him the 28th number. The earlier card title is a reason to treat the ordinal as the archive's eventual classification rather than assume every contemporary record used it consistently. [ 6 ] Prior office and administration Before the presidency, the Executive Archives listed Roosevelt as a former Vice President. Its card, created on 16 September 2019, identified him as the 34th Vice President. A later Presidential Records card identifies him as the 37th Vice President; its February 2024 activity log shows that the card's ordinal was changed from 35th to 37th. The records do not explain the numbering changes or give dates for the vice-presidential service represented by the later card, so the two entries cannot be combined into a settled chronology. [ 7 ] Two orders are catalogued under the 28th-presidency sequence. Executive Order 28-001 is titled “Creation of the Office of Government Ethics,” and Executive Order 28-002 “Dissolution of the Special Forces.” The Presidential Records board currently marks both cards “Repealed.” The board entries link to separate documents, but the local source archive contains only the card metadata, not the order texts; their provisions, dates, implementation, and reasons for repeal are therefore not established here. [ 8 ] The legislative archive also indexes Senate Concurrent Resolution 22, “To encourage President Roosevelt to resign,” with “Passed Senate” and “Passed House” labels. Senate Resolution 190, “The Roosevelt Treaty,” is labeled “Treaty” and “Passed Senate.” These are the titles and status labels preserved on the board cards; the available entries do not establish the resolutions' terms, legal effect, or whether the treaty was ultimately ratified. [ 9 ] Archival record and later listings The Presidential Records board's library card says Roosevelt's “complete works” were transferred to a library managed by NARA's Presidential Archives division and library staff, and links to a Trello page named rooseveltlibrary . This is the archive's own description of the collection; the card alone does not verify that the collection is complete or that all listed records remain accessible. The collection is part of the broader nUSA presidential-library system . [ 10 ] The available sources document Roosevelt as a presidential candidate, officeholder, former Vice President, and subject of later legislative records, but do not provide a reliable full account of his later public roles. For the election chronology and the archives responsible for preserving these records, see 2019 presidential elections , United States Congress , and NARA . title: Archivist Act of 2020 (nUSA)
text: The Archivist Act of 2020 is the title of a two-page roleplay bill, S. 244, dated 5 April 2020. It sets out a process for preserving signed legislation in the NARA database and attaching legislative copies to Trello records. The PLD catalogs the card as “Public Law 80-2,” but its description says the attached document is archived, and the available copy does not by itself establish enactment or compliance. [ 1 ] Proposed records workflow S. 244 directs the Archivist to download a bill after presidential signature and upload a copy to the NARA database. It also allows a link or PDF as the stored copy. The bill presents this as an archival step following signature, rather than a rule for deciding the bill’s policy merits. [ 2 ] The document further calls for signed legislation to be attached to Trello cards, citing problems with Google Drive availability. This creates a second copy or pointer in the legislative record system alongside the NARA database entry. The text records the workflow the bill proposed; it is not evidence that every signed bill was copied or that the process was consistently followed. [ 3 ] Status and later practice The Public Law Database card’s “Public Law 80-2” label is an index entry, while its note that the attachment is archived and the PDF’s presentation as S. 244 leave the status unresolved in the reviewed sources. The proposal can be described as a documented archival workflow without treating it as proven operative law. [ 4 ] In July 2023, Group Management Memorandum #001 described a later compliance process for legislative records, including standardized templates and metadata. The memorandum concerns archival review and acceptance; it should be read separately from the 2020 bill-copy workflow. [ 5 ] Related pages See National Archives and Records Administration (nUSA) , Public Law Database (nUSA) , National Archives Reformation Act of 2019 (nUSA) , NARA Hub , and NUSA archival policy . ↑ Public Law 80-2 card ; S. 244, Archivist Act of 2020 , pp. 1–2. ↑ S. 244 , pp. 1–2. ↑ S. 244 , p. 2; Public Law 80-2 card . ↑ Public Law 80-2 card ; S. 244 , pp. 1–2. ↑ Group Management Memorandum #001 / Volume 1 , pp. 1–2; Discord #nusa-updates, 17 July 2023, Python splitlines() line 22,658.

title: ArnieVinick
text: ArnieVinick 34th President of nUSA (NARA roster) In office 21 November 2020 – 9 January 2021 [ 1 ] Preceded by Lacryma Succeeded by LordDeathTheReaper NARA Presidential Records roster ArnieVinick was the 34th President of the United States, serving from 21 November 2020 to 9 January 2021. Elected as the Republican candidate with LordDeathTheReaper as his running mate, he introduced employment and military-service initiatives and reorganized parts of the executive branch. He resigned after admitting that he had initiated a proposed bribery arrangement, while also describing the burdens of the presidency and worsening political hostility. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] Election and transition The FEC's certified results letter reported 831 votes received, with 341 manually disqualified for alternate accounts or lack of nUSA citizenship. It named Arnie as the Republican Party's winning candidate and LordDeathTheReaper as Vice President-elect. The FEC post releasing the result appeared in #announcements on 10 November and linked the signed results letter dated 11 November. Arnie was inaugurated on 21 November, as confirmed by the contemporary invitation and oath photograph. [ 4 ] Executive orders Arnie's 21 November 2020 order sought to reduce combat tryouts for executive-branch jobs. It barred departments and agencies from using combat tryouts as a hiring standard, allowed presidential exemptions, and listed Special Forces and the Special Weapons and Tactics Team as initial exemptions; the United States Military was permanently exempted. The order's stated rationale was to emphasize other skills for most executive jobs and make combat tryouts less common. [ 5 ] On 22 December 2020, Arnie ordered the Special Weapons and Tactics Team redirected under the Department of Justice, with its commander reporting to the Attorney General. The order said the team would retain its authority to operate and enforce law. A separate Trello card records that Arnie revoked BernardCaldwell's Executive Order 32-003 establishing the Internal Affairs Institute; the card says no formal order was written, and its attached screenshot is a 23 November 2020 announcement. The screenshot documents the announcement and the stated revocation, not a surviving signed instrument. [ 6 ] Two orders dated 5 January 2021 created employment programs linked to military service. One established a Veterans' Assistance Program jointly managed by the Departments of Veterans Affairs and Commerce and Labor, with a database of veterans' employment status and active-duty personnel and a process for participating agencies to consider eligible veterans for jobs. The other directed listed federal agencies to offer promotions or promotional points to eligible employees after at least 30 days of honorable military service, subject to agency rules and exclusions for capped senior positions. The documents establish what the orders directed; the archive does not show how fully the programs were implemented. [ 7 ] Resignation On 9 January 2021, Arnie submitted a signed resignation to Secretary of State ThomasLaRusso, effective at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Standard Time. His accompanying farewell admitted initiating a proposed bribe involving a longtime friend and accepted responsibility. He apologized to the officials who had served honestly in his administration and said his conduct had undermined their work. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] The farewell also described personal and political strain. Arnie said that the presidency had ceased to be enjoyable, that he had lost friends and that its responsibilities had been greater than anticipated. He regretted leaving much of his campaign agenda unfinished, while praising his appointees and the Veterans' Assistance Program, which he described as still being developed. He expressed confidence in LordDeathTheReaper's succession and urged citizens to remain engaged and hold their leaders accountable. [ 2 ] Arnie connected the country's difficulties to increasing toxicity, which he believed had driven the community away from its earlier peak. This was his assessment of the political climate at the time of his departure, rather than a measured account of player activity. [ 2 ] Other recorded office A judiciary-board profile identifies LewisFPowellJr (ArnieVinick) as an Associate Justice of the Supreme Court, appointed by President ArnieVinick, with an incumbency beginning 22 December 2020 and retirement on 19 April 2021. The profile does not explain how that service related to Arnie's presidential tenure, so the dates are reported as recorded rather than treated as a separate presidential term. [ 8 ] The NARA board also contains a separate empty card titled “ArnieVinick, 42nd.” That ordinal conflicts with the compiled presidential table, which lists Cyxlinder as the 42nd President. The available records do not reconcile the two entries, so the separate card is not treated here as evidence of another Arnie presidency. Both files were linked by ghostz in #white-house , 9 January 2021, 2:17 p.m. PST. title: August 2020 nUSA–United Kingdom ultimatum
text: The August 2020 nUSA–United Kingdom ultimatum was a diplomatic and military threat issued by President BernardCaldwell during his second term in the Roblox nUSA roleplay community. A four-page document dated 6 August 2020 presents a joint ultimatum by nUSA and a Zimbabwe roleplay government. It says a state of war would exist if the United Kingdom group did not accept specified demands by 7 August. A separate two-page congressional document dated 7 August is headed Declaration of War against the United Kingdom , but the copy supplied here contains only introductory text and a link back to the ultimatum. These records establish the threat and a proposed resolution; they do not, on their own, show that the resolution passed or that a later battle occurred. [ 1 ] Background The ultimatum says that an earlier set of demands had been withdrawn after the exile of a person it calls Finley. It accuses the United Kingdom government of continuing diplomatic insults and threats and says attempts at a diplomatic resolution had failed. These are the nUSA and Zimbabwe signatories' account of the dispute, not an independent record of the United Kingdom's conduct. The document names Prime Minister Phentemjerker and a leader of the Yada Clan among those from whom apologies were sought. [ 2 ] The document is signed in the names of BernardCaldwell, Vice President Lacryma , Secretary of State Federated C. Enfield, White House Chief of Staff Tacus N. Enfield, Principal Deputy Secretary of State Jask M. Enfield, and Savage_Yada, identified there as Zimbabwe's premier and the Yada Clan's leader. The signatures identify who the ultimatum represented as supporting it; the supplied copy does not independently verify each person's consent or role beyond the text of the document. [ 3 ] Demands and proposed war resolution The ultimatum demanded a public apology to the United States, its citizens and government; a separate apology to Jask M. Enfield; the playing of the United States anthem at parliamentary sessions for three months; United Kingdom support for United States votes in the roleplay United Nations General Assembly and Security Council for three months; and reopening diplomatic channels. It stated that rejection would produce a state of war at midnight British Summer Time on Friday, 7 August 2020. The deadline and threatened consequence are claims made by the ultimatum, not proof of a subsequent declaration or combat. [ 4 ] The second file presents itself as an 81st Congress joint resolution introduced by Teasoup of Florida on 7 August, with BernardCaldwell named as President. Its first page announces a declaration of war, but the text supplied stops after the beginning of Part II. The second page links to a Google Drive copy of the ultimatum, whose content matches the separately supplied four-page file. No vote tally, final enacted text, presidential signature on a completed resolution, or battle report is contained in these two files. Their relationship to any actual hostilities remains to be established from further contemporary records. [ 5 ] Distinction from the April war The April 2020 nUSA–United Kingdom war occurred under President Reset4K , who publicly described peace talks on 11 April. The August ultimatum is dated almost four months later and names BernardCaldwell as President. Both involve United Kingdom roleplay counterparts, but the reviewed files do not state that the August dispute was a continuation of the April conflict or identify the same negotiated treaty. They are treated here as separate events pending further evidence. [ 6 ] References ↑ An Ultimatum to the United Kingdom , 6 August 2020, pp. 1–3; Declaration of War against the United Kingdom , 7 August 2020, pp. 1–2. title: AustinBoBoston1
text: AustinBoBoston1 is a Roblox nUSA community archivist whose documented work covered judicial records and later leadership of the National Archives and Records Administration (nUSA) (NARA). On 9 March 2024, an appointment announcement elevated Austin from Assistant Archivist for the Judicial Branch to Archivist of the United States. It said Austin had been involved with NARA since 2022 and had preserved judicial records after first serving as a District Judge. [ 1 ] Judicial records and appointment The March 2024 announcement described Austin’s earlier archival portfolio as judicial records and noted that the appointment allowed continued service as an Associate Justice. The stated basis for the exception was that both roles required political abstention. This was a contemporaneous appointment description; the export does not provide a full record of Austin’s judicial or archival start and end dates. [ 2 ] NARA’s monthly update for July 2024 lists one law, four executive orders, and six Supreme Court opinions among the records summarized. It signs off with Austin as Archivist of the United States and cherrydearest as Deputy Archivist. A September staff spotlight separately called Austin a NARA Archivist and FEC Legal Commissioner and credited them with development-team quality assurance and work on an inauguration update. [ 3 ] Records work and leadership transition In August 2024, NARA advertised an Executive Archivist (Assistant Archivist) opening whose tasks included recording executive orders, statements, appointment dates, and nominations, liaising with the cabinet, and managing a records Trello. The post directed candidates to Austin or Dearest with questions, indicating Austin’s involvement in NARA staffing at that time. It does not assign Austin every executive-record task in the posting. [ 4 ] A later verified nUSA announcement selected snowbleed as the next Archivist in February 2025. The announcement names the next officeholder but does not say when Austin’s service ended or describe the handoff, so the exact length of Austin’s tenure remains unspecified in the available records.
