title: BUDDHA (nUSA president)
text: BUDDHA President of nUSA In office By 9 August 2017 – end date unverified Preceded by Not established Succeeded by Not established BUDDHA was an account serving as President of the nUSA Roblox roleplay community in at least August–October 2017. The archived Discord identifies BUDDHA as President in public notices and records an announced plan to leave office on November 1, 2017, but it does not establish the exact start date or fully document the transition that followed. [ 1 ] Executive orders and public access In a September 4, 2017 message, BUDDHA described executive-branch policy regulation as a presidential duty and summarized several administration orders. The measures included a national tryout schedule, a Federal Exchange intended to generate government funds and help pay for uniforms, rules requiring reasons for dropping Justice Department cases, explanations for employee dismissals, an anonymous employee complaint system, and monthly personal days for federal employees. [ 2 ] BUDDHA reposted the order summaries on September 14, saying the material should be easy for the public to access. The channel's copies describe what the administration said the orders would do; the archive does not establish whether every proposal was implemented or what effects it had. [ 3 ] He also directed users to accounts where they could follow government activity, listing the White House and Supreme Court accounts alongside his and the Vice President's accounts. In a separate October message, he invited users to send him complaints and requests directly. [ 4 ] Constitution and State of the Union On September 8, the channel announced that a new constitution had been ratified. The announcement does not identify BUDDHA as its author or describe his role in the ratification process, so it establishes the announcement rather than personal authorship. [ 5 ] On September 17, BUDDHA posted that a transcript of his State of the Union address was available for people who could not attend or watch its Twitch broadcast. The archived Discord preserves the notice and link, but not the speech's contents. [ 6 ] United Nations and departure On October 14, BUDDHA linked an application to the United Nations. The next day he announced that nUSA had been readmitted after work with allies, while another channel post separately said the application had passed the General Assembly and was awaiting a Security Council vote. The available posts preserve the administration's account of the process, not independent verification of its status within the separate roleplay organization. [ 7 ] On October 30, BUDDHA announced that he and Vice President @not sam would resign on November 1, and said a statement about a smooth transition and the reasons would be available. The archive's next-day post says a new President had taken office following the resignations of “SurpriseParty” and “JustYourDailyNoob”; it does not directly resolve how those names correspond to the BUDDHA and @not sam accounts. This leaves the outgoing transition's identity record incomplete. title: Bakedgoods
text: Bakedgoods 25th President of nUSA In office 4 April 2019 – 21 July 2019 [ 1 ] Preceded by Procursive Succeeded by Smallchomama1234 (interim) 45th President of nUSA In office 8 July 2022 – 16 September 2022 [ 1 ] Preceded by hopp_fr Succeeded by Jtport NARA presidential roster Bakedgoods was the twenty-fifth and forty-fifth president of the United States. His first presidency followed the removal of Procursive in early April 2019 and ended with his resignation on 21 July. His later administration in 2022 revoked earlier executive orders, reorganized internal oversight and established a Federal Combatant Coordinator. [ 2 ] Vice presidency On 19 February 2019, Bakedgoods was confirmed as Vice President. He thanked President Dralian for the nomination and Congress for its support. [ 3 ] Following Procursive's presidential oath on 21 March, Bakedgoods was again nominated and sworn in as Vice President. This appointment placed him in the succession position when Procursive's presidency ended. [ 4 ] Presidency and departure A White House memorandum dated April 6, 2019, is signed by Bakedgoods as President and directs executive-branch departments and agencies to maintain an employee database with updated rosters. The memo lists agencies and says intelligence databases would remain classified. Its stated completion deadline predates the memo, an apparent internal date error that does not affect its identification of Bakedgoods as President. [ 5 ] Bakedgoods resigned on 21 July 2019. Vice President Smallchomama1234 was to serve until President-elect Josh took office. [ 6 ] Bakedgoods later held the forty-fifth presidency, between hopp_fr and Jtport . His dated executive orders establish presidential service from 29 July through at least 5 August 2022; the exact beginning and end of that later term remain unspecified. [ 7 ] Second presidency Bakedgoods returned as the forty-fifth President after hopp_fr and before Jtport. Executive orders dated 29 July–5 August 2022 establish actions of this administration, although its exact oath and departure dates remain unspecified. [ 8 ] Executive orders On July 29, 2022, Executive Order 45-001 revoked all prior executive orders except those that required a department or other entity to close. The order said the revocations took effect immediately. [ 9 ] Also dated July 29, Executive Order 45-002 directed the Bureau of Internal Affairs to shut down and returned its powers to their original departments, effective immediately. [ 10 ] Executive Order 45-003, dated July 30, restored Executive Order 12-006 and directed that the Special Forces and SWAT groups reopen with the same staff they had before Executive Order 45-001. [ 11 ] An August 5 order, numbered Executive Order #0004 in its text and catalogued by the board as 45-004, established a Federal Combatant Coordinator to direct federal agencies during an invasion of Washington, D.C. The order directed federal combative and law-enforcement entities to join the Secret Service Discord. During an invasion, the coordinator would have authority over federal agencies, coordinate with agency directors and military leadership, and be selected by the President with advice from the Secretary of Defense and the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. The order also invoked martial law from 12:01 a.m. on Friday, August 5, until noon the following Monday, and said the order would expire at the end of the war. [ 12 ] All four orders are catalogued as repealed. Their repeal dates and the reasons for repeal remain unspecified. [ 13 ] Succession and the 2019 Bar controversy Bakedgoods's first presidency followed the removal of Procursive . The Senate convicted his predecessor on four articles and declined to disqualify him from future office. Bakedgoods was exercising presidential authority by 6 April. On 7 May, the Supreme Court invalidated three of the articles but sustained the remaining one, leaving Procursive's removal intact. [ 14 ] During this presidency, the administration also faced a constitutional dispute over the legal profession. Bakedgoods signed S. 147 on 27 April, attempting to move regulation of the Bar into the executive branch. Kirkman's class action produced a District Court injunction, and a successor measure sought to retain the arrangement while addressing concerns affecting existing practitioners. [ 15 ] The litigation continued through the end of Bakedgoods's presidency. On 28 July, a week after his resignation, the Supreme Court struck S. 147 down in full. Its judgment held that the executive could not administer the admission and discipline of court officers. The controversy connected the administration's legislative program with a lasting institutional dispute over the Federal Bar and separation of powers. title: Bathamza
text: bathamza 58th President of nUSA (NARA roster) In office 22 November 2025 – 8 June 2026 [ 1 ] Preceded by aConArtist Succeeded by jsjsjbsd NARA Presidential Records roster bathamza (also addressed as BathamzaShia in announcements) is listed as the 58th President of the Roblox nUSA roleplay government. An official announcement reported that he was sworn in on 22 November 2025 with Vice President aConArtist . A March 2026 committee notice again called the same pair President-elect and vice-President-elect and scheduled a further inauguration for 21 March. NARA's roster later placed jsjsjbsd after bathamza as the 59th President, and Bathamza issued a resignation statement on 8 June 2026. The reviewed records do not give the exact time of the transfer or his successor's oath. [ 2 ] Roles before the presidency Records from several institutions associate bathamza with local and federal government before the 58th presidency. The District of Columbia council board contains ordinance-list cards headed “28th Council – Mayor bathamza” and “29th Council – Mayor bathamza.” A Senate records board lists bathamza as a Class I member and as President pro tempore, while a House board has an archived membership card. These entries support service in those offices or rosters but do not by themselves provide complete terms, election results, or a sequence among them. [ 3 ] The congressional archive also has a passed-nominations card titled BathamzaShia to be Solicitor General . The card does not preserve a service date. In an announcement from 2025, bathamza was included among applicants accepted as probationary community moderators; that community-management role should be kept distinct from the roleplay offices. The two records document additional activities without showing how long bathamza held either position. [ 4 ] Election, inauguration, and second announced ticket On 17 November 2025, an inaugural-committee message congratulated bathamza as President-elect and advertised a ceremony for 22 November. The National Elections Administrator's 22 November report said bathamza had “just been sworn in” as the 58th President alongside aConArtist, and reported a peak of 123 unique players at the event. This is direct evidence of the inauguration, though the reviewed message does not give a vote tally or describe the campaign. [ 5 ] The March 19, 2026 inaugural-committee notice again congratulated bathamza and aConArtist on an election, calling them President-elect and vice-President-elect and scheduling an oath on March 21. The archive excerpt preserves the plan but no subsequent oath report or certified result for that election. It suggests a further term, while the exact March transition cannot be independently fixed from these messages alone. The later NARA board names jsjsjbsd as the next numbered President but does not state when that succession occurred. [ 6 ] Spring 2026 contested result The Spring 2026 presidential election produced conflicting public result records. The FEC's 14 March certification named Forward nominee warlockings the winner with 98 votes to Pioneer nominee bathamza's 90, and named Epicwarrior_99 vice-President-elect. It reported 284 ballots cast, 188 valid and 96 invalid. On 16 March, an owner account published an internal review alleging improper access to live vote data during filtering and reported a blind re-filter with revised totals of bathamza 117 and warlockings 109. That post did not include a replacement FEC certification in the reviewed archive. Its two-page change log lists 40 voter-status corrections, but no candidate totals. The 19 March inaugural-committee notice then called bathamza and aConArtist President-elect and vice-President-elect, without resolving the discrepancy between the FEC certificate and later management account. [ 7 ] Resignation and succession In a White House statement dated 8 June 2026, bathamza announced that he was resigning the presidency. He described nearly eight months in office across two consecutive terms and cited outside commitments and exhaustion as reasons. The letter also recounts earlier service as a House representative, deputy mayor under AlexJCabot, and later mayor, supporting a fuller sequence of offices than the archival roster cards alone provide. It addressed jsjsjbsd as the leader of the next administration. [ 8 ] That evening, the National Elections Administrator's Senate results post included a statement vacating the presidential seat. The War Room reported that bathamza's election to the Senate prompted the vacancy and that Vice President jsjsjbsd had assumed the presidency under the roleplay 25th Amendment, with an oath still expected. N-SPAN separately reported jsjsjbsd as acting President pending an oath. These contemporary accounts support the June transition, while the reviewed sources do not record the exact oath time. [ 9 ] Proposed impeachment and later records In April 2026, Representative Jace_Lol123 introduced two House resolutions alleging dereliction of duty and failure to carry out constitutional responsibilities. Their attached texts are two-page proposals, not judicial findings. The congressional board files both H. Res. 4 and H. Res. 6 under Failed Items , so their existence does not establish that the House impeached bathamza or that the allegations were proven. The reviewed archive has no Senate conviction arising from either resolution. [ 10 ] A Supreme Court petition records a claim that President bathamza imposed an executive-branch blacklist without notice or hearing. That petition states a litigant's allegation; the card alone does not establish a court ruling or the facts asserted. A later Senate Class I membership card shows bathamza in the Senate archive, but its creation or update timestamp cannot be treated as a presidential departure date. The available presidential records also lack an order collection attributed to bathamza, limiting conclusions about his administration's policies. title: Benda v. United States (nUSA)
text: 2018 decision on federal employment complaints and judicial power Benda v. United States Supreme Court of the United States Full case name Benda587 v. United States Docket 05–75 Decided 21 October 2018 Prior proceedings Certified question from District Court case 3:18–1658 Holding Section 401(g) unconstitutional on its face Opinion Holmes, joined by Marshall, Bork and O’Connor Dissent from judgment Gorsuch and Stewart Nonparticipation Kavanaugh, Kennedy and Jackson Law applied Article III; section 401(g) of the August 2018 appropriations legislation Benda v. United States was a Supreme Court decision of 21 October 2018 that invalidated a mandatory administrative barrier to litigation by federal employees. Section 401(g) of the Consolidated Appropriations and Authorizations Act of August 2018 required complaints within the National Labor Authority's jurisdiction to be heard by that body before a court could consider them. The Court held the provision unconstitutional on its face, allowing employees to bring unlawful-employment complaints directly to court. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] The dispute concerned more than the order in which a complaint was filed. It tested whether an executive institution could exercise broad and effectively unreviewable authority over disputes involving the government as employer. The Court's answer linked access to justice with the constitutional division between administrative government and independent adjudication. [ 3 ] Background Benda587 filed suit in the United States District Court for the District of Columbia , challenging the requirement under Article III. The District Court certified the constitutional question to the Supreme Court in case 3:18–1658. The administrative body named in the legislation, the National Labor Authority, had become known as the Office of the Federal Inspector General by the time of the decision. [ 4 ] Congress's requirement placed a compulsory first hearing between an employee and a court. A worker alleging unlawful dismissal or another unlawful employment action could not simply choose a judicial forum. The statute did not make that route depend on the worker's consent, and the breadth of the authority's jurisdiction made the restriction important across federal employment. [ 5 ] Article III analysis Chief Justice Holmes approached the question through the distinction between public and private rights. Congress had greater latitude to assign public-rights disputes to bodies outside Article III, and the Court accepted that most of the matters covered by section 401(g) fell within that category. It nevertheless refused to treat the label as decisive. The nature and importance of the rights, the tribunal's power, consent and Congress's reasons for choosing the administrative forum all remained relevant. [ 6 ] The Court found several defects working together. The employment rights involved were important to accountability, transparency and electoral freedom. The authority possessed unusually broad jurisdiction, its decisions were effectively unreviewable, and employees were compelled to submit to it. Congress had supplied no sufficient justification for imposing that arrangement. The Court therefore concluded that section 401(g) exceeded constitutional limits on nonjudicial adjudication. [ 7 ] Justice and rational justification The opinion also identified independent grounds for invalidation. Legislation governing judicial procedure could not contradict basic principles of justice or lack any rational justification. Applying those principles, the Court found the compulsory barrier unjustifiable under the circumstances. Its reasoning thus combined a structural Article III analysis with objections to the fairness and purpose of the procedure itself. [ 8 ] Holmes's opinion was joined by Justices Marshall, Bork and O'Connor. Gorsuch and Stewart dissented from the judgment; Kavanaugh, Kennedy and Jackson did not participate. The decision invalidated the challenged statutory requirement, rather than adjudicating every federal employment grievance or guaranteeing that an employee would prevail on the merits. [ 9 ] Consequences The immediate consequence was to remove the compulsory administrative first hearing for claims such as unlawful termination. Federal employees gained the option of seeking judicial relief directly. In the institutional history of the period, Benda sits alongside the later Bar litigation : both controversies concerned attempts to place functions closely connected with the courts under executive authority, although they involved different laws and different legal questions. [ 10 ] [ 11 ] The ruling belongs to the body of pre-2023 case law later affected by the legal reset . Its place in the history of employment rights and judicial independence remains distinct from the question of whether its precedent continued to govern after that reset. [ 12 ] ↑ Benda v. title: BernardCaldwell
text: BernardCaldwell 20th President of nUSA In office 21 July 2018 – 26 July 2018 [ 1 ] Preceded by TimGeithner Succeeded by Lordsights 32nd President of nUSA In office 21 July 2020 – 16 September 2020 [ 1 ] Preceded by Technozo Succeeded by Lacryma NARA presidential roster BernardCaldwell is an American politician who served as the 20th and 32nd President of nUSA . Before becoming President, he was elected to the House of Representatives in May 2017. [ 2 ] His first Presidential term lasted from 21 to 26 July 2018, and his second from 21 July to 16 September 2020. [ 1 ] His first term was marked by a war with the United Kingdom and impeachment by the House of Representatives . He returned to office after winning the Summer 2020 election with Lacryma . His second administration pursued changes to law enforcement and executive-branch oversight and issued an ultimatum to the United Kingdom. He also faced several sanctions imposed by Clan Management. [ 3 ] His involvement in the rival United States groups HUSA and BUSA became a recurring source of controversy in nUSA. Clan Management regarded BUSA as a continuation of HUSA and accused its organizers of threatening the community's existence. In October 2020, it permanently banned BernardCaldwell and other BUSA principals and disqualified them from nUSA citizenship. [ 4 ] 2017 House campaign and election On 2 May 2017, BernardCaldwell published a campaign speech seeking election to the House of Representatives . He criticized legislators' attendance and pledged to remain active and attend most congressional sessions. [ 5 ] His platform proposed a constitutional amendment strengthening voter requirements, electoral reform, stronger protections for Second Amendment rights, and the repeal of regulations he considered unnecessary. He also proposed legislation requiring congressional attendance and national security reforms that would expand law enforcement jurisdiction in cities. [ 5 ] On 8 May 2017, the Federal Elections Commission certified BernardCaldwell's election to House seat 23 of 24 with 20 votes. The certificate recognized him as a United States Representative and provided for a two-month term scheduled to expire on 8 July 2017. It was signed by David E. Racine, III, as Commission Overseer and Archivist of the United States. [ 2 ] First presidency and 2018 impeachment BernardCaldwell, also known as MrCaldwellRBX, was sworn in as President on 21 July 2018 in a ceremony held on Discord. Two days earlier, a congressional resolution had proposed censuring him over allegations that he promised appointments to campaign supporters. The resolution was referred to committee; its subsequent outcome is uncertain. [ 6 ] War with the United Kingdom BernardCaldwell's first presidency coincided with a war between nUSA and the United Kingdom in July 2018. On 22 July, an emergency joint session of Congress considered a declaration of war following a briefing about an alleged infiltration. Article II of the subsequent impeachment resolution accused BernardCaldwell of giving Congress faulty evidence and later blaming legislators for the escalation. It stated that the Senate initially approved a war resolution, but the House rejected it and the Senate then rejected it on reconsideration. The resolution also accused him of privately urging war while negotiating with the British government. [ 7 ] On 24 July, BernardCaldwell published a statement addressing a British ultimatum and asked citizens whether nUSA should go to war with the United Kingdom. The following day, PatrickCoyne introduced H.J. Res. 2, proposing a formal declaration of war. Its preamble stated that the British government had already declared war on the United States, and its operative provisions would authorize the President to use the country's military forces and resources against Britain. The resolution was referred to the House Armed Services and Veteran Affairs Committee; its final legislative outcome is uncertain. [ 8 ] Fighting was reported on 25 July, when a public announcement stated that nUSA had lost its first raid by a score of 101–35. That evening, Lordsights condemned the war as having begun under false pretenses and said he could no longer support either the conflict or BernardCaldwell. The handling of the British dispute became a central issue in the House's impeachment proceedings the next day. [ 9 ] [ 7 ] Impeachment and eligibility disputes On 26 July 2018, the House Judiciary Committee advanced an impeachment resolution against BernardCaldwell. The House passed the resolution, H. Res. 12, and referred it to the Senate . Its three articles accused him of unlawfully promising appointments, misconduct in a diplomatic dispute with the United Kingdom and France, and misconduct relating to a prospective judicial nominee's membership in another United States group. The outcome of the Senate proceedings is uncertain. [ 10 ] In October 2018, the Senate lifted BernardCaldwell's disqualification from holding office. Later that month, the Federal Election Commission separately disqualified him as a presidential candidate. The grounds for the FEC decision were not specified in its announcement. [ 11 ] Return to office in 2020 BernardCaldwell won the Summer 2020 presidential election as the Constitutionalist Party candidate, with Lacryma as his running mate. He received 280 votes; the National Elections Administrator reported 569 ballots received and 101 manually disqualified. The result was certified on 5 July, and BernardCaldwell and Lacryma were inaugurated on 21 July. [ 12 ] During his second term, BernardCaldwell issued executive orders on law enforcement and administrative reform. An order dated 14 August called for a joint task force to protect the District of Columbia spawn area and World War II memorial and coordinate domestic-security agencies. Another established an Internal Affairs Institute to investigate executive-branch employees, excluding violations of Clan Management's community guidelines from its jurisdiction. Subsequent orders directed agencies to create Discord channels for crime reports, established probationary training standards for federal law-enforcement recruits, and called for work on a United States Employment Center. [ 13 ] August 2020 United Kingdom ultimatum On 6 August 2020, BernardCaldwell signed a joint nUSA–Zimbabwe ultimatum to the United Kingdom . It demanded apologies, the playing of the United States anthem in Parliament, cooperation in the United Nations, and the reopening of diplomatic channels. The ultimatum threatened a state of war if the demands were not accepted by 7 August. A declaration of war was proposed in Congress on 7 August, but its passage and any subsequent fighting are uncertain. The dispute occurred during BernardCaldwell's second term, after the April 2020 war under Reset4K . [ 14 ] Management sanctions and splinter-group disputes HUSA and the 2019 blacklist BernardCaldwell's involvement with HUSA drew criticism from nUSA members in 2019. On 19 April, Real_CoolAid described him as HUSA's President. On 24 April, PatrioticCross accused him and HHPrinceGeorge of leaving nUSA to develop HUSA and recruiting developers for the rival group. Contemporary discussion also described HUSA as competing with nUSA for members and activity. [ 15 ] On 10 May 2019, Clan Management banned and blacklisted BernardCaldwell, HHPrinceGeorge, Joyiscold, Helleoh, and ApolloKnowles for six months, allowing appeals after three months. Members linked the sanctions to HUSA, and management's later BUSA announcement referred to an earlier “HUSA blacklist.” The May announcement itself did not specify the underlying conduct. [ 16 ] Suspension during his second presidency During BernardCaldwell's second presidency, management imposed a one-week blacklist in August 2020, alleging harassment and assistance to a blacklisted person's alternate account. Management stated that the Vice President would exercise presidential powers during the suspension. [ 17 ] BUSA and permanent removal On 21 October 2020, Clan Management announced sanctions against the organizers of BUSA, which it described as a new version of the HUSA remake. A letter addressed to BernardCaldwell and signed by Clan Manager David E. Racine, III, identified him among the movement's principals and stated that he and others had worked to create a new United States group. Management characterized their actions as “rebellion and insurrection” and as harmful to nUSA's continued existence. [ 4 ] The order imposed permanent bans and citizenship disqualification, without appeal, on BernardCaldwell, Asceylos, RichoCaldwell, cashcursive, RobCaldwell, Technozo, and other BUSA Presidents, developers, and group-management members. The letter distinguished management's disciplinary authority from government proceedings concerning rebellion and stated that those proceedings would not affect its decision. The accompanying announcement exempted ordinary BUSA citizens from a blacklist unless they advertised the group or attempted to recruit nUSA members. It separately cited constitutional restrictions on officeholding for participants who had previously taken an oath of office. [ 4 ] BUSA's activity soon attracted criticism. On 28 October, Pauljkl said its games had “died on day 1,” blaming their developers. In November, Bancachuli also described the group as inactive. These comments reflected members' assessments of BUSA's decline; its formal closure date is uncertain. [ 18 ] The conflict continued beyond BUSA. On 19 December 2021, largeTitanic2 announced that membership restrictions comparable to those imposed on BUSA would apply to another United States group created by BernardCaldwell. Members were given until the following Tuesday to leave. The notice alleged earlier attacks on Trello boards, Discord servers, and groups; it did not name the new organization. title: Blastatack
text: Blastatack 16th President of nUSA In office 21 May 2017 – 21 July 2017 [ 1 ] Preceded by Sufferpoop Succeeded by SurpriseParty Blastatack, 16th Blastatack was the 16th President of the nUSA roleplay community on Roblox. Blastatack took office on 21 May 2017 after the resignation of Sufferpoop and was succeeded by SurpriseParty in July. During the administration, the group continued its municipal election program in Las Vegas and made a Supreme Court appointment at the end of the term. [ 2 ] Presidency The preceding President, Sufferpoop, announced a resignation on 21 May. Three minutes later, the #nusa-updates channel reported that Blastatack was being sworn in; two minutes after that, it announced the new President. The oath notice spells the name “Blasatack,” while the Presidential Records register and later announcements use “Blastatack.” [ 3 ] The surviving announcements from the two-month term are limited. They record city elections for the Las Vegas City Council : nominations for mayor opened in June, and voting for mayor and council followed later that month. The vice-presidential roster lists Frosty_TheSn0wman in the office from 14 June until the July transition. [ 4 ] Judicial appointments and succession On 20 July, Blastatack nominated Ryan_Revan to the Supreme Court . The Senate confirmed the nomination 7–0–1 the following day, and President SurpriseParty appointed Ryan_Revan on 21 July. The appointment was thus completed across the presidential transition. [ 5 ] The presidential roster places Blastatack immediately before SurpriseParty . The oath notice dates the start to 21 May, and the Supreme Court record documents SurpriseParty's appointment on 21 July. title: Boulder County (nUSA)
text: Colorado municipality opened in 2022 Boulder County, Colorado , was a center of municipal government and public activity that opened on 26 November 2022. Its anticipated opening influenced the reconstruction of government , preparations for attorney licensing and changes to executive agencies. In January 2024, a municipal transition moved Boulder law-enforcement personnel into Washington 's Metropolitan Police Department and placed Governor AlexReign in the interim mayoralty of the capital. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] Preparations for opening Boulder's development was accompanied by preparations to operate government within it. The Federal Election Commission's August 2022 interim schedule provided temporary congressional elections while anticipating later elections after Boulder's opening. The House elected under that arrangement had sixteen seats, and the Senate ten. These plans connected Boulder's arrival with the renewal of national political institutions. [ 3 ] The judiciary likewise planned for a new setting for legal practice. Chief Justice RummyLeroux's July notice anticipated paid attorney services and law firms in Boulder, backed by licensing through a Federal Bar Association. It identified federal trial practice in the District of Colorado and District of Columbia as subjects of forthcoming regulation. The changes were announced in advance, with further directives and examination publication still to follow. [ 4 ] President TacticalRock101 made agency readiness a priority in November. Faced with limited personnel, he furloughed several institutions whose duties could be absorbed by others, leaving open their later return. At the same time, Speaker MasonRockefeller sought firmer standards of activity and professionalism in the House. Boulder's anticipated opening thus affected both the distribution of executive personnel and the operation of Congress. [ 5 ] [ 6 ] Opening and relations with Ridgeway Rockefeller announced Boulder's opening on 26 November, coinciding with the nation's tenth anniversary. Later that day he welcomed its early activity and criticized Ridgeway's restrictions on participation by American citizens. His response was H.R. 25, a proposed measure prohibiting discrimination against people because of their participation in Ridgeway. The proposal advocated coexistence rather than an exclusive choice of allegiance for ordinary participation. [ 7 ] [ 8 ] The proposal followed the earlier Domestic Protection Act , which had distinguished foreign citizenship from foreign civil office. The two measures concerned different restrictions, but both addressed the relationship between public service and participation outside the nation. H.R. 25's introduction alone does not establish that its protections became law. [ 9 ] [ 10 ] Municipal institutions and the Washington transition By January 2024, AlexReign was governor of Boulder County, whose municipal services included a sheriff's office and fire department. On 17 January, AIex announced a transfer arrangement into Washington 's municipal institutions. AlexReign would serve as interim mayor until City Council elections; MasonRockefeller would lead the Metropolitan Police, with the Boulder sheriff as deputy chief and the CPD chief as assistant chief. [ 11 ] Police staff were directed to obtain their transferred ranks through the receiving department. The fire service transition placed Boulder deputy chief peep at the head of Washington's Fire Department, while Posiedon17 was designated to lead Emergency Medical Services. The arrangement specified that Boulder had no equivalent EMS service and that InfiniteOne, Boulder's fire chief, was also serving in management. [ 12 ] The Metropolitan Police then began organizing command staff and training its first class under the new arrangement. Rockefeller instructed personnel to wait while the department prepared to operate and announced a Metro academy replacing FLETC in that transition. Boulder's municipal personnel became part of a renewed capital service rather than transferring only as isolated individual applicants. title: Constitutionalist Party (nUSA)
text: The Constitutionalist Party was a presidential-election label in the Roblox nUSA roleplay community. The Federal Election Commission's fall 2019 records identified JamesMontagu as a Constitutionalist candidate, and a summer 2020 election certificate identified BernardCaldwell as its winning presidential candidate with Lacryma as Vice President-elect. The records do not provide a comprehensive membership register or platform, so the party's documented history is clearest around those tickets. [ 1 ] Name and earlier merger notice An October 2018 nUSA announcement said that a Constitution Party had merged into the Republican Party. Later election materials used the related but different Constitutionalist name. The reviewed documents do not state whether the 2019–2020 Constitutionalist organization descended from, revived, or was separate from the earlier Constitution Party. This article uses the label on the dated FEC and ballot records and leaves the organizational relationship unresolved. [ 2 ] JamesMontagu and the 2019 election The fall 2019 ballot listed JamesMontagu as the Constitutionalist candidate against Republican incumbent AntonioTRoosevelt. The FEC letter reported 322 votes for Montagu, with 11 disqualified, and certified him as the winner. It also said a court injunction rendered him temporarily ineligible and named his running mate TomFoley acting President-elect pending qualification. A later announcement scheduled Montagu's inauguration, which proceeded in November, but the surviving material does not explain how the injunction was resolved. [ 3 ] BernardCaldwell and the 2020 election Montagu's later Winter 2020 campaign named BernardCaldwell as his running mate, but the FEC certified the Reset4K–Technozo Democratic ticket instead. In the next presidential contest, the Summer 2020 certificate counted 569 ballots received and 101 manually disqualified, then certified BernardCaldwell and Lacryma as the winning Constitutionalist ticket. A public July 21 announcement congratulated them on the election and inauguration. These records document two campaigns involving Bernard in different positions, but do not establish a full account of party leadership between the elections. [ 4 ] An undated presidential-affiliations compilation assigns the Constitutionalist label to later figures including RalphFoley and Guggen_Pierre. Because that text lacks an author and the reviewed election documents do not independently establish those later affiliations, the present article does not treat them as settled party members. The party's later organizational fate is likewise not documented in the sources reviewed here. title: Constitutions of nUSA
text: The nUSA roleplay's constitutional record consists of multiple texts and status changes preserved in Discord announcements and Trello records. The surviving evidence identifies a Constitution marked superseded in 2017, a text instituted in July 2023, a Constitution announced as passed in November 2024, and a late-2018 text announced as readopted in May 2025. The records conflict on the provenance and intervening readoption history of the last version, so they do not support a single uncontested chronology. [ 1 ] Recorded versions The FruCon document is titled as a 2017 Constitution and marks itself void and superseded by a new Constitution dated 8 September 2017. This is a status claim on the archived copy, not a full history of which texts governed in each period after it. [ 2 ] The “RummyConst 07-17-23” document says it was published and instituted on 17 July 2023. It places NARA under Group Management control and assigns the agency responsibility for storing and maintaining public executive, legislative and judicial records, including setting retention schedules and archival processes. Those provisions describe this particular version and should not be attributed to later texts without checking them separately. [ 3 ] On 6 November 2024, Group Management announced that a new Constitution had passed after review and approval by the Senate, House, District Courts and Supreme Court. The announcement described a two-column format and said Group Management would own and maintain the linked PDF. The linked file was inaccessible during source review, so the announcement does not support a detailed account of the text's provisions. A later NARA Hub card labels “GobiesCons 11-6-24” inactive. [ 4 ] A NARA public post dated 16 May 2025 reported that a Constitution was readopted and revised through P.L. 105-1 on 12 May. The Hub card “TimCons 09-22-18” links a 17-page version whose cover says it was authored on 22 September 2018 and re-adopted on 12 May 2025. The Public Law Database separately describes a constitutional record adopted on 8 September 2017 and readopted on 17 January 2024 and 12 May 2025. The two records may refer to related versions, but the available sources do not reconcile the different origin dates or identify all revisions. [ 5 ] How status is recorded The NARA Hub uses labels including “Active Constitution” and “Inactive.” In the reviewed export, TimCons 09-22-18 bears the active label, while GobiesCons and RummyConst are marked inactive. These are board-level status markers at the export snapshot; by themselves they do not explain the legal process or exact date by which one version replaced another. [ 6 ] The July 2023 reset also voided categories of existing federal laws and precedents, but the announcement did not state that every constitutional text was voided. It was followed by a new Constitution two days later. It is therefore useful to distinguish the reset of legal materials from the dated constitutional texts and their separate active or inactive labels. title: Cursive v. United States (nUSA)
text: 2019 constitutional decision on presidential impeachment Cursive v. United States Supreme Court of the United States Full case name Procursive v. United States, et al. Docket 07–05 Argued 17 April 2019 Decided 7 May 2019 Proceeding Writ of review to the United States Government Holding Articles 2–4 invalidated; Article 1 upheld; request to vacate removal denied Principal opinion Chief Justice Holmes; different justices joined different parts Separate opinions Bork, Stewart, Pitney, Chase and Brandeis Nonparticipation O'Connor Issues Impeachment; Anytime Review; congressional oaths; due process; executive privilege Cursive v. United States , No. 07–05, was a constitutional decision of the Supreme Court concerning the impeachment and removal of President Procursive . Decided on 7 May 2019, it invalidated three of the four articles on which the Senate had convicted the President but upheld the remaining article. The Court consequently denied his request to vacate the removal. The judgment established that a President could prevail on substantial constitutional objections to impeachment without recovering the office. [ 1 ] The opinions divided over both the meaning of high crimes and misdemeanors and the judiciary's role in reviewing Congress. Chief Justice Holmes treated the case as reviewable through Anytime Review and applied the Ichigo precedents to the charges. The justices sustaining Article 1 nevertheless included critics of its use, while Brandeis favored a much narrower judicial role. The decision's practical outcome concealed substantial disagreement over the route to it. [ 2 ] Background Procursive had directed the Secret Service before joining Dralian 's presidential ticket. When Dralian declined to assume another term, Procursive became President-elect and took office in March 2019. His limited political experience and difficult relations with Congress formed the setting for the ensuing dispute. Around 23 March, the House Foreign Affairs Committee began investigating allegations involving denial-of-service attacks and exposure of private information by people connected with the intelligence community. [ 3 ] Procursive invoked executive privilege rather than testify under the committee's subpoena. Further allegations concerned his cousin's employment on his Secret Service detail and JamesMontagu 's appointment in the White House. An earlier allegation of false arrest supplied a fourth strand of the controversy. On 31 March, the House unanimously adopted articles addressing false arrest, withholding information, nepotism and the asserted national-security consequences of Montagu's employment. [ 4 ] Senate proceedings Holmes convened the Senate, House managers exhibited the articles, and senators took an oath or affirmation of impartiality. The chamber adjourned to allow preparation. During the trial, both sides presented opening statements and examined evidence, but closing statements were omitted because of time constraints. The Senate convicted on all four articles, removed Procursive and declined to disqualify him from future office. [ 5 ] Procursive had not sought a pre-emptive judicial stay before conviction. His challenge therefore sought to undo a removal that had already occurred. He disputed congressional oaths, the adequacy of the trial and the substantive validity of the articles. The Court heard argument on 17 April. [ 6 ] Questions before the Court The case presented a threshold question of justiciability: whether impeachment was solely Congress's concern or could be reviewed judicially. Beyond that, the Court considered whether the President had demonstrated invalid congressional oaths, whether the Senate had afforded constitutionally sufficient process, and whether the charged conduct met the impeachment standard established by the Ichigo cases. [ 7 ] Article 1 posed a further question because it concerned pre-presidential conduct. The Court had to consider whether an offense unrelated to the acquisition of the presidency was categorically beyond impeachment and whether a stricter inquiry into Congress's motives was justified. [ 8 ] Decision Anytime Review and procedure The Court rejected the contention that the political-question doctrine necessarily excluded review. It treated the doctrine and the restrictions associated with Nixon v. United States as matters of judicial policy and prudential concern rather than constitutional commands applicable in every setting. Those justifications did not foreclose the questions presented through Anytime Review. [ 9 ] Procursive's oath challenge failed because he had not produced sufficient evidence that members of Congress were constitutionally unsworn. His due-process challenge also failed. Impeachment was not an ordinary criminal prosecution, and the Senate did not have to reproduce all the procedures of a criminal court. The Court additionally concluded that the process provided had been adequate, including the time allowed for preparation and the defense's opportunity to present its case. [ 10 ] Articles 2, 3 and 4 The Court reaffirmed the Ichigo principle that a high crime or misdemeanor had to qualify at least as a crime or misdemeanor. It invalidated Articles 2, 3 and 4 because they failed to allege legitimate criminal offenses under that standard. The information-withholding article also raised concerns of executive privilege. The invalidations rejected those grounds of impeachment without requiring the Court to uphold every policy or appointment that had prompted congressional criticism. [ 11 ] Article 1 and removal Holmes, joined on this portion by Gorsuch, Bork and Stewart, declined to find Article 1 unconstitutional. The Court did not categorically prohibit impeachment for misconduct predating the presidency. Procursive had not advanced a more demanding standard than Ichigo or supplied sufficient evidence of constitutionally impermissible motives to justify closer scrutiny. Congress's factual conclusions were not found clearly erroneous. [ 12 ] Holmes's refusal to invalidate the charge was accompanied by a forceful criticism of its use. He regarded removal for the earlier false arrest as a serious misuse of impeachment and warned that comparable articles might fail in future cases. The judgment thus sustained the result without offering unqualified approval of Congress's conduct. With Article 1 surviving, the Court denied reinstatement. [ 13 ] Separate opinions Bork and Stewart Bork joined Holmes's opinion but emphasized that failure to establish unconstitutionality was not the same as demonstrating that Congress had acted permissibly. He questioned whether the Ichigo test sufficiently addressed the word high and suggested that ordinary criminality might not settle the constitutional inquiry into impeachment. [ 14 ] Stewart concurred in part and in the judgment. Although he had concerns about Ichigo , he regarded the absence of a properly briefed request to overturn it as decisive. The parties' reliance on the existing standard made this case an unsuitable vehicle for abandoning it. He also found insufficient evidence for the oath and due-process objections. [ 15 ] Pitney and Chase Pitney and Chase disagreed with the disposition of Article 1. Chase argued that a minor false-arrest offense could not reasonably satisfy the requirement of a high crime and warned against turning impeachment into a means of making the executive dependent on legislative political will. Pitney and Douglas joined the first part of Chase's opinion. Chase separately disputed the treatment of due process, favoring a fairness requirement suited to impeachment without importing every rule of an ordinary trial. [ 16 ] Brandeis Brandeis concurred in the judgments concerning Articles 1 and 2 but dissented on Articles 3 and 4. He favored overruling Ichigo and limiting judicial intervention in impeachment to narrow circumstances implicating separation of powers. His position sustained Article 1 through a different understanding of the judiciary's role from that used by Holmes. [ 17 ] Aftermath and significance Procursive remained removed, while Bakedgoods continued the presidency to which he had succeeded. The decision became an important expression of the Court's power to review individual impeachment charges. It also demonstrated that separate articles could receive different constitutional dispositions without requiring the entire Senate judgment to fall. [ 18 ] The case influenced the reasoning of Bork's concurrence in Hudson v. House of Representatives the following month. He invoked its discussion of limits on impeachment in criticizing subpoenas directed at judges in response to their rulings. That concurrence remained nonbinding. The broader body of case law was later affected by the 2023 nUSA legal reset , which voided existing precedent. [ 19 ] [ 20 ] External links Full decision and separate opinions ↑ Cursive v. title: Cyxlinder
text: Cyxlinder 42nd President of nUSA (NARA roster) In office 3 October 2021 – 21 November 2021 [ 1 ] Preceded by TimidSoul Succeeded by TacticalRock101 NARA Presidential Records roster Cyxlinder is listed by the nUSA Presidential Records board as the community's 42nd President. A dated executive order signed by Cyxlinder as President established a Federal Recruitment Office on November 11, 2021. A separate NARA court roster says he appointed Supreme Court Justice AustinBoBoston1, whose service began November 17. These primary records show Cyxlinder acting as President by November 11 and still being identified as the appointing President in a later roster entry; they do not establish his exact start or end date. [ 2 ] Presidential record and numbering The November 11 order created the Federal Recruitment Office as an independent executive-branch office overseen by the Executive Office of the President. It directed the office to coordinate recruitment for participating law-enforcement and public-safety agencies, including the FBI, U.S. Marshals Service, Bureau of Prisons, Department of Homeland Security, Federal Protective Service, Secret Service, and District of Columbia Emergency Medical Services. The order called for a commissioner and deputy commissioner appointed by the President, as well as two representatives from each participating agency. It set out application processes for former employees and new applicants; these provisions describe the order's intended procedures, not evidence that each was implemented. [ 3 ] The order's number differs from the ordinal in the presidential roster: its title is “41-005,” while the roster labels Cyxlinder 42nd. A later order signed by TacticalRock101 is numbered 42-002, while the roster lists TacticalRock101 as 43rd. The sources preserve these conflicting numbering systems, and do not explain how the order series was assigned. [ 4 ] Judicial appointment The NARA roster for Justice Boston identifies AustinBoBoston1 as an associate justice appointed by President Cyxlinder. It records the justice as incumbent beginning November 17, 2021, and sworn in on November 19. This roster is a contemporaneous office record for the appointment, although it does not give the date of Cyxlinder's own accession or the order of succession by which he became President.
