It also showed that Washington already existed and was being replaced or extensively reworked, linking the coming city to the earlier capital. [ 23 ] On 18 November, Squareheaddude announced a Washington trailer and said release was expected that month. The embedded video title credited Squareheaddude and Pauljkl. On 21 November, a further announcement set 1 December as the release date for the new Washington, District of Columbia. The release publicity included planned streams by Technozo and described the city as reborn. [ 24 ] [ 2 ] The rebuilt city was associated with place 1213026131, whose asset record began in late November. Release notices on 30 November and 1 December advertised an opening at approximately 5 p.m. Eastern Time on 1 December. Later that day, Squareheaddude asked citizens to report bugs and said he was undertaking fixes. Public access and maintenance therefore began together, with the city still receiving corrections after its opening. [ 14 ] [ 2 ] The first weeks brought both service recruitment and gameplay changes. On 9 December, Squareheaddude announced that council elections would wait until after the presidential elections, but invited applications to run the Metropolitan Police Department because the streets already required policing. On 12 December, he confirmed a fire update and new WASD vehicle controls. He promoted the vehicles as lag-free, a performance claim accompanying the announcement. The sequence placed policing, emergency response, and transport among the practical concerns of the newly opened capital. [ 25 ] [ 26 ] Elections and development, 2018–2019 The new city's municipal institutions developed after its release. A 17 February 2018 notice announced that planned mayoral elections had fallen through and that Technozo had been appointed mayor. It advertised the first councilor election for the new Washington, with eligibility including membership in the United States group and a rank of Middle Class Citizen or higher. The appointment and election were distinct steps in organizing local government. [ 27 ] On 25 February, the announced council winners were AdamCarpenterJr, IBreakingNewsI, Robbyiscrazy, ADVlCE, Dariel_Powell, LilWill_OG, SevMacLeod, and DevGralius. A separate announcement that evening linked the Washington council's laws-and-codes board. The council thus had both elected membership and a public legislative record, providing an institutional counterpart to the city's development and service administration. [ 28 ] Another municipal election cycle used a dedicated D.C. Elections Center in July. Preliminary voting opened on 27 July; the following day, the preliminary stage closed ahead of schedule and final voting began. The final ballot included council candidates and five mayoral candidates. On 1 August, the election administrator announced eight council winners and certified TheySinned as the mayoral winner after disqualifying the initial winner on stated electoral-fraud grounds. The disqualification was the administrator's finding and announcement; the certified result placed TheySinned ahead of the remaining eligible candidates. [ 15 ] [ 29 ] Development continued alongside these elections. On 19 November 2018, Squareheaddude announced a large Washington update and directed citizens to the update log. On 24 November, he advertised a forthcoming lawful trucking-delivery system. The proposed system would add work outside government and law enforcement, although the announcement did not establish its eventual implementation date. City development was therefore concerned with both public institutions and activities available to ordinary citizens. [ 30 ] Banking was another area of change. On 3 April 2019, Squareheaddude sought a new banking company to replace Capital Bank, inviting established companies and proposals for a new bank. The notice connected a commercial institution to the operation of the capital. It did not identify a successful replacement or announce when a successor opened. [ 31 ] In June 2019, a Washington development survey invited citizens to comment on hypothetical changes. Respondents were required to supply their Roblox usernames, and the notice offered three cash prizes. It expressly described the questions as hypothetical, making the survey a consultation rather than a list of confirmed changes. The exercise nevertheless gave citizens a direct route to express views about the city's future. [ 32 ] Performance improvements accompanied the expansion of public use. A 6 September test invited citizens to try Washington with a 45-player cap. Its stated priorities were reducing vehicle flinging, introducing a menu for new players, and increasing stability for larger servers. Participants were offered unlimited test money and asked to play normally. The test addressed both the behavior of existing systems and the accessibility of the city to newcomers; the announced cap was a test setting rather than a measurement of ordinary attendance. [ 16 ] State of Columbia controversy Main articles: State of Columbia (nUSA) and In re Federal Government (nUSA) Washington's municipal status became central to a constitutional dispute in March 2019. Congress's S. 127, titled To restore municipal government , sought to unite Washington and Las Vegas as the State of Columbia. It provided for a provisional governor, the exercise of interim executive and legislative authority, the negotiation of a constitution, and associated agency and court arrangements. The new jurisdiction was publicly announced on 2 March. [ 33 ] On 3 March, the Supreme Court invalidated the principal merger provisions in In re Federal Government , heard with Kirkman v. State of Columbia . Neither city's legislature had consented. The Court required clear, public, and unambiguous municipal approval and held that notice to local authorities could not substitute for consent. It struck sections 101–104 and dependent sections 106–107, including arrangements that could not operate independently of the invalid union. [ 6 ] The Court also rejected an attempt to avoid the consent requirement by treating Las Vegas as already deprived of municipal status under H.R. 179. It did not decide the validity of H.R. 179 itself, and observed that its language continued to refer to Las Vegas as a municipality. For the proposed union, both cities remained municipalities whose legislatures had to agree. The judgment preserved Washington's separate municipal position and made its council consequential in the exercise of federal power over local government. [ 6 ] Public activity and municipal dissolution, 2020–2023 Washington continued to host government and community activity while other cities experienced changing levels of participation. On 16 April 2020, management described Las Vegas as less active and less fully operational than Washington, while retaining Las Vegas's official-city status. The comparison indicated Washington's greater activity at that time without establishing a permanent closure of Las Vegas or a complete end to its public services. [ 34 ] Local executive initiatives also shaped public life. On 8 February 2021, DirectorPoke announced Municipal Order 10-0001, Free Pizza Fridays, offering D.C. citizens a free slice each Friday. A second order extended municipal protection privileges to the mayor's cabinet and incoming mayoral leadership. Further notices on 11 and 19 February invited citizens to participate, and a 12 February account described a successful gathering and linked photographs. The program was a municipal policy and public event; the same account requested that developers add pizza slices, indicating that the event's civic organization and its in-game objects were separate matters. [ 35 ] On 27 June 2021, management announced that declining municipal participation, assessed through activity and voting statistics, would lead to the discontinuation of local government. The notice set 1 July at midnight Eastern Time as the effective point, made the City Council and mayor's office defunct, and directed team-bearing services into the federal government. It also asked Congress to supply an appropriate law and left open the possibility of a limited reopening if activity improved. A follow-up on 2 July confirmed that the D.C. government had been dissolved the preceding night. [ 7 ] The affected services included MPD, EMS, the Fire Department, and the United States State Police. Their proposed transfer concerned administration of the city services, not the disappearance of Washington as a game or the erasure of its capital role. The management notice also distinguished the dissolution decision from the legislative work needed to regularize agency arrangements. [ 7 ] In November 2022, Boulder County opened as another center of municipal activity. Federal preparations for its opening included agency and legal-service changes. Washington nevertheless continued to matter in protective-service policy. On 25 January 2023, President TacticalRock101 restored the Federal Protective Service to active status, citing increased activity in Washington and the unavailability of the MPD team. The order demonstrated the use of federal protection to address a gap in municipal coverage. [ 36 ] [ 37 ] On the same date, management discussed Boulder development and identified a new District of Columbia as a future project for the development team. The statement invited suggestions while work continued on Boulder's Dentsville and federal facilities. Washington's next generation was therefore part of a wider program of city development before the explicit DC2/DC3 roadmap of 2024. [ 38 ] Return of municipal services and DC2 renewal, 2024–2025 In January 2024, a renewed Washington administration drew on personnel from Boulder County. AIex announced an agreement with Boulder governor AlexReign on 17 January, providing municipal staff with lateral-transfer routes into D.C. departments. AlexReign was designated interim mayor pending council elections. MasonRockefeller was appointed MPD chief, with the Boulder County sheriff as deputy chief and the CPD chief as assistant chief. Police staffs were directed to merge into the MPD and arrange their rank transfers through its leadership. [ 8 ] The same transition addressed emergency services. Boulder deputy fire chief peep was designated to lead Washington's Fire Department because Boulder's fire chief, InfiniteOne, also served in management. Posiedon17 was appointed EMS chief; the announcement stated that Boulder had no equivalent EMS service. The arrangements supplied the capital with leadership and a transfer process across several services instead of treating each appointment as an isolated recruitment. [ 8 ] Rockefeller subsequently announced preparations for a new police command and its first class. Officers were instructed to wait while the department organized its operations, and a Metro academy would replace FLETC in that transition. This training arrangement belonged to the 2024 reorganization; the later DC3 program again assigned a central role to FLETC. [ 39 ] [ 40 ] The January management transition also proposed investment in D.C. development, advertising, and partnerships. Management wanted more national activity to occur inside Washington: its example was a citizen entering the game, driving to the courthouse, and attending a trial at the actual facility. The plan linked city development to the operation of public institutions, while leaving individual projects to be completed through subsequent work. [ 41 ] Developer recruitment on 8 March distinguished work on the existing city from the new capital. Benda587 supervised current D.C.; chexburger supervised new D.C. scripting; and Sheev_PalpatineTGR supervised new D.C. building. The announcement primarily sought builders and modelers for the new project, while allowing less experienced applicants to join the current-city team. These responsibilities were the announced arrangement at that time and did not constitute an exhaustive final credit list. [ 42 ] On 11 March, management asserted the City Council's role in representing citizens to developers and directing development requests through local government. An accompanying declaration that a revised charter was active was withdrawn later that day. The reversal preserved the council as an advisory intermediary while allowing deliberation over the charter. It also clarified that federal institutions could still legislate or request additions and renovations. The episode exposed the overlap between municipal representation, federal law, and management control of the game. [ 43 ] The April owner update formally described parallel work on DC2 and DC3. UKR41NIAN promised refinements and substantial new content for DC2, including a crime and private-business update, while targeting the first quarter of 2025 for DC3. On 11 May 2024, SupremeFedoraa announced that the crime update was live, describing it as the largest update since 2017 and saying it had been developed in thirteen days. The release confirmed a crime update to the existing city, although the announcement did not enumerate every previously proposed business feature. [ 3 ] [ 44 ] Local elections continued during the development period. On 23 February 2025, the Federal Election Commission declared PeepGPT mayor-elect with 35.89 percent of the vote and announced council winners for the coming term. The notice expressly distinguished election from taking office, stating that PeepGPT would remain mayor-elect until sworn in. It gave 19 May as the term's expiry. Later in 2025, municipal elections were included alongside congressional contests in the Winter Election Extravaganza . [ 45 ] [ 46 ] DC3 Development and building program DC3 was developed as the next generation of Washington while the existing city continued to receive attention. The April 2024 roadmap set a Q1 2025 launch target and connected the project to efforts to rebuild the development team, restore activity, and establish a clearer direction following changes in senior leadership. The later 2026 opening occurred beyond that initial target. Development of a new city and continued support for DC2 were concurrent commitments rather than a completed handover in April 2024. [ 3 ] [ 9 ] The building program sought contributions from the institutions expected to use the capital. On 20 February 2025, AcidRaps advertised a DC3 building quality-assurance team with approximately five participants from each major field: judicial and legislative processes, enforcement, transport and parks, the private sector, and the military. The notice specifically referred to courts and town halls, agency buildings, road details, public-service buildings, and parks. Participants were to check representation of their sectors and help establish consistent standards for colors, doors, and materials across the map. [ 47 ] This review process treated city design as a set of spaces for different kinds of public activity. The aim was to avoid large differences in building quality while accommodating the practical needs of agencies and civilian organizations. The recruitment described planned review responsibilities, not a certification that every proposed facility was finished. It nevertheless gave judicial, legislative, service, commercial, and military users a place in the development process. [ 47 ] Funding was also addressed publicly. On 12 April 2025, American_Online introduced an nUSA Sponsor Discord subscription as a way to contribute to the development program. The announcement stated that sponsor revenue would support DC3 and advertising for the current game and said ownership members had personally invested thousands in the project. The funding claims were ownership's account; no total development budget was specified. Subscription benefits included communication privileges and access to the political feed. [ 48 ] Sponsor participation extended to playtesting. On 13 May 2026, Bathamza reported touring the DC3 White House earlier that week during a sponsor playtest. He praised its building style and gun system and described sponsors participating as Secret Service personnel with standardized uniforms, accessories, and weapons. He thanked CIonk_Man, Jon_Ral, and the development team, and expressed an expectation of release in July. His account documented the tested setting and credited contributors while remaining a participant's assessment of the experience. [ 49 ] Release schedule and paid Early Access On 29 April 2026, nUSA announced that DC3 would arrive in July. The announcement promoted a living open world, new systems, detailed environments, and a more ambitious recreation of Washington. These were development aims and promotional assessments accompanying a release forecast. The first specific public-access date followed on 10 July, when nUSA announced Early Access for 24 July at 8 p.m. Eastern Time. [ 50 ] [ 9 ] The July announcement expressly described Early Access as a beta. Systems and builds were to be polished, expanded, and refined before a full release. The city was presented as an opportunity to begin using the world under construction, with further work expected after players entered. The announcement therefore separated opening access from completing the development program. [ 9 ] Early Access opened on 24 July. The opening notice confirmed paid admission and said the game would become free at full release. Some systems were intentionally disabled and would be introduced over time. Mobile gameplay was available but not yet fully supported. Ownership also stated that the current experience did not represent the city's final form and invited feedback to help determine subsequent development. [ 9 ] The asset associated with DC3, place 140564898391131, was created on 21 July. Its later city description offered participation in Congress, policing, defense of the capital, bank robbery, and the presidency. The description presented public office and street activity within the same Washington environment. Its asset history identifies the new place separately from the 2017 city, while the July announcement supplies the opening milestone. [ 14 ] [ 51 ] Free beta On 30 August, ownership announced that DC3 would become free to enter on 4 September. The announcement described a larger, more detailed Washington with new systems and a foundation for continued additions. It again identified the forthcoming opening as a beta. The change broadened access from the paid Early Access stage without declaring the city finished. [ 10 ] Publicity on 3 September specified a noon Eastern Time opening on the following day. The 4 September notice confirmed that DC3 was open to everyone in free beta and thanked the original paid-access participants. It warned of bugs, unfinished areas, balance changes, and evolving features, and requested feedback. The free opening was therefore a second access milestone within ongoing development. [ 52 ] [ 10 ] The change in access also made Washington available to citizens who had not participated in the paid period. Management encouraged both long-standing members and newcomers to enter the city. Subsequent thanks emphasized participation, exploration, and feedback. These statements expressed ownership's enthusiasm for the opening; they did not supply independently measured attendance or establish a completed development stage. [ 10 ] [ 53 ] Government readiness and law enforcement The approach of DC3 affected executive administration before the public beta. On 4 July 2026, President Jsjsjbsd announced an executive order establishing a Task Force on DC3 Readiness. He described declining agency activity and a disorganized structure as problems that required attention before new citizens arrived. The task force, led by UndeadsValor, was to review departments, address inactive leadership, and prepare the executive branch for the new city. [ 54 ] The President returned to these preparations in his July public statements. His 14 July State of the Union cited the readiness task force among the administration's measures, and his 16 July post-election address described DC3 as an opportunity to revise agency operations, consolidate where necessary, and change hiring practices. These were presidential policy commitments tied to the new capital's arrival, rather than evidence that all planned organizational changes had already been completed. [ 55 ] Law-enforcement training was another preparation. On 8 August, an application notice for a FLETC director described the center as the centralized authority for training, examining, and certifying law-enforcement officers in DC3. Recruits were to attend before entering an agency. The same notice assigned FLETC a conduct-enforcement role, including revocation of licenses when misconduct was proven. This program connected police employment to training and certification, with a disciplinary mechanism extending across agencies. [ 40 ] The 2026 arrangement differed from the Metro academy announced during Washington's 2024 police transition. Training institutions changed as the capital's departments were reorganized. Their functions should therefore be understood in their respective periods: the 2024 academy prepared the reorganized municipal police, while the August 2026 announcement described a centralized DC3 law-enforcement system. [ 39 ] [ 40 ] Employment and early public administration On 4 September, Jsjsjbsd addressed the press and public to commemorate DC3's opening. He stated that USAJOBS had handled more than 500 applications and that agencies were conducting a program of official events. These figures were the president's account of administrative activity. His address connected the city's launch with recruitment and efforts to prepare departments for new participation. [ 56 ] Employment subsequently made direct use of city facilities. On 19 September, the President reported using DC3's new jobs system to interview candidates on the spot and hire two people. He said his chief of staff was adapting USAJOBS to accommodate the in-game system for departments and agencies with a team. The account identified an implemented hiring interaction rather than only a promised future feature: candidates could be interviewed in the city and hired through its system. [ 11 ] The integration of employment with buildings and agency teams gave Washington a practical role in public administration. Earlier recruitment had often directed citizens to contact leaders or submit external applications; the September account described city facilities used in the interview and hiring process. The president's statement also indicated that integration remained in progress, so the initial use did not establish that every agency had completed its transition. [ 17 ] [ 25 ] [ 11 ] Economic plans accompanied the launch. The 4 September address promised a forthcoming nUSA Stock Exchange under the Department of Commerce and Labor. A cabinet account the next day likewise described the market as forthcoming and said the military was working on new maps. These statements concerned planned additions. They did not establish an operational stock exchange or a completed new military map at the free-beta opening. [ 56 ] [ 57 ] Election system Main articles: Elections in nUSA and Federal Election Code (nUSA) On 7 September 2026, the Federal Election Commission invited citizens to test elections in DC3. Candidate registration was located at the District Court building, and voting booths were near MPD headquarters. Both were marked by yellow checkmarks on the minimap. Participants were asked to register candidates, gather signatures, and cast votes so that problems could be identified before a real election. [ 58 ] The notice described a normal qualification of two hours of play within the preceding thirty days for candidate registration, support of a candidate, and voting in elections or referendums. During the test, the requirement was temporarily reduced to 0.1 hours, or six minutes. Candidates could not register in two simultaneous elections; changing contests required the commission to disqualify the candidate from the first. The test therefore assessed not only voting booths but also participation requirements and candidate management. [ 58 ] On 25 September, the commission announced the forthcoming Senate and House Class I elections as the first elections in DC3. Registration was scheduled for 5–8 October, with ten signatures required from non-incumbents. Voting was scheduled for 9–11 October. Seven representatives and five senators were to be elected, with terms beginning on 11 October. The announced locations remained the courthouse registration desk and voting near MPD headquarters. [ 12 ] The commission also encouraged citizens to consult an in-game election schedule at the courthouse, saying that short reminders would replace announcements of this length. The change made the capital itself a place to obtain current electoral information, as well as to register and vote. As of the September announcement, the October contests were prospective; their outcomes were not yet part of DC3's completed election history. [ 12 ] Municipal government Charter and executive offices Washington's municipal government operates through a charter and local legislation within the wider federal system. H.R. 41, D.C. Charter Revised, was recorded as passed by both houses of Congress and signed into law. Its text provided for a mayor, deputy mayor, council, local departments, and procedures for ordinances, nominations, succession, and charter amendments. Later council records contain further charter changes, so the revised charter represents a particular framework in the city's institutional history rather than an assumption that every provision remained unchanged. [ 4 ] [ 59 ] Under H.R. 41's framework, the mayor headed municipal government and was a non-voting member of the council with a right to be heard. The mayor and deputy mayor were elected together for three-month terms. The mayor nominated department heads for council confirmation, supervised municipal employees, enforced ordinances, and could issue administrative orders consistent with higher law. title: Dearest (nUSA archivist)
text: Dearest is an account named in nUSA records as an Assistant Archivist and director of the National Wiki Archive Project. In November 2023, the National Archives and Records Administration (nUSA) announced Dearest's appointment to both roles and described the project as a way for community members to contribute to documenting nUSA history. [ 1 ] National Wiki Archive Project The appointment announcement linked the project to community history, record keeping, and historical resources, and linked to the then-public nUSA history wiki. A memorandum attached to the announcement set out the appointment and project arrangements; a later announcement said Dearest had passed the probation phase and was now a full Assistant Archivist. [ 2 ] The appointment placed public contributions within a managed archival workflow: the memo invited community contributions while requiring administrative approval for edits, describing review as a way to protect accuracy and community members. The memo also described a 90-day probationary period for the appointment. [ 3 ] Later archival work An August 2024 NARA monthly update listed “cherrydearest” as Deputy Archivist of the United States alongside AustinBoBoston1 as Archivist. The source archive uses “Dearest” in the 2023 appointment and “cherrydearest” in this later report; it does not explicitly state whether the spellings refer to the same account, so the title and earlier project role are kept under the form “Dearest.” [ 4 ] See also National Wiki Archive Project National Archives and Records Administration (nUSA) AustinBoBoston1 ↑ nUSA #nusa-updates Discord archive, 11 November 2023, Python splitlines() line 24,144. ↑ nUSA #nusa-updates Discord archive, 11 November 2023, Python splitlines() lines 24,144 and 24,148; “NARA Memo — Cherrydearest & National Wiki Project,” 11 November 2023, p. 1, PDF ; nUSA #nusa-updates Discord archive, 23 December 2023, Python splitlines() line 24,723. ↑ “NARA Memo — Cherrydearest & National Wiki Project,” 11 November 2023, p. 1, PDF ; nUSA #nusa-updates Discord archive, 11 November 2023, Python splitlines() line 24,144. ↑ nUSA #nusa-updates Discord archive, 1 August 2024, Python splitlines() line 29,008.

title: Democratic Party (nUSA)
text: The Democratic Party was an electoral label in the Roblox nUSA roleplay community. The archive identifies it in an October 2018 announcement about a proposed two-party system and in a Federal Election Commission certificate for Reset4K and Technozo in the Winter 2020 presidential election. Later compiled affiliation lists assign the Democratic label to other presidents, but the reviewed primary election evidence is strongest for the 2020 ticket. [ 1 ] Two-party proposal The October 2018 notice said that a Constitution Party had merged with the Republicans and anticipated a system centered on Democrats and Republicans. A subsequent public reaction poll invited support for either party. Its reaction counts show interest in the announcement, not verified party membership or the outcome of a formal election. The record also does not show that the Democratic Party had one stable leadership group across subsequent years. [ 2 ] Reset4K–Technozo ticket The FEC's Winter 2020 results letter certified Reset3634643, identified in the contemporary announcement as Reset4K, as Democratic President-elect and Technozo as Vice President-elect. The February result was followed by a March 21 inauguration notice and NARA roster entries for Reset4K as 30th President and Technozo as 31st. The sources link this particular election and succession to a Democratic ticket; they do not establish the internal workings of the party or which policies were collectively adopted by it. [ 3 ] The Reset4K administration's individual executive orders are described in Reset4K . Technozo later became President after serving as Vice President, according to the roster and a later congressional act. These officeholder records are evidence about the individuals; they should not be read as proof that every action of either administration was part of a Democratic Party program. [ 4 ] Changing rules for parties The management roadmap published in October 2023 proposed barring restored parties from using real-world party names. After a 2024 referendum and later MultiBallot redesign, the official list named Forward, Pioneer, and Plutocratic instead. The reviewed documents therefore support a historical Democratic label and a later change in recognized-party rules, but do not prove a current Democratic organization. title: DevGralius
text: DevGralius is an account whose archived nUSA work included election communications, Clan Management, and technical and archival responsibilities. A March 2020 retirement announcement in the group's announcements channel linked a letter describing the account's departing posts and a transfer of archival custody to the Archivist of the United States. [ 1 ] Election and management work The archived correspondence shows election-related responsibilities before the retirement. In November 2018, an announcement said election and other-affairs questions should be sent to DevGralius while its author was away; in June 2019, DevGralius posted an extension to an election deadline after an early closure error. The messages document operational communications but do not, by themselves, establish a full term in a particular election office. [ 2 ] In June 2019, DevGralius also announced that President-elect SpeakerJosh had released applications for the next administration, linking the announcement to the application document. Together, the election-time update and application notice show a practical communications role around election periods, while the surviving messages do not establish that DevGralius held the National Elections Administrator title during those episodes. [ 3 ] In September 2019, a Clan Management announcement said DevGralius had resigned as Clan Manager and Discord Moderator in order to run for office in the next term. In March 2020, the retirement letter described work across Web Services, Public Relations, Legal Counsel, Development, and engineering, as well as service as Reporter of Decisions for the United States Supreme Court. [ 4 ] The retirement letter's catalogue shows a career spanning both public-facing services and in-world institutions. It described an end to Clan Manager responsibilities in Web Services, Public Relations, Legal Counsel, and Development, plus a departure from the Chief Web Engineer role. It also recounted work as Reporter of Decisions for the Supreme Court and assignments involving District and Circuit Courts, and referred to maintaining the Judiciary Bot. The letter is a retrospective self-description of work rather than a complete staff chronology, so the article does not infer exact start or end dates for those individual posts. [ 5 ] Archive custody transfer The March 2020 letter said the archives had been held under the author's Clan Manager role and were being relinquished from Clan Management control. It left the National Archives with LargeTitanic2 , transferred custody of the official Constitution version the author had maintained, and asked that links be updated on government and court Trello boards. The letter also designated future Archivists “Protectors of the Constitution,” reflecting the author's proposed archival stewardship model. [ 6 ] The custody language separated archives from Group Management control while retaining a route for a future change: the letter said a later Archivist could ask pauljkl or Squareheaddude to bring the Archives back under that structure. Its requested link updates named Congress, the District Court, Court of Appeals, Supreme Court, and the Executive Office of the President Trellos, indicating that the transfer included cross-institutional reference maintenance as well as the Constitution file itself. title: District Court (nUSA)
text: Federal trial court in the nUSA Roblox roleplay judiciary The District Court (nUSA) is a trial-level institution in the simulated judiciary represented in the nUSA Roblox group's records. Its Trello archive is titled “United States Court” and organizes material by filing, assignment, case numbering, individual judges, appeals, NELA proceedings, and transfer to court archives. It is distinct from the Supreme Court (nUSA) , which maintains its own petitions, dockets, and order lists. These are roleplay proceedings, not real judicial authority. [ 1 ] Case and record workflow The District Court board separates an information section and bench roster from “Game Filing,” “Pending Assignment,” and case-numbering material. It groups case records under judge-specific lists and includes separate areas for appeals, NELA proceedings, and transfers to archives. The lists describe a workflow from submission and assignment to judge-organized files, but a card's appearance in a judge's list does not alone establish disposition. [ 2 ] The board contains filings as well as adjudicative records. A filing card may record parties, submission date, judge assignment, and complaint type while leaving the judge field blank; a separate decision or opinion record would be needed to establish a judgment. Filed, assigned, pending, appealed, archived, and decided are therefore not interchangeable statuses in an account of the court's work. [ 3 ] Judicial reorganization and constitutional eras A Group Management announcement on 26 November 2024 said the judicial system had suffered declining activity and bureaucracy and announced a wipe of judges and justices. It said a seven-member Group Management commission would choose replacements and that a Judicial Conference led by the new Chief Justice and Chief Judge would analyze and reform the branch after appointments. This is an announced intervention and plan; it should not be conflated with an ordinary judicial ruling or taken as proof that all planned reforms were completed. [ 4 ] The prior legal framework had changed in July 2023. Group Management announced that nUSA-generated case law and court precedent would be null and void as part of a wider reset of federal laws and congressional measures. Two days later it released a new Constitution, issued directives including court jurisdiction and records requirements, and said government institutions could resume ordinary work. This marks an announced break in the operative framework while preserving earlier judicial records as history. [ 5 ] In May 2025, ownership reported a dispute over a presidential impeachment and said the President would remain in office pending a decision by a three-judge District Court panel. The panel's 23 May opinion in Rathuzen v. United States Senate et al. found a defect in the succession of the presiding justice, ordered a fresh Senate vote, and stayed that order until a Chief Justice or eligible acting successor could be seated. Two judges wrote partial dissents. The decision did not determine the merits of the impeachment allegations or record a completed new vote. [ 6 ] Relationship with the Supreme Court and archives The Supreme Court archive includes appeal and certiorari forms that refer to District Court case numbers, consistent with a route to review lower-court matters. The two boards preserve different stages and record types: trial filings and judge-organized case files on the United States Court board, and appellate petitions and higher-court orders in the Supreme Court archive. This does not mean every District Court case was appealed. [ 7 ] The group announced NARA archival requirements in 2023 and later described judicial archivist duties covering both Supreme and District Court records. The court boards provide persistent record indexes; the available evidence does not establish that every case file is complete. title: District of Columbia City Council (nUSA)
text: Municipal legislature in the municipal government The District of Columbia City Council is Washington's municipal legislature. It considers local ordinances, resolutions and nominations and represents the capital in requests concerning its development. Its legislative and implementation responsibilities operate within the governing charter and the wider municipal framework. [ 1 ] Local government and development role In March 2024, Group Management assigned city councils a role in representing their municipalities to the development authorities and submitting development-request bills. An initial declaration that a revised D.C. Charter was active was withdrawn the same day to allow further municipal deliberation. [ 2 ] Development requests were to pass through the relevant city council, with final development decisions remaining subject to senior management discretion. The arrangement gave the council a channel for municipal representation without transferring ultimate control of development to it. [ 3 ] Activity and charter changes Municipal government has experienced periods of suspension. On 27 June 2021, declining participation and voting activity led management to discontinue local government, while leaving open a limited reopening if activity improved. Council institutions subsequently returned, although the precise resumption date remains unspecified. [ 4 ] The council's charter and standing rules govern its organization separately from individual legislative measures. In 2024, its business included the D.C. Charter Integrity Act and adoption of standing rules. Legislative approval and implementation remain distinct stages, particularly where a measure requires development action. [ 5 ] Records and relationship to federal government The council conducts municipal business while Congress considers federal legislation. Their responsibilities can intersect in matters affecting the capital, but collaboration on development does not confer general federal legislative power on the council. [ 6 ] In June 2024, NARA reported restoring City Council documents and regularly backing up its records after a risk of destructive interference. Preservation of municipal legislation became part of the broader work of protecting government archives. [ 7 ] Municipal autonomy and the return to Washington The Columbia controversy of March 2019 placed municipal consent at the center of a federal constitutional dispute. Congress attempted to combine Washington and Las Vegas without approval from either local legislature. The Supreme Court invalidated the merger under Article IV, Section 3, emphasizing that clear, public and unambiguous consent from both municipalities was required. The episode gave the councils a constitutional significance beyond routine local legislation. [ 8 ] Local executive policy also shaped public life. On 8 February 2021, DirectorPoke introduced Municipal Order 10-0001, Free Pizza Fridays, providing citizens a free slice of pizza each Friday. A companion order extended municipal protection privileges to the mayor's cabinet and incoming mayoral leadership. Subsequent notices on 11 and 19 February invited citizens to take part in the pizza program. These were mayoral measures rather than council enactments, but they formed part of the municipal government within which the council operated. [ 9 ] [ 10 ] Washington's institutions underwent another transition in January 2024. Boulder governor AlexReign was designated interim mayor pending City Council elections, and municipal personnel received transfer arrangements into Washington's police, fire and emergency medical services. The renewal of local services thus preceded the electoral completion contemplated for the council. [ 11 ] The Metropolitan Police absorbed police personnel under MasonRockefeller, while peep and Posiedon17 were designated to lead fire and emergency medical services. These changes connected the return of government to Washington with the experience and personnel of Boulder County . title: Domestic Protection Act of 2022 (nUSA)
text: 2022 law on citizenship and eligibility for civil office The Domestic Protection Act of 2022 ( DPA ) was legislation governing citizenship, foreign affiliations and eligibility for civil office. Speaker MasonRockefeller introduced it as H.R. 8 on 12 July during the Reconstruction Congress . He announced on 13 July that both chambers had adopted the measure and that it had been signed into law. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] The Act drew a sharp distinction between belonging to another American nation and serving in its civil offices. Ordinary foreign citizenship would no longer by itself justify exclusion from federal employment, but foreign civil-office service remained a basis for ineligibility at home. Its framework combined protections for participation with restrictions on public authority. [ 3 ] Citizenship and protection The Act defined domestic citizenship through national membership and status, excluding those awaiting immigration clearance or subject to a blacklist and those whose citizenship had otherwise been revoked or surrendered. It also described how citizenship could be restored through the authority or process by which it had been lost. [ 4 ] For affiliations abroad, the Act applied a broad membership definition rather than requiring full citizenship status within another nation. It prohibited discrimination in federal employment based solely on such citizenship and extended protection to former foreign citizens. People who had never held foreign civil office remained eligible for domestic office if they met the other statutory and constitutional requirements. [ 5 ] Foreign office and continuing ineligibility The protections did not extend to holding civil office in a foreign American government. That service produced an automatic domestic office bar. The law placed no expiration date on evidence of such service and required a later congressional act lifting the bar before eligibility could be restored. Leaving the foreign office did not, on its own, erase the domestic restriction. [ 6 ] The Act rescinded earlier laws imposing automatic office bars while preserving previously documented bars until both chambers removed them. It therefore replaced the governing framework without simply clearing every person's existing disqualification. An officeholder whose bar was lifted also had to return through the normal route: election for an elected office, or appointment and any required confirmation for an appointed office. [ 7 ] Congressional process For a bar imposed by congressional legislation, the House Judiciary Committee—or the House floor where no appropriate committee existed—had to make a good-faith effort to bring the individual before a hearing. Hearings were ordinarily public, with an exception for highly sensitive or classified matters. After two reasonable attempts to schedule an appearance, an uncooperative individual's absence no longer prevented further proceedings. [ 8 ] The measure then proceeded through the appropriate House and Senate committee and floor stages. The process placed the imposition and removal of congressional bars within both chambers, rather than leaving an individual's eligibility solely to an informal administrative determination. The statute was intended to take effect immediately and included a severability clause. [ 9 ] Historical setting Rockefeller presented the Act as a major achievement of reconstruction. It addressed one of the period's recurring tensions: allowing citizens to participate beyond the nation's borders while reserving public office from competing governmental commitments. Later that year, his proposed H.R. 25 responded to Ridgeway's participation restrictions through a different anti-discrimination measure. The later bill's introduction was separate from the DPA's enactment. [ 10 ] See also 2022 government reconstruction (nUSA) United States Congress (nUSA) Boulder County (nUSA) ↑ H.R. 8 legislative record ; Domestic Protection Act of 2022 , title page and sections 1–2. ↑ MasonRockefeller, announcement of the Domestic Protection Act becoming law, 13 July 2022, preserved in discord-archive-7012-1790806268742.txt , local source archive. ↑ Domestic Protection Act , sections 3–5. ↑ Domestic Protection Act , sections 3–4. ↑ Domestic Protection Act , sections 4–5. ↑ Domestic Protection Act , sections 5–6. ↑ Domestic Protection Act , sections 2 and 5. ↑ Domestic Protection Act , section 6(b). ↑ Domestic Protection Act , sections 2 and 6. ↑ MasonRockefeller, Domestic Protection Act and H.R. 25 announcements, 13 July and 26 November 2022, preserved in discord-archive-7012-1790806268742.txt , local source archive.

title: Dralian
text: Dralian 23rd President of nUSA (NARA roster) In office 15 January 2019 – 21 March 2019 [ 1 ] Preceded by Frosty_TheSn0wman Succeeded by Procursive 36th President of nUSA (NARA roster) In office 29 January 2021 – 7 February 2021 [ 1 ] Preceded by LordDeathTheReaper Succeeded by N_ightmarre NARA Presidential Records roster Dralian (also known as realDralian ) was recorded by the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) as the 23rd president of the nUSA roleplay community. Contemporary Discord records identify him as president by January 20, 2019; he said on March 13 that he would not seek another term, and the archive announced his successor’s oath on March 21. The surviving record does not establish the exact date he first assumed office. The presidential ordinal is disputed: NARA’s roster calls Dralian the 23rd president, while the oath post by his successor, Procursive, also identifies Procursive as the 23rd. [ 2 ] Election and transition The January 2019 transition followed President Frosty_TheSn0wman ’s announcement that his resignation would take effect at midnight on January 15. Dralian was identified as President in a January 20 notice inviting members to watch his first address to Congress. These posts place him in office by January 20, but do not record his oath or specify whether he became President immediately when Frosty’s resignation took effect. [ 3 ] On February 18, an election announcement named Republican Dralian and independent candidate DevGralius on the ballot for the 2019 Winter Election for President. The surviving announcement establishes that Dralian was a candidate, but the reviewed election records do not include a certified result or explain the relationship between that election and the presidential transition already recorded in January. [ 4 ] On March 13, a post attributed to Dralian thanked the community for what he described as progress over the prior two months and expressed excitement for the future. A follow-up message clarified that he was declining to seek another term, rather than resigning immediately, and said Procursive would be the next President. The archive then announced that Procursive had been sworn in on March 21. The oath post reproduced in the channel identifies Procursive as the 23rd President, creating an unresolved disagreement with NARA’s roster entry for Dralian. [ 5 ] Administration A surviving notice from February 2 records an unusually forceful announcement about the Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA): Dralian said it “no longer exists,” directed that team members be arrested, and warned that anyone found on the team would be banned. The archived statement does not include a separate order, its rationale, or evidence that arrests or bans followed. It therefore documents what the President announced, rather than the implementation or consequences of the directive. [ 6 ] Other posts document efforts to organize the executive branch and create public channels for engagement. On February 19, Dralian required federal employees to join an Executive Branch Discord within 48 hours or risk losing their jobs. On February 27, he announced the White House’s “We the People” petition system, saying that petitioners who reached a signature threshold were guaranteed a response. The source describes the announced rules and purpose, but does not preserve the threshold or a record of the system’s subsequent operation. [ 7 ] The archive also records several appointments and public events. A February 2 White House post said Dralian promoted LordDeathTheReaper to Admiral of the Navy. On February 19, Vice President Bakedgoods thanked Dralian for selecting him and said he had been sworn in after Senate confirmation. Dralian announced a State of the Union address for March 2; the archive confirms the event was publicized and the address was held, but the linked speech itself is not reproduced in the reviewed record. [ 8 ] Judicial nominations and later service In the final days of his presidency, Dralian nominated WalterMondale (identified parenthetically as “Dralian” in a court roster) to the United States Supreme Court as an associate justice. The court’s former-member card says the Senate confirmed the nomination 9–3–1 on March 21 and that he was sworn in on March 22, the day after Procursive ’s oath. The same board later listed “Justice Samuel Chase (Dralian)” as a separate associate-justice entry, but the card calls that a “Second Term”; the available records do not fully explain the name and term changes. [ 9 ] NARA’s Presidential Records board also contains a card titled “Dralian | Executive Order #23-001,” marked “Repealed.” The captured board export contains no order text or attached PDF for that card, so its title and later label do not establish what the order did, when it was issued, or when it was repealed. The same board has a separate “Dralian, 36th” President card. A later Discord retrospective lists “Dralian (9 days)” among short presidencies, but does not specify which numbered term it refers to. The later roster entry and nine-day note are treated as a separate second presidency below; the surviving records do not provide enough detail to merge the two terms into one chronology. [ 10 ] The reviewed sources do not establish prior service by Dralian as a senator, representative, mayor, or city council member. An earlier May 2018 Discord poll names him in a presidential debate, and the February 2019 ballot identifies him as a presidential candidate; neither notice establishes a prior elected office or the result of the earlier contest. [ 11 ] Second presidency The NARA Presidential Records roster lists Dralian as the 36th President, after LordDeathTheReaper (35th) and before N_ightmarre (37th). A separate, undated presidential chronology reports a term from January 29 to February 7, 2021. A linked vice-presidential roster places Dralian in that office through January 29 and Guggen_Pierre from February 4 to 7 under Dralian and N_ightmarre; an August 2024 NARA monthly update says Dralian’s presidency lasted nine days. These sources align with the reported dates, although the exports do not include a contemporaneous oath or inauguration record for this term. [ 12 ] The reasons-for-leaving-office list labels Dralian’s 36th presidency “Blacklisted,” but it does not name the authority or provide a date or explanation. The archived Presidential Records board contains a card titled “Dralian | Executive Order #23-001,” but the export has no order text or attachment, and the order number does not connect it to the 36th presidency. The reviewed records therefore do not support attributing a particular policy or blacklisting action to this term. title: Election schedule directive of 2024
text: The Election schedule directive of 2024 (Directive #003-02, “Modified Election Schedule”) was a Group Management memorandum dated 10 March 2024 that set a recurring schedule for congressional and municipal elections in the nUSA roleplay community. It assigned House elections to the first weekend of alternating months, Senate elections to the second weekend, and reserved the third and fourth weekends for municipal elections as needed; it stated that presidential election dates took precedence. [ 1 ] Background The memorandum reported that the then-current Senate and House election schedule conflicted with constitutional provisions concerning classes and terms. Its stated purpose was to modify the calendar to address that conflict. The NARA Hub's Volume 3 card lists Directive #003-02 as “Modified Election Schedule” and dates it 10 March 2024. [ 2 ] Schedule Under the directive, House elections were to occur on the first weekend of alternating months and Senate elections on the second weekend. The third and fourth weekends were held for municipal elections if needed. The letter gave presidential dates priority over the schedule it set for other races. [ 3 ] The schedule directive was one part of a broader set of 2024 management directives. A separate directive introduced MultiBallot, an election-system design centered on per-seat congressional contests and an in-game petition process. The schedule memorandum and MultiBallot document address related but distinct topics: timing of elections and ballot design, respectively. [ 4 ] See also Elections in nUSA Federal Election Commission (nUSA) MultiBallot directive of 2024 Later FEC archive records Separate from Directive #003-02's cycle calendar, the FEC announced in May 2024 that ordinary campaigning could begin 14 days before registration opened and would close after voting ended when the FEC announced it. Presidential campaign periods were excluded from this general rule and announced separately. Cite this as a subsequent operational rule, not as part of the March directive itself. title: Elections in nUSA
text: Elections in nUSA were roleplay activities conducted within the Roblox-based nUSA community to select federal and municipal officeholders. Archived announcements describe presidential, House, Senate, and municipal races, with voting taking place through Roblox games or other procedures announced by election administrators. The process and rules changed over time; the available record includes both detailed Federal Election Commission (FEC) regulations and later management directives. [ 1 ] Election administration The FEC organized and administered elections, and its notices directed candidates and voters to registration systems, voting locations, and complaint channels. A 2020 FEC publication described candidate eligibility checks, the administration of federal elections, ballot invalidation, and election officer oversight. Specific rules were tied to the relevant publication or election notice and should not be assumed to have governed every period identically. [ 2 ] The archived records show that the election experience was not always frictionless. During a May 2019 election, the FEC reported a filtering delay before it announced certification and delivery of results. In August 2019, an administrator said some voters could not access voting, described a temporary alternate voting route for affected users, and warned that duplicate voting would disqualify both ballots. These are contemporary notices about particular events, not evidence of the frequency or total impact of such problems. [ 3 ] Elections and voting venues Presidential and congressional contests are documented separately across the archive. The 2019 presidential elections (nUSA) included Winter, Summer, and Fall races. During the Summer 2019 presidential election, the FEC's result letter reported 753 ballots received and 362 disqualified, then certified SpeakerJosh as President-elect. The Fall 2019 result letter reported a distinct election and a different eligibility determination. [ 4 ] A 2019 schedule notice set separate dates for Washington, D.C. mayoral and council elections and specified registration, voting, and result dates. Federal congressional election notices likewise announced registration and voting phases by chamber and class. These records show distinct election calendars for different offices rather than a single universal election day. [ 5 ] Some voting occurred in Roblox experiences advertised as election venues. Announcements pointed voters to the “USA Secure Voting Access Area,” while the FEC's later MultiBallot announcement described moving candidate petitioning to the in-game U.S. Courthouse. The MultiBallot document was a design announcement; its contents specify the proposed workflow and do not alone establish its actual use in every subsequent election. [ 6 ] Rules and reforms A June 2024 Group Management announcement said the FEC and development team collaborated on MultiBallot, which outlined seat-specific congressional voting, incumbent labels, multiple simultaneous races, and a voter petition tool. The accompanying document also announced three official political parties and said existing and pending parties were dissolved. These points describe the system as announced in 2024. [ 7 ] A separate March 2024 election schedule directive addressed congressional and municipal cycles. It said the then-current House and Senate schedule conflicted with constitutional class and term provisions, assigned House elections to the first weekend of alternating months and Senate elections to the second weekend, and reserved the third and fourth weekends for municipal elections as needed. It said presidential dates took precedence. The rule belongs to that directive and period and should be read alongside the relevant constitutional version and later changes. [ 8 ] See also Presidential Elections in nUSA Federal Election Commission (nUSA) National Elections Administrator (nUSA) MultiBallot directive of 2024 Election schedule directive of 2024 2024 FEC election records 2024 presidential elections The Spring 2024 presidential ballot listed GeorgeGodsent and Robbiebeastpro90000 as a ticket alongside AdamStratton, StopJosh_STOP and JustinIsNotWeird, ElijahJunaid, and AugmentedReaper. The FEC’s linked result certificate names GeorgeGodsent and Robbiebeastpro90000 the winners with 330 votes, followed by AdamStratton with 227, AugmentedReaper with 10, StopJosh_STOP and JustinIsNotWeird with 8, and ElijahJunaid with 1. The certificate reports 575 post-filter votes and identifies GeorgeGodsent as President-elect for a planned March 21 inauguration. [ 9 ] The July ballot listed Pioneer Party nominee `@blanket` with `@cabot`, Plutocratic Party nominee GeorgeGodsent, and independent `@24craft`. The FEC result certificate names Teasoups as winner with 388 votes, ahead of GeorgeGodsent (379) and `24craft` (27), and calls Teasoups the 52nd President. Because the ballot and result document use different names for the Pioneer winner, the archive does not itself supply the identity crosswalk. On July 22, the National Elections Administrator described two possible transition dates for Teasoups after an election-schedule error; the post says Management would respect the incoming administration’s preference or a court decision, so it does not establish which option took effect. [ 10 ] The November presidential slate listed Teasoups with Rathuzen as the Pioneer ticket, TradeNato for Forward, and independent candidates. The November 10 FEC/Group Management post announced `@blanket`’s reelection; its attached result certificate names Teasoups and Rathuzen first, with 184 voters, followed by ApolloKorman and MitsuoMochizuki for Forward (82), Jtport (6), and adamsoups (3). The certificate records an inauguration scheduled for November 23. The sources use both `@blanket` and Teasoups for the Pioneer winner; preserve those source labels unless an independent record confirms their relationship. [ 11 ] 2025 FEC election records 2025 presidential contests The March 2025 ballot paired Rathuzen with snowbleed for the Pioneer Party, aConArtist with Frosty_TheSn0wman for Forward, and FighterHath with warlockings as independents. Rathuzen and snowbleed won with 60.75% of valid votes; the FEC declared them President-elect and Vice President-elect for a term scheduled to begin 23 March. [ 12 ] The July schedule changed during the campaign. The accessible NEA certificate names aConArtist the 56th President, but the Discord post linking it names @zapz. as President-elect. An inaugural notice identifies aConArtist and TacticalRock101 as President-elect and Vice President-elect, schedules their ceremony for 25 July, and a later post says the inauguration was starting. The inspected July records do not include an oath transcript or explicit completion notice. [ 13 ] The November results document certified Bathamza as President-elect and the 58th President. Although the schedule said the term would start 21 November, the NEA reported Bathamza was sworn in on 22 November alongside Vice President aConArtist. The 14 November ballot notice lists Mallsoft before an administrator announced the disqualification; the post gives no reason. [ 14 ] Later FEC archive records Voting systems and venues The MultiBallot system moved from testing to use in mid-2024. The nUSA owner announced test races at the in-game U.S. Courthouse on 23 June; a later notice reopened the test to try a revised backend. On 5 July, the FEC described the House Class II contest as the first election using MultiBallot, and its 8 July results notice thanked voters for using it. This confirms operational use in that contest, while the design document remains the source for features not independently described in these announcements. [ 15 ] In September 2026, the community announced testing a new election system in DC3 . The instructions invited participants to register candidates, collect signatures, and cast test votes; during the test the normal two-hour playtime threshold was reduced to six minutes. A later September notice scheduled October federal elections with registration at the DC3 courthouse, voting booths near MPD headquarters, and an in-game schedule at the courthouse. At the time of the announcement these were trial and prospective arrangements, not a completed election record. [ 16 ] Election administration disputes In March 2026, a management statement reported a revised tally after an initial FEC presidential certification and a filtering review. The initial notice reported 98 votes for warlockings and 90 for Bathamza; the subsequent management notice reported 117–109 for Bathamza, without a replacement FEC certificate in this archive and said the Commission would disable immediate result displays during filtering. The statements present management's findings and response; the available archive does not independently verify the alleged access to live vote data. title: Emperorlol01
text: Emperorlol01 is an account recorded in Federal Election Commission (FEC) results as a participant in nUSA municipal and congressional elections. The supplied election archive documents a December 2025 mayoral victory, followed by House Class I and Senate Class II election results in 2026. [ 1 ] The archive identifies the account's election activity but does not establish personal details beyond its displayed name. District of Columbia elections Emperorlol01 appeared on the FEC's December 2025 mayoral ballot with dancai123 as deputy mayor candidate. The FEC-certified results listed Emperorlol01 first with 59 votes, ahead of warlockings with 44, and a later message announced Emperorlol01 as mayor-elect. The schedule placed the start of the mayoral term on December 7, 2025, with its conclusion scheduled for April 7, 2026. [ 2 ] Congressional elections In April 2026, the FEC announced that nine House Class I representatives would be elected. Its certified House results listed Emperorlol01 first with 25 percent of the vote; the notice introduced the elected group as representatives-elect. The FEC's certified results listed Emperorlol01 tied for first with AvoidingPolitics, each at 25.81 percent, followed by three other candidates before the remaining candidates. The supplied notice does not document the oath or later completion of the term. title: FTN News
text: News organization in nUSA FTN News was a news organization in nUSA associated with the Federal Television Network . Led by founders GreatJakers1113 and Jonofdoom , it covered presidential elections, congressional leadership and military administration, published editorials, and collaborated with Reuters on a planned presidential debate. Jonofdoom served as News Director. On 12 October 2025, the founders announced the company's closure after approximately five years of operation. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] Origins and leadership FTN's founders described the company as approximately five years old at its closure in October 2025, placing its origins around 2020. In their farewell, they characterized FTN as nUSA's longest-running news source. [ 1 ] GreatJakers1113 and Jonofdoom shared leadership of the organization. Jonofdoom also wrote reporting and opinion pieces and helped create its internal code of ethics. Its publications used the corporate name Federal Television Network, Inc.; an editorial's notice also referred to FTN Media Group. [ 2 ] [ 3 ] Political reporting in 2024 FTN covered the opening of the autumn presidential campaign. On 10 October 2024, it reported campaign launches by incumbent President Teasoups and Nasanovuh, alongside a reported merger of the Plutocratic and Forward parties. Its coverage followed both the presidential contest and changes in party organization. [ 4 ] On 10 November, after the certification of Teasoups's victory, FTN reported ApolloKorman's concession. Its campaign coverage therefore extended from candidate announcements through the contest's conclusion. [ 5 ] FTN also reported on congressional leadership. Its 29 December article, “Speaker Arthur_Chen Resigns, KaceyMontagu Aims To Take Helm,” covered Arthur_Chen's departure amid a dispute over attempts to remove him as Speaker. The report addressed the transition in House leadership and KaceyMontagu's effort to secure the office. [ 6 ] Military administration coverage In January 2025, FTN published Jonofdoom's six-page report on the proposed abolition of the military Board of Governors. The report examined the competing arguments for continuity in military leadership and renewed political oversight of appointments. [ 3 ] Jonofdoom obtained comments from Secretary of Defense FighterHath, Senator RoFiles, President Teasoups and military officers, and sought a response from Group Manager AcidRaps. FighterHath defended the board as protection against politically motivated personnel changes, while RoFiles argued that its arrangements weakened accountability. Teasoups described work on a legislative replacement. The article included an anonymous service member's criticism of the board and FighterHath's stated intention to resign if it were abolished. [ 3 ] Editorial direction On 13 March 2025, Jonofdoom published “In Defense of Biased News,” responding to a controversy over NBC4's coverage of presidential candidate AConArtist. He opposed restrictions on partisan publication, favoring public rebuttal and fact-checking. At the same time, he pledged impartial reporting at FTN and referred to its internal ethics code. The publication explicitly identified the piece as his opinion rather than the position of FTN's management or staff. [ 2 ] Summer 2025 election coverage On 26 June 2025, FTN and Reuters announced a joint presidential debate scheduled for 30 June and invited questions from the public. [ 7 ] FTN subsequently projected a victory for AConArtist in the summer presidential election on 20 July. The announcement was an election projection issued by the newsroom. [ 8 ] Closure GreatJakers1113 and Jonofdoom announced FTN's closure on 12 October 2025. They explained that they could no longer devote the time needed to maintain the company. Their statement also said its DOCAL license had been revoked and that they did not intend to renew it. title: Federal Bar Association (nUSA)
text: Attorney licensing and professional regulation in the federal courts The Federal Bar Association is an institution for the admission and regulation of attorneys practicing in the federal courts. Its development has been shaped by a recurring constitutional dispute over who controls the legal profession: Congress could legislate on the Bar's structure, but executive administration of attorney licensing collided with the judiciary's authority over its own officers. The controversy culminated in the Supreme Court's 2019 invalidation of S. 147 and returned to public attention during the 2022 reconstruction . [ 1 ] [ 2 ] The Federal Bar and Supreme Court Bar were treated as distinct institutions in the 2022 reform plan. The former was intended to regulate practice in courts of original jurisdiction, while Supreme Court Bar membership carried privileges of practice in appellate courts and throughout the federal judiciary. That distinction made attorney admission more than a single examination: it defined access to different levels of the court system. [ 3 ] Executive control and the 2018 legislation The Consolidated Appropriations and Authorizations Act of August 2018 placed a new Bar system under executive control. The arrangement prompted Ultiman v. United States , in which the Supreme Court recognized concerns about the separation of powers. Before the Court finally resolved that issue, the Executive Reform Act changed the system, placing the Bar within the judiciary while retaining executive representation. Ultiman was dismissed as moot, leaving the constitutional question unsettled. [ 4 ] [ 5 ] The practical stakes were substantial. A licensing authority could decide who was permitted to represent clients, discipline practitioners and shape access to the courts. Assigning those powers to the executive placed the admission of court officers under a different branch of government. The later litigation turned on that institutional relationship rather than a general constitutional entitlement to practice law. [ 6 ] The two S. 147 measures In 2019, Congress returned to the executive-control model through the Reviving the Bar Act, known in the litigation as old S. 147. President Bakedgoods signed S. 147 on 27 April. J. A. Kirkman brought a class action for members of the Supreme Court Bar, and the District Court issued an injunction on separation-of-powers grounds. The Board of Law Examiners did not defend the original measure in the District Court proceedings described by the Supreme Court. [ 7 ] [ 8 ] Kirkman then worked with the original measure's sponsors on a successor, the Private Representation Revitalization Act, also designated S. 147. It addressed concerns affecting existing Supreme Court Bar members while retaining the central arrangement that had produced the constitutional challenge. Kirkman and the Board sought to dissolve the injunction so that the replacement law could operate. The Court of Appeals vacated the injunction without an affirmative merits argument establishing why it should be lifted. [ 9 ] SheldonParty's intervention SheldonParty , a member of the plaintiff class, sought substitution as class representative to pursue an appeal. His intervention kept the constitutional issue before the courts after the original representative and the licensing authority had agreed to seek dissolution of the injunction. On 17 June, the Supreme Court temporarily enjoined both the earlier and replacement S. 147 measures pending its decision. [ 10 ] [ 11 ] An earlier stay application, In re Kirkman , had been denied on 29 May. That order left the absence of a Bar-license requirement in the lower courts undisturbed at the time, but it did not settle the underlying law's constitutionality. The final decision came two months later. [ 12 ] [ 13 ] Judicial control restored Main article: Party v. Board of Law Examiners (nUSA) On 28 July 2019, the Supreme Court reversed the Court of Appeals and struck S. 147 down in its entirety. Justice Pitney's opinion held that licensing attorneys was an exercise of judicial power. Congress could not transfer that power to the executive without violating the separation of powers. The Court also rejected the proposition that there was a constitutional right to practice law: the successful challenge rested on which branch administered admission, rather than an unrestricted individual right to admission. [ 14 ] Justice Bork, joined by Justice Chase, agreed that executive administration was unconstitutional but warned against reading the decision too broadly. Congress could still regulate the form and structure of the Bar, provided that administration remained with the judiciary. This distinction preserved a legislative role in professional regulation while denying the executive control over the courts' officers. [ 15 ] The 2022 licensing plan On 14 July 2022, Chief Justice RummyLeroux announced plans to commission the Federal Bar Association through Chief Justice Directive 13, subject to revision by the Supreme Court. The association would regulate admission to federal trial practice, maintain lists of licensed attorneys and help create a path from legal practice to judicial clerkships and appointments. Existing attorneys would receive a fourteen-day interval after publication of the first examination before licensing became compulsory. [ 16 ] The plan connected professional regulation with the approaching opening of Boulder County . Attorneys were to be allowed to charge fees and establish law firms as businesses. RummyLeroux proposed a twenty-question examination covering general law, jurisprudence, scenarios and ethics, with fourteen multiple-choice questions, four short answers and two essays. Supreme Court Bar holders would retain broad practice privileges but would not serve as association directors or committee members. [ 17 ] [ 18 ] The July memorandum was advance notice of changing standards, rather than confirmation that every element had already taken effect. Its proposed system nevertheless differed decisively from the arrangement struck down in 2019: the new association was to remain subordinate to the Supreme Court.
