title: Federal Election Code (nUSA)
text: FEC rules governing elections in the nUSA roleplay community The Federal Election Code (also called the National Federal Election Code ) is a published collection of election rules enforced by the Federal Election Commission (FEC) in the Roblox-based nUSA roleplay community. The FEC's December 2025 edition describes the code as internally enacted rules for elections managed by the Commission, distinct from rules written by the United States Congress in the roleplay. The code is a dated source: the FEC reserved the ability to update it and vary enforcement, and later announcements documented amendments. [ 1 ] Publication history The FEC's rules were published in more than one edition. In February 2024, the Commission linked “2024 nUSA Election Regulation v3” and emphasized enforcement of the campaign-period rules. In July 2025, National Elections Administrator Jtport announced the first completed edition of “PortCode,” which he described as a Federal Election Code. On 1 December 2025, the FEC announced a new collaborative code that drew on PortCode and community input. Its release notice said the new edition would take effect after the elections scheduled to begin the following day. [ 2 ] The December 2025 code's preamble says that the Commission prepared it to explain rules enforced by the FEC, including directions drawn from the nUSA Constitution and the District of Columbia Charter. It describes the regulations as internally enacted by the Commission, applicable to FEC-managed elections, and subject to variation and revision as community needs change. The code identifies the National Elections Administrator as a Board of Owners appointee and gives the office responsibility for elections assigned to its control. [ 3 ] Provisions in the December 2025 edition The code covers Commission organization and oversight, election dates and transitions, party admission and primaries, candidate registration, ballot eligibility, voter screening, misinformation, presidential and mayoral running-mate letters, classified election records, evidence, voter eligibility, appeals, polling safety, government and military conduct, and the Hatch Act. It assigns the FEC a role in filtering and certifying party-primary results and requires parties to submit internal rules for record keeping. Its provision that voter records remain classified appears alongside a separate provision allowing the Commission to publish aggregate results without revealing individual voting activity. [ 4 ] Eligibility rules in that edition set minimum citizenship periods by office: one month for the House and D.C. City Council, two months for the Senate and D.C. mayor, and six months for President. The code also set signature thresholds of 10 for House, 15 for Senate, 20 for President, 10 for City Council, and 15 for mayor, while authorizing the National Elections Administrator to waive or change the thresholds. It required background screening of candidates and voters and prohibited alternate-account participation in FEC-managed elections. These provisions describe the December 2025 text, not an immutable schedule for every election. [ 5 ] The code also prescribed conduct rules. The December 2025 edition required a new campaign server created no earlier than one week before registration, set conditions for campaign messaging bots, and required candidates and campaigns to act in good faith. It established an appeal process under which a person challenging an FEC decision had to present a preponderance of evidence that the decision was improper, while stating that appeal was not a right under the code. Its legal-regulation article restricted use of military and government resources for campaigning, barred political activity by specified public employees, and protected those employees' right to vote and express opinions as private individuals. [ 6 ] Later amendments and administration Later notices show that campaign-server rules changed. On 1 July 2025, Jtport said prior server use was permissible in the current election because the policy was not expressly written into the code then in use. In February 2026, the National Elections Administrator first announced that campaign servers could be created no earlier than one week before registration, then revised the rule so servers could be created on or after the permitted campaign period began. In March 2026, the FEC announced that campaigns also had to provide server links and transfer ownership of campaign and transition servers to an account delegated by the Commission within 48 hours of creation. [ 7 ] On 26 May 2026, the NEA announced a code addition allowing a presidential candidate who met citizenship requirements to create an exploratory committee of no more than seven members. The notice said such a committee required FEC recognition, could not campaign or advertise before the campaign season, and could not create a campaign server before the permitted period. The notice linked an attached proposal and code, but those later consolidated texts have not been verified here; the announcement establishes the change as stated at that time. [ 8 ] The full code linked in the May and July 2026 announcements was not readable in this review. The December 2025 edition and later amendments should therefore be cited separately when describing a particular rule or election cycle. title: Federal Election Commission (nUSA)
text: The Federal Election Commission (nUSA) (FEC) was an election-administration body in the Roblox-based nUSA roleplay community. Its records describe work on federal and congressional elections, including setting or applying rules, managing registration and voting, reviewing ballots, and certifying results. The Commission used committees and election officers, with the National Elections Administrator appearing as a senior officer in its publications. [ 1 ] Organization and remit The FEC's January 2020 regulations say the Commission prepared a public compilation of election legislation and internal rules that applied to elections it administered. The document lists congressional and presidential committees, statutory officers, investigators, and the Office of the National Elections Administrator. It also describes candidate eligibility review and ballot administration under the rules it compiled. [ 2 ] The Commission's procedures assigned it authority to review candidate eligibility, manage election incidents, and invalidate ballots for violations of its regulations. The publication assigned the National Elections Administrator authority to remove election officers for specified violations, including unauthorized release of election material. These are provisions in the 2020 publication, rather than evidence that every listed power was exercised in every election. [ 3 ] Election administration Archived announcements show the Commission announcing candidate ballots, opening voting, handling complaints, and delivering results to congressional officers. In May 2019, for example, it announced that a filtering delay affected the release of results, then reported certification and delivery of election results to the Speaker of the House. During the Summer 2019 presidential election, its National Elections Administrator delivered results to Congress and named a President-elect and vice-President-elect. [ 4 ] The Commission's name appears in records as both “Federal Election Commission” and “Federal Elections Commission.” Separate election committees also appear in the records: the Fall 2019 plan calls itself the Federal Elections Presidential Committee while identifying itself as an official document of, and approved by, the Federal Election Commission. The records therefore support distinguishing the committee from the Commission rather than treating “FEPC” and “FEC” as interchangeable names. [ 5 ] Later records In September 2023, Group Management thanked goleros for leading both the FEC and the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA), documenting overlapping leadership at that time. An October 2023 appointment notice named TacticalRummy as National Elections Administrator while also assigning responsibility for running NARA. In June 2024, Group Management said the Government GM liaison posts would be merged “with NARA remaining separate”; that notice described NARA's relation to the management structure and did not announce a merger of NARA and the FEC. [ 6 ] A June 2024 announcement said Group Management and the FEC had collaborated on “MultiBallot,” a proposed redesign of congressional seat elections and political parties. The separately titled MultiBallot directive of 2024 describes the new system; the announcement and design document establish what was announced, while the reviewed records do not by themselves show how consistently the system was used afterward. [ 7 ] See also Elections in nUSA National Elections Administrator (nUSA) 2019 presidential elections (nUSA) Later FEC archive records Rules and public oversight The Commission's public rules changed over time. In May 2024, it moved the usual start of campaigning to 14 days before registration opened, with presidential campaign periods announced separately. Its June 2024 notices also published an eligibility board listing Roblox user IDs the FEC considered valid or ineligible and allowed members to challenge a listing through a ticket. A separate evidence notice rejected screenshots and required unedited GIFs or videos showing a Discord refresh or reopen cycle. These notices document the Commission's practice in 2024; they should not be treated as a complete or current code. [ 8 ] In December 2025, the FEC released a 20-page Federal Election Code that it described as a public compilation of rules enforced by the Commission. Its preamble says the code's rules were internally enacted, applied to FEC-managed elections, and could be varied or updated by the Commission. The code covers party primaries, candidate and voter eligibility, screening, evidence, appeals, election records, campaign conduct, polling safety, government and military restrictions, and political activity by government employees. Its signature schedule varied by office and expressly allowed the National Elections Administrator to change or waive thresholds. Later announcements document amendments, so the December 2025 edition is a dated snapshot rather than a complete statement of later practice. [ 9 ] The FEC's procedures were also tested by disputes and errors. In June 2024, a public notice said Senior Commissioner SolarGeneral had been temporarily suspended while the Commission reviewed internal procedures and staff; the archive contains no conclusion to that review. During the March 2026 presidential election, a management statement described an internal review of the filtering process and a blind re-filtering of ballots after it said an official had accessed live vote data during filtering. The resulting recount changed the announced result and prompted a stated safeguard against immediate result display. The event is described separately at Spring 2026 presidential election recount (nUSA) , with the claims attributed to the management statement. [ 10 ] Election systems and certification The Commission worked with management and developers on MultiBallot, which was tested in June 2024 and first used for a House Class II election in July. Announcements documented a further backend test, the first operational election, and an FEC-certified result, providing evidence of implementation beyond the design document. [ 11 ] In September 2026, the National Elections Administrator said certification of winners in FEC-managed federal and municipal elections belonged solely to the Commission and directed judges to administer oaths to House Class II winners who had not been sworn in by the House. This notice records the NEA's stated view during a seating dispute; the available archive does not document the House's response or a final resolution. title: Forward Party (nUSA)
text: The Forward Party was an official political party in the Roblox nUSA roleplay community's 2024 election-system redesign. Group Management named it among three selected parties in the June MultiBallot document, and an October announcement described it as the opposition to the then-current-government Pioneer Party . Later FEC notices identify Forward as an official party in 2025 and 2026, although they do not establish its status on every intervening day. [ 1 ] Recognition and electoral role The MultiBallot proposal replaced then-existing and pending parties with Forward, Pioneer, and Plutocratic. It proposed party names beside candidates on ballots, contests for individual congressional seats, and in-game petitions to qualify for the ballot. Forward's inclusion gave it an official place in that planned system; the text did not set out a distinct Forward platform, leaders, or membership figures. [ 2 ] An October management notice said there were two official parties and linked Forward's Discord as “Opposition.” Its invite preview described a community server established in June 2024. The word “opposition” in this source describes the party's relationship to the government at the time of the notice; it does not establish an election result for each seat or a permanent constitutional designation. [ 3 ] Later archival references District Court records include cases titled Jsjsjbsd v. The Forward Party and other suits naming Forward as a party. The reviewed index cards show that litigation involving the organization was filed or indexed, but the titles alone do not establish the claims, rulings, or the party's legal status when each case was brought. The 2024 official-party notices are therefore stronger evidence for recognition than later docket names are for continuing political power. [ 4 ] The earlier MultiBallot and October announcements did not provide a full officer roster or certified presidential ticket. Later election records identify Forward nominees and officers, as detailed below; affiliation at a particular date is best tied to those dated notices rather than inferred from service during months when Forward was the designated opposition. [ 5 ] Election archive additions In August 2024, the National Elections Administrator identified ArmanFoley as Forward chairman and said members had chosen to have him appoint three National Committee members. On 10 October, the FEC announced a temporary merger of Plutocratic into Forward and named Mr_Choo chair and RobertTLincoln vice chair during the transition. The merger notice does not establish how long the arrangement lasted. [ 6 ] In the 16 March 2025 presidential election, the certified Forward ticket was aConArtist and Frosty_TheSn0wman. It received 123 votes, of which 112 were valid (28.0%); Pioneer ticket Rathuzen/Snowbleed won with 243 valid votes. In October 2025, the Forward National Committee disqualified ArmanFoley from the party's presidential primary. The FEC's subsequent decision found the committee exceeded its charter and election-code authority, vacated the disqualification, and directed the party to reinstate Foley or conduct a supervised rerun if the primary had concluded. The FEC announced the reversal on 21 October, and an announcement two days later named ArmanFoley as the Forward presidential nominee. [ 7 ] In the 2026 presidential cycle, the FEC first identified Sheev_PalpatineTGR as the Forward candidate, then certified AguilaBread as the replacement Forward nominee on 5 July. In the final certified election results, AguilaBread and running mate EdmundCarter received five votes; Pioneer ticket Epicwarrior_99/AnthonyRBurgess received 114, and independent jsjsjbsd won with 131. The FEC's 2026 revamp also approved a formal Forward platform, but the supplied archive lists the platform PDF without preserving its URL or contents. title: Frosty TheSn0wman
text: Frosty_TheSn0wman 22nd President of nUSA In office 13 November 2018 – midnight after 15 January 2019 (Tennessee time) [ 1 ] Preceded by Lordsights Succeeded by Dralian NARA presidential roster Frosty_TheSn0wman is a Roblox account recorded in nUSA community sources as Vice President in October 2018 and President Frosty in January 2019. A poll listed Frosty among candidates for the next presidential term that October, but the archive does not establish the election result or the date he took office. [ 2 ] Vice presidency and transition On October 6, Frosty warned the community about an account impersonating him and identified himself as Vice President. The next day's community poll asked whom members supported for the next presidency and listed Frosty, mario and AcidRaps as candidates. The post records a poll rather than a certified election result. [ 3 ] By January 13, 2019, the archive identified him as President Frosty and reproduced a statement attributed to his presidential account. The sources reviewed do not include his oath or specify when the transition from Vice President to President occurred. [ 4 ] Disputed foreign policy On January 13, after the Senate (nUSA) rejected the Treaty of Washington, Frosty posted that the time for considering peace was over and that the military stood ready to fight the United Kingdom. The archive records the Senate result and his public position; it does not independently establish the events or claims underlying the Roblox roleplay conflict. [ 5 ] The next day, the channel linked a presidential statement about future conflict with the United Kingdom and a separate document described as a Russian ultimatum. The accompanying ultimatum document set out Russia's in-world demands, including an apology and resignations by U.S. intelligence leaders and President Frosty. These are demands made in the roleplay document, not independently verified events. [ 6 ] On January 14, a post attributed to Senator SmallCho's Special Counsel's Office reproduced the beginning of a statement saying the office had found sufficient information to determine that the President, Chief of Staff and other officials had committed “high crimes.” The archived excerpt is cut off before describing the alleged conduct, and the reviewed messages do not establish the proceeding's final disposition. The statement is therefore treated here as the Special Counsel's claim, not a finding independently verified by the source archive. [ 7 ] Resignation On January 15, Frosty announced that his resignation as President would take effect at midnight. In the statement reproduced in the Discord archive, he criticized what he described as nUSA's recurring pattern of removing presidents each term. That was Frosty's explanation and assessment of his decision; the archive does not establish a causal link between his resignation and the Special Counsel statement posted the prior day. [ 8 ] The archived messages establish the resignation date but do not identify a successor in the same announcement. The opening and closing dates of Frosty's presidency therefore remain incomplete in this source record. title: GeorgeGodsent
text: GeorgeGodsent 51st President of nUSA (NARA roster) In office 21 March 2024 – 16 July 2024 [ 1 ] Preceded by Robbiebeastpro90000 Succeeded by saviorjoshh NARA Presidential Records roster GeorgeGodsent (also identified as HHPrinceGeorge in the NUSA presidential chronology) was the 51st President of the United States in the nUSA roleplay community. Records from his administration document executive orders to end executive-branch blacklists, establish a commission to prepare a community-adapted U.S. Code, create a clemency-review commission, and prohibit agency use of the Cipher service. A Group Management monthly report later recorded his resignation during July 2024; the reviewed primary sources do not establish its exact date or a single reason for it. [ 2 ] Election and term The Spring 2024 presidential election schedule announced March 7–17 as its registration, ballot, voting, and results period. A January 28 notice had already moved the Spring election to March 16 and set March 21 as its planned inauguration date. On April 16, an announcement said that the next day marked one month since GeorgeGodsent had been elected and taken office. These records indicate his accession in March, but they differ on the exact date; the available sources reviewed here do not include a signed inauguration record resolving the discrepancy. [ 3 ] Executive orders President GeorgeGodsent at a July 2024 gathering, saying he was signing a joint resolution declaring war on Ridgeway. The screenshot does not show the resolution text or subsequent hostilities. Executive Order 51-001, dated March 28, 2024, prohibited executive-branch blacklists or equivalent employment bars, revoked previously issued blacklists, and directed misconduct cases toward agency internal-affairs investigations or courts. The order presented this as a campaign promise and a change to executive-branch employment policy. [ 4 ] An April 9 order established a U.S. Code Commission under the Executive Office of the President. Its assigned task was to review real-world U.S. Code provisions and propose a version adapted to the Roblox community; AlexJCabot and moneymack9999 were named chair and vice-chair. The proposed code was to go to the President for approval, after which the order and commission would become moot or dissolve. [ 5 ] On May 1, the President established the Second Chance Commission to receive and review pardon and clemency requests, including possible sentence reductions. The order excluded serious offenses such as treason and bribery from ordinary review unless there was reasonable suspicion of a corrupt trial or procedural problem. It assigned the White House Counsel and Pardon Attorney leadership roles and described a process in which the commission would advise the President, who retained the decision on clemency. [ 6 ] An order dated July 7, 2024, prohibited federal executive departments and agencies from using the private Cipher service, including its bot and website. It directed the Intelligence Community to develop government-owned background-check systems and said agency leaders and directors violating the order could be terminated. The Trello archive indexes the measure as “51-004 | Cipher Ban”; the attached instrument is headed “Executive Order … To Ban the Use of Cipher” and labels itself “Executive Order 51-6.” [ 7 ] Resignation and succession An August 1, 2024 NARA monthly update retrospectively listed GeorgeGodsent’s resignation among the key events of July. The same update noted the short tenure of President saviorjoshh and the inauguration of President teasoups. It did not give GeorgeGodsent’s resignation date, explain the succession sequence, or describe a reason for his departure; accordingly, those details remain uncertain in the sources reviewed here. [ 8 ] References 2024 FEC election records In March 2024, the FEC certified GeorgeGodsent and Robbiebeastpro90000’s ticket as the winner of the Spring presidential election, reporting 330 votes for the pair. In July, the official ballot identified GeorgeGodsent as the Plutocratic Party presidential nominee; the certified results placed him second with 379 votes, behind Teasoups with 388. [ 9 ] On 25 June 2024, the FEC said the GeorgeGodsent campaign had received a warning over “predatory campaigning,” which the notice described as dismissing non-civil-office employees who supported rival candidates. This is the FEC’s account of its warning, not an independently adjudicated finding. title: Goleros
text: goleros is a Roblox nUSA community leader whose documented service centered on the Federal Election Commission (nUSA) (FEC) and the National Archives and Records Administration (nUSA) (NARA). In September 2023, Group Management said goleros had headed both bodies for a considerable period and announced that future leadership arrangements would be decided later. Earlier election notices identify goleros as National Elections Administrator and credit the FEC staff with processing election results. [ 1 ] The available announcements do not give a complete appointment or end-date chronology. Election administration A 2022 FEC employee roster lists Goleros as Administrator, although the exported roster entry is truncated before its full duties and hire date. By July 2023, election announcements identify Goleros as National Elections Administrator. A results post thanked FEC staff for filtering roughly 500 voters, and another election schedule was signed by Goleros in that title. The records support an election-leadership role but not a precise start date or a complete count of elections administered. [ 2 ] NARA leadership and departure Group Management’s September 2023 departure announcement credited goleros with heading both the FEC and NARA and described the departure as a move toward other interests. It expressed appreciation for the integrity of the election work, while leaving next steps for both agencies undecided. Since the source does not explain how the two leadership roles were combined or when either began, they should not be treated as a single office with a known term. [ 3 ] See also National Archives and Records Administration (nUSA) Federal Election Commission (nUSA) National Elections Administrator (nUSA) TacticalRummy ↑ Group Management, “Goleros Departure” (28 September 2023; Python splitlines lines 23281–23290), Discord #announcements export, discord-archive-597-messages.txt; FEC election notices (2023; Python splitlines lines 22547–22551 and 22604–22606), Discord #nusa-updates export, discord-archive-2642-messages.txt. ↑ FEC roster excerpt (2 July 2022; Python splitlines lines 20983–20997), and FEC election announcements (2023; Python splitlines lines 22542–22551 and 22600–22606), Discord #nusa-updates export, discord-archive-2642-messages.txt. ↑ Group Management, “Goleros Departure” (28 September 2023; Python splitlines lines 23286–23290), Discord #announcements export, discord-archive-597-messages.txt.

title: Group Management (nUSA)
text: Group Management (GM) is the community-management authority described in nUSA's Roblox roleplay records. It issued organizational directives, oversaw administrative appointments and, in the July 2023 constitutional framework, controlled NARA. Group Management announcements and board records are first-party accounts of roleplay governance, not acts of the real U.S. government. [ 1 ] Directives and institutional authority On 17 July 2023, GM published Memorandum #001, a package whose listed subjects included NARA, legislative archival requirements, legislature regulations and other government procedures. The companion Constitution says it was published and instituted that day. Together they establish the documented authority structure for that version of the roleplay, while leaving earlier law subject to the separate July reset announcement. [ 2 ] Memorandum #001 assigned NARA responsibility for storing and maintaining public records about the legislature, judiciary and government. It described NARA as operating autonomously from the player government while remaining under GM empowerment and oversight. Its archival screening concerned compliance with filing requirements: the memo said a passed measure rejected for archival noncompliance would not become active law. These provisions do not show NARA deciding the policy merits of a bill. [ 3 ] Resets and later records The July 2023 legal reset was announced by GM as voiding existing federal laws, case law and congressional resolutions, motions and awards from 6 p.m. Eastern time on 15 July. GM then introduced the new Constitution and archival framework. These were in-community rules; the announcement's sweeping language should be read as the stated scope of the roleplay reset, not a claim about real legal effect. [ 4 ] GM's records also label later instruments by status. The NARA Hub lists Group Management Directives Volumes 1 and 2 as repealed and Volume 3 as active in its export; these labels describe the board's recorded status at the snapshot, not proof of the operation of every directive on every date. A June 2024 announcement said NARA would remain separate from a merged government-liaison post even though the same manager held NARA responsibilities. This shows an institutional distinction alongside overlapping personnel roles. [ 5 ] Relationship to the constitutions The Constitution announced on 6 November 2024 was described as approved by the Senate, House, District Courts and Supreme Court, with Group Management owning and maintaining the PDF. The source copy was inaccessible during archive review, so the announcement supports the reported approval and ownership process but not a detailed summary of its clauses. In 2025, a separate Constitution was announced as readopted and revised by P.L. 105-1; the sources disagree about the underlying text's origin date. See Constitutions of nUSA and 2025 constitutional readoption in nUSA . title: Guggen Pierre
text: Guggen_Pierre 39th President of the United States In office 16 July 2021 – 21 July 2021 [ 1 ] Preceded by RalphFoley Succeeded by LeoVinick NARA Presidential Records roster Guggen_Pierre , also styled GuggenPierre , was the 39th President of the United States , serving from 16 to 21 July 2021. Previously vice president under RalphFoley , he succeeded him following his resignation and completed the remaining days of the presidential term before LeoVinick 's scheduled inauguration. His five-day presidency included judicial appointments and a series of executive nominations. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] Vice presidency The Federal Election Commission certified the Winter 2021 election on 14 March. Its results letter declared RalphFoley the winning Constitutionalist presidential candidate and Guggen_Pierre vice president-elect. The Commission reported 444 ballots received and 111 disqualified for alternate accounts or lack of citizenship. It also waived the requirement for the president-elect to submit a separate letter to Congress declaring his vice-presidential choice and certified Guggen directly from the campaign. [ 2 ] The compiled vice-presidential chronology dates his service under RalphFoley from 21 March to 16 July 2021. That service preceded his accession to the presidency rather than constituting a separate presidential election victory. [ 3 ] Presidency Succession and the remaining term RalphFoley announced his resignation shortly after midnight Eastern time on 16 July, thanking the country for the preceding months in office. Guggen succeeded him five days before the next administration was due to take office. The Summer 2021 election had already been certified in LeoVinick's favor on 12 July, and the FEC's term plan set the inauguration for 21 July. [ 4 ] [ 5 ] The brevity of the presidency reflected a succession near the end of an existing term. Guggen's departure coincided with the scheduled inauguration, rather than an early resignation from a new four-month administration. [ 1 ] [ 5 ] Appointments and nominations Guggen nominated Yiddished and Kind_Yada to Supreme Court vacancies in the opening hours of his presidency. The court's records date their confirmations and swearing-in to 16 July, with Senate votes of 6–0–0 for Yiddished and 4–3–0 for Kind_Yada. [ 6 ] [ 7 ] Other opening announcements appointed r6kt as White House chief of staff and SurpriseParty to a Senate vacancy. They also nominated bobbert as vice president. The latter nomination was accompanied by criticism of congressional bureaucracy and praise for his experience in the community; it was a nomination rather than a verified confirmation. [ 8 ] The administration announced further nominations for executive departments and agencies, including homeland security, treasury, the FBI and SWAT. Some nominations were revised almost immediately: a Secretary of Defense nomination was rescinded in favor of retaining SolarGeneral, and a transportation nomination was later changed to a deputy position. These announcements indicate active staffing changes despite the limited time remaining in the term. [ 9 ] Activity and municipal reorganization Guggen's presidency coincided with the implementation of a management decision to discontinue municipal government. On 18 July, Aerium announced that five municipal groups had been cleared: the Metropolitan Police Department, State Police/Nevada Highway Patrol, Washington Emergency Medical Services, Washington Fire Department and City Council. He said they could reopen after legislation incorporated them into the federal government. The change implemented an earlier management announcement, rather than a new policy originating with Guggen. [ 10 ] Activity in Washington was uneven during this period. A White House invitation on 18 July advertised 44 players in the capital, even as municipal institutions were being reorganized. The announced count represents a particular session and does not establish the city's average activity throughout the term. [ 11 ] Handover to LeoVinick On 21 July, Ronnie invited citizens to the inauguration of the new administration. LeoVinick issued a signed nomination notice that morning, naming his administration's officers and declaring nominees acting officers pending Senate confirmation. Guggen's tenure ended at that scheduled transition. [ 12 ] References ↑ 1.0 1.1 1.2 Nusapedia presidential chronology ; NARA Presidential Records, Guggen_Pierre, 39th . The contemporary RalphFoley resignation was posted on 15 July 2021 at 9:01 p.m. PDT, corresponding to 16 July at 12:01 a.m. EDT. The post states his resignation but gives no detailed reason for leaving. The same account posted presidential documents named RALPHIUSS in July 2021. NARA's presidential card was subsequently renamed from RalphFoley to Ralphiuss. ↑ 5.0 5.1 Federal Election Commission, Summer 2021 election plan , p. 5; results letter , 12 July 2021, p. 1. ↑ White House announcements, Yiddished nomination and chief-of-staff appointment , 15 July 2021, 9:21 p.m. PDT, and Kind_Yada nomination , 9:46 p.m. PDT. Both were posted after midnight EDT on 16 July. title: History of the United States
text: National history from the foundation of nUSA in 2012 The history of the United States dates from the foundation of nUSA by Nightgaladeld on 26 November 2012. The country developed a presidency, Congress, courts and public-service agencies alongside a succession of cities and changing ownership arrangements. National life initially centered on Washington, D.C. , while Las Vegas became an important center of employment, commerce, municipal elections and news coverage. The later rebuilding of Washington and the development of Boulder County changed the settings in which citizens worked, voted and participated in government. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] An ownership crisis in July and August 2013 produced competing claims to presidential authority before Nightgaladeld recovered the group and an election brought Marinio and Lumidas to office. Subsequent governments developed recruitment and electoral procedures, reorganized agencies and contested the limits of executive, legislative and judicial power. The attempted State of Columbia in 2019 tested federal authority over municipalities, while Procursive 's impeachment produced a major dispute over judicial review of removal from office. [ 4 ] [ 5 ] [ 6 ] [ 7 ] [ 8 ] The early 2020s combined political turnover, external conflicts, rival United States groups and uneven participation. Municipal government was discontinued in 2021 amid declining activity and voting, before new reconstruction efforts and Boulder provided further settings for public institutions. The July 2023 legal reset nullified the earlier federal legal framework and was followed by a new Constitution and management-supervised archival procedures. Management resignations and the shutdown of several administrative services late that year preceded Pauljkl 's transfer of ownership to UKR41NIAN and Dilliuss in January 2024. [ 9 ] [ 10 ] [ 11 ] [ 12 ] [ 13 ] The 2024 rebuilding was followed by a four-person ownership partnership in January 2025 and further constitutional and electoral disputes, including Rathuzen 's impeachment trial and conflicting presidential results in March 2026. Spikers replaced AdamStratton on the ownership board in February 2026. DC3 opened in paid early access in July and free beta in September, adding integrated electoral, training and employment systems while development continued. By September 2026, the country's elected institutions, administrative ownership and public activity operated within another generation of the capital. [ 14 ] [ 15 ] [ 16 ] [ 17 ] [ 18 ] [ 19 ] [ 20 ] [ 21 ] Chronological overview Major periods and turning points Period Principal developments 2012–early 2013 Foundation; Constitution and Bill of Rights; original Washington; early elections and recruitment. [ 22 ] [ 23 ] [ 2 ] 2013 Ownership and presidential crisis; recovery of the group; Marinio–Lumidas election and reconstruction. [ 5 ] [ 6 ] 2014–2017 Agency and electoral development; Las Vegas civic life; executive reorganization; Washington rebuild. [ 24 ] [ 3 ] 2018–2019 Impeachments; State of Columbia; Procursive's removal and judicial challenge; more elaborate election administration. [ 25 ] [ 7 ] [ 8 ] 2020–2021 Reset4K's disqualification and removal; HUSA/BUSA sanctions; municipal-government discontinuation. [ 26 ] [ 27 ] [ 9 ] [ 10 ] 2022–2023 Executive reconstruction and Boulder; Jtport's acquittal; legal reset; late-2023 service and management crisis. [ 28 ] [ 29 ] [ 11 ] [ 13 ] 2024 Ownership transfer and rebuilding; municipal consolidation; executive and congressional disputes; judicial reset. [ 30 ] [ 31 ] [ 32 ] 2025–September 2026 Collective ownership; constitutional readoption and Rathuzen crisis; election disputes; developer-board transition; DC3 beta and integrated civic systems. [ 14 ] [ 33 ] [ 15 ] [ 17 ] [ 19 ] Foundation and the first capital, 2012–2013 Foundation and constitutional design Nightgaladeld founded the United States on 26 November 2012. During the following month, the government developed a constitutional framework, a statement of rights and a capital in Washington, D.C. . The first arrangements combined a national administration with proposed state and territorial institutions. From the outset, the presidency, the legislature and the judiciary were distinct offices, while the group's owner exercised practical control over the community in which those institutions operated. [ 1 ] The Constitution published on 26 December outlined a bicameral Congress, a presidency and a Supreme Court. Congress could legislate and participate in decisions concerning war and treaties; constitutional amendments required agreement by both chambers and approval involving the president and the Court. The House's representation was tied to the size of the states, at one representative for each fifty members, while each state was to have two senators. The proposed terms were considerably longer than those used in later electoral arrangements: representatives would serve ten months, with a review or election in the fifth month, and senators twelve months, with a review in the sixth. The extent to which all these arrangements operated is uncertain. [ 22 ] Statehood was defined partly through membership and partly through the existence of a functioning civic setting. The Constitution specified membership thresholds for states and territories, provided for a return to territorial status if membership fell below forty, and required a place with more than one hundred visits. A legislature's meeting place and a federal court building were among the expected facilities. The prescribed balance between citizens' shops or buildings and government offices favored civilian construction: five citizen buildings were required for each office building. These provisions connected representation to the development of inhabited places and attempted to give businesses and ordinary residents space alongside government. [ 22 ] The Bill of Rights, published the same day, addressed speech, assembly and the press; possession of arms and self-defense; protection of property and businesses; searches and warrants; due process and jury trial; and voting. These rights came with qualifications and could be changed subsequently. In particular, the initial voting provision allowed a voter to take back a vote, whereas the January 2013 vice-presidential poll prohibited changing one. The developing constitutional order therefore included both a statement of general rights and rules for particular electoral procedures, which did not remain identical across successive announcements. [ 23 ] Washington and public employment The early White House grounds, identified by J_B as 25 March 2013. Uploaded by J_B on 11 June 2020 at 10:13 p.m. [ 34 ] Washington became the center of national administration and public recruitment. On 20 January 2013, Nightgaladeld publicly presented the city and linked its original place. In a recruitment notice later that day, he identified Washington as the official city of the United States and advertised jobs in the Secret Service, Homeland Security, the Central Intelligence Agency, Capitol Police and White House staff. Taxi driving appeared alongside these public offices. The capital thus offered civilian employment as well as a setting for security agencies and political officials. [ 2 ] The early capital brought together several different forms of participation. Citizens could seek an agency position, join the political institutions or perform a service within the city. The recruitment notice presented these activities as parts of the same national community, rather than restricting membership to election participation or military service. Its mixture of protective, intelligence, legislative-security and civilian work anticipated the later importance of agency recruitment, transport and public employment in both Washington and Las Vegas. [ 2 ] The first electoral procedures Early elections combined citizen participation with approval by national officeholders. A January 2013 vice-presidential selection began with a citizen poll to choose five finalists. The posted intermediate tallies changed as voting continued: jbn011 led the reported count, followed by Sk8terdude545, while Baxterknite and 97tomtom were among the other finalists. A subsequent posting replaced the initial fifth finalist with hithop3000. These announcements described successive stages of the selection rather than a completed appointment. [ 35 ] The second poll, opened on 26 January, listed those five candidates and prohibited alternate-account votes, duplicate votes, self-voting and changes to a submitted vote. The winner of the citizen poll would then be considered by Congress, White House staff and the founders. Selection therefore involved more than a single national ballot: popular support provided an initial result, but the announced process retained a further institutional vote. The original procedure also shows that account eligibility and repeat voting were concerns well before the later development of the Federal Election Commission's filtering systems. [ 36 ] The ownership and presidential crisis of 2013 Account compromise and temporary custody In July 2013, a dispute over the ownership of the national group developed into a conflict over presidential authority. On 27 July, Nightgaladeld reported that his account had been compromised and that he was seeking assistance from Roblox moderators. A separate post announced that Katie would hold the United States until his account was safe. This was an announced temporary custodial arrangement; the subsequent transfer and retention of the group became the central issues in the crisis. [ 37 ] The following day, the Emergency Defence and Advisory Council issued a statement saying that government and law-enforcement functions remained operational. The statement cautioned that a full explanation of the incident had not yet been established and promised further information. It was signed by Lumidas in his national-security capacity, Nick00788 in his intelligence capacity and Moolah as president. Their intervention sought to maintain administrative continuity while the group's ownership was uncertain. [ 38 ] By the end of July, the group was under Moolah60 's control. Nightgaladeld alleged that his compromised account had left the group, Katie had claimed it and TheEvidence had transferred it to Moolah. Marinio later published an account containing purported conversations from 27 July. In that account, Nightgaladeld initially asked Katie to hold the group and subsequently directed that it be transferred to Moolah. Marinio denied personally making the transfer and said that TheEvidence had used the account to do so. The participants disagreed over the meaning and legitimacy of the transfer; the accusation that the account compromise was deliberately arranged was not established by an independent finding. [ 39 ] Competing claims to leadership The dispute widened when gmf34 assumed the presidency. In a statement on 30 July, he said that Moolah had taken custody after the previous owner left and had permitted him to become president as the next official in command. He credited Moolah with work on the capital, scripts, interfaces and group ranks. Nightgaladeld, in a separate statement that evening, objected that no election had occurred and criticized Moolah's continuing possession of the group. The disagreement concerned both the legitimacy of presidential succession and whether ownership would return to the founder. [ 4 ] Gmf34's program promised clearer constitutional arrangements, departmental organization, a functioning Congress and reinvestment of national funds. It also proposed more cities, business lots and housing, together with the removal of car licenses and restrictions he considered unlawful. The program presented development and administrative reform as a response to the change of leadership. Implementation of the program is uncertain. [ 4 ] The crisis also prompted resignations and public argument. The chief of staff resigned on 30 July, questioned the retention of the group and discussed earlier conversations about eventual Moolah ownership. The statement expressly left uncertain whether the breach had been deliberately arranged. In August, a Citizens Voice post demanded elected leaders, trained officials, freedom of expression and the removal of the group-holder rank. A response defended the existence of voting and institutions under the current administration and noted that Moolah had previously been elected. These exchanges exposed competing understandings of legitimate government without providing a reliable measure of support for either side. [ 40 ] Development discussion continued during the political dispute. On 9 August, Moolah announced plans for a Dunkin' Donuts building in Washington and invited suggestions for its features. An accompanying reply referred to custom animations. The proposal concerned the same capital around which the dispute over ownership and access was unfolding, but the opening date is uncertain. The capital remained an object of competing administrative and development programs throughout the crisis. [ 41 ] Nightgaladeld continued to pursue recovery through customer support. In an 8 August post, he described supplying the group link and waiting beyond an expected response period. He also announced plans for reform, a separate holder and presidential election, and the exclusion of officials whom he accused of disloyalty. These were his intended measures while ownership was still contested, rather than evidence that every threatened expulsion had occurred. [ 42 ] Restoration and the August election On 15 August, Nightgaladeld publicly acknowledged that the United States had been returned and thanked customer service. His statement promised a return to democracy and elections, while excluding those he regarded as responsible for the dispute. The precise moment of restoration is uncertain. On 16 August, Gmf34 resigned all his offices and announced his departure, citing the turn of events and an inability to remain sufficiently active. [ 5 ] Restoration did not immediately end disagreement over the administration of the capital. Nightgaladeld said that he intended to clear arrest records and locate scripts which, he alleged, Moolah had used to interrupt access to his Washington and direct players elsewhere. The statement linked the political controversy to the practical question of which capital citizens could use. The claimed interference remained an accusation, rather than a technical finding establishing the operation or removal of the scripts. [ 43 ] The new presidential contest was organized through Democratic and Republican party groups. Instructions published on 16 August called for party membership, meetings and debates, neutral moderators and the selection of three candidates from each party. Candidates were also required to provide running-mate information. The process sought to restore a structured election after the competing presidential claims of July, with parties serving as the mechanism for choosing a field of candidates. [ 44 ] The results announced on 26 August gave the Marinio–Lumidas ticket 163 votes, ahead of Brian987987–RodgerDodger with 63. The remaining tickets received much smaller totals. Nightgaladeld identified Marinio and Lumidas as the winners and said further instructions would follow. The result announcement was followed the same day by a first-week agenda signed by Marinio as president and Lumidas as vice president. The precise date of the oath ceremony is uncertain. [ 6 ] Reconstruction under Marinio, August–December 2013 Government recruitment and congressional elections Marinio's reconstruction program emphasized staffing, elections and the relationship between agencies and the capital. His campaign had promised regular congressional elections, constitutional judicial appointments, a complete cabinet, stronger enforcement of rights and additional cities. It also proposed applications across government and a work-permit system for police. Marinio defended his conduct during the ownership crisis by saying that he and other officials had remained to preserve institutions. That explanation was part of his campaign account; his subsequent administration placed recruitment and reorganization at the center of its announced agenda. [ 45 ] The first-week agenda proposed a police education and work-permit scheme involving Labor and Education. It concentrated the active Washington agencies on the Secret Service, Homeland Security and Capitol Police and called for officer testing. The proposed division between recruitment, training and field service sought to make agency employment more systematic. It was an announced program, and its full implementation across the agencies is uncertain. [ 46 ] Congressional elections followed. Applications announced on 31 August distinguished Democratic and Republican affiliation, restricted alternate accounts and specified campaign conduct. The procedure also addressed eligibility for directors and deputies and directed submissions to a designated election account. For that contest, one senator and four representatives were to be elected. The ballot published the same day permitted one Senate vote and one House vote and set a closing time for the following day. [ 47 ] Transport, businesses and access to employment The administration's plans extended beyond office appointments. During the August campaign, Marinio described inspecting Washington with Lumidas and considering a Department of Transportation station. Subsequent planning mentioned buses, the restoration of transport activity, bail and the use of money within the city. These proposals treated the capital as a place requiring services and circulation as well as government headquarters. The proposed station and bus network awaited implementation. [ 48 ] Affordability became another issue in government recruitment. In November, Marinio proposed protection for applicants who could not afford required uniforms. The proposal was explicitly linked to Roblox's clothing price floor and differences in the income available to paid and unpaid members. It sought to prevent inability to buy a uniform from becoming sufficient grounds for refusing employment. The proposal addressed a material barrier to agency employment; its passage is uncertain. [ 49 ] In his half-term report on 1 November, Marinio presented reconstruction, an operating Congress and checks and balances as achievements of the administration. He also referred to an alliance with Italy and departmental reform, while announcing further work concerning the military, businesses, the United Nations, the judiciary and the Constitution. His estimate that reconstruction was largely complete was an assessment of his own administration, rather than a measured national indicator. The breadth of the report nevertheless reflected an agenda that joined institutional recovery to public commerce, diplomacy and military organization. [ 50 ] Departmental reform and limits on presidential authority Departmental reform brought the president into disagreement with those controlling the capital's development. On 4 November, Marinio said that his Federal Department Reform had been cancelled after developers and Nightgaladeld opposed changes to Washington's teams. The dispute concerned the extent to which reorganizing government departments also required changing the way agencies were represented within the city. [ 51 ] A second-reading proposal later that day separated administrative departments from the field agencies represented by teams. It allowed academies and tryouts for agency recruitment, dropped the original education scheme and proposed removing a Secret Police group which the president regarded as unofficial. The revised proposal attempted to accommodate the practical distinction between a government's organizational chart and the agencies available in Washington. Its publication after the cancellation statement leaves the final extent of the reform uncertain. [ 52 ] Contested removal and Lumidas's succession Marinio's presidency ended in a contested removal on 30 December. In a statement that day, he identified himself as a former president, said that he had been impeached and criticized Congress's conduct and the Chief Justice's absence. He also announced another presidential campaign. His statement supplies the date of the removal dispute, while the precise congressional instrument and grounds are uncertain. [ 53 ] On 2 January 2014, Marinio argued that the trial had violated the Constitution because the Chief Justice had not presided. He said that Nightgaladeld had declined to restore him because Lumidas had already been sworn in, and claimed that he was entitled to resume office. Lumidas's separate statement the same day recognized his own succession from the vice presidency and the selection of former Speaker Aerium as vice president. The dispute continued over the validity of the removal. [ 54 ] Government and cities, 2014–2015 Agency personnel in a historical gameplay image identified by Josh as dating from 2014. Josh uploaded it on 24 December 2024 at 11:51 p.m.; the capture date and photographer are unidentified. By early 2014, nUSA's federal administration was combining elections and public-service recruitment with development of multiple cities. Lumidas 's January transition announcement marked the beginning of a new administration. He established academy-based recruitment for agencies and a Commission of Academies, while allowing agency directors to approve exceptions. A contemporary employment directory listed law enforcement, intelligence, Congress, C-SPAN, NASA, military, labor, commerce, treasury and technology offices, with entry routes including academies, interviews and tryouts. [ 24 ] The administration also sought to establish civilian and military institutions. Congressional notices in January listed a bill on Defense Logistics Agency organization, but later executive action ordered that agency closed, citing the approval of two competing groups and uncertainty over director authority. The sequence illustrates the difference between legislative approval notices and an agency's continued operation. In February, election instructions issued by Federal Election Commission chairman Marinio described voter registration, one unchangeable vote, restrictions on alternate accounts, and a forum ballot. [ 55 ] In February 2014, Nightgaladeld congratulated Zeyad and Suddenrush on winning an election, while also referring to unrest in the rebuilt Washington and police-abuse reports in Washington and New York. By July, White House rules specified Secret Service escort authority and conditions for visitors holding access passes, reflecting the development of access and security procedures around executive settings. [ 56 ] Aerium's administration and the January 2015 transition The later 2014 administration of Aerium addressed the limits of intelligence collection, the organization of protective services, and electioneering by federal employees. One order allowed citizens and foreign nationals to withdraw consent for agencies to retain their information, requiring removal within seven days. It exempted anonymous analytical programs, targeted programs personally approved by the President and Vice President, and surveillance legally authorized by a federal judge. The distinction between general recordkeeping and specifically authorized surveillance became part of the administration's stated privacy policy. [ 57 ] Aerium also ordered the Federal Protective Service recognized as an official agency within Homeland Security following the shutdown of Special Forces. The order directed the transfer of non-abusive Special Forces personnel under the National Security Advisor's supervision. Its preamble acknowledged disagreement over whether Congress had approved the service, and Aerium cited a statement by Speaker Jcmand supporting executive recognition of agencies. The reorganization therefore involved both personnel and a dispute about the respective authority of the President, Congress and judiciary. [ 58 ] On 9 November 2014, Aerium imposed stricter restrictions on campaign advertising through federal agency walls and agency teams. The order prescribed dismissal for prohibited advertising, while limiting who could impose the punishment and requiring evidence to be available for review. An official unable to supply that evidence could face dismissal and the reinstatement of the affected employee. Private requests for political support remained permissible; government Skype rooms and unsolicited mass campaign chats received separate rules. Vice President Pathwaysbball and Speaker Jcmand endorsed the order. These provisions show that campaigning, workplace discipline and communication platforms were already closely connected before Discord became a principal national archive. [ 59 ] Pathwaysbball subsequently became President. His January 2015 reelection campaign ended in withdrawal rather than a renewed term. In a statement on 19 January, he acknowledged reduced activity during his final weeks, explained that outside commitments prevented him from sustaining the required participation, and endorsed Jcmand. He also praised his military administration's reconstruction work. The statement is an early example of a President explicitly connecting withdrawal to the time demands of office, even while elections and other government institutions continued to operate. [ 60 ] Development of Washington and Las Vegas Las Vegas emerged as a separate city setting before its main group-associated asset was created. Roblox metadata dates a Pauljkl-authored predecessor place to 17 September 2013 and the main group-associated place to 28 June 2014. A June 2014 police guide identified Pauljkl as city creator and police chief and described ranks, internal affairs and specialized divisions. The next day, moderator Verbero announced a planned removal of Pauljkl and the Las Vegas place, citing alleged misconduct; Pauljkl disputed the explanation, and other members objected to separating the city from nUSA. The notice set 4 July as a proposed removal date, but that outcome is uncertain. The date of the city's public opening is uncertain. [ 61 ] Washington underwent a rebuild in early 2014. A March petition asked for the former city to return, citing broken purchased passes and dissatisfaction with the replacement. Nightgaladeld replied that the new Washington was a beta and that earlier features were being transferred. In June, the founder announced planned in-game-money car and gun shops in the new city, while a July post reported that Las Vegas purchases were failing after a platform update and that the product had been disabled. Washington and Las Vegas continued to develop as separate cities; the date of the earlier Washington rebuild is uncertain. [ 62 ] Las Vegas and Washington developed as connected but distinct civic settings. A March 2015 statement described Las Vegas and Washington as already existing and Miami and New York as under development, without documenting the completion of the latter two. Game passes, in-game purchases and city-specific services linked municipal life to Roblox commerce. [ 3 ] Nightgaladeld announced Jcmand and Lumidas as winners after excluding invalid ballots: Jcmand received 298 valid votes, SuddenRush 280, and Smoothie71 227. Pathwaysbball withdrew and endorsed Jcmand. In a separate dispute, Nightgaladeld said that Jcmand and Economic would not face fraud charges for promoting immigrants contrary to an election rule; affected ballots were excluded and ranks reverted. The notice records a decision not to charge the candidates, rather than a finding of fraud. [ 63 ] The new administration reorganized federal offices through executive orders. Jcmand's first order abolished several departments and agencies, placed Special Forces in domestic law enforcement, and assigned the Office of Management and Budget to the Executive Office of the President. A subsequent order described executive and employment authority for the Vice President. The orders changed the departments and agencies named in the federal structure. [ 64 ] The Las Vegas Strip, including the Luxor complex. The capture date and photographer are unidentified. Municipal lawmaking and everyday services The Las Vegas City Council made local services and access rules subjects of lawmaking. Its process treated development as a second stage after a bill's vote: measures could enter an update queue managed by the city's developer, while the Development Council held separate approval and veto authority. In 2015, proposals and completed development records addressed housing customization, ATMs for deposits and withdrawals, and police entry to the casino for enforcement. The casino measure allowed officers carrying enforcement equipment to enter without a pass while barring them from gambling. The city process took ideas through a bill and council vote; approved developments entered an update queue and were moved to a finished list when built. These measures tied everyday infrastructure and policing to the elected municipal government. [ 65 ] The council's authority also faced a proposed federal reorganization. In May, the Senate Advancement Caucus proposed dissolving it and replacing it with a Nevada government. Pauljkl and municipal representatives opposed the change, while KOTwarrior noted that the proposal had not passed the House. A September debate then addressed the council's combined legislative and development role: Pauljkl said agencies seeking teams first went to Congress for approval, while critics questioned developers' influence over municipal decisions. The disputes exposed a recurring separation between elected authorization and control of implementation. [ 66 ] Mayoral elections supplied another measure of local participation. Bailey552 won 289 of 554 votes in August 2015, and Flammus won 217 of 471 votes in November. The campaigns preceded the city's more detailed 2018 charter and show that municipal offices were contested before the later charter standardized terms and appointments. [ 67 ] See also: Las Vegas City Council Private enterprise and the boundary between government and founder management also entered public debate. Nightgaladeld announced a Founders Private Intelligence Agency in March 2015, describing it as a private organization outside government reporting requirements and planning a Washington team. [ 68 ] Emperorlol01 with a City Council title, in a screenshot he identifies as taken in 2015. Screenshot credited to and uploaded by Emperorlol01 on 22 August 2025 at 7:09 p.m. [ 69 ] Washington in an image identified by J_B as dating from 2015. Uploaded by J_B on 16 February 2021 at 4:55 p.m. [ 70 ] Federal reorganization under SuddenRush12G, 2016–2017 SuddenRush12G being inaugurated for his second term as President of the United States. SuddenRush12G 's presidency, which began in January 2016, brought a broad reorganization of the executive branch, security services and public employment. Before his inauguration, the State Department had described ambassador appointments, reporting and normalization with the United Kingdom and Russia. In April, an executive order regulated private businesses through Commerce and the Small Business Administration; a separate courthouse hub and national-security council appeared as proposals, but their opening and passage were not confirmed. [ 71 ] His opening executive order abolished the Department of Education, its academies and universities commissions, the Securities and Exchange Commission, and the Department of Housing and Urban Development. A second order, the “One USA Order,” barred executive employees from holding citizenship in another United States government and gave current staff 24 hours to renounce such affiliation or face dismissal. Both measures sought to consolidate federal service under a single national government. [ 72 ] In February, SuddenRush12G nominated NorthFuze to the Supreme Court; the President announced Senate confirmation on 27 February. In March he nominated TimGeithner , describing him as a constitutionalist with political experience, but that announcement did not confirm Senate action. By May, he said that he had appointed five justices and again called on Congress to replace inactive judges. The appointments and vacancies made judicial staffing part of the administration's early program. [ 73 ] The administration imposed detailed controls on sensitive offices and facilities. A 26 January prison-clearance order divided access among Justice officials, investigators, local emergency services, intelligence agencies and protective details, with visitor, road and airspace restrictions around the federal prison. In February, SuddenRush12G dissolved the Federal Intelligence Agency, citing repeated misconduct, and required presidential access to executive branch communication rooms, documents and boards. The order dissolving the FIA presented misconduct as the administration's reason for the action; it was not a judicial finding against individual members. [ 74 ] An attempt to expand the White House chief of staff's powers lasted two days. An order of 20 February authorized the chief of staff to supervise and discipline executive personnel, demand reports, audit departments and impose employment blacklists, while keeping the office outside presidential succession and subject to presidential removal. On 22 February SuddenRush12G revoked the order after opposition that it concentrated too much authority in one official. He described the proposal as an effort to maintain continuity during his absences, acknowledged public resistance and appointed a new chief of staff. The reversal became a visible instance of executive policy being withdrawn after public criticism. [ 75 ] Executive employment became a prominent area of policy. A March order permitted citizens with six months' standing to petition for the removal of an executive officer; a petition with 75 qualifying signatures could lead to removal with presidential approval. Agency heads were also required to explain an employee's dismissal upon request. A separate order directed executive officers to carry out court arrest orders, while limiting the use of arrest teams bearing that designation in nUSA cities. These rules connected public petitions and judicial directives to executive personnel practice. [ 76 ] A separate March statement invited public comment on the Special Forces' leadership after SuddenRush12G cited petitions and complaints about its direction. He asked whether its commanders should be replaced but did not announce a dismissal in that statement. [ 77 ] The administration also created the Diplomat

text: hopp_fr 44th President of nUSA (NARA roster) In office 11 January 2022 – 8 July 2022 [ 1 ] Preceded by TacticalRock101 Succeeded by Bakedgoods NARA Presidential Records roster hopp_fr is listed in the National Archives and Records Administration's presidential roster as the 44th President of the nUSA . Before that presidency, the Federal Election Commission certified him as the vice-presidential running mate on TacticalRock101's 2021 presidential ticket. The reviewed roster and Discord archive do not establish the dates or circumstances of his later presidential term. [ 2 ] 2021 presidential election The Federal Election Commission's Fall 2021 ballot listed TacticalRock101 and hopp_fr as the Independent ticket. Voting was scheduled for November 15–16, with results due November 18 and an inauguration scheduled for November 21. [ 3 ] In a November 16 certification letter, National Elections Administrator largeTitanic2 reported 304 votes, of which 47 were disqualified, and certified TacticalRock101 as President-elect. The letter said the President-elect had submitted hopp_fr as his vice-presidential candidate under the Twelfth Amendment, and declared hopp_fr vice-President-elect, with inauguration planned for November 21. A separate Discord announcement confirmed TacticalRock101's inauguration on that date; the reviewed announcement did not independently confirm hopp_fr's oath. [ 4 ] Presidency The NARA roster places hopp_fr after TacticalRock101 as the 44th President and before Bakedgoods as the 45th. Its entry gives no term dates, election result, Vice President, executive actions, legislation, or reason for departure. The reviewed Discord exports contain no contemporaneous account of the 44th administration, so the roster order alone is not used to infer a term start or end date. title: House of Representatives (nUSA)
text: Lower chamber in the federal legislature The House of Representatives is the lower chamber of Congress . Its members conduct legislative business, organize committees, investigate public affairs and initiate impeachment proceedings. The chamber is led by the Speaker , with majority and minority leadership and parliamentary officers supporting its work. [ 1 ] Membership and organization The nUSA House chamber in May 2025. The screenshot labels GatoGaviria as Speaker and Captaina_Nico as Clerk. The House has used a twenty-member arrangement divided into two electoral classes, with alternating two-month terms. Chamber size and electoral arrangements have changed across constitutional periods; the temporary reconstruction elections of 2022 instead provided sixteen seats. [ 2 ] House organization includes the Speaker, majority and minority leaders and whips, the Clerk and Parliamentarian. Its committees have covered the judiciary, government oversight, foreign affairs, homeland security and armed services, rules and ethics, and intelligence. Assignments and committee structures are subject to the rules of the relevant chamber and session. [ 3 ] Recorded proceedings In November 2017, the House rejected a proposed declaration of war against North Korea, and President SheldonParty suspended the military effort. In July 2018, a Judiciary Committee impeachment measure against BernardCaldwell advanced to the chamber, which passed it for Senate consideration. [ 4 ] Standing rules govern proceedings alongside parliamentary officers and committee organization. Proposed legislation moves through committee and floor consideration and, where applicable, to the Senate and President. Internal leadership elections and ordinary lawmaking are distinct parts of chamber business. [ 5 ] Constitutional and records changes The July 2023 reset voided existing federal laws, case precedent and congressional resolutions, motions and awards. A new Constitution and legislative directives followed on 17 July, allowing Congress to resume normal business. The transition changed the operative legal framework while leaving earlier House proceedings part of the nation's history. [ 6 ] The ninety-eighth Congress began on 19 August 2024. NARA required accurate session labels on bills and warned that incorrectly labeled measures would not be archived. This requirement concerned preservation of legislative records, rather than the passage or rejection of a bill. [ 7 ] Reconstruction and the reform of parliamentary work The 2022 reconstruction placed the House at the center of efforts to renew government. Speaker MasonRockefeller invited citizens into discussions of constitutional rewriting, recruited staff for leadership and committee offices, and urged participation while national activity was low. On 25 April, Congress entered a constitutional convention scheduled to continue until 31 May, following concurrent resolutions and Supreme Court consent. [ 8 ] August's interim election schedule called for sixteen representatives and the replacement of the entire chamber. By November, vacancies again posed a practical problem: Rockefeller reported eight open seats and sought special elections. The need to fill those seats accompanied his efforts to make attendance and personal service meaningful obligations of membership. [ 9 ] [ 10 ] On 9 November, the House adopted Rockefeller's proposed standing rules. They reorganized committees, clarified leadership duties, established a legislative process, and set standards of member conduct and activity. The reforms also allowed educational initiatives such as tours and internships. Rockefeller's preceding proposals had emphasized limiting absences and tightening proxies so that elected members normally represented their constituents themselves. [ 11 ] Investigations and judicial independence The House's investigatory authority had generated an earlier constitutional dispute in Hudson v. House of Representatives . A committee subpoenaed three federal judges, then rescinded the subpoenas before the Supreme Court intervened. The Court denied review on 25 June 2019. In a nonbinding concurrence, Bork and Chase warned that questioning judges in response to their rulings could exceed a legitimate legislative purpose. The denial left that broader question unresolved rather than affirming the original subpoenas. title: Hudson v. House of Representatives (nUSA)
text: 2019 subpoena dispute and nonbinding concurrence on judicial independence Hudson v. House of Representatives Supreme Court of the United States Full case name RS_Hudson et al. v. House of Representatives Docket 07–20 Decided 25 June 2019 Disposition Petition for review denied Separate opinion Bork, joined by Chase, concurring in denial Subject Congressional subpoenas to judges Precedential status No merits holding on subpoena constitutionality Hudson v. House of Representatives , No. 07–20, was a dispute over subpoenas issued by a House committee to three federal judges. The Supreme Court denied review on 25 June 2019 after the House rescinded the subpoenas. Justice Bork, joined by Justice Chase, wrote a concurrence questioning the constitutionality of compelling judges to answer congressional inquiries in response to their rulings. The Court did not decide that constitutional question on the merits. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] Background and disposition The petition challenged a committee's use of subpoenas against judicial officers. By the time of the Court's disposition, the House had unilaterally rescinded them. Bork regarded further intervention as unnecessary and concurred in denial. He nevertheless cautioned that the denial should not be understood as endorsing the subpoenas' original legality. [ 3 ] The case therefore ended without an order compelling or prohibiting judicial testimony. Its importance lies in the constitutional reasoning offered by two justices and in the distinction between the end of a dispute and a final resolution of the legal question it raised. [ 4 ] Bork's concurrence Bork treated congressional subpoena power as implied from the Necessary and Proper Clause and limited by a legitimate legislative purpose. He examined three possible justifications for subpoenas issued in response to judicial rulings: lawmaking, impeachment and Congress's informing function. He found none sufficient in the circumstances he considered. [ 5 ] For lawmaking, Bork argued that courts ordinarily explain their interpretations in written opinions. Congress could amend legislation, and parties could seek appellate review, but Congress lacked a proper purpose in demanding additional explanations from judges about their interpretive process. The extent of an opinion's explanation was itself part of the judiciary's exercise of power. [ 6 ] For impeachment, he invoked Cursive v. United States and the principle that Congress could not use impeachment in retaliation for judicial acts. For the informing function, he emphasized the independence of Article III courts and rejected extending an agency-based rationale to inquiries into judges' decisions. Those conclusions supported his skepticism toward ruling-responsive subpoenas, rather than a general prohibition on every conceivable congressional inquiry involving a judge. [ 7 ] Significance and limits The concurrence linked the House's investigative powers with the broader struggle over separation of powers in 2019. It furnished a reasoned statement in defense of judicial independence, but Bork acknowledged that full adversarial proceedings might reveal a justification he had not considered. He left a future case to decide whether such subpoenas should be held unconstitutional. [ 8 ] Neither the denial nor the concurrence established a binding merits rule. The case is consequently best understood as an important judicial statement accompanying an unresolved constitutional question, distinct from the definitive invalidations in In re Federal Government and Party v. Board of Law Examiners . [ 9 ] External links Denial of review and concurrence ↑ RS_Hudson v.
