title: Impeachment of Procursive
text: 2019 impeachment, removal and constitutional review of President Procursive The impeachment of Procursive was a confrontation between the presidency and Congress that ended in the President's removal from office in 2019. The House unanimously adopted four articles on 31 March, and the Senate subsequently convicted him on all four. Procursive challenged the result before the Supreme Court . On 7 May, the Court invalidated three articles but upheld the remaining charge, leaving his removal in force. [ 1 ] The case brought two questions into direct conflict: how far Congress could go in removing a President, and how far the judiciary could go in reviewing that removal. Procursive won significant parts of his constitutional challenge without recovering the presidency. The Senate had declined to disqualify him from future office, so the judgment sustained his removal rather than a permanent prohibition on public service. [ 2 ] A presidency under pressure Procursive entered office after Dralian declined to assume another term. His experience lay chiefly in the Secret Service, which he had directed before becoming Dralian's running mate. Once President, he encountered congressional opposition and secured confirmation of Bakedgoods as Vice President, but his relationship with Congress soon deteriorated. [ 3 ] Around 23 March, the House Foreign Affairs Committee opened an investigation into allegations that people connected with the administration's intelligence community had participated in denial-of-service attacks and the exposure of private information. The committee subpoenaed Procursive. He invoked executive privilege and declined to testify. The inquiry was followed by allegations that he had employed his cousin on his Secret Service detail and endangered national security by hiring JamesMontagu in the White House. Those allegations joined an older accusation of false arrest from his law-enforcement service. [ 4 ] Articles of impeachment Article Allegation Supreme Court disposition 1 False arrest, arising from conduct before the presidency Upheld; removal remained in force 2 Withholding information from Congress Invalidated 3 Violation of an anti-nepotism statute Invalidated 4 Jeopardizing national security by employing JamesMontagu Invalidated The House's unanimous vote on 31 March sent all four articles to the Senate. The charges combined an alleged criminal act with objections to presidential secrecy and appointments. That distinction became central to the eventual judicial decision: the Court rejected the latter three articles because they did not allege legitimate criminal offenses under the impeachment standard it applied. [ 5 ] The withdrawn resignation During the confrontation, Procursive attempted to resign with effect at midnight and then withdrew the resignation before that time. A challenge to the withdrawal reached the Supreme Court in Psychodynamic v. Procursive , also styled Dynamic v. Cursive . The Court denied review on 4 April. [ 6 ] Justices Pitney and Chase, joined by Stewart, Brandeis and Douglas, issued a statement defending the distinction between an announced resignation and one that had already taken effect. They reasoned that a resignation could be withdrawn before its effective time but could not be recalled after it had become final. Their statement accompanied a denial of review; it did not constitute a binding judgment on the merits. Procursive's departure therefore cannot be understood simply as an uncontested voluntary resignation. [ 7 ] Senate trial and removal Chief Justice Holmes convened the Senate to receive the articles. House managers presented them, and senators took an oath or affirmation of impartiality. The chamber then adjourned to give the prosecution and defense time to prepare. At trial, both sides made opening statements and examined evidence. Time constraints led the Senate to dispense with closing statements; attempts to shorten the defense's allotted time were not allowed. [ 8 ] The Senate convicted Procursive on every article and removed him, while declining to impose disqualification from future office. Procursive had not obtained a pre-emptive judicial stay preserving his position during review. Bakedgoods was exercising the presidency by 6 April, when he issued an executive-branch employee-database memorandum. [ 9 ] [ 10 ] Constitutional review Main article: Cursive v. United States (nUSA) The Supreme Court heard argument on 17 April and decided the case on 7 May. Procursive challenged the fairness of the Senate trial, the validity of congressional oaths and the substance of each article. The Court rejected the oath challenge for lack of sufficient evidence. It also rejected his due-process argument, explaining that impeachment did not require all the procedures of an ordinary criminal trial and that the Senate's process had been constitutionally adequate. [ 11 ] The Court nevertheless subjected the charges themselves to review. Under its Ichigo precedents, an impeachable high crime or misdemeanor had to qualify at least as a crime or misdemeanor. Articles 2, 3 and 4 failed that standard; the information-withholding article also raised questions of executive privilege. Article 1 survived. The Court did not categorically exclude misconduct predating the presidency from impeachment and found no sufficient basis for closer scrutiny of Congress's motives in this instance. [ 12 ] The justices disagreed over the proper reach of judicial intervention. Brandeis would have abandoned the Ichigo standard and confined review to narrow circumstances involving separation of powers. Other separate opinions disputed the treatment of Article 1 and the meaning of high crimes and misdemeanors. The final result combined a substantial rebuke to Congress's charging decisions with the survival of its most consequential action: removing the President. [ 13 ] Historical significance The impeachment demonstrated that a congressional conviction could survive even when most of its supporting articles were unconstitutional. It also made Anytime Review an important instrument in the struggle between Congress and the presidency. Those decisions belong to the constitutional order preceding the 2023 legal reset , which later voided existing case law and precedent; their historical significance should be distinguished from their continuing legal force. title: In re Federal Government (nUSA)
text: 2019 decision invalidating the State of Columbia's governing framework In re Federal Government Supreme Court of the United States Consolidated case Kirkman v. State of Columbia, et al. Dockets 07–01 and 07–02 Decided 3 March 2019 Proceeding Anytime Review, including Court-initiated review Opinion Per curiam Holding Sections 101–104 of S. 127 unconstitutional; sections 106–107 inseverable and invalid Law applied Constitution, Article IV, Section 3 Subject Municipal consent and severability In re Federal Government , heard with Kirkman v. State of Columbia , was a Supreme Court decision of 3 March 2019 invalidating the principal provisions of S. 127, which sought to combine Washington, D.C. , and Las Vegas into the State of Columbia . The Court held that the merger lacked the constitutionally required consent of both municipal legislatures. It also struck dependent agency-transfer and court provisions because they could not operate independently of the invalid merger. [ 1 ] The per curiam ruling combined a municipal-autonomy holding with a substantial severability analysis. Its remedy preserved some ancillary provisions while preventing the proposed state from acquiring its governor, transferred agencies and judicial system. The Court also used the case to warn that officials remained bound by constitutional limits even when they anticipated judicial restraint. [ 2 ] Background Congress passed S. 127 as a plan for reorganizing municipal government. The Act asserted a union of Las Vegas and Washington , named the new jurisdiction Columbia, and supplied a provisional governor exercising interim authority. It also provided for agency transfers and a court system. Columbia's creation was publicly announced on 2 March. [ 3 ] [ 4 ] [ 5 ] Article IV, Section 3 prohibited the joining of existing municipalities without the consent of the affected legislatures. The statute relied in part on H.R. 179's supposed demunicipalization of Las Vegas, but the Supreme Court noted that the measure itself referred to Las Vegas as a municipality. The Columbia dispute reached the Court through both Court-initiated review and Kirkman's petition. [ 6 ] Constitutional issue The central question was whether Washington and Las Vegas had consented to the merger. The Court found no record of a vote by either municipality approving the union. It required consent that was clear, public and unambiguous. The possibility that municipal authorities had received notice could not substitute for the affirmative legislative approval required by the Constitution. [ 7 ] The Court did not decide H.R. 179's legality. Even assuming that measure valid, its language did not remove the constitutional problem presented by joining two municipalities without consent. The federal legislature could not circumvent the consent requirement through an unsupported description of Las Vegas's status. [ 8 ] Decision Invalid merger provisions The Court struck sections 101 through 104. Section 101 asserted the merger; section 102 named the jurisdiction and assigned its march and anthem; section 103 declared an intention to establish it swiftly; and section 104 created the provisional government. Each depended on the unlawful union, and the provisional government attempted to transfer the existing municipalities' sovereign powers to a governor they had not authorized. [ 9 ] Severability S. 127 contained a severability clause, expressing Congress's preference that valid portions survive. The Court nevertheless declined to rewrite interdependent provisions to make them workable. A severability clause could guide the remedy but could not require the judiciary to perform legislative reconstruction. [ 10 ] Section 106 required transfers of agencies to Columbia's provisional governor. With the governor's office invalid, the provision had no meaningful use. Section 107 established courts whose appointment system and duties depended on Columbia's institutions and laws. Removing those dependencies would strip the offices of their purpose and redesign the law. Both sections were therefore inseverable and were struck in full. [ 11 ] The effective-date clause, severability clause and section 105 disclaimer concerning development were preserved. They either had no independent operative effect or confirmed the existing position without depending on the unlawful merger. The Court thus invalidated Columbia's governing machinery rather than the whole statute indiscriminately. [ 12 ] Aftermath and significance The ruling ended the statutory framework for Columbia a day after the public creation announcement. pauljkl separately announced its dissolution through founder authority. The judicial decision established the constitutional defect in the merger, while the separate dissolution represented another exercise of authority against the project. [ 13 ] [ 14 ] The Court's concluding warning emphasized that constitutional duties did not depend on whether a court was expected to intervene. Officials could not expand their authority through manipulation of statutory forms. In institutional terms, the case demonstrated both the protection of municipal consent and the reach of Anytime Review in disputes over the structure of government. title: JamesMontagu
text: JamesMontagu 29th President of nUSA In office 21 November 2019 – 21 March 2020 [ 1 ] Preceded by AntonioTRoosevelt Succeeded by Reset4K NARA Presidential Records JamesMontagu was the twenty-ninth President of the United States. He took office on 21 November 2019 after winning the fall election and was succeeded by Reset4K in March 2020. His presidency included a dispute with Russia over California and Alaska, internal-affairs reforms and a brief blacklist that was subsequently overturned. [ 2 ] Earlier office and presidential campaign A February 2019 announcement listed JamesMontagu among the winners of a House candidacy. The results post does not identify his seat or specify how long he served, and the reviewed records do not verify a prior mayoralty, city council seat, or Senate office. [ 3 ] In October 2019, JamesMontagu ran for President as the Constitutionalist Party's candidate. The election announcement listed him as [CON] JamesMontagu, and Discord advertised campaign rallies on October 13 and 15. The Federal Election Commission's October 21 results letter reported 653 votes overall, including 322 for Montagu (11 disqualified), and certified him as the winner. [ 4 ] The certification also recorded a major qualification dispute: it said Montagu was “not disqualified, but declared ineligible” under an injunction, and identified his running mate TomFoley as acting President-elect until Montagu qualified. The archive reviewed here does not include the ruling that resolved the injunction. By November 20, however, a Discord notice announced an inauguration for President-elect Montagu the next evening; a November 21 post advertised his presidency inauguration. These notices establish that his inauguration proceeded, but do not explain the intervening legal or administrative decision. [ 5 ] A message posted on October 23 thanked voters and opened applications for the “Montagu Administration of 2019.” It described the coming term as a chance to change the country's direction and named AcidRaps as chief of staff contact. The archived campaign record does not preserve a fuller platform or a final staff list in that announcement. [ 6 ] Presidency Screenshot of a 9 February 2020 post by JamesMontagu praising the nUSA military, with an image of a Roblox military formation. JamesMontagu (center) standing with two Supreme Court justices, circa 1 March 2020, as identified by the image contributor. The visible in-game labels name Frosty_TheSn0wman (left) and LukeHellner (right). A screenshot supplied for this archive shows a post from the JamesMontagu account dated 9 February 2020. Montagu praised the nUSA military and thanked Secretary of Defense Smallsights and service members. Its attached picture depicts a formation of Roblox characters; the screenshot does not identify the event or location shown. [ 7 ] The Executive Archives records a Senate-confirmed first slate of senior officials. Royalfirel31 was nominated for Secretary of Commerce and Labor on November 21 and confirmed on November 24, 2019; Rualdownload was nominated for Director of National Intelligence on November 21 and confirmed on November 23. King_Bradley and AlphaTrooper05 were nominated to lead the Joint Chiefs of Staff on November 21 and confirmed two days later. Other records list later confirmations, including Smallsights as Secretary of Defense in January 2020 and Verzai as Secretary of State in February. [ 8 ] Two executive orders in the Presidential Records board are attributed to Montagu. Executive Order 29-001 established the Bureau of Internal Affairs after the Office of Government Ethics closed. The 11-page order described the bureau as an executive-branch oversight and investigative body for employee compliance, ethics, and alleged crimes, with limits on its authority. Executive Order 29-002, dated March 9, 2020, exempted military personnel serving in executive agencies from mandatory events when military service was required during martial law, a state of war, or assistance to an ally. The board now labels both orders “Repealed,” without stating when or why they were repealed. [ 9 ] National Security Presidential Memorandum 004, dated 10 February 2020, imposed a temporary executive hiring freeze through 20 February and required stronger background checks, while allowing individual hiring decisions with White House chief-of-staff approval. Memorandum 005, dated 15 February, directed American forces to intervene in a reported coup in New Zealand and secure Government House. [ 10 ] In legislation, Discord reported that Montagu vetoed the Military Office Expansion Act of 2019 on November 24. A separate notice that day announced his signing of the National Veterans Day Establishment Act. The Public Law Database later indexed a related measure as Public Law 77-1 and marked it repealed. The records reviewed do not establish the date or reason for that repeal. A later House card for the JamesMontagu Legacy Recognition Act is filed under “Rescinded Bills,” so it does not establish an enacted law from his presidency. [ 11 ] Blacklist and end of term Letter dated 17 February 2020 from JamesMontagu to President-elect Reset, offering advice before the transfer of office. JamesMontagu at a podium during Reset4K's inauguration, in a screenshot supplied as an image of his outgoing address. After the election, Montagu sent Reset a White House letter dated 17 February 2020. It offered advice about criticism, choosing trusted advisers, and involving citizens in decisions, and wished the incoming President success. The letter shows Montagu publicly acknowledging the coming transfer of office; it does not establish the exact date he left office. [ 12 ] Montagu participated publicly in the transition at Reset4K's inauguration, where he delivered an outgoing address. The full text of that address remains unspecified. [ 13 ] On January 11, 2020, the Coalition Against Abuse announced that it had blacklisted Montagu and described him as a former President. The next day, founder Pauljkl wrote to Montagu that, after a hearing, Clan Management had revoked the blacklist and that Montagu would serve the remainder of his term. The records therefore document a brief interruption and reversal, not a permanent removal from the presidency. [ 14 ] Montagu ran again in the Winter 2020 presidential election with BernardCaldwell as his running mate. The Federal Election Commission certified Reset3634643 of the Democratic Party as the winner on February 17; its letter reported 277 votes for Reset3634643 and 242 for Montagu before the listed disqualifications. A Discord notice on March 20 scheduled Reset4K's inauguration for the next day, and the NARA roster assigns Reset4K the 30th presidency after Montagu. The same Discord export separately says Technozo would give an inaugural address on March 21, without explaining the occasion. The reviewed records do not include Montagu's resignation or a direct account of the transfer of office, so March 21 is the latest documented boundary for his term, rather than a confirmed time of departure. [ 15 ] The Russian dispute and internal-affairs reform In January 2020, Montagu's administration confronted Russia over claims to California and Alaska. After Russia rejected an American ultimatum, Montagu declared that he had a duty to defend the states. On 14 January, the White House announced a state of war, while Vice President BernardCaldwell reported that both chambers had passed the war resolution. [ 16 ] On 22 January, the administration announced a negotiated peace treaty and stated that Russia had agreed to return the disputed states. It explicitly conditioned the end of the state of war on Senate ratification. The announcement therefore marked a diplomatic agreement awaiting a constitutional step, rather than proving that ratification had already occurred. [ 17 ] [ 18 ] The administration also pursued centralized oversight of federal employment. On 27 February, Montagu issued an order outlining the establishment, duties and jurisdiction of the Bureau of Internal Affairs. A 2 March notice invited complaints about abuse within departments and agencies. The measure placed the bureau within the administration's effort to make internal accountability accessible across institutional boundaries. title: Jcmand
text: Jcmand 9th President of nUSA In office 20 January 2015 – 15 February 2015 [ 1 ] Preceded by Pathwaysbball Succeeded by Lumidas NARA Presidential Records Jcmand was the ninth President of the Roblox nUSA roleplay community. He took office on 20 January 2015 after Pathwaysbball and left the presidency in February, when Lumidas completed the term. Congress impeached and convicted him. His administration issued a series of executive orders that reorganized federal agencies, expanded the Vice President's authority, changed military and intelligence command structures, and created a public process for reviewing alleged abuse by executive employees. [ 2 ] Presidency Jcmand's first orders reshaped the executive branch. On 21 January, he abolished the departments of Energy, the Interior, Agriculture, and Housing and Urban Development, along with the Environmental Protection Agency, the U.S. Trade Representative, and NASA. The same order established the Special Forces as a domestic law-enforcement agency and created an Office of Management and Budget under the Executive Office of the President. A separate order that day designated the Vice President as the executive branch's second-ranking official and authorized the Vice President to dismiss most executive employees below Cabinet rank. [ 3 ] The administration also changed military command. Jcmand established an Office of the Interim Commander in Chief, placed its holder fourth in the presidential line of succession, and gave it authority over the armed forces. The office reported to the presidency, while the Vice President shared the President's commander-in-chief powers. Jcmand appointed Defense Secretary David Billiot to the new role. Another order established Special Source Operations under the Office of the President, set a tiered clearance system, reorganized U.S. Cyber Command, and placed the Special Forces within the Department of Homeland Security. [ 4 ] Jcmand's employment order allowed citizens with at least six months of citizenship to petition for the removal of executive employees. A petition needed 75 valid signatures and was subject to restrictions on eligibility and publicity; the President and Vice President were exempt from removal under the process. Agency heads were also required to give dismissed employees a reason on request. A further order created a five-member Council of Abuse within the Department of Justice and barred the attorney general and other Justice officials from access to its deliberations. Council members reviewed reported cases on a public Trello board; three votes triggered dismissal from all agencies and departments, while suspension could be used for less serious offenses. Jcmand or the Vice President was to review the cases at the end of each week. [ 5 ] His later orders dissolved several entities, including the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency, the Defense Logistics Agency, and the Federal Aviation Administration; moved intelligence research back under the State Department; and transferred local police departments in Las Vegas and Washington, D.C. , out of federal control. A January order also recognized Vendetta as a civil-rights movement group and barred executive employees from arresting its members unless they committed a crime. [ 6 ] Impeachment and succession Jcmand's presidency ended after Congress impeached and convicted him. Lumidas , his Vice President, then completed the remaining portion of the term. Jcmand's later record in the presidential archive preserves eight executive orders from the administration; they document an active effort to alter the size, authority, and internal command of the federal government during his short tenure. title: JoshMiller
text: SpeakerJosh 27th President of nUSA (NARA roster: JoshMiller) In office 21 July 2019 – 29 August 2019 [ 1 ] Preceded by Smallchomama1234 (interim) Succeeded by AntonioTRoosevelt Archived Discord transition notices, 21–22 July 2019 SpeakerJosh (also referred to as Josh in nUSA announcements) is a Roblox account recorded as President of the nUSA roleplay community beginning in July 2019. He was identified as President-elect in June, and a transition post on July 21 said he was expected to be sworn in later that day. By July 22, Josh was issuing presidential announcements. NARA later catalogued the same-period presidency as “JoshMiller, 27th,” with July orders filed under the visually similar “JoshMiIIer” spelling. The chronology and orders strongly associate those archival names with SpeakerJosh, although the sources reviewed do not supply an explicit alias statement or account ID. [ 2 ] Prior office A June 3, 2019 Federal Elections Commission announcement delivered House Class I results to the “outgoing Speaker, @Josh.” Together with the later SpeakerJosh President-elect announcement and July presidential posts, this supports a prior Speaker of the House role for the same 2019 political identity. The export does not preserve a platform account ID linking every display name, so the earlier office is stated from the dated record rather than from a verified account profile. [ 3 ] Election and transition On June 18, 2019, an nUSA update announced that President-elect SpeakerJosh had released applications for the next administration. The attached application described a term scheduled from July 21 through November 21, 2019, and set a five-day application window. It said transition team members would score applications, allowed the team to disqualify applicants, and provided for random extra moderation. This was a published staffing procedure, not a record of who was ultimately selected for each job. [ 4 ] On July 21, a channel post said outgoing President Bakedgoods had resigned, Vice President SmallCho had been sworn in temporarily, and President-elect Josh was expected to take office later that day. The next day, Josh's account announced Executive Order J-001. The archive establishes this handover sequence but does not supply the exact time or text of his oath in the messages cited here. [ 5 ] The campaign and handover appear in the wider record of the 2019 presidential elections (nUSA) . Executive administration In the first weeks of the term, Josh announced a change to White House recruiting: executive-branch applications would use the White House website, with the transition proceeding gradually while question packs were prepared. The announcement said White House intern applications were already available and clarified that recruitment had not stopped. In a separate notice, the White House sought a videographer to create regular communications videos, described as an alternative to relying only on press releases. [ 6 ] The archive records Josh announcing seven medals and an August press statement about executive recruitment. It does not preserve the criteria for the medals or identify the eventual recipients in those posts, so the notices show the actions announced rather than their later effects. [ 7 ] Two July orders are preserved in the NARA presidential archive. J-001, dated July 22, overhauled the executive-branch blacklist process and set out an interim appeal arrangement; its text refers to the “Josh administration.” J-002 addressed removal of NSFW channels and content from executive communications servers. The J-002 PDF header says July 24 while its signature block says July 22; a July 24 Discord message records the President announcing that the order had been signed. These sources establish the orders' text and release notices, but not full enforcement or later effects. [ 8 ] Russia conflict During the Roblox roleplay war with Russia in July 2019, Josh posted that the United States should condemn harassment based on gender, sexuality, race, religion or opinion. A two-page public letter from July 24 framed the conflict as a dispute over United Nations Department of Political Affairs negotiations. In the letter, Josh said the United States had accepted Russia's proposed war terms and submitted parallel terms of its own, but that Russia had rejected the U.S. proposals; these are his administration's claims in the conflict. [ 9 ] On July 27, nUSA announced a 2–0 victory over Russia and Josh posted a statement celebrating it. On August 1, Josh announced a new declaration of war with the United Kingdom against Russia/Soviet Union, and the channel reported that both houses of the United States Congress (nUSA) had passed a declaration of war. The archive therefore records two distinct stages: an announced end to the July conflict and a later campaign for a second one. These were community roleplay events, not real-world military actions. [ 10 ] The application set a planned November 21 end date, but Josh left office earlier, on 29 August 2019. title: Jsjsjbsd
text: jsjsjbsd 59th President of nUSA (NARA roster) In office From 8 June 2026 (accession; oath date uncertain) [ 1 ] Preceded by bathamza Succeeded by Not established NARA Presidential Records roster jsjsjbsd is the fifty-ninth President of the United States. He assumed presidential duties following bathamza 's resignation in June 2026 and won the summer presidential election. His administration consolidated military operations and opposed restrictions on executive appointments through legislative vetoes. [ 2 ] Earlier elections and offices The Federal Election Commission's July 2023 results announcement named jsjsjbsd among six winning Senate candidates. Later in 2023, it included the name among major candidates invited to a November presidential debate. The archive excerpt establishes an invitation, not an election victory in that contest. A separate local ballot placed jsjsjbsd among candidates for a council seat, followed by an ineligibility notice saying the candidate had resigned the candidacy; the two records concern a different election from the presidential debate. [ 3 ] The congressional nominations archive records a passed nomination for jsjsjbsd as Secretary of State. Its card title supports Senate action but does not establish a full tenure. A 2025 concurrent resolution proposed appointment as Auditor General after asserting that the President had not submitted a candidate list within the required window. The attached two-page text sets out a two-month office and investigatory and reporting duties, but it contains a placeholder for the date of presentation and inconsistent resolution labels. The board places the item under Concurrent Resolutions ; without an enactment record, the document should be read as the text of a proposed appointment rather than conclusive proof that jsjsjbsd served the term. [ 4 ] The Senate records board also has archived membership cards for jsjsjbsd. A later passed-nominations card names jsjsjbsd for Vice President. The records consulted here do not give an oath date for that vice presidency or explain how it relates to the subsequent 59th-presidency roster entry. Senate and congressional listings show a multi-office career, but the available cards cannot support an unbroken chronology of service. [ 5 ] Presidency and limits of the record jsjsjbsd succeeded bathamza in June 2026. His administration subsequently issued Executive Order 9 on military consolidation and vetoed S. 1 and S. 2 in July. An invitation scheduled his inauguration ceremony for 22 July, although the exact time of the oath remains unspecified. [ 6 ] The Supreme Court board includes a petition naming jsjsjbsd as respondent in a case brought by Rand0mAxis, and another case filed by jsjsjbsd in an earlier court archive. These docket titles establish litigation involving the account, not the merits or outcomes of the cases. The congressional board also contains a concurrent-resolution card on a congressional gold medal for jsjsjbsd and a failed card proposing removal of one; their titles and list locations do not prove that a medal was awarded or taken away. [ 7 ] June 2026 succession jsjsjbsd at the presidential lectern during an inauguration ceremony. The supplied screenshot does not establish the date. President bathamza 's 8 June 2026 resignation statement named jsjsjbsd as the leader of the next administration. After that day's Senate election result, The War Room reported that Vice President jsjsjbsd had assumed the presidency under the Twenty-fifth Amendment but had not yet been sworn in. N-SPAN described him the following morning as acting President pending an oath. These reports and bathamza's letter establish the announced transition; the reviewed sources do not supply the oath record or exact time at which acting service became a regular presidency. [ 8 ] 2026 presidential election In the Summer 2026 presidential election, jsjsjbsd ran as an independent. The final ballot listed no vice-presidential running mate for the candidacy, although the FEC had earlier announced receipt of a letter naming ZhangJinping. The FEC said it would not add that pick to the ballot and that a Vice President would have to be nominated under law if jsjsjbsd won. One opponent, FuriousTurtle06, withdrew after voting opened; the FEC said voters could not recast ballots. [ 9 ] On 16 July, the National Elections Administrator certified jsjsjbsd as President-elect with 131 votes, ahead of the Pioneer ticket of Epicwarrior_99 and Anthony R. Burgess (114) and the Forward ticket of AguilaBread and EdmundCarter (5). The FEC stated that 297 ballots had been cast and 254 were valid, although the itemized candidate totals sum to 250. The election schedule had set a presidential term from 21 July to 21 November 2026; these are announced term dates, and the reviewed FEC export contains no oath or inauguration report. On 22 July the FEC said a Vice President needed to be nominated but did not name a nominee or record confirmation. A later 14 September notice opened campaigning for the November 2026 election and said that registration and voting dates would follow; the reviewed export includes no result or successor for that race. [ 10 ] The Spring 2026 contest also involved jsjsjbsd as a Forward primary candidate: Warlockings won that primary 22 votes to 18. The FEC later imposed a 45-day blacklist after reporting that two non-citizens had voted in the primary, but on 17 March it announced that a successful appeal reduced the blacklist to one day, already served. The primary investigation and sanction did not disqualify jsjsjbsd from the later Summer presidential race in the records reviewed here. [ 11 ] Military consolidation and legislative vetoes In July 2026, jsjsjbsd ordered a major military reorganization . An order dated 8 July suspended independent Marine Corps and Air Force operations and recruitment, directing Marine personnel into the Army and Air Force personnel into the Navy. Air Force special-operations personnel were assigned to Naval Special Warfare Command. The President announced the measure on 9 July following discussions with military leadership. [ 12 ] [ 13 ] The order preserved transferred personnel's ranks, awards and service records. It also kept the suspended branches in legal existence, permitting their restoration by a later executive order or congressional act. The administration thus concentrated active military operations while protecting both individual standing and the possibility of institutional revival. [ 14 ] On 21 July, jsjsjbsd vetoed S. 1 and S. 2. He objected to S. 1's treatment of public-servant neutrality and to S. 2's restrictions on acting appointments and the filling of vacancies. His veto message characterized both as legislative encroachments on executive authority and stressed the ability to maintain a functioning administration. Those constitutional objections were his stated grounds for rejecting the bills, rather than a Supreme Court judgment on them. [ 15 ] That day's inauguration invitation scheduled a ceremony for 22 July at the Capitol's East Portico. The invitation supplies a planned ceremony date, separate from the electoral term schedule and earlier assumption of presidential duties; it does not establish the precise time the oath was actually administered. title: Jtport
text: Jtport 46th President of nUSA (NARA roster) In office 16 September 2022 – 30 October 2022 [ 1 ] Preceded by Bakedgoods Succeeded by TacticalRock101 NARA Presidential Records roster Jtport was the forty-sixth President of the United States, succeeding Bakedgoods and preceding TacticalRock101 . His presidency included a 2022 impeachment trial ending in acquittal. He also served in the legal profession and judiciary and became National Elections Administrator in June 2025. [ 2 ] Legal service A Supreme Court Bar Membership card states that Jtport was admitted to the bar on February 2, 2021, following two months in the inferior bar and on the recommendation of Justice Barrett. [ 3 ] Presidency Jtport's presidential service fell between Bakedgoods's second administration and TacticalRock101's return to office. The Senate acquitted him on all charges on 22 October 2022, and TacticalRock101 was publicly welcomed as President by 30 October. The exact transition date remains unspecified. [ 4 ] Later service On May 20, 2025, Group Management named Jtport to a three-judge District Court panel convened to decide a dispute over the status of President Rathuzen and the attempted impeachment proceedings. The announcement said the panel would issue a public, binding decision within 72 hours after the case began; it identified Waffles, Jtport, and Moneymack as the judges. [ 5 ] On June 30, 2025, the verified nUSA announcements account said Jtport had been selected as National Elections Administrator. The announcement described him as a jurist of six years' standing and a former President, and said he had the organization's confidence to maintain election integrity. [ 6 ] Impeachment trial and acquittal Jtport's presidency faced an impeachment trial in 2022. On 22 October, aConArtist announced that the Senate had acquitted him on every charge presented to the chamber. The acquittal distinguishes his case from proceedings that ended in removal, including the earlier Procursive impeachment . [ 7 ] [ 8 ] The trial took place amid disputes over Senate procedure and administration. Secretary of the Senate hankwim55 resigned that office in September, alleging improper decisions over committee business, proxies and staffing. He remained a senator for Jtport's trial and announced his resignation from the chamber on 2 November after the proceeding had concluded. His criticism reflected a participant's position, rather than an adjudicated finding against Senate leadership. [ 9 ] By 30 October, Speaker MasonRockefeller was welcoming TacticalRock101 and GameLab as President and Vice President. The sequence establishes that Jtport's acquittal preceded the next administration; acquittal itself was not his removal from office. The preserved trial announcement does not supply the articles or usable individual vote totals, which remain unspecified here. title: Lacryma
text: Lacryma 33rd President of nUSA (NARA roster) In office 16 September 2020 – 21 November 2020 [ 1 ] Preceded by BernardCaldwell Succeeded by ArnieVinick NARA Presidential Records roster Lacryma was the thirty-third President of the United States, succeeding BernardCaldwell in 2020 and followed by ArnieVinick . Compiled presidential histories date the term to 16 September–21 November; contemporary notices identify him as Vice President in July and September and document his later diplomacy and proposed military action against Hawaii. [ 2 ] Vice presidency and succession On 21 July 2020, the public announcement congratulated BernardCaldwell and Lacryma as the new President and Vice President. At a reconciliation event roster posted on 8 September, the executive delegation still listed BernardCaldwell as President and Lacryma as Vice President. The compiled presidency history dates Lacryma's accession to 16 September and says Lacryma finished BernardCaldwell's term, but the reviewed primary Discord and Trello material does not include an accession notice, oath, or explanation for the change. The FEC later certified ArnieVinick as the next President-elect on 11 November; its letter named LordDeathTheReaper as Vice President-elect. The compiled history dates the end of Lacryma's presidency to 21 November, when ArnieVinick's term began. [ 3 ] The related vice-presidential history lists Lacryma as Vice President under BernardCaldwell from 21 July to 16 September 2020, then lists BruceASnyder as Vice President under Lacryma from 24 September to 17 November. That source is an undated compilation and does not explain the gap between 16 and 24 September. Discord independently confirms the Bernard–Lacryma pairing on 21 July and 8 September, but not the later dates or the BruceASnyder appointment. [ 4 ] Legislative and judicial service Records outside the presidency identify Lacryma as a senator and sponsor of Public Law 53-3, the Military Command Act, which granted specified military leaders permission to use the nUSA group shout for recruitment and notices. The Trello entry is catalogued as a public law and names Lacryma as its sponsor; it does not give a sponsorship date in the card text. [ 5 ] During the 2020 presidential sequence, Trello records say Lacryma nominated AlexJCabot as Deputy Attorney General and Archivist of the United States; the cards report Senate confirmations on 28 September and 21 November, respectively. A judiciary-board profile also says Associate Justice SheldonParty (Lacryma) began a second term on 30 October 2020 after Senate confirmation. These are separate appointment and judicial records; the archive does not establish their exact relation to the presidential term beyond the dates stated in those cards. [ 6 ] Diplomacy and the Hawaii dispute Lacryma's public diplomacy included a September 2020 summit with Russia, China and Ghana and a November meeting with Russia's President and delegation. In the latter, he emphasized maintaining relations with the Russian Federation through the approaching change of administration. [ 7 ] The closing days of his presidency also brought a confrontation over Hawaii. On 20 November, Lacryma called for an emergency joint session to authorize military action. He presented Hawaii as American territory under hostile occupation and argued that the armed forces could secure a quick victory. He proposed former President SurpriseParty as military governor, assigning the proposed office responsibility for the imprisonment and trial of the opposing authorities. title: LargeTitanic2
text: LargeTitanic2 is a Roblox nUSA community member documented as an archivist, Clan Manager, and election administrator. A March 2020 retirement letter transferred the National Archives to LargeTitanic2 as Archivist and assigned that office custody of the official version of the nUSA constitution. Later records document separate Clan Management and election-administration appointments, but do not say whether the archival appointment continued through those later roles. [ 1 ] Transfer of the National Archives In the March 2020 letter, the retiring officeholder said the Archives had previously been under Clan Management and were being relinquished from that control to Archivist LargeTitanic2. The letter named LargeTitanic2 and future archivists “Protector of the Constitution” and transferred responsibility for the official constitution version maintained during the author’s archival service. It also requested that the official constitution link be updated on several government boards. This documents a specific custody transfer; the letter does not name NARA or establish a continuous term after the transfer. [ 2 ] Management and election administration A November 2021 public appointment notice says Clan Management approved LargeTitanic2 as a trial Clan Manager with the Founder’s assent. It assigned general Clan Management duties, including oversight of ban moderation and community engagement, and named LargeTitanic2 National Elections Administrator with Federal Elections Commission oversight. The notice establishes those appointments as of that announcement, but says nothing about whether they replaced or overlapped the 2020 archival responsibility. [ 3 ] On 25 January 2025, a verified nUSA announcement said LargeTitanic2 had been selected as National Elections Administrator, with a stated mandate to rebuild a smaller, more streamlined election system for the next-generation game. On 19 March, another verified post announced that they planned to step down to focus on education and work; it opened the NEA position and described the office’s election, verification, and scheduling responsibilities. These notices document a later return to election leadership and a March departure plan, not an uninterrupted term from 2021 or a return to the Archivist office. title: Las Vegas
text: City in Nevada, United States Las Vegas Country United States State Nevada Municipal legislature Las Vegas City Council Principal developer Pauljkl Main city place created 28 June 2014 Las Vegas is a city in Nevada, United States, historically distinguished by its casinos, municipal government, and extensive police and public-service institutions. Developed principally by Pauljkl, it became an important center of civic activity alongside Washington, D.C. . Its economy combined gambling, banking, housing, and the sale of vehicles and weapons, while its government brought elected officials into decisions over both local law and the development of the city. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] The city's history spans an earlier place created in September 2013, the main city place created in June 2014, successive municipal charters, and disputes over the boundary between local, federal, and development authority. In March 2019, the Supreme Court of the United States invalidated legislation that attempted to unite Las Vegas and Washington as the State of Columbia without the consent of their municipal legislatures. Las Vegas subsequently experienced declining activity, followed by revival efforts and commemorative gatherings, including its tenth-anniversary celebration on 28 June 2024. [ 3 ] [ 4 ] [ 5 ] History Early development Pauljkl's earlier Las Vegas place was created on 17 September 2013. By May 2014, he was discussing its development, including problems affecting the movement and replication of automated characters. The main nUSA city place was created on 28 June 2014 under the ownership of the United States group. These two stages account for the city's association with both a 2013 origin and a June 2014 anniversary. [ 3 ] [ 6 ] The transition occurred amid a public dispute over the city's relationship with the federal administration. On 27 June 2014, Verbero announced plans to remove Pauljkl and Las Vegas, alleged misconduct, and promised a replacement Washington city. Pauljkl challenged the allegations and requested a fuller explanation. He also quoted an earlier notice that described retaining funds within the group as a reason for the proposed separation and identified 4 July as the intended removal date. Bailey552 opposed the split, warning that it would damage activity in both Las Vegas and the wider United States. [ 7 ] The main group-owned place was created the following day. Las Vegas subsequently developed an elected municipal government and an expanding range of public services. [ 3 ] [ 2 ] Municipal expansion During the middle of the decade, elected municipal government became an important part of Las Vegas's administration. The Las Vegas City Council considered local laws, public-service arrangements, and changes to the city's infrastructure. Residents could submit ideas for legislation, while approved development measures entered an implementation queue managed by Pauljkl. This gave city politics a direct connection to changes in banking, housing, transport, and access to public facilities. [ 2 ] Mayoral elections attracted substantial participation. In August 2015, Bailey552 won 289 of 554 votes, with an announced term running from 24 August to 24 November. In November, Flammus won 217 of 471 votes; his forthcoming term was announced as 1 December to 1 February. In September 2016, Technozo defeated King_Fruits and AcidRaps with 350 of 733 votes. The differing announced terms preceded the three-month terms prescribed by the 2018 charter. [ 8 ] [ 9 ] [ 10 ] [ 11 ] Municipal institutions also prompted disputes over who should govern the city. In May 2015, the Senate Advancement Caucus proposed dissolving the city council in favor of a Nevada government. Pauljkl and municipal representatives opposed the reorganization. KOTwarrior noted that the proposal had not passed the House, and the council continued to operate. [ 12 ] Charters and constitutional status Mr_Barron's September 2017 charter addressed municipal rights, the limits of federal authority, and powers reserved to the city. Congressional admission legislation subsequently referred to a municipal charter resolution of 10 September 2017 and provided for Las Vegas's admission on an equal footing with other municipalities. [ 13 ] [ 14 ] In April 2018, Pauljkl announced that the city council would be suspended for a single term so that pending bills could be implemented. Elections were expected to resume in July. The interruption reflected a backlog between legislative approval and development, rather than a permanent dissolution of municipal government. [ 15 ] The charter adopted on 30 September 2018 described itself as the city's fourth charter. Prepared principally by FederatedCommander and revised under Mayor Tacus_NOT, it defined the mayor, deputy mayor, council, city attorney, inspector general, police administration, and Development Council. It combined elected institutions with explicit protections for development authority. [ 11 ] The attempted establishment of the State of Columbia brought Las Vegas's status before the Supreme Court in 2019. S. 127 sought to unite Las Vegas and Washington and created associated governmental arrangements. On 3 March, the Court struck down sections 101, 102, 103, 104, 106, and 107. Neither city's legislature had consented to the union, and dependent provisions concerning executive authority, agencies, and courts could not stand. The Court did not determine the validity of H.R. 179, but rejected the argument that its wording had successfully deprived Las Vegas of municipal status. [ 4 ] Decline and later gatherings By late 2019 and early 2020, organized gatherings increasingly sought to restore activity in Las Vegas. On 16 April 2020, management acknowledged that the city was less active and less fully operational than Washington, while emphasizing that it remained an official city subject to the usual community enforcement rules. [ 16 ] President Reset4K promoted a renewed activity campaign in April 2020 and reported seeing Las Vegas Police Department patrols. Restoring activity did not automatically restore elections: Aerium stated on 9 April that the Federal Election Commission would not conduct Las Vegas elections, regardless of a proposed Revival Act, and that municipal elections required the necessary independence to obtain management certification. [ 17 ] Occasional gatherings continued into 2023. In May 2024, UKR41NIAN announced a one-day return and plans for a tenth-anniversary party on 28 June, while stating that casino and gambling content would have to be removed. The anniversary gathering opened on 28 June after an announced delay. Organizers also exempted offenses committed in Las Vegas during the event from prosecution, establishing special conditions for the celebration. [ 18 ] [ 19 ] [ 5 ] [ 20 ] Government Las Vegas's municipal government centered on the mayor and city council. Under the 2018 charter, the mayor was chief executive, responsible for the integrity and effectiveness of municipal operations. Appointments to department leadership and other unelected offices required council approval. The mayor also reported to the council on finances, legal affairs, agency activity, and administrative goals. [ 11 ] The deputy mayor managed day-to-day administrative affairs and served as mayor pro tempore during the mayor's suspension or temporary inability to act. If both mayoral offices became vacant, the council president assumed temporary leadership. The council could impeach the mayor, investigate municipal affairs, approve appointments, and enact local laws. The charter prescribed three-month terms for both mayor and councilors. [ 11 ] Development authority followed a separate structure. A Development Council veto rule took effect on 23 June 2015, and the 2018 charter expressly authorized that body to veto bills. It also required approval of development products and denied the city council authority over the Development Council. Pauljkl was identified as its manager; a membership record also listed Squareheaddude. Consequently, an elected majority could authorize a proposal without ensuring its immediate implementation. [ 21 ] [ 22 ] [ 11 ] [ 2 ] Economy and city life Casinos and nightlife were central to Las Vegas's public identity. The city also offered vehicle and weapon purchases, housing, banking, and employment through public institutions. Its economy therefore brought visitors, residents, merchants, and law-enforcement personnel into the same commercial spaces. [ 1 ] Banking expanded through an ATM measure proposed in May 2015. The proposal sought to make deposits, withdrawals, and transfers available away from the central bank and specifically excluded ATM robbery. The expansion was subsequently marked completed. A housing update proposed the previous month also reached completion. Debate over the proposal considered interior customization alongside more extensive alterations to residential buildings. [ 23 ] [ 24 ] Casino access became a municipal public-safety issue. Bailey552's July 2015 measure allowed officers equipped for enforcement to enter without purchasing the casino pass, while withholding the right to gamble. Its implementation separated access for police duties from access as a customer. [ 25 ] Las Vegas and Washington maintained separate currencies. In December 2017, Pauljkl explained that Las Vegas's casino and the sale of money made a shared currency problematic under his interpretation of Roblox's rules. The separation limited the financial integration of the two cities even while they belonged to the same federal system. [ 26 ] Transport and public services Transport development included buses, airport connections, and changes to private vehicles. A Department of Transportation bus proposal in October 2016 was completed. A further Bus Service measure passed 5–0–0 in March 2017 and envisaged stops planned with the mayor and a bus developed by Tremolo. Its service team was subsequently recorded as completed. [ 27 ] [ 28 ] Airport destinations were expanded through a measure debated in September and October 2016. Technozo proposed links to development and election locations; Los Angeles was added during revision. The measure passed and the development was completed, connecting municipal transport with both civic participation and the development of other locations. [ 29 ] Vehicle systems also changed. By August 2017, Squareheaddude was polling residents about the adoption of WASD driving controls. Earlier that year, a completed measure removed vehicle fuel; Pauljkl justified the change as eliminating server work for a little-used feature. Proposed reuse of gas stations prompted further debate over the city's medical facilities. [ 30 ] [ 31 ] Police, medical care, and prison The Las Vegas Police Department was a major institution from the city's early development. Pauljkl's June 2014 guide identified him as police chief and beccer15 as deputy chief, alongside officers, senior officers, internal-affairs personnel, and division chiefs. By the 2018 charter, municipal police administration was assigned to a sheriff appointed by the mayor with council consent. The sheriff controlled departmental administration and discipline and could appoint an undersheriff. [ 32 ] [ 11 ] Medical provision also changed through municipal action. In 2016, a local emergency medical services team replaced the Department of Health and Human Services. Pauljkl said the department had been given two weeks to improve its activity before the replacement proceeded; participants disputed the quality of service and the relationship between federal and local providers. The completed EMS team marked a shift toward municipal provision. [ 33 ] Las Vegas Prison brought federal security policy into the city's institutional life. On 26 January 2016, President SuddenRush12G issued an order defining agency clearances, supervised visits, guest limits, and restrictions on nearby roads and airspace. The order distinguished access by authorized officials from visits by other persons and imposed conditions on movement around the facility. [ 34 ] See also Las Vegas City Council State of Columbia Washington, D.C. title: Las Vegas City Council
text: Municipal legislature of Las Vegas Las Vegas City Council ( LVCC ) was the municipal legislature of Las Vegas , Nevada. It enacted local laws, scrutinized city administration, approved appointments, and considered changes to public services and infrastructure. Its distinctive combination of legislative and development responsibilities made the council a meeting point between elected government and the people responsible for building and maintaining the city. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] The council's powers evolved through successive charters and disputes over municipal autonomy. Its influence over development was limited by the separate Development Council, which could veto legislation and approve or reject development products. The elected council also faced proposals for federal reorganization, a temporary suspension in 2018, and the attempted incorporation of Las Vegas into the State of Columbia in 2019. [ 3 ] [ 1 ] [ 4 ] History Municipal and development functions By 2015, the council was considering measures affecting housing, banking, and access to the casino. Its work extended beyond regulating conduct: it could also request changes to the facilities and services available in Las Vegas. The council's procedure allowed ideas from residents and councilors to become bills, followed by a vote and, where development was required, entry into Pauljkl's update queue. Completed work was incorporated into the city and moved into the finished stage. [ 2 ] [ 5 ] [ 6 ] This arrangement produced recurring arguments over the proper scope of municipal government. In May 2015, the Senate Advancement Caucus proposed dissolving the council in favor of a Nevada government. Pauljkl and municipal representatives opposed the change, while KOTwarrior noted that it had not passed the House. The proposal exposed a disagreement over whether Las Vegas should retain its own legislature or be reorganized under a broader state structure. [ 7 ] In September 2015, further debate addressed the council's combined lawmaking and development role. Pauljkl defended that combination and explained that agencies requesting teams were first directed to Congress for approval. Other participants criticized the influence of developers over municipal decisions. The disagreement concerned both the council's responsibilities and the limits of its ability to direct implementation. [ 8 ] Charter development and suspension The September 2017 charter addressed municipal rights and reserved powers. Congressional legislation admitting Las Vegas as a municipality referred to a charter resolution of 10 September and provided for its admission on equal terms with other municipalities. [ 9 ] [ 10 ] On 18 April 2018, Pauljkl announced that there would be no council for a single term, allowing developers to catch up with bills that had remained pending. He expected the next council elections in mid-July. The interruption illustrated a practical weakness of the council's development role: passing measures could generate obligations more quickly than those measures were completed. [ 11 ] The fourth city charter, adopted on 30 September 2018 under Mayor Tacus_NOT, set out a detailed legislative and administrative framework. FederatedCommander was its principal author, with contributions from Tacus_NOT, Nermonile, and former mayor Mr_Barron. The charter vested municipal legislative power in the council while protecting the separate authority of the Development Council. [ 1 ] Columbia and later election disputes The attempted creation of the State of Columbia made municipal consent a constitutional issue. S. 127 sought to combine Las Vegas and Washington , but neither municipal legislature consented. On 3 March 2019, the Supreme Court invalidated the union and related provisions. The judgment established that Congress could not accomplish the proposed consolidation while bypassing the legislatures of the affected municipalities. [ 4 ] Declining activity later complicated efforts to revive municipal government. In April 2020, Aerium stated that the Federal Election Commission would not conduct Las Vegas elections, regardless of a proposed Revival Act, and that management would not certify municipal elections lacking the required independence. Renewed city gatherings therefore did not, by themselves, resolve the arrangements for electing a council. [ 12 ] Composition and elections Council membership was not constant throughout its history. An August 2018 election announcement offered seven seats. The September 2018 charter specified eight members, excluding the mayor, deputy mayor, and serjeant at arms, and prescribed election from districts or wards. It set councilor terms at three months. These were distinct dated arrangements rather than a single unchanging system. [ 13 ] [ 1 ] Council and mayoral contests were conducted separately. In June 2017, mayoral nominations required a ballot thread supported by 30 signatures; mayoral voting opened on 17 June and councilor voting on 26 June. Election announcements directed voters to the dedicated municipal election location. [ 14 ] The council President kept the journal of proceedings and, under the 2018 charter, was responsible for weekly releases describing measures that had passed, failed, or awaited a vote. The office also had a role in executive succession: if both mayor and deputy mayor resigned, the President became mayor pro tempore pending new mayoral elections. [ 1 ] Powers and procedure Legislation and oversight The 2018 charter authorized the council to adopt local laws consistent with the city charter and the Constitution of the United States, provide for their enforcement, and investigate municipal affairs through the council or its committees. Votes on final passage were recorded by ayes and noes. The charter required a mayoral or deputy-mayoral signature before a local law was deemed adopted. [ 1 ] The council also exercised substantial administrative oversight. Mayoral appointments to department leadership and other unelected offices required its approval. It could approve the filling of council vacancies, impeach the mayor after charges and an opportunity for a defense, and suspend the mayor while charges were pending. The city attorney was appointed with its advice and consent, and removal of that officer required impeachment by a council majority. [ 1 ] The charter's voting provision referred to a majority affirmative vote of six council members, alongside its specification of eight council seats. Earlier measures used different recorded voting totals; the March 2017 Bus Service proposal, for example, passed 5–0–0. Voting practice thus differed between the earlier council and the framework prescribed in 2018. [ 1 ] [ 15 ] Relationship with the Development Council The Development Council was distinct from the elected city council. Its veto rule took effect on 23 June 2015. The 2018 charter authorized it to veto any bill it deemed appropriate, denied the city council power over it, and required its approval for development products supplied by councilors or contractors. Pauljkl was named as manager and was required to notify the council of new development members; a separate membership record listed Pauljkl and Squareheaddude. [ 3 ] [ 1 ] [ 16 ] Legislative passage and implementation were consequently separate steps. A measure might be approved politically but remain in the development queue. The council's procedure distinguished successful votes from finished updates, and the 2018 suspension demonstrated the consequences of an accumulated backlog. [ 2 ] [ 11 ] Selected measures The council's practical influence can be seen in several completed changes: Banking: the 2015 ATM expansion provided for deposits, withdrawals, and transfers away from the central bank; the proposal excluded ATM robbery. [ 6 ] Casino policing: Bailey552's July 2015 measure allowed officers equipped for enforcement to enter the casino without a casino pass, while prohibiting them from gambling. [ 17 ] Medical services: a completed emergency medical services team replaced federal DHHS provision in 2016. Pauljkl defended the change as a response to inadequate activity after a two-week opportunity to improve, while other participants disputed the circumstances. [ 18 ] Airport connections: a 2016 measure expanded destinations, including election and development locations, with Los Angeles added during revision. [ 19 ] Bus service: the March 2017 measure approved a service with a bus developed by Tremolo and stops to be planned with the mayor. [ 15 ] These measures connected the council's constitutional responsibilities to ordinary city life. Access to money, movement between locations, medical care, and police entry to commercial premises all became subjects of municipal decision-making. title: LeoVinick
text: LeoVinick 40th President of the United States In office 21 July 2021 – 1 September 2021 [ 1 ] Preceded by Guggen_Pierre Succeeded by TimidSoul NARA Presidential Records roster LeoVinick was the 40th President of the United States , serving from 21 July to 1 September 2021. A Republican, he won the Summer 2021 presidential election with TimidSoul as his running mate. He resigned before the end of his scheduled term, citing real-life responsibilities and an inability to give the presidency sufficient attention. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] Election The FEC's June 2021 election plan scheduled the Summer 2021 presidential term for July 21 through November 21. A ballot notice published on July 9 listed LeoVinick as the Republican candidate, alongside candidates from other parties and independents. On July 12, the National Elections Administrator certified LeoVinick as the winner and President-elect; the letter reported 301 votes received and 84 disqualified for alternate-account use or lack of nUSA citizenship. It also stated that LeoVinick had submitted TimidSoul as his vice-presidential candidate on June 26. [ 4 ] The elected term was scheduled to run from 21 July to 21 November 2021. [ 5 ] Impeachment and acquittal On 10 August 2021, the House of Representatives impeached LeoVinick on three articles. His Senate trial began on 14 August. [ 6 ] On 15 August, the Senate acquitted him after each article failed to receive the required two-thirds affirmative vote. [ 7 ] In a statement following the verdict, LeoVinick thanked the senators and citizens who had supported him and pledged renewed efforts to improve national activity. [ 8 ] Resignation On 29 August 2021, LeoVinick announced his resignation, to take effect on 1 September. He said that real-life responsibilities had interfered with his participation and that the motivation he had felt at the beginning of his term had faded. Unable to give the presidency his full attention, he argued that stepping aside would better serve the country's recovery than remaining in office. He maintained that reviving the group had been his administration's central aim. [ 3 ] His farewell also addressed concerns about inactivity. LeoVinick argued that criticism of Ridgeway and the Clan Managers did not fully explain the country's difficulties. He acknowledged that Washington, D.C. required management involvement, but considered limited engagement by the Clan Managers only one contributing factor. He also argued that persistent perceptions of national decline discouraged activity and urged his critics to direct their efforts toward revival. [ 3 ] TimidSoul succeeded him on 1 September 2021. A White House announcement that evening confirmed that Judge AustinBoBoston1 had sworn TimidSoul in as president minutes earlier. title: LordDeathTheReaper
text: LordDeathTheReaper 35th President of nUSA (NARA roster) In office 9 January 2021 – 29 January 2021 [ 1 ] Preceded by ArnieVinick Succeeded by Dralian NARA Presidential Records roster LordDeathTheReaper was the 35th President of the United States in the Roblox nUSA roleplay community. The FEC certified Lord as Vice President-elect on the ArnieVinick ticket on 11 November 2020; NARA's Presidential Records board later lists Lord as the 35th President. An undated presidency-history compilation dates the term to 9–29 January 2021 and records a resignation. A signed executive order dated 17 January confirms Lord acted as President during that period, but the reviewed primary archive does not establish the exact transition dates or the reported reason for leaving office. [ 2 ] Vice presidency and succession The FEC's Fall 2020 results named Lord Vice President-elect alongside ArnieVinick. The undated compiled office histories list Lord's vice-presidential service under Arnie from 21 November 2020 to 9 January 2021, followed by the presidential term. No inauguration notice or contemporaneous succession document for Lord was located in the inspected Discord exports. The NARA board's ordinal roster supports the sequence from Arnie's 34th presidency to Lord's 35th, while the exact transition date comes only from the compiled histories. [ 3 ] Executive action On 17 January 2021, Lord signed Executive Order 35-001, repealing ArnieVinick's order reducing combat tryouts within the executive branch. The order said the administration considered tryouts necessary in the current nUSA environment and stated that the repeal was effective immediately. The preserved NARA board export contains one order card for the 35th presidency. [ 4 ] Earlier public offices Before the 35th presidency, Lord served as an admiral in the United States Navy. A White House post preserved in #nusa-updates on 2 February 2019 described Lord's promotion as the first person in U.S. history to obtain that rank. Trello appointment records also identify Lord as Administrator of the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, nominated by President JamesMontagu on 19 March 2020 and confirmed by the Senate on 21 March. Another Trello card lists Lord as Secretary of Veterans Affairs, but the captured card has no appointment dates or further description. [ 5 ] Presidential records The NARA board links a presidential library that says Lord's records were transferred to its Presidential Archives division and library staff. The library description calls the collection complete, but the available board capture contains only that description and the one 35-001 order card, so the accessible materials do not independently establish the completeness of the transfer. [ 6 ] The same NARA board has another empty card titled “LordDeathTheReaper, 46th.” The compiled presidential table instead assigns the 46th presidency to Jtport. The archive does not explain this discrepancy, and this article relies on the 35th-presidency record for the period following ArnieVinick. title: Lordsights
text: Lordsights 21st President of nUSA In office 26 July 2018 – 13 November 2018 [ 1 ] Preceded by BernardCaldwell Succeeded by Frosty_TheSn0wman NARA presidential roster Lordsights is a Roblox account identified in nUSA records as President during 2018 and as a presidential candidate in 2019. The archived Discord first records a presidential action on July 26, 2018, and announced his resignation on November 13, 2018; the sources reviewed do not state the date he first took office. [ 2 ] Administration An early recorded action was appointing a White House Chief of Staff. In August, the archive publicized a Federal Employment Center executive order and described the center as intended to help people obtain government jobs. On August 19, Lordsights said he had directed agencies to develop more realistic training facilities and uniforms; another post announced an executive order establishing a National Guard. These are recorded announcements of administration plans and actions, not independent assessments of their effect. [ 3 ] Other messages connect these projects to military and executive-branch facilities. In August, the channel said a Federal Law Enforcement Center facility was nearly complete. In September, Lordsights announced funding for a training base for both the military and executive branch. The archive also records an inspection announcement for more than 95 service members and a report that the base was funded for both branches' use. [ 4 ] In October, Lordsights announced confirmation of his third Supreme Court nominee and the release of an October budget. The announcements show the administration communicating appointments and budget documents through the channel, but do not preserve the nominee's identity or the budget's contents. [ 5 ] Military activity and departure In August 2018, nUSA announced that it had won its first defense against Malta with a score of 1,000–243, followed by a Lordsights post marked “1–0.” This was a Roblox roleplay conflict reported by the community. In November, an announcement said his administration deployed the military to Las Vegas in response to what it called a “terrorist migrant Caravan”; the label and stated reason belong to that in-world announcement. [ 6 ] On November 13, the channel announced that Lordsights had resigned. The notice does not provide the resignation's terms or identify an immediate successor. [ 7 ] Impeachment and later candidacy In September 2018, an impeachment vote in the House of Representatives (nUSA) passed and was sent to the Senate (nUSA) . The channel's follow-up expressly said Lordsights had not been removed from office; the preserved notice does not give a final Senate outcome or reproduce the full resolution's basis. [ 8 ] In 2019, Lordsights appeared as a presidential candidate in the 2019 presidential elections (nUSA) . On September 30, the Coalition Against Abuse published a warning. The notice records the organization's finding of a community-guideline violation and says further violations could bring a ban and election disqualification. This is the organization's stated decision, not an independently established finding in the available record.
