title: Lumidas
text: Lumidas 4th President of nUSA In office 30 December 2013 – 25 February 2014 [ 1 ] Preceded by Marinio Succeeded by Zeyad567 6th President of nUSA In office 30 July 2014 – 23 September 2014 [ 1 ] Preceded by Zeyad567 Succeeded by Aerium 10th president of nUSA In office 15 February 2015 – 20 July 2015 [ 1 ] Preceded by Jcmand Succeeded by Zeyad567 NARA Presidential Records, 4th ; NARA Presidential Records, 6th ; NARA Presidential Records, 10th Lumidas was the fourth, sixth, and tenth president of the Roblox nUSA roleplay community. His administration records range from a response to civil unrest and a proposed career-guidance program to changes in agency recruitment and military command. A 2017 sequence of presidents lists three separate Lumidas presidencies; he served in 2013–2014, again in 2014, and in 2015. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] Presidential terms The 2017 list places Lumidas after Marinio , then after Zeyad567 , and later after Jcmand , with Zeyad567 following his tenth presidency. NARA’s later roster identifies these entries as the fourth, sixth, and tenth presidencies. His three periods in office ran from 30 December 2013 to 25 February 2014, 30 July to 23 September 2014, and 15 February to 20 July 2015. [ 1 ] [ 3 ] Fourth presidency An order archived as Executive Order #4-001 directed federal agencies to deploy to Washington, D.C. , after what it described as rioting, protests, and the start of a war with the United Kingdom. It raised the alert to DEFCON 2 and called for continuous federal staffing and intelligence monitoring. The archival copy lists the original date as unknown, so the events and response cannot be placed more precisely in Lumidas’s fourth term from this document alone. [ 4 ] Sixth presidency An order establishing a Commission of Academies proposed centralized supervision of recruitment academies at federal agencies. It assigned the commission to the Department of Education and directed affected agencies to set up academies, with deadlines in August 2014. The document is catalogued as Executive Order #4-002, but its text calls itself Lumidas’s “first executive order as 6th President.” For that reason, its contents cannot be assigned confidently to the fourth or sixth term from the archive numbering alone. [ 5 ] Tenth presidency The surviving #10 series gives the clearest account of Lumidas’s military policy. Executive Order #10-001 established a War Council composed of the President, interim commander in chief, and the secretaries of state and defense, with senior military and intelligence officials participating as advisers or at the President’s invitation. The council was authorized to advise on military matters and deploy forces during crises or war. The order also prescribed detention, dismissal, and treason proceedings for members who leaked intelligence. [ 6 ] Three further orders revised military recruitment and command. Lumidas abolished obstacle-course tryouts at federal agencies, citing their limited relevance to work in the country’s cities and favoring combat simulations, reaction tests, and grammar tests. He authorized the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff to decommission military officers. A fourth order created a Military Enlistment Overseer to review enlistment policy, applications, and related discipline. The archival covers give no original signing dates for these orders, so they document the policies attributed to the tenth presidency without establishing their precise order of implementation or duration. [ 7 ] Orders catalogued in the #4 series Other orders catalogued in the #4 series addressed campaign activity on official USA properties, required senior officials to answer USA-related messages, and proposed a “What Job Should I Get?” career-guidance program. The program was described as a planned group and place where staff would guide citizens toward political, law-enforcement, or business careers; the order anticipated a 29 September 2014 launch. The available document describes the plan and launch date but does not confirm that the service opened. Because Executive Order #4-002 identifies itself as Lumidas’s first order as sixth President, the catalog numbers alone do not establish which term each #4-series order belongs to. [ 8 ] Other policy records A separate Lumidas proposal submitted as Public Law 28-1 would have opened USA audit logs to middle- and upper-class citizens. In his message to Congress, Lumidas framed the measure as a way for citizens to identify corruption and learn from the group’s history, while limiting prosecution to activity recorded after the bill became law. The surviving archive includes his request and signature, but does not include a congressional vote or a separate enactment record. The document does not establish which of his presidential terms it belongs to. [ 9 ] Career and legacy Lumidas later served as director of the National Security Agency under President SuddenRush12G , according to a December 2016 profile of that administration. In a November 2016 essay, former Vice President TimGeithner recalled working with Lumidas’s diplomatic team during negotiations over international recognition in 2015. Geithner credited the team with winning recognition for nUSA over a rival United States roleplay group, while noting his own short service as a deputy secretary of state during the negotiations. The essay is a participant’s retrospective account, rather than a contemporaneous diplomatic record. title: Main Page
text: Welcome to the nUSA Wiki A local history of the Roblox nUSA community 160 articles · About the sources · All pages Featured article The President of the United States was the leading elected office in the Roblox nUSA roleplay government. The history spans early group holders, elections, succession through vice presidents, executive orders, constitutional changes, and periods of controversy. A linked roster follows the presidents from 2012 through the latest numbered archive entry. title: Mallsoft
text: Mallsoft 56th President of nUSA (NARA roster) In office 2025 (exact dates unverified) Preceded by snowbleed Succeeded by aConArtist NARA Presidential Records roster Mallsoft is listed by NARA as the 56th President of the Roblox nUSA roleplay government. The surviving presidential roster places Mallsoft between snowbleed and aConArtist , but its card does not record an oath or term dates. Mallsoft also appears in records of Group Management, the vice presidency, and the community's courts. These records span several years and do not by themselves form an uninterrupted account of one office. [ 1 ] Earlier administrative and judicial roles Mallsoft appears in early nUSA Discord material as a clan manager. During 2019 and 2020, management announcements directed community-engagement questions to Mallsoft and sought ideas for activities intended to increase participation. These notices document an administrative role and stated outreach plans, but they do not establish the result of the proposals. [ 2 ] The congressional nominations archive has entries for Mallsoft as Vice President, Associate Justice of the Supreme Court, Chief District Court Judge, and Chief Judge. Those cards are filed among Passed Nominations , yet their titles alone do not establish the dates or length of service in each office. A Supreme Court former-member card specifically lists Justice Mallsoft in an associate-justice seat from 5 December 2024 to 24 January 2025 and names President Teasoups as the appointing President. The court record offers a firmer date range for that judicial term than the nomination titles do for the other posts. [ 3 ] Presidency and later records The NARA card identifies Mallsoft as the 56th President, following snowbleed. The reviewed presidential board does not attach an executive order, memorandum, election certificate, or inauguration announcement to the profile. Consequently the sources available here do not justify exact term dates or attribution of a specific policy to Mallsoft's administration. The successor in the roster is aConArtist, whose inauguration was announced for July 25, 2025; the announcement does not itself say when Mallsoft ceased to hold office. [ 4 ] The congressional archive also contains a measure titled Impeaching Mallsoft, Chief Judge of the District Court . Its wording concerns Mallsoft's judicial office, not the presidency. A title and archived card do not establish that its allegations were proven or that the measure removed Mallsoft. Separate court records index disciplinary matters and litigation involving the account; their existence is not a substitute for reading the outcomes of those cases. [ 5 ] 2025 FEC election records NARA's Presidential Records roster lists Mallsoft as the 56th President. In the checked 2025 election records, Mallsoft appears on the 14 November Winter Presidential Election ballot and was disqualified later that day. The notice gives no reason. No dated election result, succession notice, or oath establishing Mallsoft's presidential service was located in the reviewed source set. NARA's ordinal is an archival listing, not enough by itself to establish a term or transition; it also conflicts with the July 2025 FEC certificate calling aConArtist the 56th President. title: Marinio
text: Marinio 3rd President of nUSA In office 26 August 2013 – 30 December 2013 [ 1 ] Preceded by Moolah60 (after a disputed transition) Succeeded by Lumidas NARA Presidential Records Marinio was the third President of the Roblox nUSA roleplay community. His administration issued a November 2013 executive order barring federal employers from requiring applicants without Builders Club membership to wear a particular outfit, and advanced a congressional measure establishing elected city mayors. He took office after the disputed end of Moolah60 's presidency; he served from 26 August to 30 December 2013. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] Presidency Marinio took office after Moolah60's disputed presidency and was succeeded by Lumidas. An earlier list of presidents omitted Moolah60, placing Marinio directly after Nightgaladeld; the presidential roster recognizes Moolah60 as the second President and Marinio as the third. The precise date of Marinio's accession is not established by a contemporary instrument. [ 3 ] On 29 November 2013, Marinio issued Executive Order #3-001 on hiring requirements. It prohibited federal agencies from making a specific outfit mandatory for applicants who did not have Builders Club membership, describing such a rule as discrimination based on social and economic status. The order threatened employment termination, federal court proceedings, criminal records, and suspension from federal agencies for officials who enforced the requirement. The surviving copy records the order’s text and stated effective time, 12:30 p.m. Eastern; it does not document how widely agencies applied it. [ 4 ] Congressional records also associate Marinio with a city-government measure. Public Law 6-1 proposed elected mayors responsible for local construction, security, ordinances, and civic events. The proposal set eligibility and election rules, including a minimum of 50 votes and a 10-point margin. The Public Law Database links a separate post as Marinio’s signature record; the surviving card presents the bill and signature link but does not supply a vote tally or enactment date. [ 5 ] Later public service A December 2016 profile of President SuddenRush12G described Marinio as the President under whom SuddenRush12G led the United States Special Forces. This is a later account of SuddenRush12G’s career and does not provide additional dates for Marinio’s presidency. title: Metropolitan Police Department (nUSA)
text: Municipal police service of Washington, D.C. The Metropolitan Police Department ( MPD ) is Washington, D.C. 's municipal police service. Its January 2024 reorganization brought personnel from Boulder County into a consolidated capital department under Chief MasonRockefeller. The transition included a new command structure, lateral transfers and a departmental academy intended to prepare a new class of officers. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] Municipal role The MPD provides the capital's front-line municipal policing. Its place within local government distinguishes it from federal protective and investigative agencies. The availability of municipal policing also affected federal deployments: in January 2023, President TacticalRock101 restored the Federal Protective Service to active status, citing increased activity in Washington and the unavailability of the Metropolitan Police service. [ 3 ] That order illustrates a practical connection between local and federal institutions. A lapse in the capital's municipal policing could leave federal agencies carrying additional responsibilities. The later MPD reorganization sought to build a staffed and trained local service rather than relying solely on the continued availability of other agencies. [ 4 ] [ 5 ] The 2024 consolidation On 17 January 2024, AIex announced an agreement with Boulder governor AlexReign providing municipal personnel a route into Washington 's departments. Rockefeller was appointed MPD chief, the Boulder County sheriff was designated deputy chief, and the CPD chief was designated assistant chief. Police staffs were to merge into the MPD and arrange their rank transfers through department leadership. [ 6 ] The police consolidation was one element of a wider local-government transition. AlexReign would become interim mayor pending council elections; appointments were also made for Washington's Fire Department and Emergency Medical Services. The capital's policing arrangements therefore developed alongside the replacement of its municipal leadership and other emergency services. [ 7 ] Training and command recruitment Later on 17 January, Rockefeller asked personnel not to begin operational service while the department organized its command staff, transferred employees and prepared its first class. He announced a DC Metro Academy in place of FLETC for prospective MPD recruits. The academy was intended to give officers the knowledge and professional preparation needed for municipal policing, with applications expected that weekend. [ 8 ] The department sought six to eight additional command staff. Preference went to applicants with command experience in DPD, BCSO or CPD. A second preference covered FLETC-certified applicants with command experience in the FBI, Secret Service or National Guard, while applications remained open to others. The recruitment priorities combined local-service experience with a route for qualified federal personnel. [ 9 ] The transition was announced as work in progress. Rockefeller's instructions separated appointment and transfer from operational readiness: a place in the organization did not immediately authorize officers to begin duty before training and command arrangements were complete. title: Moolah60
text: Moolah60 2nd President of nUSA In office 9 June 2013 – 14 August 2013 (de jure); de facto tenure ended 27 July 2013 [ 1 ] Preceded by Nightgaladeld Succeeded by Marinio (after a disputed transition) Presidential Records Moolah60 was the second President of the Roblox nUSA roleplay community. Elected on 9 June 2013, he succeeded the group's founder, Nightgaladeld , who became his Vice President. His short presidency ended amid a contested transition involving Gmf34 and the group owner. The distinction between his election and the later dispute over his authority remains central to accounts of nUSA's earliest constitutional crisis. [ 2 ] Election and presidency Moolah60 won the presidency on 9 June 2013. His election was constitutionally valid, a point expressly preserved in the later presidential record despite controversy surrounding his conduct in office. Nightgaladeld, the outgoing President and owner of the Roblox group, served as Vice President. This arrangement placed the founder inside the elected administration while he also retained ownership of the platform on which its government operated. [ 3 ] The surviving material establishes the election and succession more clearly than the administration's policies. No verified executive orders or enacted laws attributable to Moolah60 have been identified in the reviewed presidential archive. His historical significance rests chiefly on the way his presidency exposed the tension between an elected government and the group owner's separate power over the Roblox community. [ 4 ] Disputed end of the presidency A retrospective chronology distinguishes Moolah60's formal tenure, ending on 14 August 2013, from his effective exercise of the office, which it dates only to 27 July. It describes Gmf34 as exercising presidential authority after that date without a constitutional election, followed by a short period of direct rule by Nightgaladeld before Marinio became the third President on 26 August. These dates and characterizations come from a later reconstruction; the original removal and succession instruments have not been located. The later records nevertheless retain Moolah60 as the second President rather than erasing his election. [ 5 ] An archived list of presidents records Moolah60 as having been blacklisted after leaving office, without giving a date, decision text, or grounds. Nightgaladeld's December 2017 list of past presidents omits him, whereas the later presidential roster and archival list include him. The stronger evidence for his place in the succession is the explicit record of his election and recognition as the second President. [ 6 ] See also President of the United States Nightgaladeld Marinio ↑ Nusapedia, “President of the United States” , presidential chronology, accessed 30 September 2026. ↑ Moolah60, 2nd , Presidential Records, election note; Nightgaladeld, 3rd vice president , Vice Presidential Records; presidential chronology , 2013 entries. ↑ Moolah60, 2nd , Presidential Records; Nightgaladeld, 3rd vice president , Vice Presidential Records; Nightgaladeld's 2017 group-holder statement . ↑ Presidential Records board , presidents and early executive-order sections; Moolah60 presidential entry . ↑ presidential chronology , 2013 succession entries; Moolah60 presidential entry , note affirming his constitutional election; Marinio, 3rd , Presidential Records. ↑ List of Presidents of nUSA and Reasons for Leaving Office , local archival copy; former-presidents list , 4 December 2017; Moolah60 presidential entry .

title: MultiBallot directive of 2024
text: The MultiBallot directive of 2024 (Directive #003-09) was a Group Management announcement describing a redesign of elections in the nUSA roleplay community. Announced on 21 June 2024, the document named three official political parties, described seat-specific congressional races and simultaneous elections, and set out an in-game petition process for ballot access. The sources establish what the directive announced; they do not by themselves establish the extent to which its system was implemented in later elections. [ 1 ] Announcement and parties The public announcement presented MultiBallot as an upgrade developed with the FEC and development team. The accompanying document named the Forward, Pioneer, and Plutocratic parties as the three official parties. It said existing and pending parties were dissolved effective immediately and that attempts to form additional parties would violate the community guidelines. These were statements in Group Management's announcement and its attached design document. [ 2 ] Seat-based elections The design document described a seat system for congressional elections. Rather than electing a slate of candidates through one class-wide tally, the announced model assigned each legislator an individual seat and presented a separate race for each seat. A voter could vote once in each seat-specific race, and incumbents would be identified on the ballot and compete to retain their seats. [ 3 ] The document also described simultaneous elections and a petition tool for candidate ballot access. It said registration would move to the in-game U.S. Courthouse, where candidates would receive a tool to collect voter signatures. Its examples and explanatory text present the intended workflow, not an independent record of later election operations. [ 4 ] Context The announcement identified the FEC as a collaborator and presented MultiBallot as a change to election rules and party organization. The Commission was separately described in its regulations as an election-administration body. The directive therefore belongs to the history of electoral administration in nUSA, while its claims about improvements and benefits remain the document's stated rationale. [ 5 ] See also Federal Election Commission (nUSA) Elections in nUSA Election schedule directive of 2024 Later FEC archive records The archive documents a test followed by a live election. On 23 June 2024, nUSA's owner announced test races at the U.S. Courthouse; the test was reopened to exercise a revised backend on 26 June. On 5 July, the FEC said the House Class II election was the first election using MultiBallot, and on 8 July certified results while thanking voters for using the system. The announcement and design document therefore establish both the system's proposed features and its initial use; they do not establish how consistently it was used later. title: N ightmarre
text: N_ightmarre 37th President of nUSA (NARA roster) In office 7 February 2021 – 21 March 2021 [ 1 ] Preceded by Dralian Succeeded by Ralphiuss NARA Presidential Records roster N_ightmarre was recorded on the NARA Presidential Records board as the 37th President of the nUSA roleplay community. The roster places the presidency after Dralian’s 36th term and before Ralphiuss’s 38th. An undated compiled presidential chronology reports a term from February 7 to March 21, 2021; the linked vice-presidential list also records N_ightmarre’s vice presidents serving during February and March, with the last listed term ending March 21. The primary records reviewed confirm presidential activity by February 27 but do not contain a contemporaneous oath or transition record for the reported start date. Three executive orders attributed to the administration address homeland-security coordination, internal-affairs oversight, and off-team robbery by executive-branch employees. [ 2 ] Homeland security Executive Order 37-001, signed at the White House on February 27, 2021, established a Homeland Security Council as an advisory body to the President. It created a Homeland Security Advisor and deputy advisor, assigned the advisor to chair the council and oversee domestic operating intelligence agencies alongside the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, and set weekly council meetings and reports. The order describes its intended structure and duties; the archive does not document implementation. [ 3 ] Internal-affairs oversight Executive Order 37-002, dated February 28, 2021, established N_ightmarre’s Freedom Initiative (NFI) as an independent executive-branch agency overseen by the Executive Office of the President. The order said the NFI followed the abolishment of the Internal Affairs Institute and would oversee internal-affairs work across executive agencies, receive complaints, investigate suspected misconduct, and review some disciplinary actions. It also set limits: the order excluded Clan Management community-guideline matters from NFI jurisdiction, capped suspensions, and provided an appeal process for investigated employees. These are provisions of the order; the available sources do not establish how often the agency used them. [ 4 ] Other executive actions A second order, dated March 4, 2021, allowed executive-branch employees to rob “off team” without agency discipline for robbery. It preserved the Department of Justice’s ability to bring criminal charges, and permitted agency internal-affairs offices to pursue reports about conduct other than robbery. The order’s title referred to equality among executive-branch “Kings and Queens”; the operative text framed the policy as a response to employees’ inability to afford in-game currency and alleged threats or blackmail. The record documents the rule as written, not its implementation or effects. [ 5 ] On March 6, a presidential memorandum rescinded or revoked four earlier directives: a Reset4K memorandum concerning Calculatous and the White House, Josh Miller’s order banning NSFW content in federal communication servers, and two Jcmand executive orders concerning executive reform and executive entities. The memo does not list N_ightmarre’s three orders; although the Presidential Records export labels those three order cards “Repealed,” the export does not identify the repealing instrument or date, so their repeal cannot be attributed to this March 6 memorandum from the reviewed text. [ 6 ] Judicial roster The Supreme Court board lists an associate justice under the name “Justice Guggen_Pierre (N_ightmarre),” with service beginning March 8, 2021; it records Senate confirmation by a 6–0–1 vote and identifies N_ightmarre as the appointing President. The record does not explain the relationship between the presidential and judicial labels or provide an end date for the judicial service. [ 7 ] The NARA presidential roster numbers N_ightmarre’s presidency 37th, between Dralian’s 36th and Ralphiuss’s 38th. The separate chronology reports February 7–March 21, 2021; the accompanying reasons list instead says N_ightmarre “Finished ArnieVinick’s term,” which conflicts with the ordinal sequence and the reported dates. The reasons list does not explain this conflict and is not a contemporaneous election or transition record. title: NARA Hub
text: The NARA Hub is a Trello directory for archival and government-record boards associated with the Roblox roleplay community nUSA. Its board is titled “NARA || Hub”; the retained export contained nine lists and 73 cards when reviewed in September 2026. The hub links to community records and administrative documents and is distinct from the real-world U.S. National Archives and Records Administration. [ 1 ] Organization The hub groups cards under a National Archives and Records Administration list and a “Main Trellos” directory. The latter points readers to the Public Law Database (nUSA) , Presidential Records (nUSA) , Congress, court, and state or municipal record boards. These links make the hub a navigation point across separately maintained Trello boards; a link alone does not establish that a destination is complete or authoritative. [ 2 ] Other hub lists preserve constitution and charter material, group-management directives, templates, archive-board links, and informational role cards. Some linked collections are explicitly marked old or unfinished. The presence of historical, draft, and active-labeled material on one directory reflects the breadth of the collection rather than a single uniform status. [ 3 ] Records and scope The hub’s linked boards organize records by institution and form. The Public Law Database is arranged by congressional periods and includes legislation and status labels; the Presidential Records board separates executive orders, memoranda, proclamations, pardons, and presidential-library material into lists. These are roleplay records and indexes, not records of the actual United States government. [ 4 ] The hub action history shows that directory cards for the Public Law Database and Presidential Archives were added on 17 July 2023, with further board links added in 2024. This dates the Trello directory entries, not the creation of every linked institution or collection. [ 5 ] Development of the directory Group Management announced new NARA and Congress Trello boards on 17 July 2023, following Memorandum #001’s introduction of NARA and its archival requirements. The announcement described the Hub as a directory containing links to the other Trellos required for use. This is the clearest dated statement of the Hub’s initial announced function in the reviewed record. [ 6 ] The board network expanded after launch. The Hub action history dates its Public Law Database and Presidential Archives directory cards to 17 July 2023; it records the D.C. City Council and Supreme Court links in March 2024, and District Court plus several archive-board cards in April 2024. These dates describe additions to the directory, not necessarily when the linked boards or their underlying records began. [ 7 ] Directory limits and snapshots The Hub’s archive list points to separate Public Law, District Court, Executive, and legislative collections. Two labels preserve status information directly: one executive archive card is marked “Not Finished,” and an older legislative archive card is marked “OLD.” Those labels warn that a linked repository may be incomplete or superseded; they do not describe every board linked by the Hub. [ 8 ] The September 2026 export captures one moment in a changing directory. The role cards also show why the directory should not be treated as a timeless roster: its action history records successive Archivist-card description changes in January 2024, February 2025, and August 2025, while the card description in the reviewed snapshot names ZhangJinping. This chronology concerns the Trello card’s content, not independent confirmation of each appointment. title: NUSA (Roblox group)
text: nUSA is a Roblox-based political roleplay community whose records use the name United States of America and stage federal institutions, elections, legislation and court proceedings. Its constitutions, agencies and statutes describe rules for that community's roleplay; they are not instruments of the real United States government. The surviving record reflects successive organizational resets and constitutional versions rather than one uninterrupted legal system. [ 1 ] Scope and records The archive documents an in-game federal government with legislative, executive and judicial records, and a separate Group Management layer. A July 2023 Group Management announcement introduced a Constitution, directives on NARA and legislative archives, and new Trello boards for NARA and Congress. Those records show the roleplay's institutional framework at that time; they do not establish the same offices or rules as current real-world U.S. institutions. [ 2 ] The National Archives and Records Administration (nUSA) is one of the recordkeeping institutions named in the 2023 framework. The contemporary Constitution assigned it public-record storage and maintenance for the roleplay's Congress, Judiciary and Executive, while Memorandum #001 described operational autonomy from the player government under Group Management oversight. That arrangement is specific to the 2023 framework and should not be projected automatically onto later constitutions. [ 3 ] Institutional chronology An archival custody letter dated 13 March 2020 says the Archives and the official Constitution copy were transferred from Clan Management control to Archivist LargeTitanic2. The document is evidence of a custody handoff, but does not establish that every later version of NARA had the same organization or authority. [ 4 ] In July 2023, Group Management announced a reset of federal laws, case law and congressional resolutions, motions and awards, effective 15 July, followed by a new Constitution and directives on 17 July. In September it credited goleros with leading NARA and the Federal Elections Commission; an October appointment assigned TacticalRummy responsibility for running NARA alongside election-administration duties. The overlap documents portfolios held by individuals, not a merger of the institutions. [ 5 ] The 6 November 2024 announcement said a new Constitution had passed after review by the Senate, House, District Courts and Supreme Court, and that Group Management would own and maintain its PDF. The linked file was not accessible in the reviewed archive. In May 2025, NARA announced a readoption of a Constitution associated with Timothy F. Geithner, creating a later constitutional status marker; the source record does not reconcile all version dates. [ 6 ] Constitutional sequence The NARA Hub and Public Law Database preserve several differently dated constitutional records. These include a text marked superseded in 2017, the Constitution instituted in July 2023, a Constitution announced as passed in November 2024, and a document presented as a 2018 Constitution readopted in May 2025. A separate Public Law Database card gives the same general later readoption a 2017 origin and a January 2024 date. See Constitutions of nUSA , 2024 Constitution of nUSA and 2025 constitutional readoption in nUSA for the source-by-source account. title: NUSA archival policy
text: The NUSA archival policy refers to rules and statements recorded for handling government and community records in the nUSA roleplay project. The sources include a broad NARA Hub statement permitting deletion, redaction, or censorship to protect people working abroad and to prevent conflict, as well as more specific 2023 requirements for public records and legislative submissions. These are community governance records and do not describe real United States archival law. [ 1 ] Access and redaction The Hub carries a statement that documents “may be deleted, redacted, or censored in any fashion” for the stated purposes of protecting the identities of people serving abroad and protecting the United States from conflict. The same wording appears on the Public Law Database board. The statement records broad discretion on those boards; by itself it does not identify a particular deletion decision or establish how frequently the policy was used. [ 2 ] Preservation and review The July 2023 Constitution assigns NARA responsibility for storing and maintaining public records for Congress, the judiciary, and the executive, and for setting retention schedules and archival processes. Group Management Memorandum #001 describes NARA as overseen by Group Management while operating autonomously from the player government. Read together, the instruments place recordkeeping within the community’s administrative framework while describing operational independence from elected roleplay government. [ 3 ] The memorandum also sets requirements for legislative submissions, including standardized templates and metadata. It says NARA may decline archival approval for noncompliant passed bills and that such a bill does not become active law; the archival check is limited to compliance rather than policy substance. This is a specific workflow described in the 2023 memorandum, separate from the broader redaction statement on the Trello boards. [ 4 ] Applied requirements and continuity An August 2024 notice applied record requirements to congressional session labels. It warned that bills carrying the wrong session number would no longer be archived or logged, while granting an exception to bills already moving through the legislative process. The notice named the 98th Congress as beginning on 19 August. It presents a concrete rule about how records were labeled and logged, including a transition exception, rather than a general decision about legislation’s substance. [ 5 ] A June 2024 quarterly-audit announcement described a separate continuity measure. NARA said it restored D.C. City Council records removed because of the holder’s personal security concerns, and that it had backed up boards to separate storage points, at frequent but undisclosed times. The notice links availability and restoration to community safety and says the backups were meant to reduce the risk posed by an “Admin Attack.” This is an announced practice at a particular date, not proof of a permanent schedule or a complete backup history. [ 6 ] These examples show that archival practice combined record formatting, access decisions, restoration, and backup. The source record supports describing the announced rules and individual reported actions; it does not justify assuming that every board was complete, that every rule was applied uniformly, or that every deletion or acceptance decision followed the same procedure. title: National Archives Reformation Act of 2019 (nUSA)
text: The National Archives Reformation Act of 2019 is the title of a five-page roleplay legislative document, S. 188, dated 21 July 2019. It proposed reorganizing the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) as an independent agency to curate, maintain, and manage the National Archives. Although a Trello card catalogs it as “Public Law 75-1,” the attached PDF calls itself a bill and the card says the attached version was archived; the available records do not establish enactment or implementation. [ 1 ] Proposed structure The bill divided the proposed archive into executive, legislative, Supreme Court, inferior-court, and general records subdivisions. It described the agency as responsible for curation and maintenance across those branches and record classes. These provisions describe the proposed design in S. 188; the archived copy does not establish that the subdivisions were created or operated as written. [ 2 ] S. 188 proposed an Archivist appointed by the President with Senate confirmation and a National Archives Board. It also assigned ownership and administration of the underlying storage system to a designated Clan Manager. The bill paired an independent archival agency with a separately administered technical storage system. [ 3 ] Record status and later context The PLD places the item under a public-law number, while the card says the attached version is archived. The PDF’s bill title and date provide evidence of a proposed framework, but the reviewed material does not include a vote, presidential signature, effective-date clause, or implementation report. [ 4 ] Later records describe other stages of archival organization: the Archivist Act of 2020 (nUSA) proposed a bill-copy workflow, and the July 2023 framework announced a new NARA board and records requirements. Those later records do not show that S. 188’s specific governance structure took effect. [ 5 ] Earlier and later archival records The proposed structure in S. 188 resembles a reorganization rather than a claim that archival work began in 2019. The PLD’s earlier Public Law 39-5 card describes an archive group that had shut down for inactivity and a conditional proposal to restore it. Its Public Law 56-5 card later describes an existing NARA that needed reorganization and names records such as passed laws, executive orders, and Supreme and federal court decisions. The accessible records do not establish a continuous chain of implementation between those entries and S. 188. [ 6 ] In the 2023 framework, Group Management issued a separate NARA memorandum and legislative archival requirements and published a new Trello hub. These later materials document a new archival framework, but they do not state that all five S. 188 subdivisions, its Board, or its Clan Manager storage arrangement were implemented as drafted. title: National Archives and Records Administration (nUSA)
text: The National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) is an archival institution in the nUSA Roblox roleplay community. Community records assign it responsibility for preserving government documents, while its reporting line and exact title changed across different periods. It is separate from the real U.S. National Archives and Records Administration; its claimed powers apply within the roleplay. [ 1 ] Organization and remit The July 2023 Constitution places NARA under Group Management control and assigns it storage and maintenance of public records for the roleplay legislature, judiciary and executive, including authority to set retention schedules and archival processes. Memorandum #001 describes NARA as autonomous from the player government. Read together, these documents describe GM oversight with operational distance from elected or in-roleplay government; they do not define the full boundary of that autonomy. [ 2 ] Memorandum #001 also established a records workflow for legislative items. It required standardized public forms and specified descriptive information. NARA could decline to archive a measure that failed archival requirements; the memo said that such a measure would not become active law. The stated decision was about archival compliance rather than the political or policy substance of the measure. [ 3 ] Institutional history The records do not establish one simple founding date. A Public Law Database entry proposes restoring a National Archive group said to have shut down for inactivity, but its wording is conditional and does not prove that proposal passed. A separate 2019 archival reformation measure is filed under a public-law label, while its attached PDF presents itself as a bill and the available record does not settle enactment or implementation. These should be treated as proposals or documentary records unless a passage record is available. [ 4 ] A March 2020 retirement letter records a concrete transfer of the Archives from Clan Management control to Archivist LargeTitanic2, with custody of the official Constitution version also assigned to the Archivist. The letter establishes that custody event but does not show that every later NARA agency structure or statutory authority was transferred at the same time. [ 5 ] In 2023, GM publicly introduced NARA directives and new archival boards. Subsequent announcements document leadership and staffing changes: a September 2023 announcement credited goleros with leading NARA, an October appointment assigned TacticalRummy to run it, and a March 2024 notice announced AustinBoBoston1 as Archivist. These announcements document dated role claims, but do not provide a complete succession list or resolve differences among titles such as administrator, manager and archivist. [ 6 ] Archives and versioning NARA's collections were described as covering public executive, legislative and judicial records. A June 2024 NARA update reported an audit, restoration of previously removed D.C. Council records and frequent backups of Trello boards. This is the agency's own operational report and indicates that board content could be removed and later restored; it does not establish that the archive was complete or continuously available. [ 7 ] Constitution custody and NARA's role vary by version. The 2023 Constitution contains an explicit NARA mandate; the Constitution announcement of November 2024 says Group Management would own and maintain its file, but the linked PDF was inaccessible to the reviewed archive. The May 2025 copy was presented as a readopted and revised Constitution and does not contain a searchable NARA clause. Absence of that clause from the later PDF does not by itself prove a change in agency policy. title: National Elections Administrator (nUSA)
text: The National Elections Administrator (NEA) was a senior election-administration office associated with the Federal Election Commission (FEC) in the nUSA roleplay community. A 2020 FEC publication identifies the NEA among the Commission's officers and assigns the office oversight duties involving election staff and certification. Later appointment and announcement records use the title alongside NARA responsibilities, showing that office portfolios could overlap without making the institutions identical. [ 1 ] Responsibilities The FEC's January 2020 regulations list Aerium as National Elections Administrator and place the office within the Commission's organizational directory. The publication says the NEA could remove election officers for violations of the publication, unauthorized release of election material, or concealment of an act violating election rules. The same document says its regulations concerned elections managed by the Commission and could change over time. [ 2 ] The NEA also appears in election result records as the official who certified outcomes and delivered them to Congress. In June 2019, David E. Racine, III signed the Summer presidential election letter as National Elections Administrator and Senior Overseer of the FEC; in October, the Fall election results letter identifies Aerium as National Elections Administrator and records certification and delivery to Congress. [ 3 ] Appointments and concurrent roles A Group Management appointment record posted in October 2023 assigned TacticalRummy the National Elections Administrator role while also directing them to run NARA and coordinate with branches. A June 2024 management notice said NARA would remain separate from a merged Government GM liaison post and that Rummy would remain NARA GM; it described the management arrangement and did not establish that the NEA and NARA were a single agency. [ 4 ] In 2026, Archivist Zhang Jinping announced gabezilla090909 as Deputy National Elections Administrator, signing the post with both Archivist and NEA titles. This announcement documents a later deputy appointment and the author's concurrent titles, but does not establish a complete succession list for the office. [ 5 ] See also Federal Election Commission (nUSA) Elections in nUSA 2019 presidential elections (nUSA) Later FEC archive records Later election administration The December 2025 Federal Election Code described the National Elections Administrator as an appointed FEC position whose election assignments were set by the Board of Owners. In March 2026, the NEA announced a code amendment requiring candidates to provide links to campaign or transition servers and transfer server ownership to an account delegated by the Commission within 48 hours. In May, the NEA announced a separate code addition for presidential exploratory committees, limiting their size and prohibiting campaigning or campaign-server operation before the permitted period. [ 6 ] In September 2026, the NEA asserted that the FEC held sole authority to certify federally and municipally administered election winners and asked judges to administer oaths to winners who had not been sworn in by the House. This is evidence of the NEA's published position in that episode, not a full account of the unresolved institutional dispute. title: National Wiki Archive Project
text: The National Wiki Archive Project was a community-history initiative associated with NARA in the nUSA roleplay community. A November 2023 appointment memo named Cherrydearest as Assistant Archivist and project director and invited public contributors to add historical material to a wiki. The memo described approval controls for edits and a probationary appointment; it documents the project’s stated plan, not the completeness or long-term operation of the site. [ 1 ] Appointment and contribution model The memo assigned Cherrydearest both an Assistant Archivist role and direction of the project. It described the wiki as a place where community members could contribute history, while requiring administrative approval of edits to protect accuracy and member safety. The arrangement combined open contribution with review before changes appeared. [ 2 ] The appointment was initially subject to a 90-day probation. A December 2023 announcement later said Cherrydearest had completed probation and become a full Assistant Archivist. That announcement confirms the staff-status change described there; it does not report the project’s article count, editorial history, or completeness. [ 3 ] Relationship to the archive The project extended the archive’s stated scope from legal and administrative instruments toward community history. The appointment record places it within NARA staffing, while the July 2023 framework separately assigns NARA responsibility for public records concerning the legislature, judiciary, and government. The sources describe related but distinct goals: public-history contributions and formal government-record handling. [ 4 ] The preserved sources identify the site as nusahistory.wiki and record the appointment and probation completion, but do not establish whether the site remains active or how its contents were maintained over time. title: News media in nUSA
text: News media in nUSA refers to the user-run outlets and individual contributors that publish news, opinion, polling, interviews, and event coverage about the Roblox nUSA community. The reviewed Discord archive documents formats including written reporting, election polls, candidate interviews, advertised debates, and editorial articles. Its outlets' reports and their claims about impartiality are primary evidence of what they published, not independent verification of the events they describe. [ 1 ] Reporting and election coverage In July 2025, Associated Press Electionwatch invited members to participate in polling about presidential and Senate elections. A follow-up post gave four ticket totals and cautioned that the sample was not precisely representative because some supporters were inactive in the main nUSA community. The outlet described the polling as run by Columbia Media Group and later as part of that group; the posts do not constitute certified election returns. [ 2 ] News outlets also organized candidate coverage. On 26 June 2025, FTN News and Reuters advertised a presidential debate for 30 June and solicited audience questions. On 9 November, a post under *The Hill* banner said it had completed interviews with the Pioneer and Forward nominees and planned nonpartisan coverage of the fall election. The archive's posts disagree about whether the June debate took place before or after a candidate withdrawal, so the event is best described as scheduled unless another record resolves the sequence. [ 3 ] Editorial standards and disputes Outlets published both reporting and opinion. A March 2025 FTN article titled “In Defense of Biased News” was expressly labeled an editorial, and its accompanying note said the views belonged to the author rather than the publisher or staff. It argued that partisan articles should be allowed; this is evidence of a debate about press standards, not a binding rule. [ 4 ] In May 2026, an NBN News opinion post criticized Next Gen News and called it a state-media outlet. The post identified itself as opinion and said its claims were not verified reporting. A separate NBN-branded publication called “Fact Checking ACON Files” offered a competing position on a disputed dossier, but its attached pages combine argument and partisan assertions; it should be attributed to the publisher rather than treated as an independent determination. [ 5 ] Another NBN post accused NGN of plagiarism; the export includes the accusation and a named PDF attachment but no direct PDF URL in the message block, so the allegation cannot be evaluated from the available attachment. [ 6 ] FTN News FTN News published election projections and covered debates, political disputes, and Group Management changes. For example, it issued a July 2025 presidential-election projection and separately reported on the proposed sunset of the Board of Governors. These are news items by FTN, not official election results or management orders. [ 7 ] On 12 October 2025, GreatJakers1113 and Jonofdoom announced that FTN would close. They described the outlet as about five years old and as nUSA's longest-running news source, and cited the time required to maintain the company and a revoked DOCAL license. Those statements are the founders' own account of the outlet's history and closure; the archive reviewed here does not include the licensing order. title: Nightgaladeld
text: Nightgaladeld 1st President of nUSA In office 26 December 2012 – 9 June 2013 [ 1 ] Preceded by Office established Succeeded by Moolah60 Presidential Records Nightgaladeld was the founder and first President of nUSA , a United States government roleplay community on Roblox. He held the presidency during the community's formative months and retained ownership of its Roblox group long after leaving elected office. His ownership gave him a role in the group's continuity that extended beyond the formal powers of the President. [ 2 ] Founding and first presidency nUSA commemorates 26 November 2012 as its founding date. Nightgaladeld became its first President during the initial organization of the government. A later presidential chronology dates his term from 26 December 2012 to 9 June 2013. Isner and Jbn011 served successively as Vice President. The first administration established the elected presidency within a Roblox group whose owner retained control over membership, ranks, and the infrastructure in which the government operated. [ 3 ] Moolah60 was elected as the second President on 9 June 2013. Nightgaladeld then served as his Vice President, becoming the first former President to hold that office. The surviving vice-presidential chronology carries his service into late July. Later accounts differ on the authority exercised by Moolah60, Gmf34, and Nightgaladeld during the following weeks; a retrospective presidential chronology describes a brief period of direct rule by Nightgaladeld in August before Marinio took office. That episode is not counted as a second elected presidency in the presidential roster. [ 4 ] On 20 January 2013, Nightgaladeld publicly presented Washington, D.C. and linked its original place. A recruitment notice that day identified it as the group's official city and advertised federal and civilian jobs, including Secret Service, Capitol Police, taxi driving, and White House staff. [ 5 ] Group ownership and later role Nightgaladeld remained the group's owner through subsequent administrations. In 2013, he ordered a restart of congressional elections amid declining legislative activity. The intervention became known in the community as a “Carlos wipe”, after his given name, and was still invoked as a precedent in debates about institutional resets more than a decade later. [ 6 ] On 4 December 2017, Nightgaladeld announced that he was transferring group ownership to developer pauljkl . In his farewell message, he reflected on four years of managing the community and published a list of early presidents and vice presidents. The transfer ended his direct control of the Roblox group, though he remained a prominent figure in its historical identity. The group continued to memorialize him in its public description and anniversary messages; a 2020 presidential proclamation designated “Nightgaladeld Day”. title: November 2024 Presidential Election (nUSA)
text: November 2024 Presidential Election November 2024 Presidential Election Voting 8–10 November 2024 Result announcement 10 November 2024 Certified or announced winner Teasoups Vice Presidential candidate Rathuzen Valid ballots or voters 308 The November 2024 Presidential Election in nUSA returned Teasoups to the presidency. The Pioneer ticket of Teasoups and Rathuzen received 184 votes, ahead of ApolloKorman and MitsuoMochizuki with 82. The FEC and Group Management certified the result on 10 November. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] Campaign The campaigning period opened on 10 October. FTN News reported that incumbent President Teasoups and Nasanovuh had launched campaigns; the same outlet reported a merger of the Plutocratic and Forward parties, with Forward continuing and former Plutocratic caucus members becoming independents. [ 4 ] An 18 October campaign announcement PDF said Nasanovuh intended to run on a Plutocratic ticket, while an Inside Edition News post on 14 October had said that Nasanovuh's campaign was suspended and that he endorsed ApolloKorman. The campaign announcement and suspension report conflict; the timing of Nasanovuh’s withdrawal is uncertain. [ 5 ] By 1 November, news posts identified three major tickets: Teasoups with Rathuzen, ApolloKorman with MitsuoMochizuki, and Forward nominee TradeNato with Razvanpaul. The FEC’s final notice lists TradeNato among candidates who withdrew on 8 November; the results page lists the remaining candidates and their vote totals. [ 6 ] The ApolloKorman campaign received a warning from the FEC on 15 October after a complaint alleged that a campaign leader used Discord announcement channels in other communities to urge members to join nUSA and vote for ApolloKorman and another candidate. Reuters News described the FEC as finding repeated campaign announcements; the linked FEC/Group Management warning itself is the primary source for the commission’s stated action. [ 7 ] During the campaign, Teasoups’s campaign released a defense and military platform. The document proposed changes to nUSA institutions and agencies, including the Department of Defense and intelligence organizations; the proposals did not establish that those changes were enacted. [ 8 ] Election and candidates The 7 November ballot also listed TradeNato, stratnixon, Sheev_Palpatine with AdremiCross, and Joobz2121 with EmperorXD. It described ApolloKorman as independent, while the result certificate labeled his ticket Forward. The certificate did not explain the changed affiliation or stratnixon’s absence from its final distribution. adamsoups appeared in the certificate but not in that ballot notice. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] Voting The election opened on 8 November, with Reuters News reporting that voting would close on 10 November at 3 p.m. Eastern Time. On election day, outlets posted competing calls before the FEC announcement: Fact Feed Network prematurely called the race for ApolloKorman at 1:17 p.m., while The American Times projected a Teasoups win thirteen minutes later. These were media reports and projections, not the official result. title: Party v. Board of Law Examiners (nUSA)
text: 2019 decision invalidating executive control of attorney licensing Party v. Board of Law Examiners Supreme Court of the United States Full case name SheldonParty v. Board of Law Examiners, et al. Docket 07–18 Decided 28 July 2019 Prior proceedings District Court injunction; Court of Appeals vacated injunction Holding Court of Appeals reversed; S. 147 struck down in its entirety Opinion Pitney, joined in full by Holmes, Gorsuch, O’Connor, Stewart and Douglas Concurrence in part Bork, joined by Chase Nonparticipation Brandeis Issue Separation of powers and attorney licensing Party v. Board of Law Examiners , No. 07–18, was a Supreme Court decision of 28 July 2019 invalidating S. 147, legislation placing administration of the Bar under executive control. The Court held that licensing attorneys was an exercise of judicial power and could not be transferred to the executive without violating the separation of powers. It also reversed the Court of Appeals for vacating an injunction without affirmative legal arguments supporting that action. [ 1 ] The case emerged from a class action originally led by J. A. Kirkman. SheldonParty became class representative after Kirkman and the Board sought to dissolve the injunction against the licensing arrangement. His intervention prevented their agreement from ending the challenge to the allocation of power between the branches. [ 2 ] Background The Consolidated Appropriations and Authorizations Act of August 2018 had placed a Bar system within the executive branch. Ultiman v. United States challenged that arrangement, but statutory changes made the case moot before the Court resolved its separation-of-powers concerns. The constitutional issue returned when the Reviving the Bar Act, old S. 147, again placed administration under executive control. [ 3 ] [ 4 ] President Bakedgoods signed S. 147 on 27 April 2019. Kirkman challenged the law on behalf of Supreme Court Bar members. The District Court entered judgment against the arrangement and issued an injunction. Kirkman then helped develop a successor, the Private Representation Revitalization Act, new S. 147, addressing concerns specific to existing practitioners while retaining the disputed allocation of administrative authority. [ 5 ] Lower-court proceedings and substitution Kirkman and the Board sought dissolution of the injunction after the successor measure became law. The Court of Appeals vacated it without a presentation affirmatively challenging it on the merits. SheldonParty, a member of the plaintiff class, sought substitution as representative so that he could continue the appeal. The Supreme Court granted substitution. [ 6 ] A 29 May stay application in In re Kirkman had been denied without finally settling the merits. On 17 June, the Supreme Court temporarily enjoined both versions of S. 147 pending its disposition of SheldonParty's appeal. Those orders formed intermediate stages rather than substitutes for the final constitutional ruling. [ 7 ] [ 8 ] Issues and arguments SheldonParty argued that the Court of Appeals had erred by vacating the injunction without legal grounds and that both versions of S. 147 were unconstitutional. The appeal required the Court to distinguish an agreement between litigants from an adequate legal basis for reversing judicial relief. It also presented the unresolved question from the earlier Bar controversy: could the executive regulate admission of officers practicing before the courts? [ 9 ] The litigation also raised a due-process theory associated with the burdens placed on attorneys. The Court distinguished injury sufficient to establish standing from a constitutional right to practice law. Establishing that regulation affected clients and income did not by itself establish that the Constitution guaranteed professional admission. [ 10 ] Opinion of the Court Justice Pitney held that the Court of Appeals had exceeded its authority by vacating the injunction without legal arguments supporting the action. The absence of a party wishing to maintain the injunction did not answer whether the underlying constitutional defect remained. The Court reversed that appellate disposition. [ 11 ] On the merits, the Court treated admission and exclusion of attorneys as judicial functions. Attorneys were officers of the courts, and control over their admission and discipline was necessary to the administration of justice. Executive selection and regulation of those officers would interfere with judicial power vested in the Supreme Court and inferior courts. The opinion struck S. 147 down in its entirety. [ 12 ] The Court rejected the separate claim of a constitutional right to practice law. Its holding protected judicial administration of the profession rather than removing the judiciary's ability to impose admission standards. Holmes, Gorsuch, O'Connor, Stewart and Douglas joined Pitney's opinion in full; Bork and Chase joined in part, and Brandeis did not participate. [ 13 ] Bork's concurrence Bork, joined by Chase, agreed that executive administration violated judicial power but cautioned against a broader exclusion of Congress. In his view, Congress could regulate the Bar's form and structure so long as administration stayed with the judiciary. His partial concurrence confined the structural objection to the transfer of administration rather than all legislative involvement in professional regulation. [ 14 ] Subsequent developments The case became a central part of the Federal Bar's institutional history. In July 2022, Chief Justice RummyLeroux announced a planned association subordinate to the Supreme Court, combining licensing, ethics and professional development with preparations for paid legal services in Boulder County. The memorandum was advance notice of a forthcoming directive; its significance was the intended placement of regulation within the judiciary. [ 15 ] The 2023 legal reset later voided existing case law and precedent. The 2019 judgment remains part of the historical explanation for the struggle over Bar control, while its pre-reset legal force should not automatically be treated as continuing unchanged. title: Pathwaysbball
text: Pathwaysbball 8th President of nUSA In office 29 November 2014 – 20 January 2015 [ 1 ] Preceded by Aerium Succeeded by Jcmand NARA Presidential Records Pathwaysbball was the eighth President of the Roblox nUSA roleplay community. He followed Aerium in November 2014 and was succeeded by Jcmand in January 2015. Before becoming President, he served as Aerium's Vice President. During his own administration, Jcmand served as Vice President and succeeded him as President. [ 2 ] Vice President under Aerium Pathwaysbball served as Vice President during Aerium's administration. On 9 November 2014, he publicly supported Aerium's Executive Order No. 004, which established penalties for government employees who advertised for political support in agency spaces. The order set out who could dismiss employees, required officials to retain evidence for enforcement, and distinguished public advertisements from private requests for support. Its signatories placed Pathwaysbball among the administration's senior executive officers before he assumed the presidency. [ 3 ] Presidency Pathwaysbball's administration is documented by a law closing the Department of Housing. The measure originated in the House Committee on Abuse, chaired by Jcmand , and described the cabinet post as abused and the department as ineffective. Congress designated it Public Law 9-3; Pathwaysbball signed it, and the measure called for the department's immediate shutdown. [ 4 ] Pathwaysbball left the presidency on 20 January 2015, when Jcmand took office. The NARA presidential records list preserves Pathwaysbball as the eighth President, while the later presidential chronology gives the start and end dates and identifies Jcmand as his successor. The vice-presidential register dates Jcmand's service under Pathwaysbball from 7 December 2014 through the presidential transition, documenting a direct transfer of executive authority within the administration. [ 5 ] In 2016, Pathwaysbball co-founded the Roblox State of Firestone community with FedoraMasterB98, according to the group's description. This later work extended his roleplay activity beyond nUSA. [ 6 ] See also President of the United States Aerium Jcmand Presidential Records (nUSA) ↑ Nusapedia, “President of the United States” , presidential chronology, accessed 30 September 2026. ↑ Pathwaysbball, 8th , NARA Presidential Records; Nusapedia presidential chronology ; NUSA Archives, vice-presidential records . ↑ Executive Order No. 004 (Aerium) , signed 9 November 2014; NUSA Archives, vice-presidential records . ↑ Public Law 9-3, “The Department of Housing Shutdown Act of 2014” , including the bill text and signature link to Pathwaysbball's signing post . ↑ Pathwaysbball, 8th and Pathwaysbball, 8th , NARA records; Nusapedia presidential chronology ; NUSA Archives, vice-presidential dates . ↑ State of Firestone, official Roblox group description .

title: Pauljkl
text: pauljkl is a founder and former owner of the nUSA (Roblox group) whose documented contributions include developing the community's Las Vegas game and overseeing a transfer of group ownership in 2024. Archived group communications identify him as nUSA's founder and describe his work on the Las Vegas city experience. [ 1 ] Founder and game development An October 2017 announcement described Las Vegas as nUSA's primary city and credited pauljkl with updating, maintaining, and adding features to it. The same announcement's author was a Clan Manager, making the statement contemporary praise by a group official rather than a technical changelog or independent measure of the game's popularity. [ 2 ] A 2019 group announcement reported that, after discussion, pauljkl appointed himself to the roleplay Federal Reserve Board of Governors and assigned Federal Reserve Police members a law-enforcement role limited to protecting the in-game Federal Reserve Bank. The announcement described this as being pursuant to Public Law 47-3; it records the group's stated roleplay arrangement, not a real-world appointment. [ 3 ] Ownership handover On 17 January 2024, pauljkl announced that he had agreed to transfer ownership of nUSA to UKR41NIAN and Dilliuss, whom he described as successor co-owners. The statement also said Boulder County and its associated games would be discontinued after the transfer, and framed the change as the end of his tenure as founder. [ 4 ] A roster reproduced in the announcements archive lists pauljkl as “Founder” in Group Management with a hire date of 24 April 2022. Because that roster records an administrative entry rather than the group's creation, it is best read as a dated staff-record field, not as the founding date of nUSA. [ 5 ] The founder's role also touched records administration. A 2020 retirement letter from Clan Manager DevGralius said the archives had been under Clan Management, then relinquished them from that structure to Archivist LargeTitanic2. It said a future Archivist could ask pauljkl or Squareheaddude whether the Archives should return to Clan Management. This describes an owner's role in the governance framework for records; it does not identify pauljkl as the Archivist or as the day-to-day operator of the Archives. [ 6 ] A later Group Management tribute gives one view of the relationship between ownership and NARA staffing. In August 2024, the retirement tribute for TacticalRummy stated that Rummy began as NARA Administrator under pauljkl on 28 February 2022, before being promoted to the Group Manager team. Because this date is retrospective, it documents how the 2024 announcement described the history rather than a contemporaneous 2022 appointment notice. [ 7 ] The records therefore show different aspects of the founder's legacy: an early role in the game's development, authority over a later ownership handover, and a connection to the management structure surrounding archival administration. They do not establish that he continued to hold an operational office after the January 2024 transfer announcement. [ 8 ] Stewardship and succession The January 2024 post characterized the transfer as the end of pauljkl's tenure as founder and asked the community to welcome the new owners. It also framed the group as the result of a long-running community effort rather than a single game project, while specifically identifying the Boulder County project as one that would end in the transition. [ 9 ] See also Washington, D.C. title: Pioneer Party (nUSA)
text: The Pioneer Party was one of the official political parties named in the 2024 MultiBallot redesign of the Roblox nUSA roleplay community. The June design document recognized Pioneer, Forward, and Plutocratic; an October announcement subsequently named Pioneer as the current-government party in a two-party arrangement with Forward as opposition. Later FEC notices document its candidates and leadership changes, though the supplied archive does not preserve the full 2026 platform text. [ 1 ] Formation under MultiBallot Group Management's June 2024 plan said existing and pending parties were dissolved while three chosen parties, including Pioneer, would be recognized. It proposed that party affiliations and incumbency markers appear on ballots and that congressional candidates compete for individual seats. The design framed the changes as making elections more accessible to new members. These are the authors' stated purposes; the document is not an independent evaluation of turnout or representation after the change. [ 2 ] In October, a management announcement said there were then two official political parties. It linked to Pioneer as the “Current-Government” party and Forward as “Opposition”; the embedded invite preview showed a Pioneer server established in June 2024. This is direct evidence of the party's position in that October announcement, not proof that it held a majority in every government body or retained official recognition indefinitely. [ 3 ] Officeholders and limits of the archive An undated compiled presidential-affiliations list calls teasoups a Pioneer. Teasoups is independently documented as President in NARA's roster and signed July 2024 executive orders. Later FEC ballots list a Pioneer nominee as @blanket and an election certificate names the winner as Teasoups; the reviewed records do not include a direct account-identity crosswalk between those labels. The same caution applies to attempts to infer every member of the Pioneer Party from the administration it supported. [ 4 ] The reviewed MultiBallot and October announcement identify the party and its official positioning, but they give no bylaws, candidate-selection record, membership roll, or later dissolution notice. The exact period of Pioneer recognition after October 2024 cannot be fixed from those documents alone. [ 5 ] Election archive additions On 7 August 2024, the National Elections Administrator identified JamesMontagu as Pioneer chairman and reported his call for emergency elections to fill four National Committee seats. At the same time, the FEC listed blanket and Cabot as Pioneer's summer presidential ticket. The FEC later suspended Pioneer primaries and endorsements through 10 February 2025, citing alleged campaigning in a voting area and voter intimidation by party leadership; on 12 January it announced that the sanctions had been lifted. These are the FEC's stated grounds and action, not an independent finding in this article. [ 6 ] Pioneer presidential nominees Rathuzen and Snowbleed won the 16 March 2025 election with 243 valid votes (60.75%); Forward's aConArtist/Frosty_TheSn0wman ticket received 112 valid votes, and the independent FighterHath/warlockings ticket received 45. The FEC's 6 July 2025 certified House results also identified several Pioneer candidates, including ClaireWolfwere, FuriousTurtle06, FlagMan023, ImmortalEthxn, thanhson23464, and brickizpro. These records establish party-labeled candidacies and results, not party leadership roles. [ 7 ] In October 2025, the House announcement named Bathamza as the Pioneer presidential nominee. Bathamza also won the Pioneer presidential primary in March 2026 with 21 votes, ahead of aConArtist (10) and UncleVicent (0). In July 2026, the Pioneer ticket of Epicwarrior_99 and AnthonyRBurgess received 114 votes in the certified presidential election, finishing behind independent jsjsjbsd (131). The FEC's 2026 revamp approved a formal Pioneer platform and scheduled party-chair and committee elections; the supplied FEC-channel export does not include certified results for those party offices.
