title: Plutocratic Party (nUSA)
text: The Plutocratic Party was a political organization recognized at different points in the Roblox nUSA roleplay community. A congressional board listed a Plutocratic Party among official parties in 2024, and Group Management's June 2024 MultiBallot design named it one of three officially recognized parties alongside Forward and Pioneer . SurpriseParty and SheldonParty were leading organizers of a revival around 2016, and the party again held a prominent congressional position during Reset4K’s 2020 presidency. Its successive revivals and later recognition do not establish uninterrupted organization throughout the intervening years. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] Early organization and the 2016–2017 revival The rise of the Plutocratic Party in 2016–2017 followed an earlier organization called Plutocracy. It was already a subject of congressional restrictions in January 2015: Jcmand published a resolution suspending the party's recognition on that senatorial ballot and treating its candidates as independents. His accompanying Senate proceedings recorded the ballot suspension passing with five ayes and one abstention. A separate Plutocracy removal bill passed the Senate but was still awaiting the House. The two actions had different procedural statuses and did not establish a permanent disappearance of the movement. [ 3 ] SurpriseParty and SheldonParty became central organizers of its later revival. In a joint departure statement dated 13 February 2017, SurpriseParty recalled beginning discussions to revive the party a little over a year earlier. SurpriseParty described being its first senator and claimed that within months it had obtained supermajorities in both houses of Congress, breaking a period of Democratic predominance. The statement was signed by SurpriseParty as former chairwoman and representative, Stellaric as former vice chairman and Senate President pro tempore, and SheldonParty as former national campaign manager and senator. Their account identifies the leadership of the revival, while the January 2015 records establish that Plutocracy itself predated that effort. [ 4 ] The party's gains were also acknowledged outside its leadership. In June 2016, Republican chairmanship candidate FallenBrute complained that the Republicans had fallen behind both the Democrats and the Plutocrats, and called for renewed Republican organization. Although written as a campaign appeal, his statement provides a contemporary indication that the Plutocrats had become a substantial competitor to the established parties. [ 5 ] Plutocratic campaigns combined employee rights, executive accountability and private enterprise. Twittered's January 2017 Senate campaign proposed closer scrutiny of executive performance, stronger employment protections, attention to the Justice Department's case backlog, and easier business registration. Both SurpriseParty and SheldonParty publicly endorsed the candidacy. The campaign also exposed differences within the party: Twittered said the party favored leaving the United Nations, but personally preferred renegotiating the United States' relationship with it. A party position and an individual candidate's diplomatic preference therefore did not always coincide. [ 6 ] The February departure statement cited repetitive political activity, declining enjoyment and competing commitments, and stressed that the signatories were leaving party and congressional posts rather than nUSA altogether. SurpriseParty soon returned to parliamentary leadership. The Court of Election Review's certified March Class I Senate results listed SurpriseParty under the Isocracy label with 51 votes, alongside LukeHefner with 50. On 25 April, Vice President Blastatack announced SurpriseParty’s election as Senate Majority Leader and Apolloqi's as Minority Leader. These records show both the organizers' continued participation and the changing party labels under which they served. [ 4 ] [ 7 ] Return during Reset4K’s presidency The Plutocrats again became a significant congressional force during Reset4K's presidency, with SurpriseParty returning to Senate leadership and SheldonParty active in the same political circle. Cooperation was publicly visible in April. On 19 April, Reset announced a meeting with the Plutocratic Senate caucus on a legislative agenda and promised to work with the party to reduce military bureaucracy. On 21 April, he linked the temporary Federal Law Enforcement Training Center to prospective work with the Plutocratic caucus on a permanent institution. On 30 April, GeorgeGodsent announced a planned Congressional Petitions Center in agreement with Senate Majority Leader SurpriseParty. [ 8 ] By June, public discussion reflected a break between Reset and the older party leadership. On 25 June, BernardCaldwell predicted that SurpriseParty and SheldonParty would take the presidency from him, while other participants described opposition within the Plutocratic Senate. These statements show how the confrontation was understood by contemporaries; the formal causes and result of removal were recorded separately in the election ruling and impeachment proceedings. Earlier cooperation with the caucus did not ensure continued support through those proceedings. [ 9 ] Recognition during 2024 The United States Congress board holds a card headed Plutocratic Party in an “Official Parties” list, with a party Discord invite and no completed group link. This records board recognition, not a full constitution, platform, or membership list. Following a referendum, Group Management announced that parties would be disbanded effective 28 April 2024. A new June MultiBallot document then recognized Plutocratic among three selected parties while dissolving other current and pending parties. These sources show how the formal rules could change within months. [ 10 ] The MultiBallot document provided for party labels to appear next to candidates on ballots and proposed individual-seat races in Congress. It did not identify the Plutocratic Party's officers, nominees, or policy agenda; later FEC notices identify its summer 2024 nominee and chairperson. A subsequent October announcement referred to only Pioneer and Forward as official parties. The temporary merger described below helps explain the changed party arrangement, but the available notice gives no formal dissolution date. [ 11 ] People and source limits The retrospective affiliation compilation describes Akacoolguy96 as joining the Plutocrats in January 2024 and GeorgeGodsent and saviorjoshh as Plutocratic. Their presidential articles document their offices, elections, and actions separately. The affiliation claims in the compiled list have no author or attached contemporaneous party certification in the reviewed collection, so this article does not infer that their administrations followed a common Plutocratic platform. The party also appears in litigation titles, but a docket title does not establish a case outcome or the truth of a claim involving the party. [ 12 ] Election archive additions In summer 2024, the Federal Election Commission listed GeorgeGodsent as the Plutocratic presidential candidate, with a vice-presidential candidate displayed as a deleted account. The same ballot listed Pioneer’s blanket/Cabot ticket and independent 24craft. On 7 August, the National Elections Administrator reported that Nasanovah had won the Plutocratic chairperson election after the opposing candidate conceded. [ 13 ] On 10 October 2024, Group Management and the FEC ordered a temporary merger of Plutocratic into Forward after the parties reported difficulty gaining members. The order allowed four days for Plutocratic members to join Forward, named Mr_Choo as chairman and RobertTLincoln as vice chairman, and made sitting Plutocratic-caucused members of Congress independent. The announcement did not give an end date for the temporary merger. A 2025 announcement later described Forward and Pioneer as the two official parties, but did not state when Plutocratic's official recognition ended or whether the party had been revived. title: Political parties in nUSA
text: Political parties in nUSA have organized presidential and congressional campaigns in the Roblox nUSA roleplay community, but their permitted forms have changed repeatedly. The surviving record documents parties modeled on American politics, periods of independent candidacies, a management ban and conditional restoration, and a 2024 system that recognized three new official parties. Party names, affiliations, and elections in this article refer to the roleplay community, not the real United States. [ 1 ] Early parties and American-party names By September 2017, President BUDDHA publicly encouraged involvement in nUSA parties and named both the Isocracy Party and a Republican Party account. He described Isocracy as moderate and the Republicans as conservative-leaning. His message also promoted a political action committee, Right to Rise. It illustrates the variety of formal and informal organizing then visible, although the message does not establish each group's legal status or full membership. [ 2 ] An October 2018 announcement said a Constitution Party had merged into the Republican Party and anticipated a two-party system of Republicans and Democrats . This was a contemporary announcement of a merger, rather than proof that all later groups calling themselves “Constitutionalist” were the same organization. In 2019 and 2020, election records identified JamesMontagu and BernardCaldwell as Constitutionalist presidential candidates, while other certified candidates appeared under Republican and Democratic labels. [ 3 ] The party label attached to a President can be less certain than the office. An undated list linked from an unofficial Nusapedia presidency page assigns affiliations to many early presidents, but numerous entries say “need source,” and the document's plain-text export contains no author or revision history. This wiki therefore uses dated campaign notices and Federal Election Commission (FEC) certificates when possible, and treats the compiled affiliations as leads where those records are missing. [ 4 ] Bans, restoration, and the 2024 referendum An October 2023 Group Management roadmap said parties had previously been banned because of problems they caused within the community. It proposed reconsidering them after three months of improved conduct, including fewer early resignations, less misuse of office against rivals, and cooperation with moderation. Proposed restrictions included FEC administration of party primaries and a ban on names matching real-world parties. This was a conditional proposal, not a document proving restoration happened in October. [ 5 ] On 20 January 2024, an announcement said parties were again allowed to form under new FEC regulations. A subsequent referendum changed that position: an April 2024 results post reported 167 participants and 102 votes in favor of removing parties, and Group Management announced that parties, PACs, and attempted substitutes would be disbanded effective 28 April at 8:59 p.m. The announcement established a rule for that period, not a permanent end to political organization. [ 6 ] MultiBallot and later party system In June 2024, Group Management's MultiBallot document recognized three official parties: Forward , Pioneer , and Plutocratic . It stated that existing and pending parties were dissolved and that additional parties would violate community rules. The same proposal displayed party labels and incumbency on ballots, assigned individual congressional seat races, and moved ballot-access petitions into the game. These were the design's stated rules and aims; the document alone does not establish how uniformly they were enforced. [ 7 ] By October 2024, another official message called Pioneer the current-government party and Forward the opposition, saying there were two official parties at that time. This differed from the June three-party design, and the reviewed announcement does not explain when or why Plutocratic lost that position. Earlier congressional board cards had also listed Publican and Reformist among “Official Parties,” illustrating that the label described different sets of groups at different moments. [ 8 ] Reading the archive The FEC, congressional board, Discord announcements, and NARA roster serve different purposes. A certified election result supports an electoral affiliation; an official-party card supports recognition at the time it was filed; a later roster supports succession; and a member's public statement supports what that person claimed. None automatically proves a platform, membership list, or uninterrupted party existence. The elections overview and individual President articles give the election-specific context behind the affiliations discussed here. [ 9 ] Election archive additions A 23 October 2025 announcement described Pioneer and Forward as the two official parties and named Bathamza (Pioneer) and ArmanFoley (Forward) as their presidential nominees. The statement also left a route for independent candidates, so “two official parties” did not mean independent candidacies were barred. In May 2026, the FEC began a further revamp of those two parties, canceled scheduled party elections, preserved memberships and congressional caucuses, and provided for interim chair and vice-chair leadership while formal platforms were prepared. In June, the FEC announced that the Forward and Pioneer platforms had been approved as official governing documents and scheduled elections for party chairs and committees. The archive contains the election call but not certified chair or committee results. [ 10 ] 2024 FEC election records The July 2024 presidential ballot provides dated candidate-level evidence for the party labels then in use: `@blanket` ran with `@cabot` under Pioneer, GeorgeGodsent ran under Plutocratic, and `@24craft` was listed as Independent. The November presidential result certificate instead identifies a Pioneer ticket of Teasoups and Rathuzen and a Forward ticket of ApolloKorman and MitsuoMochizuki, alongside two independent candidates. These election records show the labels used on those ballots and do not by themselves establish each party’s full membership or platform. [ 11 ] On 23 October, an election notice said presidential and congressional party primaries were underway and labeled Pioneer the “Current-Government” party and Forward the “Opposition.” These labels describe the notice’s framing at that date; the same archive’s July ballot had also listed the Plutocratic Party, and the notice does not explain Plutocratic’s status change. title: President of the United States
text: The President of the United States is the chief executive of the United States . The President appoints executive officials, issues executive orders, signs or vetoes legislation, and represents the country in foreign affairs. Presidents enter office through election or succession from the vice presidency. The office's authority has developed under successive constitutions and is limited by Congress, the judiciary, and Group Management . [ 1 ] The presidential succession is numbered through the 59th presidency, held by jsjsjbsd . Separate presidencies of the same person receive separate numbers; BernardCaldwell , Dralian , Bakedgoods , TacticalRock101 , and teasoups have held office more than once. The numbering contains an unresolved duplication: both teasoups and Rathuzen are designated the 54th President. [ 2 ] Origins and the first administrations The United States was founded by Nightgaladeld on 26 November 2012, and Nightgaladeld became its first President. From the beginning, the presidency existed alongside the separate authority of ownership and management. In December 2017, ownership transferred to pauljkl. Presidential leadership and control of the country's governing infrastructure therefore remained distinct sources of authority. [ 3 ] The early succession passed from Nightgaladeld and Moolah60 through Marinio , three separate presidencies of Lumidas , and two of Zeyad567 . SuddenRush12G served two consecutive terms in 2016, reorganizing federal agencies and security functions through executive orders. TimGeithner , the 19th President, developed recordkeeping systems and repeatedly revised the intelligence establishment during his 2018 term. Agency organization and administrative reform became recurring concerns of the early presidency. [ 4 ] By 2017, the presidency formed part of an active political system encompassing campaigns, Congress, law-enforcement agencies, and political parties. BUDDHA encouraged participation in parties, including Isocracy and the Republicans. His use of the presidential title does not align with the later numbered succession, leaving his position in the chronology disputed. [ 5 ] Elections, terms, and succession Presidential elections are administered by the Federal Election Commission (FEC) and its National Elections Administrator . The Fall 2019 election plan specified a four-month term, from 21 November 2019 to 21 March 2020. The FEC certified JamesMontagu as the winner, but an eligibility injunction prevented him from qualifying immediately. His inauguration proceeded in November. The episode illustrated the distinction between winning an election, qualifying for office, and assuming the presidency. [ 6 ] Vice-presidential succession has repeatedly maintained executive leadership between elections. Smallchomama1234 was sworn in for a brief interim period on 21 July 2019 after Bakedgoods resigned and before Josh's expected oath. Technozo , elected Vice President in 2020, later became President. Subsequent holders of the presidency included former vice presidents Lacryma , LordDeathTheReaper , Rathuzen , and snowbleed . The circumstances and precise dates of some transitions remain uncertain. [ 7 ] The presidency has operated under several party systems. Republican, Democratic, and Constitutionalist tickets contested elections between 2018 and 2021. After periods of restrictions on party activity, an official-party system established in 2024 recognized Forward, Pioneer, and Plutocratic. By October, only Pioneer and Forward retained official status. These changes altered the organizations through which candidates campaigned and presidents built political support. [ 8 ] Executive authority in practice Appointments, staffing rules, and executive orders give presidents substantial influence over the operation of the federal government. Dralian introduced executive-employee participation measures and a petition system in 2019. SpeakerJosh issued orders concerning executive blacklists and official communications. JamesMontagu established the Bureau of Internal Affairs and imposed a temporary hiring freeze. Through these measures, presidents directed personnel policy, internal oversight, and communication across executive agencies. [ 9 ] Executive orders have also addressed emergency powers and the machinery of government. Reset4K issued a broad series of administrative measures in 2020. During Bakedgoods 's second presidency in 2022, an order created a Federal Combatant Coordinator and invoked temporary martial law during an invasion. In 2024, GeorgeGodsent ended executive-branch blacklists, established commissions to review legal codes and clemency requests, and prohibited agency use of the Cipher service. teasoups subsequently established a Federal Register and reporting procedures. Successive administrations thus reshaped the executive branch through both emergency measures and administrative reform. [ 10 ] Legislation and diplomacy are central parts of presidential activity. JamesMontagu exercised both the veto and the power to sign legislation, including a veterans' observance act. SpeakerJosh and Congress issued statements during conflicts with Russia in 2019. Such episodes placed the President at the center of legislative disputes and the public presentation of foreign policy. [ 11 ] Constitutional and management limits The constitutional basis of presidential authority has changed repeatedly. The 2017 Constitution was superseded; a new framework followed the legal reset of 2023 , another Constitution was announced as passed in 2024, and an earlier text was readopted in 2025. These changes make constitutional powers and restrictions dependent on the period in which a President served. Under the 2023 framework, the National Archives and Records Administration had public-record duties but remained under Group Management oversight. [ 12 ] Group Management has exercised authority over the legal and political framework within which presidents govern. In July 2023, it voided existing federal laws, judicial precedent, and congressional resolutions, followed by a new Constitution and archival directives. In 2024, it ordered political parties disbanded after a referendum, then selected new official parties through MultiBallot. Presidential authority has therefore been shaped by management intervention as well as constitutional revision, legislation, and judicial decisions. [ 13 ] Conflict, removal, and continuity Impeachment, resignation, eligibility disputes, and management intervention have each interrupted or threatened presidential tenure. The House voted to impeach BernardCaldwell in July 2018 over allegations involving appointments and conduct; a final Senate conviction is not established. Lordsights faced impeachment proceedings and later announced his resignation. JamesMontagu encountered an eligibility injunction following the 2019 election and a management blacklist in January 2020. The blacklist was reversed after a hearing, allowing him to serve the remainder of his term. [ 14 ] In February 2024, Group Management removed Akacoolguy96 and imposed a one-month blacklist; Robbiebeastpro90000 was then named acting President. GeorgeGodsent resigned later in 2024, although the exact date and reason remain uncertain. In 2026, two resolutions proposing the impeachment of bathamza failed. Their allegations did not result in an impeachment conviction. [ 15 ] The constitutional crisis of May 2025 disrupted the impeachment proceedings against Rathuzen . Ownership stated that the Chief Justice had been expelled during the trial, two other justices had been blacklisted, and a remaining justice had refused to certify the impeachment. The question was referred to a District Court panel, and Rathuzen remained President pending its decision. This interim arrangement preserved his tenure while the validity of the proceedings remained unresolved. [ 16 ] Alongside contested changes of government, scheduled inaugurations in 2020, 2021, and 2025 provided a regular means of transferring executive authority. Vice-presidential succession, election administration, and judicial proceedings offered different mechanisms for maintaining continuity. NARA's presidential collections and the later Public Law Database supported the preservation of executive and legislative acts across administrations. [ 17 ] Presidential transitions in 2025 The presidential transitions of 2025 combined scheduled elections with an unresolved impeachment dispute. The FEC declared Rathuzen and snowbleed President-elect and Vice President-elect in March, and they were publicly identified as President and Vice President on 23 March. Rathuzen remained in office during the impeachment dispute in May. In July, the FEC certified aConArtist as the 56th President, and an inaugural notice paired him with Vice President-elect TacticalRock101 . The later numbered succession instead places snowbleed 55th, Mallsoft 56th, and aConArtist 57th; the discrepancy and the date of Mallsoft's accession remain unresolved. Bathamza was certified as the 58th President-elect in November and was publicly reported sworn in on 22 November alongside Vice President aConArtist. [ 18 ] The 2026 presidential transition The Spring 2026 presidential election produced conflicting results. The scheduled term ran from 21 March to 21 July. On 14 March, the FEC certified Warlockings and vice-presidential candidate Epicwarrior_99 , reporting 98 votes for Warlockings and 90 for Bathamza . An internal review published by American_Online on 16 March reported that a blind re-filter changed the totals to 117 for Bathamza and 109 for Warlockings. The correction notice listed changes to voter status without a candidate tally, leaving the certifications and reported recount unreconciled. On 8 June, Bathamza issued a resignation statement naming jsjsjbsd as the leader of the next administration. Contemporary news reports stated that Bathamza's election to the Senate vacated the presidency and that Vice President jsjsjbsd succeeded him, with an oath still pending. [ 19 ] [ 20 ] The FEC certified jsjsjbsd as President-elect on 16 July, reporting 131 votes for him in the Summer 2026 election. It announced 297 ballots cast and 254 valid, although the three published ticket totals added to 250. The next term was scheduled for 21 July–21 November. Because jsjsjbsd's ticket had appeared on the ballot without a vice-presidential candidate, a 22 July notice called for a vice-presidential nomination. The date of his inauguration for the new term and the outcome of that nomination remain unconfirmed. On 14 September, the FEC opened campaigning for the November election, with registration and voting details to follow. [ 21 ] Numbered succession, 2012–2018 Dates of service follow the cited presidential chronology and contemporary succession notices. Dates of accession, inauguration, and the scheduled term can differ; disputed or incomplete transitions are qualified below. [ 22 ] The first nineteen numbered presidencies covered sixteen people. Lumidas held three separate numbered presidencies and Zeyad567 two. Moolah60 is designated the second President, although his presidency was omitted from an early succession list. title: Presidential Records (nUSA)
text: The Presidential Records board is a Trello collection linked from the NARA Hub for records associated with the President and Vice President in the nUSA roleplay community. The hub calls its link “Presidential Archives,” while the accessible board is titled “Presidential Records.” It is an organized roleplay collection, not an archive of the real U.S. presidency. [ 1 ] Board organization The board separates materials into lists for executive orders, memoranda, national-security presidential memoranda, presidential decision and review directives, proclamations, signing statements and veto messages, and pardons. A separate “Translated” list and a “Research” list distinguish those holdings from the main instrument categories. List placement records the board’s cataloguing scheme; it does not by itself show that a document is an original, an operative instrument, or a complete record. [ 2 ] The board also has lists for presidents and vice presidents and for Presidential Libraries. A card titled “NARA Presidential Libraries” describes a library function and assigns archival roles in its own board snapshot. Personnel and descriptions on such cards can change; they are not a basis for an undated account of current officeholders. [ 3 ] Library and community records In December 2025, a NARA server announcement invited participants to share historical items and stories, submit complaints, record oaths, and allow former presidents and the sitting President to submit documents to presidential libraries. This describes public-facing functions announced for the community server, not proof that all former administrations’ records were collected. [ 4 ] Board scope and archival caveats The board export reviewed for the archive research snapshot contained 14 lists and 376 cards. The lists separate executive materials by document type and add distinct “Translated” and “Research” areas. Those categories preserve context about how an item was stored or presented, but they do not establish whether a translation is authoritative, whether a research copy is an original, or whether the board contains every record from an administration. [ 5 ] NARA’s August 2024 monthly update offers a dated example of the records breadth the project reported: it listed one public law, four executive orders, and six Supreme Court opinions for July, alongside presidential resignation and succession events. This connects the presidential collection to a wider government recordkeeping program, but the monthly post does not inventory what was stored in each Trello list. [ 6 ] The December 2025 server announcement describes a later public submission route for Presidential Library materials. It asks former presidents and the sitting President to open an inquiry ticket to submit historical documents, with access roles granted through that process. This source documents the announced intake procedure rather than completed library holdings. [ 7 ] The board’s collections sit alongside the broader records network linked by the NARA Hub . Executive materials may relate to legislative and court records indexed elsewhere, but the boards remain distinct collections. See Public Law Database (nUSA) and NUSA archival policy . title: Presidential libraries (nUSA)
text: Presidential libraries (nUSA) are record collections represented in the Roblox nUSA community's National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) Trello system. The Presidential Records board includes a "Presidential Libraries" list with individual library cards for former presidents Timothy F. Geithner, Antonio T. Roosevelt, Reset4K, and LordDeathTheReaper; the cards describe the collections as containing each President's works and say records were transferred to the library under NARA's Presidential Archives division. [ 1 ] Those completeness and custody statements are the cards' own descriptions; the entries do not by themselves establish that every presidential record survives in a public, complete collection. [ 2 ] Trello library records Each of the four library cards names the former President and identifies NARA's Presidential Archives division and library staff as the collection managers. The Geithner card names him as the 19th President; the Roosevelt card names him as the 28th; the Reset4K card as the 30th; and the LordDeathTheReaper card as the 35th. Their titles and numbers are preserved as supplied by the NUSA board and refer to its in-universe presidential sequence. [ 3 ] The cards point to separate Trello pages for the Geithner, Roosevelt, Reset4K, and LordDeathTheReaper collections. The records board also contains a reusable "Template" card for presidential-library items. Its fields ask for a document name, archivist, document type, and document link, with options for Roblox forum, Google document, or another file format. The template indicates how a submission may be described; it is not itself evidence that a particular document was submitted or reviewed. [ 4 ] Community submissions and scope On 28 December 2025, a NARA server refresh announcement invited former Presidents and the sitting President to submit historical documents from their time in office for addition to their Presidential Library. The post said members could request access through an inquiry ticket and also advertised channels for sharing historical stories, contacting NARA, filing complaints, and recording oaths. This shows that submission and community-history functions were being promoted at that date; it does not establish that all earlier library collections were complete or that every submitted item was catalogued. [ 5 ] The available records thus show an intended archival model built around President-specific collections, NARA staff, separate Trello collection pages, and later community submissions. They do not supply a comprehensive inventory of records across all administrations. For the broader record system, see Presidential Records (nUSA) and National Archives and Records Administration (nUSA) . title: Procursive
text: Procursive President of the United States In office 21 March 2019 – 4 April 2019 [ 1 ] Preceded by Dralian Succeeded by Bakedgoods NARA presidential records Procursive was President of the United States in 2019 and a former director of the Secret Service. His brief presidency developed into a confrontation over congressional investigations, executive privilege and the limits of impeachment. The House impeached him on four articles on 31 March, and the Senate convicted and removed him. He subsequently won the invalidation of three articles before the Supreme Court, but the surviving charge left his removal in force. [ 2 ] Secret Service and accession Before entering presidential politics, Procursive rose to the directorship of the Secret Service. Dralian selected him as his running mate, then declined to assume another presidential term. Procursive consequently became President-elect and took the oath on 21 March 2019. His inaugural message promised to preserve the Constitution and defend democracy. [ 3 ] [ 4 ] Procursive called himself the twenty-third President in his oath announcement, while the National Archives' presidential sequence places him twenty-fourth, immediately after Dralian. His accession date is 21 March; the conflicting numbering does not change the order of succession. [ 5 ] Presidency Procursive nominated Bakedgoods as Vice President, and Bakedgoods was sworn in on the day of the presidential transition. Securing the Vice President's confirmation was one of the administration's early successes, but the President faced resistance from Congress and had limited progress on his legislative agenda. [ 6 ] [ 7 ] Around 23 March, the House Foreign Affairs Committee began investigating allegations of denial-of-service attacks and exposure of private information involving people connected with the administration's intelligence community. Procursive declined to comply with a subpoena to testify, invoking executive privilege. Disputes over his appointments intensified the confrontation: critics alleged nepotism in the employment of his cousin on his protection detail and challenged the appointment of JamesMontagu to his White House staff on national-security grounds. [ 8 ] Impeachment and resignation controversy Main article: Impeachment of Procursive The House unanimously adopted four impeachment articles on 31 March. They alleged false arrest, withholding information from Congress, nepotism and a national-security risk arising from Montagu's employment. The false-arrest accusation concerned conduct before Procursive became President, bringing his Secret Service career into the center of the dispute. [ 9 ] Procursive also announced a resignation effective at midnight, then withdrew it before that time. The Supreme Court denied review of the withdrawal on 4 April in Psychodynamic v. Procursive . Five justices joined a nonbinding statement explaining that a resignation could be recalled before taking effect. The episode left the Senate proceedings, rather than a straightforward voluntary departure, central to the end of his presidency. [ 10 ] The Senate convicted him on all four articles and removed him, but did not disqualify him from future office. Bakedgoods was acting as President by 6 April. Procursive challenged the removal, alleging defects in congressional oaths, the Senate trial and the substantive grounds of impeachment. [ 11 ] [ 12 ] Supreme Court challenge The Court heard his case on 17 April and delivered its decision on 7 May. It rejected the oath and due-process challenges but invalidated Articles 2, 3 and 4. Applying the Ichigo standard, it concluded that those articles did not allege legitimate criminal offenses; the withholding-information charge also implicated executive privilege. Article 1 survived, and the Court denied reinstatement. [ 13 ] The result gave Procursive a partial constitutional victory while confirming the loss of the office. His case became an important episode in the history of judicial review of impeachment, exposing sharp differences among the justices over the definition of high crimes and misdemeanors and the extent of the judiciary's authority over Congress. title: Public Law Database (nUSA)
text: The Public Law Database (PLD) is a roleplay records index linked from the NARA Hub . Its Trello board groups records into congressional-period lists and includes dedicated sections for the National Archives and Records Administration, constitutional material, and notes. Its cards preserve bill texts and status descriptions; board organization is evidence of how records were catalogued, not independent proof that every listed measure became operative law. [ 1 ] Trello index The PLD includes older and newer congressional-period lists, including a pre-reset list and later-period lists. It also contains records bearing labels such as active, repealed, void, failed, or archived. This structure preserves legislative history and status assertions side by side; a particular measure should be checked against its own bill or law text and associated record. [ 2 ] NARA-related records illustrate why entries need to be read individually. Public Law 39-5 describes re-establishing an archive group conditionally “if passed”; Public Law 75-1 lists the 2019 reformation measure but marks its attached version archived; Public Law 80-2 likewise marks the Archivist Act attachment archived. Their list locations and public-law numbering do not by themselves resolve passage or implementation. [ 3 ] Earlier NARA entries Public Law 39-5 recounts that an earlier National Archive group, which its author said had kept a record of NUSA events, had closed for inactivity. The proposed remedy was to recreate the group and appoint a chair through presidential appointment and Senate approval; the card expressly conditions those steps on the bill passing. It is therefore a record of a proposed restoration, not proof that it occurred. [ 4 ] Public Law 56-5 describes a “current” NARA “to be revamped” and sets out a wider records role: maintaining passed laws by Congress, executive orders by presidency, Supreme Court and federal-court decisions, and lists of offices and past officeholders. Its organization section establishes the proposed Archivist role, a Deputy Archivist, and staff. The card is undated in its text, so it supplies evidence of a later organizational proposal in the PLD’s congressional-period arrangement but not a firm calendar date. [ 5 ] The newer PLD includes the archived S. 188 and S. 244 attachments alongside these older entries. That mixture makes the database useful as a record of proposals and institutional changes, while underscoring that an indexed law number, card title, and archived text are separate evidence from a signed enactment or demonstrated practice. [ 6 ] 2023 legal reset On 15 July 2023, Group Management declared nUSA federal laws, case law and court precedent, and congressional resolutions, motions, and awards null and void. Its announcement said the Colorado Criminal Code and real-life U.S. Code would apply in the interim. On 17 July, a second announcement released Memorandum #001, a new Constitution, and archival requirements, and directed users to the new NARA Hub and Congress boards. The PLD’s pre-reset and later period lists preserve records on both sides of this break; list inclusion alone does not establish that an older measure remained in force afterward. [ 7 ] Later spreadsheet announcement On 26 February 2025, an Archivist announcement introduced a public spreadsheet intended to track active, repealed, and nullified laws in a structured and accessible form. The announcement described it as replacing or supplementing the earlier Trello index. It records an intended transition and function; it does not verify that every spreadsheet entry was complete or that the Trello board ceased to be available. [ 8 ] The PLD is linked from the NARA Hub and relates to the National Archives Reformation Act of 2019 (nUSA) and Archivist Act of 2020 (nUSA) . Its records concern nUSA roleplay institutions rather than actual U.S. legislation. title: Publican Party (nUSA)
text: The Publican Party appears in the Roblox nUSA congressional archive as an “Official Parties” entry. Its card supplies a party name, a Discord invite, and a Roblox group link. A separate blank template card also bears the Publican title. These cards document recognition and organizational links when they were filed, but do not by themselves establish a platform, leadership roster, or the party's full lifespan. [ 1 ] Congressional-board record The completed party card distinguishes Publican from other entries on the board, including Plutocratic and Reformist cards. The listing describes a party Discord and a Roblox group, rather than a nomination result or an election return. The separate placeholder card shows that the archival board was also used for incomplete entries; an “Official Parties” list location should be read as an administrative classification at the time, not as proof of uninterrupted activity. [ 2 ] Possible presidential association An undated list of presidential party affiliations assigns the Publican label to Robbiebeastpro90000 , whom NARA records as its 50th President. The accessible election and succession records reviewed for Robbie show his vice-presidential and acting-presidential roles, but not a contemporaneous Publican nomination or certificate. The affiliation is consequently a lead from the compiled list, not a verified basis for describing his administration as a Publican party government. [ 3 ] Group Management later disbanded parties after an April 2024 referendum, then selected Forward, Pioneer, and Plutocratic for the June MultiBallot system. Publican is absent from the latter three-party list. The reviewed documents do not establish its exact formation or dissolution date, or whether members continued to organize informally after the change in official recognition. title: Ralphiuss
text: Ralphiuss 38th President of nUSA (NARA roster) In office 21 March 2021 – 16 July 2021 [ 1 ] Preceded by N_ightmarre Succeeded by Guggen_Pierre NARA Presidential Records roster Ralphiuss was recorded by the NARA Presidential Records board as the 38th President of the nUSA roleplay community, between N_ightmarre (37th) and Guggen_Pierre (39th). A separate, undated presidential chronology reports a term from March 21 to July 16, 2021, and the linked vice-presidential roster lists Guggen_Pierre as Vice President under President RalphFoley from March 21 to July 16. The compiled chronology provides these dates, but the reviewed primary records do not include an inauguration or transition document for Ralphiuss. [ 2 ] Presidential record The archived Presidential Records export contains no executive-order or memorandum card under Ralphiuss’s name. The 38th-President card is present in the Presidents list, but has no description or attached document in the export. This leaves the specific policies and actions of the term undocumented in the reviewed archive. [ 3 ] Name in the archival record The board’s action history says the card was renamed from “RalphFoley, 38th” to “Ralphiuss, 38th” on December 25, 2023. This is a later edit to the archival card, not evidence that the presidency occurred on that date. The compiled presidency and vice-presidency lists continue to use “RalphFoley” for the 38th presidency. Together with the 2023 card rename, these records suggest that Ralphiuss and RalphFoley refer to the same roleplay identity, though the reviewed sources do not explicitly document the alias. title: Rapidaax
text: Rapidaax 14th President of nUSA In office 25 February 2017 – 14 April 2017 [ 1 ] Preceded by TheySinned Succeeded by Sufferpoop NARA presidential roster Rapidaax is the Roblox account listed as the 14th President of the nUSA roleplay community. He served from 25 February to 14 April 2017, between TheySinned and Sufferpoop . Four surviving executive orders from his administration addressed employee appeals, access to federal jobs, presidential protection, and veterans' reemployment. [ 2 ] Executive programs On 27 February 2017, an order titled “iWork Program” established a Board of Appeals to review claims of wrongful termination and vote on reinstatement. The six-member board was to be led by the Secretary of Commerce and Labor. The order identified whistleblowing, retaliation, broken written promises, and political activity as protected grounds; it excluded cabinet members, agency directors, and the U.S. Press Secretary from reinstatement by the board. [ 3 ] Executive Order 14-002, dated 1 March, created the HIRE group as a route into public employment. It set eligibility rules for job seekers, including active job searching and a background check, and directed federal departments and agencies to hold at least one tryout or interview each week. [ 4 ] On 8 March, Rapidaax redefined Task Force Kilo as a presidential protection unit under the Department of Homeland Security. The order made it a replacement for the existing Presidential Protection Detail and set out its relationship with the Secret Service. [ 5 ] An order dated 5 April established the Veterans Relations Council and a Veteran Reemployment Program. The program was assigned to the Department of Veterans Affairs and was designed to identify fields of interest, train unemployed veterans, and place participants with federal agencies, municipal services, or private entities. [ 6 ] Succession The presidential chronology records Sufferpoop as Rapidaax's successor on 14 April 2017. Sufferpoop resigned on 21 May, when Blasatack was sworn in as his successor. title: Rathuzen
text: Rathuzen 54th President of nUSA (NARA roster) In office 23 March 2025 – 2025 (departure date uncertain) [ 1 ] Preceded by teasoups Succeeded by snowbleed NARA Presidential Records roster Rathuzen is listed by the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) as the 54th President of the nUSA roleplay government. He was announced as President-elect Teasoups's Vice President-elect in November 2024 and was publicly inaugurated as President on March 23, 2025. NARA's roster also records him as the 64th Vice President, while its list contains another President card labeled “54th” for Teasoups; the surviving records do not explain the duplicated presidential ordinal or the vice-presidential numbering. [ 2 ] Vice presidency and inauguration Rathuzen, labelled Vice President, is visible in the seats at the right of a White House ceremony. The display beside the stage refers to a presidential election; the screenshot does not establish its date. An announcement on November 10, 2024, said President Teasoups and Vice President-elect Rathuzen would be sworn in on November 23. Teasoups's Executive Order 008, issued on November 23, identified the date as the start of that administration's second term. NARA's roster lists Rathuzen separately as the 64th Vice President, but the available announcement and roster card do not include the oath text or explain the ordinal. [ 3 ] The owner-affiliated announcements archive publicized Rathuzen's presidential inauguration on March 23, 2025, and another same-day post congratulated “President of the United States Rathuzen.” A following post identified snowbleed as Vice President. NARA's roster lists Rathuzen as the 54th President. The reviewed records do not provide a certified result or a primary document describing the mechanism by which he became President. [ 4 ] Executive orders The NARA Presidential Records board preserves five Rathuzen orders under card identifiers 55-001 through 55-005. Their attached texts use Federal Register executive-order numbers 012 through 016, a difference in numbering the archive does not explain. [ 5 ] Executive Order 012, “Fair Recruitment System,” dated March 25, 2025, directed agencies to use hiring standards that did not require prior experience for lower-ranking or non-terminating positions. It encouraged transparent criteria, feedback, and appeals and prohibited discrimination on listed protected grounds. It assigned the Department of Commerce and Labor responsibility for collecting employment procedures and establishing an appeals system. [ 6 ] Executive Order 013, dated April 21, directed the Department of Homeland Security to audit federal law-enforcement agencies. The prescribed primary audits covered events, promotions, internal affairs, activity, and forward plans; optional secondary audits could cover policy changes, joint events, and training. Findings were to be sent to DHS and the White House, with public release left to the discretion of the President and DHS Secretary. [ 7 ] Three orders dated May 12 addressed law-enforcement conduct and employment. Executive Order 014 prohibited “door cuffing,” “cuff rushing,” and taser spamming, while permitting door blocking only during active protective or security details by specified protective agencies; it provided for suspension or termination for violations. Executive Order 015 restricted on-duty political discussion, advocacy, and endorsements by federal officers and prohibited using federal employment for political advantage. Executive Order 016 required federal agencies to verify that new hires held at least the group rank of “American Citizen”; people still undergoing immigration were not to be hired until verified. The orders assigned reporting and enforcement functions to the Department of Homeland Security's investigations office, with agency-level discipline described in the texts. [ 8 ] Impeachment and constitutional dispute In a May 20, 2025, message to the community, the owner said the President's impeachment trial had been disrupted when the Chief Justice was expelled and two Associate Justices were blacklisted, and that Justice RummyLeroux had refused to certify the impeachment. The owner described the situation as a constitutional crisis and referred the dispute to a three-judge District Court panel, stating that Rathuzen would remain President unless the court decided otherwise. On 23 May, the panel held that the trial's presiding-justice succession was defective, ordered a new Senate vote, and stayed its order until a Chief Justice or eligible acting successor could be seated. The opinion did not decide the underlying allegations. [ 9 ] On May 26, an owner-affiliated announcement said an attached formal letter addressed events “concerning the 25th Amendment,” actions by the Vice President and Cabinet, and the legal standing of President Rathuzen. The archived announcement does not reproduce the letter's contents; it establishes that the matter remained a public subject of dispute, but not the letter's conclusions or the eventual outcome. [ 10 ] Presidential ordinal NARA's Presidential Records board contains both “Rathuzen, 54th” and “Teasoups, 54th.” Teasoups's November 23, 2024, Executive Order 008 calls itself the beginning of that administration's second term, and its attached text was signed by Teasoups as President; the March 2025 announcements identify Rathuzen as the incoming President. The sources reviewed do not state whether the duplicate 54th is an error or reflects the archive's counting method. This article therefore uses NARA's labels as roster entries, without treating the ordinal as a settled chronology. [ 11 ] 2025 FEC election records The FEC's March 2025 ballot listed Rathuzen and snowbleed as the Pioneer Party ticket. Its 16 March results notice reported 60.75% for the pair and declared them President-elect and Vice President-elect, with 23 March as the scheduled start of the term. On 23 March, an owner-affiliated post announced that Rathuzen's inauguration was happening, and later posts identified him as President and snowbleed as Vice President. These records support the announced transition but do not include the oath text. On 20 May, ownership stated that Rathuzen remained President during the impeachment dispute; the District Court's 23 May opinion later ordered a fresh Senate vote while staying the order until a lawfully seated presiding justice was available. title: RealDralian
text: Dralian 23rd President of nUSA (NARA roster) In office 15 January 2019 – 21 March 2019 [ 1 ] Preceded by Frosty_TheSn0wman Succeeded by Procursive 36th President of nUSA (NARA roster) In office 29 January 2021 – 7 February 2021 [ 1 ] Preceded by LordDeathTheReaper Succeeded by N_ightmarre NARA Presidential Records roster Dralian (also known as realDralian ) was recorded by the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) as the 23rd president of the nUSA roleplay community. Contemporary Discord records identify him as president by January 20, 2019; he said on March 13 that he would not seek another term, and the archive announced his successor’s oath on March 21. The surviving record does not establish the exact date he first assumed office. The presidential ordinal is disputed: NARA’s roster calls Dralian the 23rd president, while the oath post by his successor, Procursive, also identifies Procursive as the 23rd. [ 2 ] Election and transition The January 2019 transition followed President Frosty_TheSn0wman ’s announcement that his resignation would take effect at midnight on January 15. Dralian was identified as President in a January 20 notice inviting members to watch his first address to Congress. These posts place him in office by January 20, but do not record his oath or specify whether he became President immediately when Frosty’s resignation took effect. [ 3 ] On February 18, an election announcement named Republican Dralian and independent candidate DevGralius on the ballot for the 2019 Winter Election for President. The surviving announcement establishes that Dralian was a candidate, but the reviewed election records do not include a certified result or explain the relationship between that election and the presidential transition already recorded in January. [ 4 ] On March 13, a post attributed to Dralian thanked the community for what he described as progress over the prior two months and expressed excitement for the future. A follow-up message clarified that he was declining to seek another term, rather than resigning immediately, and said Procursive would be the next President. The archive then announced that Procursive had been sworn in on March 21. The oath post reproduced in the channel identifies Procursive as the 23rd President, creating an unresolved disagreement with NARA’s roster entry for Dralian. [ 5 ] Administration A surviving notice from February 2 records an unusually forceful announcement about the Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA): Dralian said it “no longer exists,” directed that team members be arrested, and warned that anyone found on the team would be banned. The archived statement does not include a separate order, its rationale, or evidence that arrests or bans followed. It therefore documents what the President announced, rather than the implementation or consequences of the directive. [ 6 ] Other posts document efforts to organize the executive branch and create public channels for engagement. On February 19, Dralian required federal employees to join an Executive Branch Discord within 48 hours or risk losing their jobs. On February 27, he announced the White House’s “We the People” petition system, saying that petitioners who reached a signature threshold were guaranteed a response. The source describes the announced rules and purpose, but does not preserve the threshold or a record of the system’s subsequent operation. [ 7 ] The archive also records several appointments and public events. A February 2 White House post said Dralian promoted LordDeathTheReaper to Admiral of the Navy. On February 19, Vice President Bakedgoods thanked Dralian for selecting him and said he had been sworn in after Senate confirmation. Dralian announced a State of the Union address for March 2; the archive confirms the event was publicized and the address was held, but the linked speech itself is not reproduced in the reviewed record. [ 8 ] Judicial nominations and later service In the final days of his presidency, Dralian nominated WalterMondale (identified parenthetically as “Dralian” in a court roster) to the United States Supreme Court as an associate justice. The court’s former-member card says the Senate confirmed the nomination 9–3–1 on March 21 and that he was sworn in on March 22, the day after Procursive ’s oath. The same board later listed “Justice Samuel Chase (Dralian)” as a separate associate-justice entry, but the card calls that a “Second Term”; the available records do not fully explain the name and term changes. [ 9 ] NARA’s Presidential Records board also contains a card titled “Dralian | Executive Order #23-001,” marked “Repealed.” The captured board export contains no order text or attached PDF for that card, so its title and later label do not establish what the order did, when it was issued, or when it was repealed. The same board has a separate “Dralian, 36th” President card. A later Discord retrospective lists “Dralian (9 days)” among short presidencies, but does not specify which numbered term it refers to. The later roster entry and nine-day note are treated as a separate second presidency below; the surviving records do not provide enough detail to merge the two terms into one chronology. [ 10 ] The reviewed sources do not establish prior service by Dralian as a senator, representative, mayor, or city council member. An earlier May 2018 Discord poll names him in a presidential debate, and the February 2019 ballot identifies him as a presidential candidate; neither notice establishes a prior elected office or the result of the earlier contest. [ 11 ] Second presidency The NARA Presidential Records roster lists Dralian as the 36th President, after LordDeathTheReaper (35th) and before N_ightmarre (37th). A separate, undated presidential chronology reports a term from January 29 to February 7, 2021. A linked vice-presidential roster places Dralian in that office through January 29 and Guggen_Pierre from February 4 to 7 under Dralian and N_ightmarre; an August 2024 NARA monthly update says Dralian’s presidency lasted nine days. These sources align with the reported dates, although the exports do not include a contemporaneous oath or inauguration record for this term. [ 12 ] The reasons-for-leaving-office list labels Dralian’s 36th presidency “Blacklisted,” but it does not name the authority or provide a date or explanation. The archived Presidential Records board contains a card titled “Dralian | Executive Order #23-001,” but the export has no order text or attachment, and the order number does not connect it to the 36th presidency. The reviewed records therefore do not support attributing a particular policy or blacklisting action to this term. title: Republican Party (nUSA)
text: The Republican Party was a political party label used in the Roblox nUSA roleplay community. A 2017 presidential message called it conservative-leaning and pointed members to a party social-media account. Later election records identify Republican presidential tickets, including those of SpeakerJosh , AntonioTRoosevelt , ArnieVinick , and LeoVinick . The surviving records document those campaigns more clearly than they document one continuous party organization across all the intervening years. [ 1 ] Early public presence and merger In September 2017, President BUDDHA encouraged members to follow the Republican Party account and described the party as conservative-leaning. The message also mentioned the moderate Isocracy Party, showing that Republicans were one of several visible groups. On 7 October 2018, a separate announcement said a Constitution Party had merged into the Republicans and predicted that Democrats and Republicans would become the central parties. It does not provide a merger agreement, membership count, or proof that the projected two-party arrangement persisted. [ 2 ] Presidential campaigns A 2019 administration application called for staffing the incoming Josh/Clutch government, and the archive announced SpeakerJosh as President-elect in June. The undated presidential-affiliations compilation identifies JoshMiIIer as a Republican and says an election certification supported that label; the accessible transition announcements establish the presidency but do not themselves reproduce the certification. In the fall contest, an October 2019 ballot explicitly listed AntonioTRoosevelt as the Republican candidate against Constitutionalist JamesMontagu. Montagu won the FEC-certified vote, and Roosevelt's incumbent term ended with Montagu's November inauguration. [ 3 ] In November 2020, the Federal Election Commission certified Republican ArnieVinick as the winner of the fall presidential election and LordDeathTheReaper as Vice President-elect. In the summer 2021 contest, the FEC certified LeoVinick on a Republican ticket with TimidSoul. Both cases connect the party label to specific certified elections; they do not alone describe a party platform or a permanent leadership structure. [ 4 ] Later status Group Management's October 2023 roadmap for restoring parties proposed that new parties should not use real-world party names, citing Roblox terms of service. The June 2024 MultiBallot design instead recognized Forward, Pioneer, and Plutocratic as official parties. The reviewed records do not establish whether a Republican organization continued outside that official-party framework, so this article describes the documented historical label rather than a current party.
