title: Reset4K
text: Reset4K 30th President of the United States In office 21 March 2020 – 27 June 2020 [ 1 ] Preceded by JamesMontagu Succeeded by Technozo Speaker of the House of Representatives In office August–September 2022 [ 2 ] Preceded by MasonRockefeller Succeeded by GameLab2017 NARA presidential record Reset4K , also known as Reset3634643 , is an American politician who served as the thirtieth President of the United States from 21 March to 27 June 2020. Elected as the Democratic candidate with Technozo as vice president, he defeated incumbent JamesMontagu in the winter presidential election. His administration pursued changes to federal employment, law-enforcement training, military commissions, intelligence administration and executive accountability. [ 3 ] [ 1 ] His presidency combined an extensive program of executive orders with diplomatic negotiations and repeated confrontations with Congress. An initial Senate conviction was overturned by the Supreme Court in April. In June, the Federal Election Commission disqualified him from seeking reelection, and a second impeachment ended in his conviction and removal. Technozo succeeded him before BernardCaldwell won the summer election. [ 4 ] [ 5 ] [ 6 ] Reset later returned to congressional leadership as Speaker of the House in August 2022. During a period of institutional reconstruction, he advocated transparency, a public process for reviewing officeholding bars and renewed participation by returning citizens. [ 2 ] [ 7 ] Presidential campaigns Summer 2019 election Reset contested the summer 2019 presidential election as an independent under the name Reset3634643. He finished second with 137 votes, behind Republican SpeakerJosh , who received 209. Blastatack received 32 and Kind_Yada 13. The Federal Election Commission considered a motion to disqualify Reset, but it failed by one vote in favor, three against and two abstentions. His candidacy therefore remained eligible through certification of the result. [ 8 ] Winter 2020 election In the winter 2020 election , Reset ran as the Democratic candidate against JamesMontagu and a wider field. The certified result gave Reset 277 votes and Montagu 242, a margin of 35. The Commission reported receiving 1,078 ballots and excluding 493 for alternate accounts or failure to hold citizenship. It declared Reset president-elect on 17 February and certified Technozo as his running mate after the required notice to Congress. [ 3 ] The election returned a new president while preserving a scheduled interval between certification and accession. Reset took the oath on 21 March, succeeding Montagu. His administration began with a series of cabinet appointments and measures intended to organize federal agencies and the transfer of executive responsibilities. [ 1 ] [ 9 ] Presidency Inauguration and administration Reset4K, center in the rear row, with government officials in an image published in March 2020. [ 10 ] Reset appointed AlexanderFitzpatrick White House chief of staff on 21 March. KaceyMontagu and largeTitanic2 were nominated and confirmed that day as secretaries of State and the Treasury respectively. TacticalRock101 was confirmed as secretary of Defense on 28 March. In April, iBuzBae became secretary of State and ThePelicanator secretary of Commerce and Labor, both following nominations on 14 April and Senate confirmations on 16 April. [ 11 ] Judicial appointments included AlexJCabot as chief district judge. Reset nominated him on 14 April, and the Senate confirmed him two days later by 16 votes to one. Reset also nominated Tony_Giordano to the Supreme Court on 17 June; the Senate confirmed him unanimously. [ 12 ] Transition planning and executive coordination Reset established a White House Transition Coordinating Council to organize succession planning, prepare briefing material and improve communication between agencies and incoming presidential teams. The chief of staff chaired the council, which included senior advisers and representatives of eligible candidates. A Federal Transition Coordinator was to assemble information needed by the president-elect and serve through the first month of the incoming administration. Selection and dismissal of the coordinator rested with the incoming president, while the outgoing president was prohibited from terminating the appointment. [ 13 ] A separate order created a Homeland Security Council to advise the president on domestic threats and coordinate senior law-enforcement officials. It placed the presidential homeland-security adviser in the chair, with the secretary and deputy secretary of Homeland Security as co-chairs. Its responsibilities included regular meetings, reports to the president and communication during attacks or other security emergencies. Federal agencies were represented alongside municipal and military officials, bringing several jurisdictions into a common advisory structure. [ 14 ] Other orders addressed executive conduct and public communication. His religious-liberty order directed agencies to protect religious and political expression while retaining restrictions on harmful, derogatory or explicit conduct. An announcement policy allowed the president, vice president and cabinet to reserve an important national group announcement for twelve hours during a crisis. Judicial officers, congressional leadership and Management were exempt from that executive restriction. [ 15 ] Intelligence and employee vetting Employee vetting became a substantial part of the administration's security policy. An initial order granted designated agency leaders access to ECHELON and created Special Source Operations within the National Security Agency to examine prospective federal employees. A revision transferred those functions to an Internal Vetting Operations Division within Homeland Security. Employers were to report existing staff for review, while new employees required clearance before beginning their duties. Ordinary applications were to be cleared or flagged within twenty-four hours, with an exception for intelligence appointments and provision for different standards according to the position. [ 16 ] On 16 April, Reset established a six-member presidential commission to oversee the transfer of assets and information from ECHELON. The commission could organize replacement recording systems, administer clearances for the transfer and issue directives to executive departments and agency heads. The president retained authority to appoint and remove its members. The order made information management and classified-material transfers part of a wider reorganization of the federal government. [ 17 ] Law-enforcement training and employment On 21 April, Reset established a temporary Federal Law Enforcement Training Center under Homeland Security. It was to certify federal law-enforcement personnel and publish successful certifications. The president appointed its director and the chair of a School for National and Homeland Security Affairs, which would develop arrangements for exempted agencies. The training center could deny certification but could not directly dismiss personnel from their employing agencies; officers who failed certification faced suspension, and employers were to terminate those who failed twice. [ 18 ] The order initially remained in force until 11 May, subject to presidential renewal. Reset presented it as a trial whose results would inform a permanent institution developed with the Plutocratic caucus. Its examination requirements depended on a further curriculum order, distinguishing the establishment of the training authority from the commencement of every certification requirement. [ 18 ] [ 19 ] A companion employment initiative directed the secretary of Commerce and Labor to develop a United States Employment Center connecting prospective employees with vacancies. Reset intended it eventually to serve as an employment hub for certified law-enforcement personnel. The policy linked wider access to government work with his proposed training system, rather than treating recruitment and certification as separate concerns. [ 20 ] The administration also introduced a White House internship program on 7 May. It provided for twenty interns, with ten to be selected for staff positions and the remainder eligible for further advancement. Duties included tracking presidential documents, assisting departments and arranging authorized tours. Applications were to open every four weeks. Security restrictions limited access to gates and the presidential emergency facilities, and interns had to sign a nondisclosure agreement. [ 21 ] Military organization Reset's military reforms included an order of 19 April standardizing Officer Training School and Officer Candidate School. Programs were to comprise aptitude testing and interviews, instruction and examination in military doctrine, and final processing with published results. An Officer Promotion Review Board chaired by the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff would approve or reject commissions by majority vote. Service secretaries were restricted to direct commissioning of warrant officers, while branch training commands retained responsibility for assessing candidates. [ 22 ] On 13 May, he placed the Coast Guard under the Department of the Navy in both wartime and peacetime. The order cited inactivity and insufficient oversight, assigned administrative and operational supervision to the secretary of the Navy, and provided for Defense oversight when required. It retained the Coast Guard's military ranks, made its commandant and vice commandant members of the Joint Chiefs, and applied the officer-training requirements introduced in April. Maritime protection, rescue and support for wartime operations formed its stated duties. [ 23 ] Clemency, merit and disciplinary powers On 25 April, Reset created a Clemency and Pardon Advisory Board to consider wrongful convictions and disproportionate sentences. A presidentially appointed chair and co-chair would organize review, with seven delegates considering applications. The board could investigate, hear voluntary testimony and recommend relief, while the final decision to issue a pardon remained with the president. Its procedures included majority voting and opportunities for attorneys to submit applications. [ 24 ] His Merit for All order of 30 April created a Merit Systems Protection Board to consider complaints about unfair promotion decisions, abuse and mistreatment of federal employees. The board fell under the training center and consisted of a chair, deputy chair and three members. Its role was advisory: it could recommend action to the president but could not directly intervene in an agency. The president retained appointment and dismissal authority over the board. [ 25 ] The administration also retained executive employment blacklists. An order dated 29 April defined four tiers: three weeks, four weeks, eight weeks and permanent exclusion. Designated senior officials could impose them, employers were required to check the registers before hiring, and an appeal process was to be available through the Executive Office of the President. [ 26 ] Reset separately established the Presidential Medal of Extraordinary Service for exceptional heroism or service, including prevention of foreign or domestic disasters. The order required evidence or supporting witnesses and limited awards to two per presidential term. It prohibited sale or forgery of the distinction and required publication of a transcript or recording when an award ceremony was private. [ 27 ] Relations with Congress and the Plutocrats Reset initially worked with the Plutocratic Party on parts of his legislative and administrative agenda. On 19 April, he announced a meeting with the party's Senate caucus and promised cooperation to reduce military bureaucracy. His temporary training-center proposal likewise envisaged a permanent institution developed with the caucus. SurpriseParty returned to Senate leadership during this period, and a Congressional Petitions Center announced on 30 April was presented by GeorgeGodsent as a joint initiative with her as Senate majority leader. [ 28 ] [ 19 ] By late June, public discussion reflected a rupture with the older party leadership. On 25 June, BernardCaldwell predicted that SurpriseParty and SheldonParty would take the presidency from Reset, while other participants described opposition within the Plutocratic Senate. The earlier cooperation had therefore given way to a public confrontation during the reelection campaign and second impeachment. These assessments concerned the political alignment of the dispute; the legal actions against Reset proceeded through the Commission, House and Senate. [ 29 ] Foreign policy Diplomatic initiatives Reset pursued diplomatic contacts soon after taking office. On 23 March, he met Finland's president and prime minister to discuss a treaty and United Nations matters. The next day he met Bahrain's king and delegates, with Finland's prime minister also attending. These meetings accompanied an agenda of treaty negotiations and cooperation with foreign governments. [ 30 ] War with the United Kingdom Reset4K's announcement of peace talks with the United Kingdom, published on 11 April 2020. [ 31 ] The April 2020 war with the United Kingdom began during Reset's presidency. The United States Military's later account dates the opening of fighting to 2 April. On 11 April, Reset announced that he had spoken with the king and expected a treaty recognizing a stalemate. The military subsequently identified the settlement as the Hillsborough Accords and credited it with securing American sovereignty. [ 31 ] [ 32 ] Russia, Ukraine and foreign security On 21 April, Reset met Russia's prime minister and placed the United States at REDCON2, describing intervention in the Russia–Ukraine dispute as likely. The following day, he briefed the military on attacks he attributed to the Pakistani government and announced American withdrawal from the Russia–Ukraine conflict. In June, he met the Russian president to discuss NATO–CSTO relations and other diplomatic issues. [ 33 ] His foreign-security order of 25 April cited attacks attributed to Pakistani representatives as grounds for stronger domestic safeguards. It regulated the detention of designated foreign threats, required coordination between Homeland Security and Justice, and directed publication of national-security designations. It also restricted unauthorized dealings with foreign representatives, protected invited foreign guests against threats and required executive employees to leave designated hostile nations within seventy-two hours. Ordinary foreign membership was not itself grounds for dismissal under the order. [ 34 ] Impeachments and removal April impeachment and reinstatement An impeachment trial was scheduled for 4 April, with restricted entry to the Senate proceedings and a public broadcast. Following a Senate conviction, the Supreme Court issued an administrative stay that allowed Reset to remain president while his challenge was considered. [ 35 ] The first impeachment concerned alleged witness tampering, obstruction of a congressional committee and conspiracy to impede a law-enforcement officer. On 20 April, the Supreme Court overturned the removal in Reset4K v. United States . It rejected his procedural and political-motive challenges but held that the surviving articles did not allege constitutionally impeachable offenses. The opinion was released on 26 April. [ 4 ] Reelection campaign and disqualification Reset sought reelection in the summer contest. A Fox News debate and town hall announced for 22 May included him alongside NikolaKalinic, RandomBlox and BernardCaldwell. The campaign subsequently became the subject of an official complaint. [ 36 ] [ 5 ] On 25 June, the Federal Election Commission disqualified Reset from the presidential election. Its letter found a violation of Article XII of the Federal Election Regulations and related summer campaign rules. Those provisions governed expenditures intended to influence voting and political advocacy exchanged for money, employment, appointment, contracts or other benefits. The ruling allowed an appeal through the Commission. [ 5 ] [ 37 ] June impeachment and succession Technozo during the presidential succession on 27 June 2020. Aerium published the image at 7:21 p.m. PDT and announced his oath in the adjacent message. [ 38 ] The House approved three articles of impeachment on 25 June, separately from the election disqualification. The articles alleged offers of money to Representative Krenth for an official apology and a Senate seat to Representative Jtdalejr88 for his resignation; campaign funds offered to a potential voter for a Jailbreak game pass; and military authority used to pressure servicemembers to support him. These were the House's allegations; the subsequent conviction notice specified Article I. [ 6 ] [ 4 ] On 27 June, the Supreme Court denied a preemptive stay, finding that Reset had not demonstrated likely success on the merits. The ruling concerned interim relief rather than a final judgment on all three charges. [ 4 ] The Senate convicted Reset on Article I that day, ending his presidency. Technozo took the presidential oath immediately afterward. The succession therefore followed the vice president's accession, rather than a direct transfer to BernardCaldwell, who won the subsequent summer election and took office in July. [ 6 ] [ 39 ] Later career Speaker of the House, 2022 Reset returned to congressional leadership in August 2022, succeeding MasonRockefeller as Speaker. Jtport welcomed him on 22 August, and Reset delivered his own opening address that evening. His speakership formed part of efforts to restore federal participation during the period of reconstruction following Ridgeway's separation. [ 2 ] [ 7 ] In his address, Reset blamed corruption, hostility and the Ridgeway rupture for damage to national institutions, while calling for impartiality and transparency. He proposed an “unbar hub” through which returning citizens could seek a second opportunity to hold office. A further announcement that evening offered a public review process involving meetings with congressional members by voice or text. His attribution of the earlier decline to Ridgeway was his political assessment, while the proposed review mechanism sought to restore participation and make congressional leadership answerable to applicants. [ 7 ] On 22 August, he formally invited the president to deliver a State of the Union address to a joint session of Congress on 28 August. The invitation described instability and rapid changes of leadership and asked the administration to explain its plans for national revitalization. On 25 August, Reset published new standing rules for the House. His office also advertised recruitment for a Capitol Police chief and a channel for direct contact with the Speaker. [ 40 ] His speakership ended in September. The congressional succession places the end of his tenure on 12 September and the beginning of GameLab2017's on 14 September. The circumstances of his departure are uncertain. [ 2 ] Presidential records Reset's presidential papers are administered by the National Archives and Records Administration through the Reset4K Presidential Traphouse. His executive-order series runs from 30-001 to 30-020 and includes a revision of the employee-vetting order. The surviving policies encompass transition arrangements, security coordination, federal recruitment, military training, employment protections and clemency. title: Ridgeway
text: Ridgeway , officially the State of Ridgeway , is a polity and community centered on Ridgeway County . Established on 4 July 2020 under a county charter within the United States , it developed a local government, judiciary, police institutions and a county game. Its original developers were Squareheaddude, devGralius and Pauljkl . Ridgeway separated from the United States during a dispute among its developers in January 2022. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] A Ridgeway County sheriff's vehicle in a promotional image posted by Squareheaddude on 12 September 2020, before the public launch. The county opened to the public on 21 November 2020. Designed around policing and local institutions, it offered an alternative to Washington, D.C. and Las Vegas . By January 2022, the division between Ridgeway's active community and the weakened federal government had become a prominent political issue. The developer separation ended the original three-person partnership, while Ridgeway continued independently. The original developers reunited in January 2024, when Pauljkl returned to Ridgeway after relinquishing ownership of nUSA. [ 4 ] Later relations with nUSA included disputes over membership, a formally declared war in July 2024 and subsequent arrangements for joint events. [ 5 ] [ 6 ] [ 7 ] Origins and development The county project Ridgeway originated as a project by three developers who had previously worked within the nUSA community. Squareheaddude created the map, terrain, vehicles, visual identity and much of the game's visible equipment. Pauljkl and devGralius developed its backend, scripted features and technical optimizations. The partners initially kept development private. Squareheaddude later described a development period of almost a year before release, with approximately three quarters of that work conducted privately. [ 3 ] Pauljkl described the project's purpose as rebuilding the policing experience offered by Washington and Las Vegas. In his account, their older code was vulnerable to exploitation, and a new county game would allow the developers to replace it and introduce different police interactions. Although the developers later disagreed about the distribution of work and the project's direction, their accounts agree on its origins as a joint undertaking with Squareheaddude responsible for building and Pauljkl and devGralius for scripting. [ 8 ] [ 3 ] A later Ridgeway community history dates the beginning of development to July 2019. By September 2020, the project was being publicly demonstrated: on 12 September, Squareheaddude announced a planned weekend stream and warned that the available screenshare places would be limited. A further preview stream took place immediately before the November launch. [ 9 ] [ 10 ] Establishment within the United States Ridgeway's founding charter was adopted on 4 July 2020. H.R. 67, introduced that day by ZartaVex with Risen_Orbs, Libres, JordiHarris and Ridgeway's Developer Oversight, provided for the admission of Ridgeway County within the State of Ridgeway. The congressional archive classifies the measure as Public Law 80-11. It authorized the county to maintain defense forces and allowed appeals from its judiciary to the United States Supreme Court. [ 1 ] The charter defined Ridgeway County as a political subdivision of the United States and designated the City of Milton as its seat. It distinguished the county's local institutions from the federal government while binding them to the United States Constitution. County officers' oaths required them to uphold that Constitution, and eligibility for the County Board included a period of United States citizenship. [ 2 ] Ridgeway nevertheless possessed considerable local autonomy. Its governmental structure included an elected five-member County Board, an elected County Executive, county courts and elected law-enforcement offices. The Board served four-month terms and the Executive a six-month term. The charter also recognized municipal police and fire services, the Sheriff's Office, State Police, National Guard and Law Enforcement Training Center. [ 2 ] Developer Oversight held extensive authority over the project's practical operation. The charter reserved control of groups, records and technical resources to the developers and required their approval for changes affecting game systems. They could veto measures affecting the game or community welfare, and charter amendments required their consent. This made the developers' partnership consequential to both the county's institutions and its continued development. [ 2 ] Public launch and growth, 2020–2021 Paid access and initial reception Ridgeway County opened on 21 November 2020 with an initial access price of 1,000 Robux. The launch announcement introduced the county's separate communications server and promised information about the first Law Enforcement Training Center intake in both the nUSA and Ridgeway communities. The developers invited purchasers to join them for demonstrations and bug testing. [ 5 ] Launch-day access was disrupted by a Roblox purchasing problem. Squareheaddude directed users to a separate purchase experience before joining the main game. That evening, Pauljkl thanked purchasers and said the reception had exceeded the team's expectations. The following day, Squareheaddude announced planned releases of the National Guard and Law Enforcement Training Center alongside fixes for launch bugs. [ 11 ] The price was reduced to 500 Robux on 1 December 2020 and to 100 Robux on 18 January 2021. These changes substantially lowered the cost of entering the county, although access remained paid at those dates. [ 12 ] Local institutions and the federal community Ridgeway's emphasis on county institutions gave its police, courts and elected offices a distinct identity. Its local government operated under a detailed charter rather than functioning solely as another federal city. Law-enforcement recruitment was tied to the county's training system, while public demonstrations, development notices and bug testing helped organize the community around the game. [ 2 ] [ 5 ] [ 11 ] Its association with nUSA continued after release. On 2 October 2021, ShadowCulture explicitly included Ridgeway among the assets moderated by the Coalition Against Abuse. At the same time, the county's own communications and local institutions increasingly provided a separate center of activity. [ 13 ] [ 5 ] That growth did not produce uniform enthusiasm throughout nUSA. In June 2021, GeorgeGodsent argued that Ridgeway was sustaining agencies while the wider community struggled with electoral enthusiasm. Other participants complained about development priorities or preferred the style of the older cities. These contemporary disagreements show that Ridgeway's appeal and its relationship to federal activity were contested well before the developer separation. [ 14 ] Developer separation and independence, January 2022 Breakdown of the partnership The developer dispute involved both the direction of the game and the partners' working relationship. Their published accounts described disagreements over moderation, outside influence, development effort and attempts at reconciliation. Both sides presented the relationship as having deteriorated over an extended period, although they differed sharply over responsibility. [ 3 ] [ 8 ] On 14 January 2022, Squareheaddude issued a memorandum announcing that the partnership should be dissolved. He alleged that Pauljkl had behaved destructively and publicly disparaged his contributions. Squareheaddude also acknowledged that he and devGralius had contributed to the drama and neglected the wider community amid factional conflict. The memorandum rejected their own departure as the preferred solution and promised further updates after the hiatus. [ 3 ] Pauljkl's response attributed the deterioration partly to outside influence and disagreements about management. He argued that concerns had not been communicated effectively and defended his development work. He also disputed the handling of moderation cases, particularly the definition and enforcement of rules concerning transfers of items between accounts. [ 8 ] An edited recording uploaded by Coulter Ellis on 15 January preserves an argument with Pauljkl in which Squareheaddude proposed 40 percent revenue shares for himself and David and 20 percent for Paul. Paul's written response instead said Squareheaddude's proposed arrangement assigned David the 20 percent share; Paul advocated equal 30 percent shares with a further 10 percent reserved for advertising. The participants' accounts therefore disagree about the proposed allocation. [ 15 ] [ 8 ] Squareheaddude also alleged that Paul had threatened legal action and described an unsuccessful reconciliation after Paul's roles were removed. He advocated separating the communities, while Paul referred to an earlier recorded call. The alleged threats remain Squareheaddude's assertions. [ 15 ] Separation from nUSA Political tensions were already public by 9 January. President TacticalRock101 described relations between nUSA and Ridgeway as a “Cold War” and said that the parties had been unable to agree on battles. On 10 January, he resigned, connecting the federal government's difficulties to management priorities and the state of its remaining city. [ 16 ] [ 6 ] The dates assigned to Ridgeway's separation differ. The older nUSA encyclopedia places secession on 9 January and recognition on 15 January. Ridgeway's later history associates independence with the developer separation of 14–16 January and identifies 15 January as the date commemorated by its County Board. Contemporary nUSA discussion includes claims of independence on both 9 and 15 January. The political confrontation, dissolution of the development partnership and adoption of independent institutions were related developments within the same month. [ 17 ] Squareheaddude and devGralius continued the Ridgeway project after the original partnership ended. A state constitution bears a ratification date of 20 January 2022. It provided for a governor, lieutenant governor, seven-member Senate and state judiciary. Ridgeway's community history dates the transition to its state-government structure to 28 March 2022, a later milestone than the date printed on the constitution. [ 18 ] [ 19 ] Relationship to the nUSA activity crisis A user-supplied activity comparison showing 69 players in Ridgeway County and none in Washington, D.C. The visible local clock reads 14 January 2022, 6:21 p.m.; the timezone and original photographer are unknown. The counts represent one moment during the developer dispute. Ridgeway's separation occurred during a wider crisis of federal activity and confidence. In his resignation, TacticalRock101 alleged that management and developers had abandoned nUSA for Ridgeway, that the federal community's remaining functioning city was outdated and that he had received insufficient support to carry out the presidency. These were the outgoing president's criticisms, rather than a technical audit of either game. [ 6 ] On 16 January, Speaker MasonRockefeller described nUSA as severely weakened and approaching collapse. He said colleagues had moved to Ridgeway, American Roleplay and other communities. His proposed response was to consolidate resources and cooperate with the president and Senate leadership to rebuild the federal community. [ 20 ] The contemporary activity screenshot illustrates the imbalance: at the displayed time on 14 January, Ridgeway County showed 69 active players and Washington showed zero. It establishes that contrast at one instant, rather than either game's average population or the direction of every player's movement. [ 21 ] The crisis cannot be reduced to the developer confrontation alone. The discussion of weak electoral enthusiasm in June 2021 preceded the January split, and MasonRockefeller identified several destinations for departing members. Ridgeway's growing activity, disputes about attention to the older cities and the eventual separation formed part of that broader loss of participation and institutional confidence. [ 14 ] [ 20 ] Independent institutions The state constitution established separate legislative, executive and judicial branches. The Senate comprised seven members serving four-month terms. The governor served a four-month term, commanded the state's forces and exercised executive powers, with the lieutenant governor occupying additional legislative and military responsibilities. The constitution also provided for an elected attorney general, secretary of state and sheriffs. [ 19 ] The judiciary included a Supreme Court with a chief justice and four associate justices, together with a Superior Court for civil and criminal proceedings. The Supreme Court possessed appellate jurisdiction and authority over court administration. Constitutional oaths required allegiance to the State of Ridgeway. Developer Oversight retained a role in constitutional amendment alongside amendment by popular election. [ 19 ] The independent constitution thus differed from the original county charter in its framework of allegiance and institutions. The earlier charter placed the county within the United States and provided federal appellate connections; the state constitution organized authority around Ridgeway's own government and courts. [ 2 ] [ 19 ] Later relations with the United States Boulder County and membership disputes During 2022, nUSA developed Boulder County as another county project. In October, Pauljkl described planned features beyond those of the older Ridgeway project, including player-created fires, towing, a casino, vehicle customization, jobs outside formal teams and player-run businesses. He said assembling a development team had taken time. Boulder subsequently opened in November. [ 22 ] Boulder's launch produced a further disagreement over participation in both communities. On 26 November, MasonRockefeller criticized what he called Ridgeway's “Subversion Act” and alleged that it restricted members of the nUSA community. He introduced H.R. 25 to prohibit discrimination against immigrants, including restrictions based on Ridgeway membership. His announcement expressed an intention to secure passage; it does not itself establish that the bill became law. [ 23 ] Reunion of Developer Oversight, January 2024 On 17 January 2024, Squareheaddude announced the reunion of Ridgeway's original Developer Oversight team, almost two years after its separation. He said that the disagreements responsible for the January 2022 breakdown had been resolved and that Pauljkl had relinquished ownership of nUSA to return to Ridgeway full-time. The announcement presented the renewed partnership as a reconciliation between the original developers. [ 4 ] The reunited team divided responsibilities between Pauljkl, who would lead scripting and backend development; Squareheaddude, who would lead game design and graphics; and David (devGralius), who would lead web services and government. Squareheaddude said development had already resumed and that the request to restore access to the game had been submitted. He anticipated reopening within the next few business days and a sequence of updates introducing content planned before the downtime, followed by suitable features from Boulder County. Further announcements about government and departments were assigned to David. [ 4 ] The accompanying questions and answers linked this development reunion to the ownership change in the United States. Squareheaddude said nUSA would return to its original gameplay style under its new ownership, while Boulder would remain down indefinitely and cease to be part of nUSA. He described Boulder's quality-of-life features and backend fixes as resources for advancing Ridgeway. These were the announced development plans; the post did not establish the date of reopening or completion of the proposed transfers. [ 4 ] Pauljkl's own nUSA announcement the same day identified Dilliuss and UKR41NIAN as the incoming co-owners and said the Boulder games would be discontinued after the transfer. The two announcements connected the restoration of Ridgeway's original development partnership with a change in nUSA's ownership and municipal development direction. [ 24 ] The July 2024 war and subsequent cooperation In July 2024, the United States formally declared war on Ridgeway through H.J. Res. 2, signed by President GeorgeGodsent. Management nevertheless recognized the communities' overlapping membership. On 11 July, UKR41NIAN announced that neither community should sanction people merely for belonging to the other, with exceptions concerning personnel who volunteered for deployment. [ 7 ] [ 25 ] President-elect Blanket announced an end to the war on 22 July. The arrangement provided for joint events and allowed United States military personnel to join Ridgeway's State Guard as dual citizens. In explaining the decision, he described the war as an effort to generate activity and criticized the absence of adequate preparations, repetitive raids and the lack of an official battle game. The settlement was framed as cooperation rather than a surrender or a victory imposing concessions. [ 7 ] Connections also persisted through individual officials. In August 2024, an nUSA management announcement praised David's work in its military and public-outreach management while acknowledging that he managed Ridgeway. The separation therefore did not eliminate shared personnel or later cooperation. [ 26 ] Later activity and retained affiliations The Ridgeway County experience page in a user-supplied screenshot reported as captured around 1:30 a.m. Eastern on 1 October 2026. It shows 43 active players and more than 1.5 million visits. A screenshot supplied for 1 October 2026 shows Ridgeway County with 43 active players, more than 1.5 million visits and 12,876 favorites. Its displayed description still labels the experience early access and gives 4 July 2020 as the founding date. The group screenshot from the same reported period displays more than 42,200 members. These figures measure different forms of participation: concurrent players, cumulative visits and group membership. [ 27 ] The affiliates screenshot also shows police, fire, sheriff and law-enforcement-training groups retaining “USA” prefixes. These surviving names illustrate links to Ridgeway's earlier organization, but affiliation and naming do not by themselves establish continuing United States governmental authority over the independent state. He said assembling a development team had taken time. Boulder subsequently opened in November. [ 22 ] Boulder's launch produced a further disagreement over participation in both communities. On 26 November, MasonRockefeller criticized what he called Ridgeway's “Subversion Act” and alleged that it restricted members of the nUSA community. He introduced H.R. 25 to prohibit discrimination against immigrants, including restrictions based on Ridgeway membership. His announcement expressed an intention to secure passage; it does not itself establish that the bill became law. [ 23 ] Reunion of Developer Oversight, January 2024 On 17 January 2024, Squareheaddude announced the reunion of Ridgeway's original Developer Oversight team, almost two years after its separation. He said that the disagreements responsible for the January 2022 breakdown had been resolved and that Pauljkl had relinquished ownership of nUSA to return to Ridgeway full-time. The announcement presented the renewed partnership as a reconciliation between the original developers. [ 4 ] The reunited team divided responsibilities between Pauljkl, who would lead scripting and backend development; Squareheaddude, who would lead game design and graphics; and David (devGralius), who would lead web services and government. Squareheaddude said development had already resumed and that the request to restore access to the game had been submitted. He anticipated reopening within the next few business days and a sequence of updates introducing content planned before the downtime, followed by suitable features from Boulder County. Further announcements about government and departments were assigned to David. [ 4 ] The accompanying questions and answers linked this development reunion to the ownership change in the United States. Squareheaddude said nUSA would return to its original gameplay style under its new ownership, while Boulder would remain down indefinitely and cease to be part of nUSA. He described Boulder's quality-of-life features and backend fixes as resources for advancing Ridgeway. These were the announced development plans; the post did not establish the date of reopening or completion of the proposed transfers. [ 4 ] Pauljkl's own nUSA announcement the same day identified Dilliuss and UKR41NIAN as the incoming co-owners and said the Boulder games would be discontinued after the transfer. The two announcements connected the restoration of Ridgeway's original development partnership with a change in nUSA's ownership and municipal development direction. [ 24 ] The July 2024 war and subsequent cooperation In July 2024, the United States formally declared war on Ridgeway through H.J. Res. 2, signed by President GeorgeGodsent. Management nevertheless recognized the communities' overlapping membership. On 11 July, UKR41NIAN announced that neither community should sanction people merely for belonging to the other, with exceptions concerning personnel who volunteered for deployment. [ 7 ] [ 25 ] President-elect Blanket announced an end to the war on 22 July. The arrangement provided for joint events and allowed United States military personnel to join Ridgeway's State Guard as dual citizens. In explaining the decision, he described the war as an effort to generate activity and criticized the absence of adequate preparations, repetitive raids and the lack of an official battle game. The settlement was framed as cooperation rather than a surrender or a victory imposing concessions. [ 7 ] Connections also persisted through individual officials. In August 2024, an nUSA management announcement praised David's work in its military and public-outreach management while acknowledging that he managed Ridgeway. The separation therefore did not eliminate shared personnel or later cooperation. [ 26 ] Later activity and retained affiliations The Ridgeway County experience page in a user-supplied screenshot reported as captured around 1:30 a.m. Eastern on 1 October 2026. It shows 43 active players and more than 1.5 million visits. A screenshot supplied for 1 October 2026 shows Ridgeway County with 43 active players, more than 1.5 million visits and 12,876 favorites. Its displayed description still labels the experience early access and gives 4 July 2020 as the founding date. The group screenshot from the same reported period displays more than 42,200 members. These figures measure different forms of participation: concurrent players, cumulative visits and group membership. [ 27 ] The affiliates screenshot also shows police, fire, sheriff and law-enforcement-training groups retaining “USA” prefixes. These surviving names illustrate links to Ridgeway's earlier organization, but affiliation and naming do not by themselves establish continuing United States governmental authority over the independent state. title: Robbiebeastpro90000
text: Robbiebeastpro90000 50th President of nUSA (NARA roster) In office 15 February 2024 – 21 March 2024 [ 1 ] Preceded by Akacoolguy96 Succeeded by GeorgeGodsent NARA Presidential Records roster Robbiebeastpro90000 was the 50th President of the United States in the nUSA roleplay community, according to the community’s presidential-records index. The primary announcement reviewed for this article describes him as acting President under the line of succession after the removal of President Akacoolguy96GPT. That distinction is important: the available contemporary notice does not describe a separate presidential election for Robbiebeastpro90000. [ 2 ] Vice presidency and succession Robbiebeastpro90000 speaking in the Capitol chamber during the February 2024 State of the Union address. On December 5, 2023, the Federal Election Commission announced that Robbiebeastpro90000 had won the vice presidency on the ticket with President-elect Akacoolguy96GPT. When Group Management announced Akacoolguy96GPT’s removal on February 14, 2024, it said Robbiebeastpro90000 was acting President under the line of succession until a successor was sworn in. The announcement did not give an end date for the acting service. [ 3 ] The revised Spring 2024 election notice set March 16 as the presidential voting close and March 21 as the planned inauguration. An April 14 public message later stated that Robbiebeastpro90000 remained Vice President “until he resigns officially or” the owner directed otherwise. Together, the records establish his vice-presidential and acting-succession roles, while the reviewed sources do not include a swearing-in instrument or a dated transfer ending his acting presidency. [ 4 ] Executive records The NARA Presidential Records board indexes three documents under Robbiebeastpro90000’s name and the number 50: “Blue on Blue Arrests,” “Establishment/Restructure of the Department of Veterans Affairs,” and “Federal Government HICOM Limitations.” The Trello cards link to Google Drive documents, but the document contents were not accessible in the reviewed archive. Their titles therefore identify archived topics only; they do not establish the orders’ dates, operative terms, implementation, or status. [ 5 ] References 2024 FEC election records The FEC listed Robbiebeastpro90000 as GeorgeGodsent’s running mate in the Spring 2024 presidential election, and its result certificate named the pair the winning ticket with 330 votes. This confirms his vice-presidential candidacy and the ticket’s election result; the certificate does not describe the earlier acting presidency documented elsewhere. [ 6 ] ↑ Nusapedia, “President of the United States” , presidential chronology, accessed 30 September 2026. ↑ “Robbiebeastpro90000, 50th,” NARA Presidential Records Trello card, https://trello.com/c/VlucR9XD/42-robbiebeastpro90000-50th ; Discord #announcements, February 14, 2024, Python splitlines() lines 6273–6285. ↑ Discord #election-announcements, December 5, 2023, Python splitlines() lines 24362–24372; Discord #announcements, February 14, 2024, Python splitlines() lines 6263–6285. ↑ Discord #nUSA-updates, January 28, 2024, Python splitlines() lines 25379–25385; Discord #nUSA-updates, April 14, 2024, Python splitlines() lines 26494–26506. ↑ “Robbiebeastpro90000 | 50-001 | Blue on Blue Arrests,” https://trello.com/c/iqidQgZM/52-robbiebeastpro90000-50-001-blue-on-blue-arrests ; “Robbiebeastpro90000 | 50-002 | Establishment/Restructure of the Department of Veterans Affairs,” https://trello.com/c/oH8buGHJ/53-robbiebeastpro90000-50-002-establishment-restructure-of-the-department-of-veterans-affairs ; “Robbiebeastpro90000 | 50-003 | Federal Government HICOM Limitations,” https://trello.com/c/FShwpaEK/54-robbiebeastpro90000-50-003-federal-government-hicom-limitations . ↑ Discord #election-updates , 12 March 2024, Python splitlines() L1062–1083; FEC, Presidential Election Results , PDF, p. 1 , announced 17 March 2024 at L1180–1187.

title: Saviorjoshh
text: saviorjoshh 52nd President of nUSA (NARA roster) In office 16 July 2024 – 22 July 2024 [ 1 ] Preceded by GeorgeGodsent Succeeded by teasoups NARA Presidential Records roster Saviorjoshh was identified in the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) presidential roster as the 52nd President of the nUSA roleplay government. NARA's August 2024 monthly update retrospectively described his July presidency as six days long, the fourth-shortest in its list. A separately maintained President chronology gives his dates as July 16–22, 2024; the date range also spans six days, but the primary records reviewed do not contain a dated oath or transfer document confirming both endpoints. [ 2 ] Presidency A compiled list of presidential departures dates this term from July 16 through July 22, 2024, and says Saviorjoshh finished GeorgeGodsent's term. A separate compiled vice-presidential chronology dates his service under GeorgeGodsent from April 24 through July 17, creating a two-date overlap with the presidential term. A NARA statement on July 22 confirms that a transfer was underway but does not resolve the overlap or provide oath records. The compiled documents' plaintext copies show no author, publication date, or revision history. [ 3 ] NARA's August 2024 summary places the presidency in July and lists the resignation of GeorgeGodsent , the short tenure of Saviorjoshh, and the inauguration of Teasoups among that month's events. A compiled vice-presidential chronology lists Saviorjoshh as GeorgeGodsent's Vice President from April 24 to July 17; the compiled presidential chronology dates Saviorjoshh's term from July 16 to July 22. Those entries overlap by two calendar dates and are not reconciled by the primary archive. A July 22 NARA statement described an ongoing transition and said the next inauguration was planned for that weekend, supporting the broad timing but not the exact oath dates. [ 4 ] The NARA monthly update ranked Saviorjoshh's six-day presidency fourth among the shortest presidencies in its table, following Smallchomama1234, Guggen_Pierre, and BernardCaldwell. It listed Dralian next, at nine days. The post labels Saviorjoshh “52st,” an apparent ordinal typo; the roster card gives “52nd.” [ 5 ] Executive orders The NARA Presidential Records board preserves three orders under Saviorjoshh's name. Executive Order 52-001, “To Establish Limitations on Blue-on-Blue,” revoked Executive Order 50-001 of March 12, 2024, and set disciplinary rules for one United States officer arresting another while both were on a law-enforcement team. It authorized suspension of up to ten days or termination, assigned investigations to the FBI's Criminal Investigation Division, and provided exceptions for an officer declared “rogue” or reasonably believed to pose an immediate threat to American lives. [ 6 ] Executive Order 52-002 established a Homeland Security Council within the White House, with up to 20 presidential appointees. Its stated advisory function was to address homeland-security matters and improve communication among agency heads and law-enforcement executives; the order named several agency and force leaders for membership. [ 7 ] Executive Order 52-003 required weekly Cabinet reports to the President and White House Chief of Staff. It directed that public versions be released 48 hours after submission with classified information removed, and that relevant unsanitized reports be sent to the congressional Gang of Eight within 24 hours. The order exempted the Chief of Staff, Vice President, and Director of National Intelligence unless separately required by written policy or presidential order. [ 8 ] The three attached texts identify the orders by number and subject but do not show their signing dates in the captured copies. Accordingly, this article does not infer their issuance dates from their card creation dates. [ 9 ] Pardon A NARA board card preserves a presidential grant of clemency signed by Saviorjoshh on July 20, 2024. The document purports to pardon Saviorjoshh himself, unconditionally, for any offenses committed or alleged during 2024 through that date, including conduct before, during, and after his presidential tenure; it also directs the Bureau of Prisons to release him if confined. The available record establishes what the document says, not whether a court or other authority recognized or implemented it. [ 10 ] Succession and ordinal records NARA's August update associates Saviorjoshh's short July tenure with the later inauguration of Teasoups, and its roster separately lists Teasoups as the 53rd President. The primary sources reviewed do not supply an election certification, a presidential oath for Saviorjoshh, or a dated instrument of succession. The six-day duration is therefore attributed to NARA's retrospective monthly summary rather than reconstructed from a complete term record. [ 11 ] 2024 FEC election records The FEC’s 31 March 2024 Senate Class II result notice listed Saviorjoshh first with 44 votes. This supports a short account of his elected Senate service before the presidency. The reviewed FEC presidential ballots and result records do not show him as a presidential candidate in the July or November 2024 contests. [ 12 ] ↑ Nusapedia, “President of the United States” , presidential chronology, accessed 30 September 2026. The chronology ends this presidency on 22 July. The subsequent inauguration of teasoups was reported on 28 July; an oath date need not be identical to a formal accession date. ↑ saviorjoshh, 52nd , NARA Presidential Records board; Discord #nusa-updates, August 1, 2024, Python splitlines() L28974–L29008; Presidential reasons for leaving office , compiled Google Doc. ↑ Presidential reasons for leaving office ; Vice-presidents of nUSA: dates ; Discord #nusa-updates, July 22, 2024, Python splitlines() L28763-L28777. ↑ Discord #nusa-updates, August 1, 2024, Python splitlines() L28974–L29008; Discord #nusa-updates, July 22, 2024, L28763–L28777; Vice-presidents of nUSA: dates ; Presidential reasons for leaving office . ↑ Discord #nusa-updates, August 1, 2024, Python splitlines() L28997–L29005; saviorjoshh, 52nd , NARA Presidential Records board. ↑ Executive Order 52-001 , NARA Presidential Records board, attached PDF, pp. 1–2. ↑ Executive Order 52-002 , NARA Presidential Records board, attached PDF, p. 1. ↑ Executive Order 52-003 , NARA Presidential Records board, attached PDF, pp. 1–2. ↑ Executive Order 52-001 , Executive Order 52-002 , and Executive Order 52-003 , NARA Presidential Records board; captured card creation dates are in July 2024. ↑ Presidential Pardon of Saviorjoshh , NARA Presidential Records board, attached PDF, p. 1. ↑ Discord #nusa-updates, August 1, 2024, Python splitlines() L28974–L29005; NARA Presidential Records board . ↑ Discord #election-updates , 31 March 2024, Python splitlines() L1414–1449; FEC presidential ballot and result notices, July 2024, L3615–3638 and L3905–3919; November 2024, L6135–6159 and L6236–6250.

title: Senate (nUSA)
text: Upper chamber in the federal legislature The Senate is the upper chamber of Congress , alongside the House . It considers legislation, nominations and inter-chamber business and conducts impeachment trials. Leadership, committees and standing rules organize its proceedings. [ 1 ] Chamber records and procedure The Senate has organized membership into electoral classes, including Class I and Class II, and maintained leadership offices including the Senate President and secretary. Standing rules govern proceedings, while agendas and prescribed forms organize bills and simple, concurrent and joint resolutions. [ 2 ] Senate seats have been filled through distinct electoral classes, with certification following voting. In May 2019 the Federal Elections Commission certified seven Class III winners. By 21 July the Senate was led by ClutchAntonioVII; its business included quorum rules and discussion of a proposed NARA Reformation Act. [ 3 ] Senate's role in inter-chamber proceedings The Senate receives articles of impeachment passed by the House. In July 2018, the House forwarded BernardCaldwell 's impeachment for Senate consideration. In October, the Senate took the separate step of lifting his office bar. Referral for trial and later restoration of eligibility were different actions. [ 4 ] The July 2023 reset voided existing federal laws, case precedent and congressional resolutions and motions. A new Constitution and legislative directives followed, permitting normal congressional business to resume under a revised framework. [ 5 ] Archives and interpretation The Congress index provides Senate-floor, nomination, resolution, treaty, impeachment and constitutional-amendment lists, while the Senate-specific board preserves chamber procedures and office records. A draft, floor item, or proposal must therefore be distinguished from an adopted measure; the Congress board separately lists failed items and passed or active records. [ 6 ] Impeachment and reconstruction The Senate's trial of Procursive in 2019 culminated in conviction on all four impeachment articles and removal from the presidency, but not disqualification from future office. The Supreme Court subsequently invalidated three articles and left the remaining charge intact. That outcome exposed the distinction between the Senate's verdict and the constitutional validity of each charge supporting it. [ 7 ] Impeachment did not invariably end in removal. On 22 October 2022, the Senate acquitted Jtport on every charge brought before it. The proceeding occurred during a period of disputes over the chamber's own administration. In September, Secretary of the Senate hankwim55 resigned and accused the President pro tempore of exceeding his authority over proxies, committees and staffing. Those were the resigning secretary's allegations, distinct from a judicial finding. He remained a senator through Jtport's trial and announced his departure from the Senate on 2 November. [ 8 ] [ 9 ] Reconstruction also changed the Senate's electoral arrangements. The August 2022 interim schedule called for ten senators and the replacement of the entire chamber, with voting on 27–28 August. TacticalRummy administered oaths to newly elected senators on 28 August before the State of the Union gathering. The temporary arrangement was part of preparations for Boulder County and anticipated later elections under a new system. title: SheldonParty
text: SheldonParty 18th President of nUSA In office 1 November 2017 – 30 January 2018 [ 1 ] Preceded by SurpriseParty Succeeded by TimGeithner NARA Presidential Records SheldonParty was the eighteenth President of the United States. He succeeded SurpriseParty on 1 November 2017 and resigned before 30 January 2018, when TimGeithner was welcomed to the presidency. His later legal career included a successful challenge to executive control of attorney licensing in 2019. [ 2 ] Presidency In his first announcement as President, SheldonParty described a meeting with the Cabinet and plans to resume normal government activity. He used the presidential account SheIdonParty and is placed eighteenth in the national presidential sequence. [ 3 ] In November 2017, North Korea declared war and SheldonParty announced an intention to respond with force. The following day, the House voted against a war declaration. He accepted the chamber's decision and suspended the military effort. [ 4 ] SheldonParty also made a judicial appointment near the end of his term. The Supreme Court's personnel record for Associate Justice Exiva identifies him as the appointing President; Exiva was confirmed 10–1 on 17 January 2018 and sworn in the next day. [ 5 ] Resignation and succession SheldonParty resigned before 30 January 2018. The transition announcement thanked him and other departing officials and welcomed Timothy Geithner. The exact resignation date remains unspecified; Geithner continued the remaining presidential term. [ 6 ] The Bar litigation of 2019 In 2019, SheldonParty played a decisive role in the dispute over executive control of attorney licensing. J. A. Kirkman had obtained a District Court injunction against the Reviving the Bar Act, then worked with the law's sponsors on a replacement measure. When Kirkman and the Board of Law Examiners sought to dissolve the injunction, SheldonParty intervened as a member of the plaintiff class and secured substitution as its representative to continue the appeal. [ 7 ] His intervention kept the separation-of-powers question alive despite the agreement of the original representative and the Board. The Supreme Court temporarily enjoined the two S. 147 measures on 17 June. On 28 July, Justice Pitney's opinion reversed the Court of Appeals and struck S. 147 down entirely. Attorney licensing was judicial power, the Court held, and Congress could not assign its administration to the executive. [ 8 ] [ 9 ] The decision was a significant post-presidential contribution to judicial independence. It also distinguished control of the Bar from an unrestricted right to practice law: SheldonParty's successful challenge preserved the judiciary's authority over admission, while the Court rejected a constitutional entitlement to practice. The controversy became a central chapter in the history of the Federal Bar Association . title: SmallCho
text: Smallchomama1234 26th President of nUSA (NARA roster) In office 21 July 2019 – 21 July 2019 [ 1 ] Preceded by Bakedgoods Succeeded by SpeakerJosh (JoshMiller in NARA roster) NARA Presidential Records roster Smallchomama1234 (also identified as SmallCho ) was an officeholder in the nUSA roleplay government. The NARA Presidential Records board lists Smallchomama1234 as the 26th President. A contemporaneous announcement records an interim swearing-in on 21 July 2019, following President Bakedgoods 's resignation and pending the expected inauguration of President-elect Josh . [ 2 ] Senate and vice presidency An archived post dated 14 January 2019 reproduced a statement attributed to the Special Counsel's Office under an embedded Twitter heading that identified the account as “Senator SmallCho.” The excerpt preserved in the channel is incomplete, so it documents the title and publication of the statement, not the investigation's findings or disposition. [ 3 ] By June, SmallCho was identified as President of the Senate . A Federal Election Commission letter dated 14 June addressed SmallCho in that capacity; the election administrator said on 18 June that the results had been delivered to the Senate President and House Speaker. A later FEC results letter dated 21 October again addressed SmallCho as Senate President. [ 4 ] The July archive also identifies SmallCho as Vice President before the interim oath. On 1 July, an announcement said President wack man had transferred presidential powers to Acting President SmallCho during an absence, initially through 8 July. On 12 July, SmallCho reported that wack man had returned from vacation and resumed presidential duties. These notices establish a temporary acting role distinct from the later July 21 swearing-in. The channel does not explain how that July 12 return relates to the July 21 notice that Bakedgoods was the outgoing President. [ 5 ] Interim presidency At 6:26 a.m. on 21 July, the channel reported that Bakedgoods had “officially resigned the Presidency” and that Vice President SmallCho would serve until President-elect Josh was sworn in later that day. A post at 6:51 a.m. said SmallCho had been sworn in as President. The channel subsequently announced an inauguration livestream at 11 a.m. and thanked viewers, but the reviewed messages do not preserve the oath itself or a precise time at which SmallCho's interim tenure ended. [ 6 ] By 22 July, Josh was publicly issuing Executive Order J-001. This places the transfer to Josh after SmallCho's brief service, although the cited archive does not record Josh's oath or specify the hour of succession. A NARA monthly update in August 2024 later listed Smallchomama1234's presidency as zero days and ranked it the shortest in its summary; the July announcement itself gives no duration. [ 7 ] The reviewed July notices document SmallCho's oath and succession but do not attribute an executive order, policy announcement, or other presidential action to him during the interim period. Later that summer, the archive named him as NARA Archivist in an update to the Public Law Database. On 7 September, the Senate President Pro Tempore announced that SmallCho had passed confirmation for Vice President by a 12–0 vote; SmallCho's response said he would “once again” serve in that office. The NARA Presidential Records board also has later Vice President roster cards for Smallchomama1234, though the cited cards give no term dates. title: Snowbleed
text: snowbleed 55th President of nUSA (NARA roster) In office 2025 (accession date uncertain) – 24 July 2025 (resignation reported) [ 1 ] Preceded by Rathuzen Succeeded by Mallsoft NARA Presidential Records roster snowbleed is a Roblox nUSA community leader listed as the 55th President and selected as Archivist of the United States in February 2025. The appointment announcement described a small, two-person National Archives and Records Administration (nUSA) (NARA) focused on safeguarding community history and preparing for a next-generation game. During the following month, snowbleed signed a NARA announcement launching a Public Law Database intended to give users structured access to active, repealed, and nullified legislation. [ 2 ] The announcements do not establish the exact end of this archival appointment. Appointment and archival remit The February appointment post named snowbleed the “next Archivist of the United States” and said the role would lead a two-person agency. Its description tied archival work to preserving nUSA history and preparing records for a planned next-generation game. The wording establishes the stated mandate at appointment, not a detailed job description or a term of office. [ 3 ] Public Law Database On 26 February, a NARA announcement signed by snowbleed introduced the Public Law Database spreadsheet. It presented the database as a structured, public-access resource for tracking active, repealed, and nullified laws, in comparison with a Trello board, and said work had begun under the new leadership. This is a documented publication effort during snowbleed’s announced archival leadership; the post does not specify the database’s full coverage or provide an independent audit of its entries. [ 4 ] A March 2025 announcement selected ZhangJingping as the new Archivist. The post does not explain the timing or administrative circumstances between the February and March appointments. Accordingly, the records establish a sequence of announcements, not continuous service through a specific end date or a documented handoff between the two archivists. [ 5 ] Vice presidency An official 23 March 2025 announcement named snowbleed as Vice President under President Rathuzen . NARA's roster lists snowbleed as its 65th Vice President. The cited notices do not preserve an oath or exact service dates. [ 6 ] Presidency and contested record NARA places snowbleed after Rathuzen and before Mallsoft in the numbered presidential roster. The roster card has no description or attached transition document. No executive order by snowbleed was identified in the reviewed Presidential Records export. This limits what can be said about the policies of the administration; absence from that collection does not prove that no presidential actions occurred. [ 7 ] The congressional archive contains a resolution titled Impeachment Articles Against Vice President Snowbleed and another titled To Impeach President Snowbleed . Both are filed in the board's Failed Items list. Those titles document that impeachment measures were proposed at different stages of snowbleed's career; they do not establish the truth of the allegations or an impeachment conviction. The archive reviewed here does not give a presidential departure date or explain the transition to Mallsoft. [ 8 ] See also National Archives and Records Administration (nUSA) Public Law Database (nUSA) ZhangJingping AustinBoBoston1 2025 FEC election records In the March 2025 presidential election, snowbleed was Rathuzen's running mate on the Pioneer Party ticket. The FEC declared them President-elect and Vice President-elect on 16 March; on 23 March public announcements identified snowbleed as Vice President. NARA later listed snowbleed as the 55th President, but the checked contemporary notices do not document a presidential oath, accession date, or transfer from Rathuzen. The roster entry alone does not establish when or how a transition occurred. [ 9 ] ↑ NBC News and Portrock News, 24 July 2025, Discord news archive, Python splitlines() L18480–18510.
