title: Speaker of the United States House of Representatives
text: Presiding officer of the nUSA House of Representatives The Speaker of the United States House of Representatives is the presiding officer of the House of Representatives in nUSA . Chosen by the House, the Speaker leads its proceedings and serves as a principal representative of the chamber in its dealings with the President , the Senate , and other public institutions. The office combines parliamentary leadership with responsibilities under the Constitution and the House's standing rules. [ 1 ] The speakership has been held by future presidents, experienced legislators, and leaders of competing parties. Its history includes repeated reelections, brief tenures, contested elections, resignations, and attempts to declare the office vacant. The Speaker is distinct from the Speaker pro tempore, the Clerk, and other officers who may preside during an absence or an election. [ 2 ] Election and tenure The Speaker is elected through a vote of the House rather than a separate nationwide election. Recorded ballots identify individual representatives and their choices, including votes for competing candidates, abstentions, and uncontested confirmation votes. The membership's party balance can shape the contest, but the election remains a decision of the chamber. In June 2024, for example, the House elected jjc0308; the following month a new vote selected teasoups . [ 3 ] A June 2026 account of opening-session procedure described the Clerk calling the chamber to order and conducting a roll-call, or viva voce, election. Each member present would state a candidate's name, and a candidate receiving a majority of the votes would become Speaker-elect. The Dean of the House would administer the Speaker's oath, after which the Speaker would swear in the other members-elect. This sequence placed the election of the presiding officer before the House's ordinary legislative business. [ 4 ] Speakers may serve more than one tenure. The House's historical roster records separate periods for MasonRockefeller, Technozo , ArmanFoley, and gabezilla090909, among others. New elections can also return an incumbent to office: GatoGaviria received an eleven-to-zero vote in May 2025 and an eleven-to-zero vote with two abstentions in June. Repeat elections and returns to office mean that the number of speakerships is different from the number of people who have held the position. [ 5 ] Duties and relationship with other institutions The Speaker presides over House business and represents the chamber's leadership. House records place the office alongside party leaders, whips, committee assignments, and parliamentary officers. The Speaker's exercise of authority is governed by the Constitution and standing rules, which have changed over time. The House has maintained successive editions of those rules rather than a single unchanging procedural code. [ 6 ] Election administration is one point of contact between the Speaker and other federal institutions. In June 2019, the Federal Elections Congressional Commission delivered House election results to the Speaker. Later that month, the election administrator announced delivery of presidential results to Speaker DevinBeauclark and Senate President SmallCho . The Speaker therefore received official electoral communications on behalf of the House as well as directing its own proceedings. [ 7 ] The office also has responsibilities in presidential incapacity and succession. The constitutional provisions preserved in the Geithner Constitution required written declarations concerning presidential inability or resumption of powers to be sent to both the Speaker and the President pro tempore of the Senate. During UnitedGPT 's presidency, Executive Order 010 invoked the Twenty-fifth Amendment and temporarily placed presidential powers with the Speaker while vice-presidential nominee RickVicario awaited a congressional vote. The order provided for a transfer to RickVicario upon confirmation and reserved the President's ability to resume his powers. [ 8 ] Earlier constitutional arrangements also assigned the Speaker a role in popular referendums. Article XVI of the Geithner Constitution permitted the President, Vice President, and Speaker, acting in concurrence, to request a referendum to veto a law or executive order. It required at least sixty percent public consent. This was a provision of that constitutional edition; the office's powers must be understood within the constitutional period in which they were exercised. [ 9 ] Evolution of the Speaker's powers Voting authority and parliamentary neutrality The Speaker's voting rights have not remained constant. During the 32nd Congress, Public Law 32-1 amended the Constitution to restrict the Speaker's participation in ordinary votes. It permitted voting on expulsions and matters requiring a two-thirds vote, as well as breaking an equal division, while excluding the Speaker from the count needed to establish a quorum. Public Law 32-2 used a narrower formulation: the Speaker would not vote on bills during a convened session unless the representatives were equally divided, and would again be excluded from quorum calculations. These successive provisions distinguished the presiding officer from an ordinary voting representative and changed how the office could influence a close decision. [ 10 ] These restrictions were part of their respective constitutional arrangements rather than permanent rules for every Congress. Their significance was practical: a Speaker's presence could not, under those provisions, supply the missing representative needed for a quorum, and the gavel did not automatically carry a vote on every legislative question. Parliamentary authority and voting strength were separate sources of influence. [ 11 ] Outside employment and institutional independence Legislation also addressed the relationship between congressional leadership and executive employment. The Government Limitations Act of 2017 limited members of Congress to two executive jobs but imposed a lower limit of one on the Speaker and President pro tempore. Department and agency heads were instructed to remove employees whose congressional service placed them over the applicable limit. The measure treated leadership as requiring a greater separation from outside executive responsibilities than ordinary membership. [ 12 ] The Speaker's position nevertheless remained a point of contact with the presidency. Electoral notices, presidential incapacity declarations, and requests involving the House placed the office at the intersection of the legislative and executive branches. The temporary transfer of presidential powers under UnitedGPT's Executive Order 010 illustrated a responsibility beyond managing House debate: in the absence of an available Vice President, the Speaker could be called upon to exercise presidential authority under the succession and incapacity arrangements then in force. [ 13 ] Control of proceedings and accountability to the House Control of proceedings gave Speakers substantial practical influence, but also made their decisions a recurring subject of challenge. Disputes concerned the scheduling of sessions, recognition of members, handling of motions, voting eligibility, and whether removal proposals would reach a vote. In December 2024, Arthur_Chen's opponents sought to vacate the speakership, and contemporary coverage reported that he refused to open a vote on the proposed measure. His eventual resignation allowed the chamber to elect KaceyMontagu. The episode showed how a presiding officer's control of procedure could itself become the issue dividing the House. [ 14 ] Changes to removal thresholds could alter the strength of that control. In May 2024, contemporary coverage described the House's adoption of EggBoiler2K's rules as lowering the threshold to remove a Speaker from two thirds to a simple majority, followed by consideration of a vacancy measure against ArmanFoley. The proposed H. Res. 85 texts also set out arrangements for temporary leadership and a replacement election. Those proposals should be distinguished from a completed removal, but the debate demonstrated the importance of standing rules in determining how readily a parliamentary majority could challenge its presiding officer. [ 15 ] Formalization of leadership elections Leadership elections became more closely tied to formal House proceedings during the 2025 election dispute. Earlier records preserved remote ballots and votes among representatives, while coverage of Nasanovuh v. United States House of Representatives described judicial intervention requiring the Speaker's election to occur at a convened session. The subsequent election of GatoGaviria, certification of its result, and administration of the oath brought the choice of Speaker into a publicly witnessed parliamentary process. [ 16 ] By June 2026, the opening-session procedure described a defined sequence of Clerk-led roll-call voting, election by a majority, an oath administered by the Dean, and the new Speaker's administration of members' oaths. This account emphasized that the House must first establish its leadership before conducting regular business. Alongside the older constitutional voting restrictions and later removal disputes, it illustrates the office's development through both written rules and contested practice. [ 17 ] Historical development Early officeholders SuddenRush12G held the speakership after his presidency and signed House Judiciary Committee election instructions as Speaker in February 2017. Later that year, an official presidential announcement directed citizens to Ozzymen's account for updates from the Speaker. By October 2018, RossKaine was publicly identified as Speaker, and in February 2019 Speaker Josh advertised a House town hall. [ 18 ] The office was also held by DevinBeauclark and Disn_Ize during the following years. The preservation of its history became an express archival responsibility: the National Archives and Records Administration legislation directed the archives to maintain lists of former Speakers and presidents pro tempore, alongside other senior officeholders. [ 19 ] Leadership changes in 2024–2025 The House experienced several leadership transitions during 2024. Vinblob242's brief speakership ended with saviorjoshh taking office in February. LuckyVinick followed in March, and ArmanFoley subsequently held the chair. In June, jjc0308 won the leadership vote, followed by teasoups in July. Anthonytheking9291, Technozo, and Harkology each held the position later that year before Arthur_Chen became Speaker in October. [ 20 ] Arthur_Chen's resignation at the end of December opened a contest between KaceyMontagu and Sheev_PalpatineTGR. KaceyMontagu won and remained Speaker into February 2025, when Matrix_oc succeeded her. Technozo returned to the position in April and resigned later that month. These changes demonstrated both the influence of party coalitions and the possibility of replacing a Speaker between ordinary leadership elections. [ 21 ] Election disputes and removal The election following Technozo's April 2025 resignation became a dispute over parliamentary procedure. An initial ballot between Nasanovuh and Arthur_Chen was tied, after which Nasanovuh withdrew and supported GatoGaviria. Litigation in Nasanovuh v. United States House of Representatives interrupted the next ballot. Contemporary coverage reported that the Supreme Court required Speaker elections to take place during a convened House session rather than through remote voting, while distinguishing the election from a legislative item requiring a first reading. GatoGaviria was elected on 3 May and subsequently received further recorded votes returning him to the chair. [ 22 ] The House has also considered motions and resolutions to declare the speakership vacant. In May 2024, competing versions of H. Res. 85 sought ArmanFoley's removal, citing allegations about session activity and parliamentary conduct. The texts proposed a vacancy followed by temporary leadership and a replacement election; their introduction alone did not establish that the House adopted those measures. A separate controversy occurred in June 2026, when news coverage described Emperorlol01's removal and robloxrules756's brief assumption of the chair, with competing accounts disputing the procedure's legitimacy. [ 23 ] Recorded officeholders The following is a partial list. Periods indicate documented service or dated identification and are not a complete succession with exact inauguration and departure dates. Separate returns to the office are grouped under the same name. Speaker pro tempore and assistant Speaker service alone is excluded. Speaker Documented period or identification SuddenRush12G 2017 [ 24 ] Ozzymen September 2017 [ 25 ] RossKaine October 2018 [ 26 ] Speaker Josh February–June 2019 [ 27 ] Psychodynamic Addressed as Speaker in June 2019 [ 28 ] DevinBeauclark June 2019 [ 29 ] Disn_Ize Named in legislative delegation [ 30 ] Tacus (TacusLord) January 2020 [ 31 ] MasonRockefeller 2022–2023 [ 32 ] Reset4K 2022 [ 32 ] GameLab2017 2022 [ 32 ] David15 2023 [ 32 ] Robbiebeastpro90000 2023 [ 32 ] Siadminaj December 2023 [ 32 ] GeorgeGodsent (HHPrinceGeorge) December 2023–February 2024; earlier service as HHPrinceGeorge [ 32 ] Nasanovuh February 2024 [ 32 ] Vinblob242 February 2024 [ 32 ] saviorjoshh February–March 2024 [ 32 ] LuckyVinick March–April 2024 [ 32 ] ArmanFoley 2024 and 2025; additional later service reported [ 32 ] jjc0308 June–July 2024 [ 32 ] teasoups July 2024 [ 32 ] Anthonytheking9291 July–August 2024 [ 32 ] Technozo 2024 and April 2025 [ 32 ] Harkology August–October 2024 [ 32 ] Arthur_Chen October–December 2024 [ 32 ] KaceyMontagu December 2024–February 2025 [ 32 ] Matrix_oc February–April 2025 [ 32 ] GatoGaviria May–July 2025 [ 32 ] Sheev_PalpatineTGR August–December 2025 [ 32 ] TonyyLewinsky December 2025–February 2026 [ 32 ] gabezilla090909 2026, more than one tenure [ 32 ] Emperorlol01 March–June 2026 [ 32 ] robloxrules756 June 2026, brief disputed tenure [ 32 ] Acidraps June 2026, brief tenure recorded [ 32 ] Sharkbiteboy0225 June–August 2026 [ 32 ] RazuraHF Named in House leadership records [ 33 ] warlockings Identified as former Speaker in 2026 [ 34 ] The June 2019 records differ: an election announcement referred to the outgoing Speaker as Josh, while its attached letter was addressed to Psychodynamic. They are listed separately here without assuming that they were the same person. A December 2019 letter also addressed a Speaker Caldwell, but the surname alone does not establish a full identity. [ 35 ] Reconstruction leadership in 2022 MasonRockefeller used the speakership as a coordinating office during the 2022 reconstruction . He announced the January program, convened a joint town hall with the President pro tempore in February, and recruited staff for House offices in April. His work linked public participation with the less visible task of rebuilding committees and parliamentary administration. [ 36 ] The Speaker also served as a public advocate for specific legislative choices. Rockefeller introduced the Domestic Protection Act , announced its enactment in July, and introduced H.R. 25 in November in response to Ridgeway's restrictions on participation. The latter was a proposal for anti-discrimination protections, while the former had completed the legislative process. [ 37 ] [ 38 ] After GameLab announced a resignation effective 23 October, Rockefeller directed attention toward attendance, proxies and the chamber's own organization. His standing rules were adopted on 9 November, redefining committee work, leadership responsibilities and the legislative process. The episode illustrates a source of the Speaker's influence beyond chairing debate: proposing the procedures through which the House conducts its business. [ 39 ] [ 40 ] The office also maintained its ceremonial relationship with the presidency. Rockefeller invited TacticalRock101 to deliver a State of the Union address on 19 December. The event was subsequently postponed, demonstrating that an invitation and scheduled joint gathering were distinct from a completed address. Earlier, January 2020 presidential notices identified Tacus, using the account TacusLord, as Speaker and described him as an experienced contributor to the nation's laws. title: SpeakerJosh
text: SpeakerJosh 27th President of nUSA (NARA roster: JoshMiller) In office 21 July 2019 – 29 August 2019 [ 1 ] Preceded by Smallchomama1234 (interim) Succeeded by AntonioTRoosevelt Archived Discord transition notices, 21–22 July 2019 SpeakerJosh (also referred to as Josh in nUSA announcements) is a Roblox account recorded as President of the nUSA roleplay community beginning in July 2019. He was identified as President-elect in June, and a transition post on July 21 said he was expected to be sworn in later that day. By July 22, Josh was issuing presidential announcements. NARA later catalogued the same-period presidency as “JoshMiller, 27th,” with July orders filed under the visually similar “JoshMiIIer” spelling. The chronology and orders strongly associate those archival names with SpeakerJosh, although the sources reviewed do not supply an explicit alias statement or account ID. [ 2 ] Prior office A June 3, 2019 Federal Elections Commission announcement delivered House Class I results to the “outgoing Speaker, @Josh.” Together with the later SpeakerJosh President-elect announcement and July presidential posts, this supports a prior Speaker of the House role for the same 2019 political identity. The export does not preserve a platform account ID linking every display name, so the earlier office is stated from the dated record rather than from a verified account profile. [ 3 ] Election and transition On June 18, 2019, an nUSA update announced that President-elect SpeakerJosh had released applications for the next administration. The attached application described a term scheduled from July 21 through November 21, 2019, and set a five-day application window. It said transition team members would score applications, allowed the team to disqualify applicants, and provided for random extra moderation. This was a published staffing procedure, not a record of who was ultimately selected for each job. [ 4 ] On July 21, a channel post said outgoing President Bakedgoods had resigned, Vice President SmallCho had been sworn in temporarily, and President-elect Josh was expected to take office later that day. The next day, Josh's account announced Executive Order J-001. The archive establishes this handover sequence but does not supply the exact time or text of his oath in the messages cited here. [ 5 ] The campaign and handover appear in the wider record of the 2019 presidential elections (nUSA) . Executive administration In the first weeks of the term, Josh announced a change to White House recruiting: executive-branch applications would use the White House website, with the transition proceeding gradually while question packs were prepared. The announcement said White House intern applications were already available and clarified that recruitment had not stopped. In a separate notice, the White House sought a videographer to create regular communications videos, described as an alternative to relying only on press releases. [ 6 ] The archive records Josh announcing seven medals and an August press statement about executive recruitment. It does not preserve the criteria for the medals or identify the eventual recipients in those posts, so the notices show the actions announced rather than their later effects. [ 7 ] Two July orders are preserved in the NARA presidential archive. J-001, dated July 22, overhauled the executive-branch blacklist process and set out an interim appeal arrangement; its text refers to the “Josh administration.” J-002 addressed removal of NSFW channels and content from executive communications servers. The J-002 PDF header says July 24 while its signature block says July 22; a July 24 Discord message records the President announcing that the order had been signed. These sources establish the orders' text and release notices, but not full enforcement or later effects. [ 8 ] Russia conflict During the Roblox roleplay war with Russia in July 2019, Josh posted that the United States should condemn harassment based on gender, sexuality, race, religion or opinion. A two-page public letter from July 24 framed the conflict as a dispute over United Nations Department of Political Affairs negotiations. In the letter, Josh said the United States had accepted Russia's proposed war terms and submitted parallel terms of its own, but that Russia had rejected the U.S. proposals; these are his administration's claims in the conflict. [ 9 ] On July 27, nUSA announced a 2–0 victory over Russia and Josh posted a statement celebrating it. On August 1, Josh announced a new declaration of war with the United Kingdom against Russia/Soviet Union, and the channel reported that both houses of the United States Congress (nUSA) had passed a declaration of war. The archive therefore records two distinct stages: an announced end to the July conflict and a later campaign for a second one. These were community roleplay events, not real-world military actions. [ 10 ] The application set a planned November 21 end date, but Josh left office earlier, on 29 August 2019. title: Spring 2026 presidential election recount (nUSA)
text: The March 2026 nUSA presidential election recount and filtering review The Spring 2026 presidential election recount was a review of the March 2026 presidential election in the Roblox-based nUSA roleplay community. On 14 March, the National Elections Administrator announced an initial result of 98 votes for warlockings and 90 for Bathamza, reporting 284 total voters, of whom 188 were valid and 96 invalid. On 16 March, a separate management statement announced a blind re-filtering and a revised result of 117 votes for Bathamza and 109 for warlockings. [ 1 ] Review The 16 March statement by a nUSA owner said the election's filtering process had shown repeated changes to some voters' pending, failed, and passed statuses. It said an internal review examined website access logs and found that an FEC official had accessed live vote data while filtering, allowing that official to infer how individuals voted. The post described the resulting filtering as favoring voters for one candidate over the other and characterized it as election interference. These findings are the account given in the management statement; the archived material does not independently verify them or identify the official. [ 2 ] The statement said that management ordered a blind re-filtering of all votes, compiled a change log for both candidates to review and dispute, and issued revised totals. It also announced a change disabling immediate result displays on FEC panels before an election officially closed. The linked two-page nUSA Presidential Election Changelog lists 40 voter-status corrections: 38 restored and two revoked. It contains no candidate totals, so it cannot independently reproduce the revised 117–109 count. [ 3 ] Results The initial FEC announcement named warlockings and Epicwarrior_99 as President-Elect and Vice-President-Elect. The later management statement instead reported Bathamza with 117 votes and warlockings with 109. The reviewed archive contains no replacement FEC certification reconciling the two outcomes, and the change log does not show candidate-level vote assignments. [ 4 ] Sources and limitations The result notices and review statement are contemporary records of what the NEA and management announced. The report about an FEC official's access to live vote data is attributed to the later management statement, rather than presented as independently established fact. title: State of Columbia (nUSA)
text: Short-lived 2019 attempt to unite Washington and Las Vegas The State of Columbia was a short-lived attempt to unite Washington, D.C. , and Las Vegas under a single municipal government in March 2019. Congress's S. 127 sought to merge the cities, install a provisional government and establish a new judicial system. On 3 March, the Supreme Court invalidated the merger and its principal supporting provisions because neither city's legislature had consented to the union. [ 1 ] The project offered a sweeping replacement for the existing municipal order. Within a day of its public creation announcement, however, its legal foundation had collapsed. Columbia's failure became a constitutional warning that federal authority over local government did not include an unrestricted power to combine municipalities against their will. [ 2 ] [ 3 ] The municipal reorganization S. 127, titled To restore municipal government , envisioned a merger of Las Vegas and the District of Columbia into a single jurisdiction bearing the name State of Columbia. Its framework included a provisional governor appointed by the President with Senate consent. The governor would exercise interim executive and legislative authority while negotiating a constitution for submission to the two city councils. The councils were to retain their development responsibilities. [ 4 ] The measure supplied more than a new name. It assigned a march and anthem, contemplated the transfer of certain federal agencies and provided for a State Court of Columbia. Its judicial provisions also described a State Crime Panel within the federal District Court and addressed regulation of the legal profession. These provisions sought to create the apparatus of government around the proposed merger. [ 5 ] At 5:05 p.m. on 2 March, azahid1 publicly announced Columbia's creation. The Supreme Court took up the recently passed legislation both on its own initiative in In re Federal Government and through Kirkman's challenge to the State of Columbia. Its intervention arrived before the proposed constitutional and administrative settlement could become an enduring municipal order. [ 6 ] [ 7 ] The missing consent Main article: In re Federal Government (nUSA) Article IV, Section 3 prohibited a municipality formed by joining existing municipalities without the consent of their legislatures. The Court found no record of either city voting to approve the merger. It required clear, public and unambiguous consent from both municipalities; prior notice, even if supplied, could not substitute for that consent. [ 8 ] The legislation tried to justify the merger by referring to the demunicipalization of Las Vegas under H.R. 179. The Court rejected that route around the consent requirement. H.R. 179 itself referred to Las Vegas as a municipality, and its legality was not being decided in the Columbia case. For purposes of the dispute, both Las Vegas and Washington retained the municipal status that made their consent indispensable. [ 9 ] The Court struck sections 101 through 104: the merger, naming provisions, declaration of congressional intent and provisional government. Without a valid union, Congress could not transfer the cities' sovereign powers to Columbia's governor. The new government's existence depended on precisely the constitutional step that had been omitted. [ 10 ] Why the remaining institutions fell S. 127 included a severability clause, but that did not preserve every provision once the merger had failed. Section 106 required agency transfers to Columbia's provisional governor. With no lawful governor to receive them, the transfers had no meaningful operation. Section 107 created courts whose appointments and duties depended on Columbia's government and laws. Saving them would have required the Court to rewrite the legislation. [ 11 ] The Court therefore invalidated sections 106 and 107 as inseverable from the unconstitutional core. It preserved the effective-date provision, severability clause and disclaimer concerning development authority because those provisions could stand independently. The ruling destroyed Columbia's governing framework without declaring every word of S. 127 invalid. [ 12 ] Dissolution and legacy On 3 March, pauljkl also announced Columbia's dissolution through founder authority. The judicial ruling supplied a separate constitutional basis for the end of the merger. Later notices described the state as legally null and void, and the proposed governor, agency transfers and court system could no longer operate under the invalidated sections. [ 13 ] [ 14 ] [ 15 ] The Court closed with a warning that public officials remained bound by the Constitution even when they expected the judiciary to refrain from intervention. Columbia thus became an example of the limits of federal reorganization and of the Court's willingness to use Anytime Review to enforce those limits. [ 16 ] See also District of Columbia City Council (nUSA) Supreme Court (nUSA) United States Congress (nUSA) ↑ In re Federal Government and Kirkman v. title: State of Ridgeway
text: Ridgeway , officially the State of Ridgeway , is a polity and community centered on Ridgeway County . Established on 4 July 2020 under a county charter within the United States , it developed a local government, judiciary, police institutions and a county game. Its original developers were Squareheaddude, devGralius and Pauljkl . Ridgeway separated from the United States during a dispute among its developers in January 2022. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] A Ridgeway County sheriff's vehicle in a promotional image posted by Squareheaddude on 12 September 2020, before the public launch. The county opened to the public on 21 November 2020. Designed around policing and local institutions, it offered an alternative to Washington, D.C. and Las Vegas . By January 2022, the division between Ridgeway's active community and the weakened federal government had become a prominent political issue. The developer separation ended the original three-person partnership, while Ridgeway continued independently. The original developers reunited in January 2024, when Pauljkl returned to Ridgeway after relinquishing ownership of nUSA. [ 4 ] Later relations with nUSA included disputes over membership, a formally declared war in July 2024 and subsequent arrangements for joint events. [ 5 ] [ 6 ] [ 7 ] Origins and development The county project Ridgeway originated as a project by three developers who had previously worked within the nUSA community. Squareheaddude created the map, terrain, vehicles, visual identity and much of the game's visible equipment. Pauljkl and devGralius developed its backend, scripted features and technical optimizations. The partners initially kept development private. Squareheaddude later described a development period of almost a year before release, with approximately three quarters of that work conducted privately. [ 3 ] Pauljkl described the project's purpose as rebuilding the policing experience offered by Washington and Las Vegas. In his account, their older code was vulnerable to exploitation, and a new county game would allow the developers to replace it and introduce different police interactions. Although the developers later disagreed about the distribution of work and the project's direction, their accounts agree on its origins as a joint undertaking with Squareheaddude responsible for building and Pauljkl and devGralius for scripting. [ 8 ] [ 3 ] A later Ridgeway community history dates the beginning of development to July 2019. By September 2020, the project was being publicly demonstrated: on 12 September, Squareheaddude announced a planned weekend stream and warned that the available screenshare places would be limited. A further preview stream took place immediately before the November launch. [ 9 ] [ 10 ] Establishment within the United States Ridgeway's founding charter was adopted on 4 July 2020. H.R. 67, introduced that day by ZartaVex with Risen_Orbs, Libres, JordiHarris and Ridgeway's Developer Oversight, provided for the admission of Ridgeway County within the State of Ridgeway. The congressional archive classifies the measure as Public Law 80-11. It authorized the county to maintain defense forces and allowed appeals from its judiciary to the United States Supreme Court. [ 1 ] The charter defined Ridgeway County as a political subdivision of the United States and designated the City of Milton as its seat. It distinguished the county's local institutions from the federal government while binding them to the United States Constitution. County officers' oaths required them to uphold that Constitution, and eligibility for the County Board included a period of United States citizenship. [ 2 ] Ridgeway nevertheless possessed considerable local autonomy. Its governmental structure included an elected five-member County Board, an elected County Executive, county courts and elected law-enforcement offices. The Board served four-month terms and the Executive a six-month term. The charter also recognized municipal police and fire services, the Sheriff's Office, State Police, National Guard and Law Enforcement Training Center. [ 2 ] Developer Oversight held extensive authority over the project's practical operation. The charter reserved control of groups, records and technical resources to the developers and required their approval for changes affecting game systems. They could veto measures affecting the game or community welfare, and charter amendments required their consent. This made the developers' partnership consequential to both the county's institutions and its continued development. [ 2 ] Public launch and growth, 2020–2021 Paid access and initial reception Ridgeway County opened on 21 November 2020 with an initial access price of 1,000 Robux. The launch announcement introduced the county's separate communications server and promised information about the first Law Enforcement Training Center intake in both the nUSA and Ridgeway communities. The developers invited purchasers to join them for demonstrations and bug testing. [ 5 ] Launch-day access was disrupted by a Roblox purchasing problem. Squareheaddude directed users to a separate purchase experience before joining the main game. That evening, Pauljkl thanked purchasers and said the reception had exceeded the team's expectations. The following day, Squareheaddude announced planned releases of the National Guard and Law Enforcement Training Center alongside fixes for launch bugs. [ 11 ] The price was reduced to 500 Robux on 1 December 2020 and to 100 Robux on 18 January 2021. These changes substantially lowered the cost of entering the county, although access remained paid at those dates. [ 12 ] Local institutions and the federal community Ridgeway's emphasis on county institutions gave its police, courts and elected offices a distinct identity. Its local government operated under a detailed charter rather than functioning solely as another federal city. Law-enforcement recruitment was tied to the county's training system, while public demonstrations, development notices and bug testing helped organize the community around the game. [ 2 ] [ 5 ] [ 11 ] Its association with nUSA continued after release. On 2 October 2021, ShadowCulture explicitly included Ridgeway among the assets moderated by the Coalition Against Abuse. At the same time, the county's own communications and local institutions increasingly provided a separate center of activity. [ 13 ] [ 5 ] That growth did not produce uniform enthusiasm throughout nUSA. In June 2021, GeorgeGodsent argued that Ridgeway was sustaining agencies while the wider community struggled with electoral enthusiasm. Other participants complained about development priorities or preferred the style of the older cities. These contemporary disagreements show that Ridgeway's appeal and its relationship to federal activity were contested well before the developer separation. [ 14 ] Developer separation and independence, January 2022 Breakdown of the partnership The developer dispute involved both the direction of the game and the partners' working relationship. Their published accounts described disagreements over moderation, outside influence, development effort and attempts at reconciliation. Both sides presented the relationship as having deteriorated over an extended period, although they differed sharply over responsibility. [ 3 ] [ 8 ] On 14 January 2022, Squareheaddude issued a memorandum announcing that the partnership should be dissolved. He alleged that Pauljkl had behaved destructively and publicly disparaged his contributions. Squareheaddude also acknowledged that he and devGralius had contributed to the drama and neglected the wider community amid factional conflict. The memorandum rejected their own departure as the preferred solution and promised further updates after the hiatus. [ 3 ] Pauljkl's response attributed the deterioration partly to outside influence and disagreements about management. He argued that concerns had not been communicated effectively and defended his development work. He also disputed the handling of moderation cases, particularly the definition and enforcement of rules concerning transfers of items between accounts. [ 8 ] An edited recording uploaded by Coulter Ellis on 15 January preserves an argument with Pauljkl in which Squareheaddude proposed 40 percent revenue shares for himself and David and 20 percent for Paul. Paul's written response instead said Squareheaddude's proposed arrangement assigned David the 20 percent share; Paul advocated equal 30 percent shares with a further 10 percent reserved for advertising. The participants' accounts therefore disagree about the proposed allocation. [ 15 ] [ 8 ] Squareheaddude also alleged that Paul had threatened legal action and described an unsuccessful reconciliation after Paul's roles were removed. He advocated separating the communities, while Paul referred to an earlier recorded call. The alleged threats remain Squareheaddude's assertions. [ 15 ] Separation from nUSA Political tensions were already public by 9 January. President TacticalRock101 described relations between nUSA and Ridgeway as a “Cold War” and said that the parties had been unable to agree on battles. On 10 January, he resigned, connecting the federal government's difficulties to management priorities and the state of its remaining city. [ 16 ] [ 6 ] The dates assigned to Ridgeway's separation differ. The older nUSA encyclopedia places secession on 9 January and recognition on 15 January. Ridgeway's later history associates independence with the developer separation of 14–16 January and identifies 15 January as the date commemorated by its County Board. Contemporary nUSA discussion includes claims of independence on both 9 and 15 January. The political confrontation, dissolution of the development partnership and adoption of independent institutions were related developments within the same month. [ 17 ] Squareheaddude and devGralius continued the Ridgeway project after the original partnership ended. A state constitution bears a ratification date of 20 January 2022. It provided for a governor, lieutenant governor, seven-member Senate and state judiciary. Ridgeway's community history dates the transition to its state-government structure to 28 March 2022, a later milestone than the date printed on the constitution. [ 18 ] [ 19 ] Relationship to the nUSA activity crisis A user-supplied activity comparison showing 69 players in Ridgeway County and none in Washington, D.C. The visible local clock reads 14 January 2022, 6:21 p.m.; the timezone and original photographer are unknown. The counts represent one moment during the developer dispute. Ridgeway's separation occurred during a wider crisis of federal activity and confidence. In his resignation, TacticalRock101 alleged that management and developers had abandoned nUSA for Ridgeway, that the federal community's remaining functioning city was outdated and that he had received insufficient support to carry out the presidency. These were the outgoing president's criticisms, rather than a technical audit of either game. [ 6 ] On 16 January, Speaker MasonRockefeller described nUSA as severely weakened and approaching collapse. He said colleagues had moved to Ridgeway, American Roleplay and other communities. His proposed response was to consolidate resources and cooperate with the president and Senate leadership to rebuild the federal community. [ 20 ] The contemporary activity screenshot illustrates the imbalance: at the displayed time on 14 January, Ridgeway County showed 69 active players and Washington showed zero. It establishes that contrast at one instant, rather than either game's average population or the direction of every player's movement. [ 21 ] The crisis cannot be reduced to the developer confrontation alone. The discussion of weak electoral enthusiasm in June 2021 preceded the January split, and MasonRockefeller identified several destinations for departing members. Ridgeway's growing activity, disputes about attention to the older cities and the eventual separation formed part of that broader loss of participation and institutional confidence. [ 14 ] [ 20 ] Independent institutions The state constitution established separate legislative, executive and judicial branches. The Senate comprised seven members serving four-month terms. The governor served a four-month term, commanded the state's forces and exercised executive powers, with the lieutenant governor occupying additional legislative and military responsibilities. The constitution also provided for an elected attorney general, secretary of state and sheriffs. [ 19 ] The judiciary included a Supreme Court with a chief justice and four associate justices, together with a Superior Court for civil and criminal proceedings. The Supreme Court possessed appellate jurisdiction and authority over court administration. Constitutional oaths required allegiance to the State of Ridgeway. Developer Oversight retained a role in constitutional amendment alongside amendment by popular election. [ 19 ] The independent constitution thus differed from the original county charter in its framework of allegiance and institutions. The earlier charter placed the county within the United States and provided federal appellate connections; the state constitution organized authority around Ridgeway's own government and courts. [ 2 ] [ 19 ] Later relations with the United States Boulder County and membership disputes During 2022, nUSA developed Boulder County as another county project. In October, Pauljkl described planned features beyond those of the older Ridgeway project, including player-created fires, towing, a casino, vehicle customization, jobs outside formal teams and player-run businesses. He said assembling a development team had taken time. Boulder subsequently opened in November. [ 22 ] Boulder's launch produced a further disagreement over participation in both communities. On 26 November, MasonRockefeller criticized what he called Ridgeway's “Subversion Act” and alleged that it restricted members of the nUSA community. He introduced H.R. 25 to prohibit discrimination against immigrants, including restrictions based on Ridgeway membership. His announcement expressed an intention to secure passage; it does not itself establish that the bill became law. [ 23 ] Reunion of Developer Oversight, January 2024 On 17 January 2024, Squareheaddude announced the reunion of Ridgeway's original Developer Oversight team, almost two years after its separation. He said that the disagreements responsible for the January 2022 breakdown had been resolved and that Pauljkl had relinquished ownership of nUSA to return to Ridgeway full-time. The announcement presented the renewed partnership as a reconciliation between the original developers. [ 4 ] The reunited team divided responsibilities between Pauljkl, who would lead scripting and backend development; Squareheaddude, who would lead game design and graphics; and David (devGralius), who would lead web services and government. Squareheaddude said development had already resumed and that the request to restore access to the game had been submitted. He anticipated reopening within the next few business days and a sequence of updates introducing content planned before the downtime, followed by suitable features from Boulder County. Further announcements about government and departments were assigned to David. [ 4 ] The accompanying questions and answers linked this development reunion to the ownership change in the United States. Squareheaddude said nUSA would return to its original gameplay style under its new ownership, while Boulder would remain down indefinitely and cease to be part of nUSA. He described Boulder's quality-of-life features and backend fixes as resources for advancing Ridgeway. These were the announced development plans; the post did not establish the date of reopening or completion of the proposed transfers. [ 4 ] Pauljkl's own nUSA announcement the same day identified Dilliuss and UKR41NIAN as the incoming co-owners and said the Boulder games would be discontinued after the transfer. The two announcements connected the restoration of Ridgeway's original development partnership with a change in nUSA's ownership and municipal development direction. [ 24 ] The July 2024 war and subsequent cooperation In July 2024, the United States formally declared war on Ridgeway through H.J. Res. 2, signed by President GeorgeGodsent. Management nevertheless recognized the communities' overlapping membership. On 11 July, UKR41NIAN announced that neither community should sanction people merely for belonging to the other, with exceptions concerning personnel who volunteered for deployment. [ 7 ] [ 25 ] President-elect Blanket announced an end to the war on 22 July. The arrangement provided for joint events and allowed United States military personnel to join Ridgeway's State Guard as dual citizens. In explaining the decision, he described the war as an effort to generate activity and criticized the absence of adequate preparations, repetitive raids and the lack of an official battle game. The settlement was framed as cooperation rather than a surrender or a victory imposing concessions. [ 7 ] Connections also persisted through individual officials. In August 2024, an nUSA management announcement praised David's work in its military and public-outreach management while acknowledging that he managed Ridgeway. The separation therefore did not eliminate shared personnel or later cooperation. [ 26 ] Later activity and retained affiliations The Ridgeway County experience page in a user-supplied screenshot reported as captured around 1:30 a.m. Eastern on 1 October 2026. It shows 43 active players and more than 1.5 million visits. A screenshot supplied for 1 October 2026 shows Ridgeway County with 43 active players, more than 1.5 million visits and 12,876 favorites. Its displayed description still labels the experience early access and gives 4 July 2020 as the founding date. The group screenshot from the same reported period displays more than 42,200 members. These figures measure different forms of participation: concurrent players, cumulative visits and group membership. [ 27 ] The affiliates screenshot also shows police, fire, sheriff and law-enforcement-training groups retaining “USA” prefixes. These surviving names illustrate links to Ridgeway's earlier organization, but affiliation and naming do not by themselves establish continuing United States governmental authority over the independent state. title: SuddenRush12G
text: SuddenRush12G 12th President of nUSA In office 7 January 2016 – 21 January 2017 [ 1 ] Preceded by Zeyad567 Succeeded by TheySinned NARA Presidential Records SuddenRush12G was the 12th President of nUSA and one of its longest-serving early leaders. He succeeded Zeyad567 , won a second consecutive term in 2016, and was succeeded by TheySinned in January 2017. His presidency reorganized federal agencies, intelligence clearances, prison access, diplomatic protection, and executive employment rules. A retrospective chronology dates his service from 7 January 2016 to 21 January 2017; the exact date of his first oath remains unverified. [ 2 ] Career before the presidency SuddenRush12G entered nUSA public life through the Secret Service and subsequently led the Special Forces under President Marinio and the National Security Agency under President Lumidas . He served as Vice President to Zeyad567 , later became President pro tempore of the Senate , and held the homeland security portfolio before his presidential run. [ 3 ] SuddenRush12G being inaugurated for his second term as President of the United States. SuddenRush12G became the first nUSA President to win consecutive terms. During the second campaign, TimGeithner managed his reelection effort, drafted the 8 June 2016 announcement speech, and later joined the ticket as vice-presidential candidate. The campaign faced a controversy over allegations that then-Vice President TerenceWalsh had tried to manipulate a Senate election. TerenceWalsh subsequently left office. [ 4 ] Five vice presidents served at different points during his presidency: DavidAxelrod, TerenceWalsh, HHPrinceGeorge, TimGeithner, and AdamStratton. SuddenRush12G won a presidential contest against YouTube910 during his reelection period. Contemporary coverage credited him with 427 votes. [ 5 ] Executive reorganization SuddenRush12G began his term with an order abolishing the Department of Education, its academies and universities commissions, the Securities and Exchange Commission, and the Department of Housing and Urban Development. The 23 January 2016 “One USA Order” barred federal executive employment for people who also held citizenship in another United States government and required current staff to renounce such affiliation within 24 hours or face dismissal. These measures combined structural retrenchment with an attempt to secure nUSA's standing among competing governments. [ 6 ] Security administration was another early priority. A 26 January order established ranked access to federal prisons, with different permissions for Justice officials, investigators, local emergency services, intelligence agencies, and protective details. In February, SuddenRush12G required presidential access to executive Skype rooms, documents, and Trello boards. A separate order dissolved the Federal Intelligence Agency after accusing its leadership and members of repeated misconduct. The administration cited misconduct as its justification for the dissolution. [ 7 ] On 20 February, he substantially expanded the authority of the White House chief of staff. The chief of staff gained power to oversee and discipline executive personnel, convene meetings, demand reports, audit departments, impose or remove executive employment blacklists, and make security-threat designations. The office remained outside the presidential line of succession, and its holder still served at the President's pleasure. On 22 February, however, he revoked the chief-of-staff order after objections that it concentrated excessive power in the office. He defended its original purpose as maintaining executive continuity during his absence, but acknowledged public opposition. In the same statement he placed former President Zeyad567 on an executive blacklist, citing public distrust, and appointed Golfgames1 as chief of staff. [ 8 ] On 3 March, SuddenRush12G established a Diplomatic Security Service within the State Department to protect diplomats, foreign delegates, and senior State officials. [ 9 ] His employment order of 3 March allowed citizens who had held citizenship for at least six months to petition for removal of an executive officer; a petition with 75 qualifying signatures could result in removal with presidential approval. It also required agency heads to explain a dismissed employee's removal on request. Another March order directed executive officers to carry out court “Arrest on Sight” orders even when they thought an order erroneous, while limiting the use of teams bearing that label in nUSA cities. Those provisions illustrate the administration's effort to define both public influence over agencies and the executive's obligations to the courts. [ 10 ] The April “ORPS” order placed the Small Business Administration under the Department of Commerce and created an International Trade Administration, setting out registration and regulatory functions for businesses. In May, SuddenRush12G separated intelligence-community and Justice Department classification systems, defined Confidential, Secret, and Top Secret levels, and assigned senior officials responsibility for access decisions. [ 11 ] Judicial appointments Early in his presidency, SuddenRush12G made Supreme Court appointments and sought to address delays in the federal judiciary. On 27 February 2016, he announced that the Senate had confirmed NorthFuze, a former assistant attorney and Supreme Court clerk, as a justice. With another seat still vacant, he promised a nominee who would uphold the Constitution and decide cases promptly. He also pledged to work with Congress to remove inactive federal judges, presenting timely hearings and a speedy, just trial as priorities of his administration. [ 12 ] In a nomination announcement dated 20 March, he selected TimGeithner for the Supreme Court after a candidate review and shortlisting process. SuddenRush12G emphasized Geithner's experience in domestic and foreign politics and described him as a strict constitutionalist. He argued that justices should protect ordinary citizens rather than government or special interests. The announcement constituted a nomination; it did not announce Senate confirmation. [ 13 ] By his 29 May address, SuddenRush12G said that he had appointed five justices and was still seeking to fill the bench. He again called for cooperation with Congress to replace inactive judges. In the same address, he credited the Justice Department with improving relations between agencies and repairing the Bureau of Prisons, making judicial access and prison administration part of his account of the first term. [ 14 ] Security and military policy Alerts and intelligence operations On 22 February 2016, after briefings from the secretary of state and national security advisor about threats from the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics, SuddenRush12G ordered agencies to heightened alert. He directed deployments to Washington, D.C. , and Las Vegas, issued a travel warning for USSR member nations, and changed the readiness level from DEFCON 5 to DEFCON 4. The measures were presented as a response to threats against American cities and citizens abroad. [ 15 ] The President also sought public input on security-agency leadership. In a statement dated 13 March, he cited petitions and complaints about the Special Forces and questioned whether its oversight and leadership met his administration's expectations. He asked citizens whether the leadership should be replaced, without announcing a dismissal in that statement. [ 16 ] On 3 April, he established the National Security Medal for distinguished national-security service or exceptional acts of courage. Eligibility extended to people of any nationality, including military personnel, and permitted posthumous awards. The President or his designee would award the decoration, with recommendations supported by documentation and processed through national-security officials. The order distinguished outstanding service in a position of responsibility from acts of personal heroism. [ 17 ] On 6 April, SuddenRush12G announced that the National Security Agency had shut down PS-35, which his administration identified as a terrorist organization. He said the operation had involved weeks of preparation and that his office had been notified of its completion on 4 April. He thanked NSA personnel and promised that Special Source Operations would declassify related documents in the following weeks. [ 18 ] National Security Council National-security coordination was also the subject of the Enhancement to National Security Act of 2016. The legislative text SuddenRush12G published on 4 April proposed a council chaired by the President, with the Vice President, secretary of state, secretary of defense, attorney general, and up to seven additional presidential appointees. It assigned the council responsibility for integrating domestic, foreign, and military policies, reviewing intelligence requirements monthly, coordinating responses to transnational threats, and overseeing intelligence-community blacklists. It also provided voting procedures and presidential-consent requirements for national-security threat designations. These were the provisions of the April legislative text; the announcement itself did not record final passage. [ 19 ] Armed forces and the United Kingdom conflict In his 29 May address, SuddenRush12G described a military overhaul and said that the armed forces had just under 300 active-duty enlisted personnel. He also advocated support for former servicemembers through the Retired Veterans' Benefits and Entitlements Program. His later farewell address recalled rebuilding the military after a destructive attack on its administration. [ 20 ] [ 21 ] During his second term, SuddenRush12G led nUSA through the summer 2016 war with the United Kingdom . On 21 July, Vice President TimGeithner published a proposed joint resolution authorizing a military campaign and revoking the British alliance upon passage. The date of its formal legislative approval is uncertain. [ 22 ] The peace agreement dated 3 August acknowledged a British victory with a score of 5–0 and required both militaries to cease hostilities. SuddenRush12G and Secretary of State Lumidas were listed as the American signatories, alongside British Prime Minister SidousThePwnda. The terms included recognition of Hawaii's independence, an apology from TimGeithner to Tentacools, and measures to normalize relations and secure British diplomatic support. [ 23 ] The conflict with the United Kingdom prompted a more critical assessment of military readiness during the second term. In a report to the National Security Council on 23 October, SuddenRush12G argued that the military's internal organization and training needed substantial reform. He favored smaller, cohesive combat units over large forces that could not fight effectively, and criticized excessive emphasis on formations and obstacle courses. His report proposed an Army focused on flexible deployment and basic combat, a Marine Corps with the highest entry and training standards, and Navy and Air Force branches with larger memberships and a greater emphasis on ceremonial service and limited combat roles. [ 24 ] The proposed membership caps were 150 for the Army, 75 for the Marine Corps, and 300 each for the Navy and Air Force. A common two-day basic-training program would precede assignment to an individual branch. The first day would introduce shared standards, command structure, and basic combat; the second would emphasize repeated team fighting and assessment of discipline and cooperation. The report outlined recommendations for reform rather than announcing their implementation. [ 25 ] Second-term administration Internal Affairs Bureau and employee conduct After reelection, SuddenRush12G's 29 July statement emphasized agency competence, cooperation, and employment. He acknowledged complaints from citizens who had not received the offices they wanted, defended the qualifications of his nominees, and promised meetings with directors and Cabinet officials to organize further reforms. Russell_Jackson and Mazux signed the statement as White House chief of staff and deputy chief of staff, respectively. [ 26 ] The administration reestablished the Internal Affairs Bureau to investigate corruption and abuse within the executive branch. On 1 August, SuddenRush12G said that it had handled more than twenty cases and terminated two executive employees. He encouraged citizens to submit complaints through the Abuse Report Center, presenting a private reporting process as the route to investigation and disciplinary action. Those case totals were his administration's announced results. [ 27 ] White House Ordinance 002, issued on 3 August, tasked the bureau with enforcing an interagency respect and professionalism policy. It prohibited executive employees from disrespecting, harassing, or slandering agencies and their personnel in either public or private communications. Violations could trigger an investigation and dismissal from executive employment. The ordinance expressly applied as an employer policy to executive employees, rather than creating a criminal prohibition for the general public. [ 28 ] An order dated 25 August imposed additional communication rules on White House employees and entities working directly for the President or Vice President. It prohibited public disputes with other executive personnel, public criticism undermining White House leadership, and the circulation of material contrary to the administration's agenda. Employees were directed to raise disagreements privately or through the Internal Affairs Bureau. The enforcement process generally began with a warning and could lead to a recommendation for termination after continued noncompliance. [ 29 ] Hiring and resignation rules The National Employment Practices Reform order of 2 October limited the use of arrest records in federal hiring. SuddenRush12G argued that an arrest did not establish guilt and that paid record expungement made reliance on arrest totals financially discriminatory. Agencies were instructed to change their employment standards within one week, with the secretary of commerce and labor monitoring implementation. The order nevertheless allowed application forms to request arrest information and allowed agency heads to consider it when the number of arrests exceeded a reasonable maximum. [ 30 ] On 26 November, he established a uniform resignation protocol. General employees had to give their agency head three days' notice, while department and agency heads had to give the President one week's notice. Employees could retract notice during the intervening period; heads could withdraw it within the first three days. Noncompliant employees could face agency blacklists, and heads could face wider executive blacklists or an administrative fine of up to $50,000 in Las Vegas upon future executive employment. The administration justified the requirements as allowing time to track departures, find replacements, and maintain continuity. [ 31 ] Public and government communications SuddenRush12G promoted direct communication between citizens and officials. In December, he encouraged wider use of Twitter for information about elections, agencies, employment, and private businesses. He presented it as a way to reach legislators, Cabinet members, military leaders, and directors, and to increase government transparency. [ 32 ] On 25 December, he announced a bipartisan initiative to transfer government communications from Skype to Discord. Citing information leaks and concerns about Skype's safety, he required directors to begin using Discord and expected their staff and agents to follow. He also pointed to expanded chatroom capabilities and bots as reasons for the transition. [ 33 ] Foreign affairs and final months SuddenRush12G with the FBI during a mass patrol at the Bank of America in Las Vegas. Date unknown. On 20 February 2016, SuddenRush12G apologized to Italian President Colton, the Italian government, and Italian citizens following a breakdown in relations and war between the two countries. He attributed the rupture to poor communication and acknowledged that rogue citizens and military personnel had violated Italian sovereignty. He thanked Italy for agreeing to a peace treaty negotiated with the State Department and promised stronger oversight to prevent renewed incidents. The settlement restored peace with a country he described as a longstanding ally. [ 34 ] In his 29 May address, he reported that the State Department had made more than fifty state visits during his first term. He linked that diplomatic activity to increased international communication and highlighted both the Italian peace agreement and the response to the USSR among the administration's foreign-policy priorities. [ 35 ] The war with the United Kingdom also produced a dispute over nUSA's standing in the United Nations. In a November account, TimGeithner described nUSA's suspension from the organization and the loss of its permanent Security Council status during the crisis. TimGeithner publicly opposed withdrawal from the UN, arguing that membership was central to nUSA's diplomatic recognition. The administration also took part in international meetings and military appearances during this period. [ 36 ] Before leaving the presidency in January 2017, SuddenRush12G won election to the House of Representatives and became its Speaker. His two consecutive terms became a benchmark in later discussions of presidential reelection. The long-term survival of individual agency changes made during his presidency varied as later administrations revised the government. [ 37 ] In his farewell address on 20 January 2017, SuddenRush12G congratulated President-elect TheySinned and described the coming transfer of power as a democratic tradition. He thanked his administration, the armed forces, his vice presidents, and the electorate. Looking back over the year, he singled out military reconstruction, the new classification system, and private-sector employment as achievements, while presenting those results as collective efforts. He pledged confidence in the incoming administration and said that its success would also be the country's success. [ 38 ] In an address dated 28 January 2017, his successor TheySinned credited SuddenRush12G, TimGeithner, and Lumidas with negotiating the British peace plan. TheySinned stated that Congress had overridden SuddenRush12G's veto of the Sovereignty Act on 22 January, nullifying the arrangement, and reported a renewed British declaration of war. The renewed conflict occurred after SuddenRush12G's presidency. title: Sufferpoop
text: Sufferpoop 15th President of nUSA In office 14 April 2017 – 21 May 2017 [ 1 ] Preceded by Rapidaax Succeeded by Blasatack NARA presidential roster Sufferpoop is a Roblox account listed as the 15th President of the nUSA roleplay community. He served from 14 April until resigning on 21 May 2017; Blasatack was sworn in later that evening. Before his presidency, Sufferpoop held several offices in the Supreme Court, including chief justice, and served as Vice President under Rapidaax . [ 2 ] Judicial service Sufferpoop served as an associate justice of the Supreme Court in several periods beginning in 2014 and as chief justice from 1 July to 14 December 2015. The court roster also records him as Federal Elections Overseer from June to September 2016. [ 3 ] Presidency During his presidency, Sufferpoop nominated TimGeithner and SuddenRush12G to associate justice seats. The Senate confirmed both nominees 9–0 on 19 May 2017, and both were sworn in the following day. [ 4 ] Resignation At 9:29 p.m. on 21 May, an nUSA update announced that Sufferpoop had resigned. Three minutes later, Blasatack was reported as being sworn in; at 9:34 p.m., a second update announced that he was President. The announcements give no reason for Sufferpoop's resignation. [ 5 ] ↑ Nusapedia, “President of the United States” , presidential chronology, accessed 30 September 2026. ↑ The presidential chronology lists Sufferpoop's term as 14 April–21 May 2017: “President of the United States” , Nusapedia Wiki. NARA's roster places him as the 15th president between Rapidaax and Blastatack: Rapidaax, 14th ; Sufferpoop, 15th ; Blastatack, 16th . title: Supreme Court (nUSA)
text: Highest court of the United States The Supreme Court of the United States is the highest court in the federal judiciary. Its work encompasses review of lower-court cases, constitutional challenges, applications for emergency relief and the administration of the legal profession. The Court has also exercised Anytime Review , bringing disputes over government action directly within its constitutional scrutiny. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] The Court's history includes repeated struggles over the boundaries between the branches of government. In 2018 and 2019 it invalidated a compulsory administrative forum for employment complaints, stopped the creation of the State of Columbia, reviewed a President's impeachment and rejected executive control of attorney licensing. Later constitutional reorganizations altered the force of older precedent without erasing the institutional conflicts those cases recorded. [ 3 ] [ 4 ] [ 5 ] Jurisdiction and procedure Cases reach the Court through petitions for certiorari, appeals, applications, judicial complaints and requests for Anytime Review. Its docket distinguishes pending requests from accepted cases and final orders. Granting certiorari permits review; denying it leaves the Court without a merits decision on the question presented. Emergency orders may preserve or change the immediate position of the parties while leaving the final constitutional issue open. [ 6 ] [ 7 ] Anytime Review gave the Court an additional route into disputes over the actions of government. In the Columbia litigation, the Court initiated review alongside a petition brought by Kirkman. In Procursive's impeachment challenge, it held that the political-question objections associated with ordinary impeachment review did not prevent consideration in the Anytime Review context. The power made the Court a participant in constitutional confrontations that extended beyond appeals from routine civil or criminal judgments. [ 8 ] [ 9 ] Constitutional decisions, 2018–2019 Federal employment and access to court In Benda v. United States , decided 21 October 2018, the Court struck section 401(g) of the Consolidated Appropriations and Authorizations Act of August 2018. The provision forced federal employees to submit employment complaints to the National Labor Authority, later the Office of the Federal Inspector General, before seeking judicial relief. Chief Justice Holmes's opinion rejected the body's broad, compulsory and effectively unreviewable authority. Employees could thereafter take claims such as unlawful termination directly to court. [ 10 ] The decision combined an Article III analysis with objections grounded in basic justice and rational justification. Holmes was joined by Marshall, Bork and O'Connor; Gorsuch and Stewart dissented from the judgment. The case illustrated that describing a dispute as a public right did not end the constitutional inquiry into administrative adjudication. [ 11 ] The State of Columbia On 3 March 2019, In re Federal Government and Kirkman v. State of Columbia brought the proposed union of Washington and Las Vegas before the Court. Congress had omitted the consent of the municipalities' legislatures. The Court invalidated sections 101–104 of S. 127 and struck the dependent agency-transfer and court provisions in sections 106–107. The decision prevented the State of Columbia from acquiring a lawful governing structure and emphasized constitutional limits on federal attempts to reorganize local government. [ 12 ] Procursive's impeachment The impeachment of Procursive tested the Court's authority over Congress's most consequential sanction. After a Senate conviction on four articles, Procursive asked the Court to undo his removal. On 7 May it rejected his oath and due-process arguments, invalidated three articles, and sustained the false-arrest article. The President remained out of office even though most of the charges against him failed constitutional review. [ 13 ] The separate opinions exposed disagreement over the Ichigo standard requiring an impeachable offense to qualify at least as a crime or misdemeanor. Brandeis advocated a narrower role for judicial review and would have abandoned that standard. The case produced a divided constitutional analysis without a divided practical outcome: Procursive was not reinstated. [ 14 ] Control of the legal profession In Party v. Board of Law Examiners , decided 28 July 2019, the Court struck S. 147 in its entirety. Kirkman's original challenge to executive administration of the Bar had resulted in an injunction; after he and the Board sought to dissolve it, SheldonParty continued the appeal as substituted class representative. Justice Pitney's opinion held that attorney licensing was judicial power and could not be transferred to the executive. Bork and Chase agreed with that result while preserving Congress's authority to legislate on the Bar's structure. [ 15 ] The decision forms a central chapter in the history of the Federal Bar . It distinguished judicial control from an unrestricted right to practice law: the Court rejected the latter proposition while defending the former. [ 16 ] Orders, denials and separate statements Not every important controversy produced a binding merits ruling. In Psychodynamic v. Procursive , the Court denied review of Procursive's withdrawn resignation. Pitney and Chase, joined by three other justices, explained in a nonbinding statement that a resignation could be recalled before it took effect. Their reasoning illuminated the controversy without making the denial itself a constitutional judgment. [ 17 ] In Hudson v. House of Representatives , the Court denied review of a challenge to House committee subpoenas directed at three federal judges. The subpoenas had been rescinded. Bork's concurrence, joined by Chase, criticized legislative inquiries into judicial decisions, but that separate opinion did not transform the denial into a binding prohibition on congressional subpoenas. [ 18 ] Other 2019 dispositions resolved narrower procedural matters: Kirkman v. Bank of America concerned prejudice in a District Court dismissal, Ex parte Haven became moot, and a certified question in Board of Law Examiners v. [name withheld] was dismissed as improperly filed. Together with the major opinions, these orders show a court occupied with both constitutional disputes and the discipline of ordinary appellate procedure. [ 19 ] [ 20 ] [ 21 ] Membership, administration and the Bar The Court maintains membership and officer histories, term records, dockets, order lists, administrative directives and bound volumes. Its recorded term system has included four-month terms named after chief justices. Admission to practice and the work of clerks form part of its institutional administration as well as its adjudicatory work. [ 22 ] In July 2022, Chief Justice RummyLeroux proposed a Federal Bar Association subordinate to the Court, with licensing, ethics requirements and a path toward clerkships and judicial appointments. The proposal linked professional standards to the approaching opening of Boulder County and retained a separate Supreme Court Bar with broader practice privileges. [ 23 ] Resets and later constitutional disputes The July 2023 legal reset voided existing case law and court precedent alongside other legal materials. The replacement framework imposed archival duties and created new records arrangements for NARA and Congress. Older judgments remained part of the nation's history, while their former precedential authority did not automatically carry into the new legal order. [ 24 ] An August 2024 archives update counted six Supreme Court opinions issued during July. In May 2025, the Court became entangled in a wider dispute involving a presidential impeachment, the removal of the chief justice, sanctions against two associate justices and Justice Leroux's refusal to certify the impeachment. The President remained in office pending consideration by a three-judge District Court panel. The crisis placed the independence and continuity of the judiciary alongside the disputed legitimacy of the impeachment itself. title: SurpriseParty
text: SurpriseParty 17th President of nUSA In office 21 July 2017 – 1 November 2017 [ 1 ] Preceded by Blastatack Succeeded by SheldonParty SurpriseParty, 17th SurpriseParty was the 17th President of the nUSA roleplay community on Roblox. Her administration issued executive orders on federal hiring, employment protections, and the centralization of uniform sales. She also pursued the group's readmission to the roleplay United Nations . She announced her resignation with Vice President JustYourDailyNoob in October 2017, effective 1 November. [ 2 ] Administration SurpriseParty succeeded Blastatack on 21 July 2017. The vice-presidential roster records JustYourDailyNoob as her Vice President from that date through 1 November. By September, the administration was directing members to its public communication accounts, including the White House and Supreme Court, as well as accounts for the President and Vice President. [ 3 ] Two executive orders dated 27 July set out an employment schedule across executive agencies and departments and began moving uniform sales to the United States Federal Exchange. The first order assigned regular tryout or interview days, required minimum hiring at those events, and required written justification before an agency could set an employment cap. The second began the transfer of agency uniforms to a central store and specified that its funds could not be distributed without congressional appropriation. [ 4 ] An order dated 25 August changed the rules for dismissals and agency-wide employment reforms. It required managers to give employees a reason for termination and one week’s notice of mass reforms, while establishing an anonymous complaint process overseen by the White House chief of staff. A later order dated 28 October directed that promotions through lower and middle ranks be based on performance and prohibited nepotistic hiring. [ 5 ] United Nations and resignation In October, the administration submitted an application for nUSA to rejoin the United Nations roleplay organization. The channel first reported that the application had passed the General Assembly and was awaiting a Security Council vote. Later the same day, SurpriseParty announced that nUSA had been readmitted after weeks of work with allies. The preserved announcements do not include a Security Council vote, so the precise decision sequence is not documented in the archive. [ 6 ] On 30 October, a post under the display name BUDDHA announced that the President and Vice President @not sam would resign on 1 November and promised a statement about the reasons and transition. The next day's notice said that a successor had taken office following the resignations of SurpriseParty and JustYourDailyNoob and linked to a post from an account styled “SheIdonParty.” The export does not explain the different names used in the two notices; it redacts the successor post's Discord identity. The NARA succession register identifies SheldonParty as the next President.
