[ 17 ] The early notices linked the same group, numbered 758071, that remained associated with the later capital games. The original Washington description subsequently listed public sites including the Washington Monument, Lincoln Memorial, World War II Memorial, and White House. That description presents the landmarks associated with the surviving place, although their exact dates of addition are uncertain. The city's continuity rests on its association with the national community and capital institutions rather than an unchanged set of buildings. [ 17 ] [ 18 ] Washington's development occurred alongside the emergence of Las Vegas . An earlier Las Vegas place was created in September 2013, and its main group-associated place was created in June 2014. Las Vegas offered a distinct city environment built principally by Pauljkl , with casinos and a substantial municipal police organization. The existence of both cities gave the community more than one setting for public employment and local government, while Washington retained its identity as the federal capital. [ 19 ] The relationship between cities and national management became contentious in June 2014. On 27 June, Verbero announced a proposed removal of Pauljkl and Las Vegas, alleged misconduct, and promised a replacement Washington city. Pauljkl disputed the allegations and requested a fuller explanation. He quoted an earlier notice that gave retaining funds within the group as a reason for the proposed separation and identified 4 July as its intended date. Bailey552 opposed the split, warning that it would harm activity in both Las Vegas and the wider community. The dispute concerned control of a major city and the distribution of community activity; the announcement alone did not establish that the proposed replacement was completed. [ 20 ] Federal policy also affected Washington's local services. During Jcmand 's administration, an order transferred local police departments in Washington and Las Vegas out of federal control. The change distinguished municipal policing from the federal agencies that operated in the same cities. Later conflicts and security alerts nevertheless brought federal personnel into Washington, making the capital a place where local police work and national security responsibilities intersected. [ 21 ] On 22 February 2016, President SuddenRush12G directed deployments to Washington and Las Vegas after briefings concerning threats from the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics. His statement raised the readiness level from DEFCON 5 to DEFCON 4 and issued a travel warning. The measures were presented as protection of American cities and citizens. Washington's significance in this episode came from its place within national security planning, not from a change of map or municipal charter. [ 22 ] Rebuilding Washington, 2017 A major rebuilding effort was publicly documented in November 2017. On 2 November, Agency_Manager sought builders for a modern Washington map for the United States group, with an offered baseline of 100,000 Robux and the possibility of a higher price. The recruitment post described the project as rebuilding the current Washington and emphasized the scale of a city and the need for buildings resembling a real place. Pauljkl participated in the discussion, encouraging the recruiter to explain the project and its requirements more clearly. [ 23 ] The recruitment offer made the rebuild a project with specific construction needs, rather than an ordinary update to a single facility. Its budget figure was an initial offer, not a final account of expenditure. The description sought modern builders capable of contributing particular buildings to a larger map. It also showed that Washington already existed and was being replaced or extensively reworked, linking the coming city to the earlier capital. [ 23 ] On 18 November, Squareheaddude announced a Washington trailer and said release was expected that month. The embedded video title credited Squareheaddude and Pauljkl. On 21 November, a further announcement set 1 December as the release date for the new Washington, District of Columbia. The release publicity included planned streams by Technozo and described the city as reborn. [ 24 ] [ 2 ] The rebuilt city was associated with place 1213026131, whose asset record began in late November. Release notices on 30 November and 1 December advertised an opening at approximately 5 p.m. Eastern Time on 1 December. Later that day, Squareheaddude asked citizens to report bugs and said he was undertaking fixes. Public access and maintenance therefore began together, with the city still receiving corrections after its opening. [ 14 ] [ 2 ] The first weeks brought both service recruitment and gameplay changes. On 9 December, Squareheaddude announced that council elections would wait until after the presidential elections, but invited applications to run the Metropolitan Police Department because the streets already required policing. On 12 December, he confirmed a fire update and new WASD vehicle controls. He promoted the vehicles as lag-free, a performance claim accompanying the announcement. The sequence placed policing, emergency response, and transport among the practical concerns of the newly opened capital. [ 25 ] [ 26 ] Elections and development, 2018–2019 The new city's municipal institutions developed after its release. A 17 February 2018 notice announced that planned mayoral elections had fallen through and that Technozo had been appointed mayor. It advertised the first councilor election for the new Washington, with eligibility including membership in the United States group and a rank of Middle Class Citizen or higher. The appointment and election were distinct steps in organizing local government. [ 27 ] On 25 February, the announced council winners were AdamCarpenterJr, IBreakingNewsI, Robbyiscrazy, ADVlCE, Dariel_Powell, LilWill_OG, SevMacLeod, and DevGralius. A separate announcement that evening linked the Washington council's laws-and-codes board. The council thus had both elected membership and a public legislative record, providing an institutional counterpart to the city's development and service administration. [ 28 ] Another municipal election cycle used a dedicated D.C. Elections Center in July. Preliminary voting opened on 27 July; the following day, the preliminary stage closed ahead of schedule and final voting began. The final ballot included council candidates and five mayoral candidates. On 1 August, the election administrator announced eight council winners and certified TheySinned as the mayoral winner after disqualifying the initial winner on stated electoral-fraud grounds. The disqualification was the administrator's finding and announcement; the certified result placed TheySinned ahead of the remaining eligible candidates. [ 15 ] [ 29 ] Development continued alongside these elections. On 19 November 2018, Squareheaddude announced a large Washington update and directed citizens to the update log. On 24 November, he advertised a forthcoming lawful trucking-delivery system. The proposed system would add work outside government and law enforcement, although the announcement did not establish its eventual implementation date. City development was therefore concerned with both public institutions and activities available to ordinary citizens. [ 30 ] Banking was another area of change. On 3 April 2019, Squareheaddude sought a new banking company to replace Capital Bank, inviting established companies and proposals for a new bank. The notice connected a commercial institution to the operation of the capital. It did not identify a successful replacement or announce when a successor opened. [ 31 ] In June 2019, a Washington development survey invited citizens to comment on hypothetical changes. Respondents were required to supply their Roblox usernames, and the notice offered three cash prizes. It expressly described the questions as hypothetical, making the survey a consultation rather than a list of confirmed changes. The exercise nevertheless gave citizens a direct route to express views about the city's future. [ 32 ] Performance improvements accompanied the expansion of public use. A 6 September test invited citizens to try Washington with a 45-player cap. Its stated priorities were reducing vehicle flinging, introducing a menu for new players, and increasing stability for larger servers. Participants were offered unlimited test money and asked to play normally. The test addressed both the behavior of existing systems and the accessibility of the city to newcomers; the announced cap was a test setting rather than a measurement of ordinary attendance. [ 16 ] State of Columbia controversy Main articles: State of Columbia (nUSA) and In re Federal Government (nUSA) Washington's municipal status became central to a constitutional dispute in March 2019. Congress's S. 127, titled To restore municipal government , sought to unite Washington and Las Vegas as the State of Columbia. It provided for a provisional governor, the exercise of interim executive and legislative authority, the negotiation of a constitution, and associated agency and court arrangements. The new jurisdiction was publicly announced on 2 March. [ 33 ] On 3 March, the Supreme Court invalidated the principal merger provisions in In re Federal Government , heard with Kirkman v. State of Columbia . Neither city's legislature had consented. The Court required clear, public, and unambiguous municipal approval and held that notice to local authorities could not substitute for consent. It struck sections 101–104 and dependent sections 106–107, including arrangements that could not operate independently of the invalid union. [ 6 ] The Court also rejected an attempt to avoid the consent requirement by treating Las Vegas as already deprived of municipal status under H.R. 179. It did not decide the validity of H.R. 179 itself, and observed that its language continued to refer to Las Vegas as a municipality. For the proposed union, both cities remained municipalities whose legislatures had to agree. The judgment preserved Washington's separate municipal position and made its council consequential in the exercise of federal power over local government. [ 6 ] Public activity and municipal dissolution, 2020–2023 Washington continued to host government and community activity while other cities experienced changing levels of participation. On 16 April 2020, management described Las Vegas as less active and less fully operational than Washington, while retaining Las Vegas's official-city status. The comparison indicated Washington's greater activity at that time without establishing a permanent closure of Las Vegas or a complete end to its public services. [ 34 ] Local executive initiatives also shaped public life. On 8 February 2021, DirectorPoke announced Municipal Order 10-0001, Free Pizza Fridays, offering D.C. citizens a free slice each Friday. A second order extended municipal protection privileges to the mayor's cabinet and incoming mayoral leadership. Further notices on 11 and 19 February invited citizens to participate, and a 12 February account described a successful gathering and linked photographs. The program was a municipal policy and public event; the same account requested that developers add pizza slices, indicating that the event's civic organization and its in-game objects were separate matters. [ 35 ] On 27 June 2021, management announced that declining municipal participation, assessed through activity and voting statistics, would lead to the discontinuation of local government. The notice set 1 July at midnight Eastern Time as the effective point, made the City Council and mayor's office defunct, and directed team-bearing services into the federal government. It also asked Congress to supply an appropriate law and left open the possibility of a limited reopening if activity improved. A follow-up on 2 July confirmed that the D.C. government had been dissolved the preceding night. [ 7 ] The affected services included MPD, EMS, the Fire Department, and the United States State Police. Their proposed transfer concerned administration of the city services, not the disappearance of Washington as a game or the erasure of its capital role. The management notice also distinguished the dissolution decision from the legislative work needed to regularize agency arrangements. [ 7 ] In November 2022, Boulder County opened as another center of municipal activity. Federal preparations for its opening included agency and legal-service changes. Washington nevertheless continued to matter in protective-service policy. On 25 January 2023, President TacticalRock101 restored the Federal Protective Service to active status, citing increased activity in Washington and the unavailability of the MPD team. The order demonstrated the use of federal protection to address a gap in municipal coverage. [ 36 ] [ 37 ] On the same date, management discussed Boulder development and identified a new District of Columbia as a future project for the development team. The statement invited suggestions while work continued on Boulder's Dentsville and federal facilities. Washington's next generation was therefore part of a wider program of city development before the explicit DC2/DC3 roadmap of 2024. [ 38 ] Return of municipal services and DC2 renewal, 2024–2025 In January 2024, a renewed Washington administration drew on personnel from Boulder County. AIex announced an agreement with Boulder governor AlexReign on 17 January, providing municipal staff with lateral-transfer routes into D.C. departments. AlexReign was designated interim mayor pending council elections. MasonRockefeller was appointed MPD chief, with the Boulder County sheriff as deputy chief and the CPD chief as assistant chief. Police staffs were directed to merge into the MPD and arrange their rank transfers through its leadership. [ 8 ] The same transition addressed emergency services. Boulder deputy fire chief peep was designated to lead Washington's Fire Department because Boulder's fire chief, InfiniteOne, also served in management. Posiedon17 was appointed EMS chief; the announcement stated that Boulder had no equivalent EMS service. The arrangements supplied the capital with leadership and a transfer process across several services instead of treating each appointment as an isolated recruitment. [ 8 ] Rockefeller subsequently announced preparations for a new police command and its first class. Officers were instructed to wait while the department organized its operations, and a Metro academy would replace FLETC in that transition. This training arrangement belonged to the 2024 reorganization; the later DC3 program again assigned a central role to FLETC. [ 39 ] [ 40 ] The January management transition also proposed investment in D.C. development, advertising, and partnerships. Management wanted more national activity to occur inside Washington: its example was a citizen entering the game, driving to the courthouse, and attending a trial at the actual facility. The plan linked city development to the operation of public institutions, while leaving individual projects to be completed through subsequent work. [ 41 ] Developer recruitment on 8 March distinguished work on the existing city from the new capital. Benda587 supervised current D.C.; chexburger supervised new D.C. scripting; and Sheev_PalpatineTGR supervised new D.C. building. The announcement primarily sought builders and modelers for the new project, while allowing less experienced applicants to join the current-city team. These responsibilities were the announced arrangement at that time and did not constitute an exhaustive final credit list. [ 42 ] On 11 March, management asserted the City Council's role in representing citizens to developers and directing development requests through local government. An accompanying declaration that a revised charter was active was withdrawn later that day. The reversal preserved the council as an advisory intermediary while allowing deliberation over the charter. It also clarified that federal institutions could still legislate or request additions and renovations. The episode exposed the overlap between municipal representation, federal law, and management control of the game. [ 43 ] The April owner update formally described parallel work on DC2 and DC3. UKR41NIAN promised refinements and substantial new content for DC2, including a crime and private-business update, while targeting the first quarter of 2025 for DC3. On 11 May 2024, SupremeFedoraa announced that the crime update was live, describing it as the largest update since 2017 and saying it had been developed in thirteen days. The release confirmed a crime update to the existing city, although the announcement did not enumerate every previously proposed business feature. [ 3 ] [ 44 ] Local elections continued during the development period. On 23 February 2025, the Federal Election Commission declared PeepGPT mayor-elect with 35.89 percent of the vote and announced council winners for the coming term. The notice expressly distinguished election from taking office, stating that PeepGPT would remain mayor-elect until sworn in. It gave 19 May as the term's expiry. Later in 2025, municipal elections were included alongside congressional contests in the Winter Election Extravaganza . [ 45 ] [ 46 ] DC3 Development and building program DC3 was developed as the next generation of Washington while the existing city continued to receive attention. The April 2024 roadmap set a Q1 2025 launch target and connected the project to efforts to rebuild the development team, restore activity, and establish a clearer direction following changes in senior leadership. The later 2026 opening occurred beyond that initial target. Development of a new city and continued support for DC2 were concurrent commitments rather than a completed handover in April 2024. [ 3 ] [ 9 ] The building program sought contributions from the institutions expected to use the capital. On 20 February 2025, AcidRaps advertised a DC3 building quality-assurance team with approximately five participants from each major field: judicial and legislative processes, enforcement, transport and parks, the private sector, and the military. The notice specifically referred to courts and town halls, agency buildings, road details, public-service buildings, and parks. Participants were to check representation of their sectors and help establish consistent standards for colors, doors, and materials across the map. [ 47 ] This review process treated city design as a set of spaces for different kinds of public activity. The aim was to avoid large differences in building quality while accommodating the practical needs of agencies and civilian organizations. The recruitment described planned review responsibilities, not a certification that every proposed facility was finished. It nevertheless gave judicial, legislative, service, commercial, and military users a place in the development process. [ 47 ] Funding was also addressed publicly. On 12 April 2025, American_Online introduced an nUSA Sponsor Discord subscription as a way to contribute to the development program. The announcement stated that sponsor revenue would support DC3 and advertising for the current game and said ownership members had personally invested thousands in the project. The funding claims were ownership's account; no total development budget was specified. Subscription benefits included communication privileges and access to the political feed. [ 48 ] Sponsor participation extended to playtesting. On 13 May 2026, Bathamza reported touring the DC3 White House earlier that week during a sponsor playtest. He praised its building style and gun system and described sponsors participating as Secret Service personnel with standardized uniforms, accessories, and weapons. He thanked CIonk_Man, Jon_Ral, and the development team, and expressed an expectation of release in July. His account documented the tested setting and credited contributors while remaining a participant's assessment of the experience. [ 49 ] Release schedule and paid Early Access On 29 April 2026, nUSA announced that DC3 would arrive in July. The announcement promoted a living open world, new systems, detailed environments, and a more ambitious recreation of Washington. These were development aims and promotional assessments accompanying a release forecast. The first specific public-access date followed on 10 July, when nUSA announced Early Access for 24 July at 8 p.m. Eastern Time. [ 50 ] [ 9 ] The July announcement expressly described Early Access as a beta. Systems and builds were to be polished, expanded, and refined before a full release. The city was presented as an opportunity to begin using the world under construction, with further work expected after players entered. The announcement therefore separated opening access from completing the development program. [ 9 ] Early Access opened on 24 July. The opening notice confirmed paid admission and said the game would become free at full release. Some systems were intentionally disabled and would be introduced over time. Mobile gameplay was available but not yet fully supported. Ownership also stated that the current experience did not represent the city's final form and invited feedback to help determine subsequent development. [ 9 ] The asset associated with DC3, place 140564898391131, was created on 21 July. Its later city description offered participation in Congress, policing, defense of the capital, bank robbery, and the presidency. The description presented public office and street activity within the same Washington environment. Its asset history identifies the new place separately from the 2017 city, while the July announcement supplies the opening milestone. [ 14 ] [ 51 ] Free beta On 30 August, ownership announced that DC3 would become free to enter on 4 September. The announcement described a larger, more detailed Washington with new systems and a foundation for continued additions. It again identified the forthcoming opening as a beta. The change broadened access from the paid Early Access stage without declaring the city finished. [ 10 ] Publicity on 3 September specified a noon Eastern Time opening on the following day. The 4 September notice confirmed that DC3 was open to everyone in free beta and thanked the original paid-access participants. It warned of bugs, unfinished areas, balance changes, and evolving features, and requested feedback. The free opening was therefore a second access milestone within ongoing development. [ 52 ] [ 10 ] The change in access also made Washington available to citizens who had not participated in the paid period. Management encouraged both long-standing members and newcomers to enter the city. Subsequent thanks emphasized participation, exploration, and feedback. These statements expressed ownership's enthusiasm for the opening; they did not supply independently measured attendance or establish a completed development stage. [ 10 ] [ 53 ] Government readiness and law enforcement The approach of DC3 affected executive administration before the public beta. On 4 July 2026, President Jsjsjbsd announced an executive order establishing a Task Force on DC3 Readiness. He described declining agency activity and a disorganized structure as problems that required attention before new citizens arrived. The task force, led by UndeadsValor, was to review departments, address inactive leadership, and prepare the executive branch for the new city. [ 54 ] The President returned to these preparations in his July public statements. His 14 July State of the Union cited the readiness task force among the administration's measures, and his 16 July post-election address described DC3 as an opportunity to revise agency operations, consolidate where necessary, and change hiring practices. These were presidential policy commitments tied to the new capital's arrival, rather than evidence that all planned organizational changes had already been completed. [ 55 ] Law-enforcement training was another preparation. On 8 August, an application notice for a FLETC director described the center as the centralized authority for training, examining, and certifying law-enforcement officers in DC3. Recruits were to attend before entering an agency. The same notice assigned FLETC a conduct-enforcement role, including revocation of licenses when misconduct was proven. This program connected police employment to training and certification, with a disciplinary mechanism extending across agencies. [ 40 ] The 2026 arrangement differed from the Metro academy announced during Washington's 2024 police transition. Training institutions changed as the capital's departments were reorganized. Their functions should therefore be understood in their respective periods: the 2024 academy prepared the reorganized municipal police, while the August 2026 announcement described a centralized DC3 law-enforcement system. [ 39 ] [ 40 ] Employment and early public administration On 4 September, Jsjsjbsd addressed the press and public to commemorate DC3's opening. He stated that USAJOBS had handled more than 500 applications and that agencies were conducting a program of official events. These figures were the president's account of administrative activity. His address connected the city's launch with recruitment and efforts to prepare departments for new participation. [ 56 ] Employment subsequently made direct use of city facilities. On 19 September, the President reported using DC3's new jobs system to interview candidates on the spot and hire two people. He said his chief of staff was adapting USAJOBS to accommodate the in-game system for departments and agencies with a team. The account identified an implemented hiring interaction rather than only a promised future feature: candidates could be interviewed in the city and hired through its system. [ 11 ] The integration of employment with buildings and agency teams gave Washington a practical role in public administration. Earlier recruitment had often directed citizens to contact leaders or submit external applications; the September account described city facilities used in the interview and hiring process. The president's statement also indicated that integration remained in progress, so the initial use did not establish that every agency had completed its transition. [ 17 ] [ 25 ] [ 11 ] Economic plans accompanied the launch. The 4 September address promised a forthcoming nUSA Stock Exchange under the Department of Commerce and Labor. A cabinet account the next day likewise described the market as forthcoming and said the military was working on new maps. These statements concerned planned additions. They did not establish an operational stock exchange or a completed new military map at the free-beta opening. [ 56 ] [ 57 ] Election system Main articles: Elections in nUSA and Federal Election Code (nUSA) On 7 September 2026, the Federal Election Commission invited citizens to test elections in DC3. Candidate registration was located at the District Court building, and voting booths were near MPD headquarters. Both were marked by yellow checkmarks on the minimap. Participants were asked to register candidates, gather signatures, and cast votes so that problems could be identified before a real election. [ 58 ] The notice described a normal qualification of two hours of play within the preceding thirty days for candidate registration, support of a candidate, and voting in elections or referendums. During the test, the requirement was temporarily reduced to 0.1 hours, or six minutes. Candidates could not register in two simultaneous elections; changing contests required the commission to disqualify the candidate from the first. The test therefore assessed not only voting booths but also participation requirements and candidate management. [ 58 ] On 25 September, the commission announced the forthcoming Senate and House Class I elections as the first elections in DC3. Registration was scheduled for 5–8 October, with ten signatures required from non-incumbents. Voting was scheduled for 9–11 October. Seven representatives and five senators were to be elected, with terms beginning on 11 October. The announced locations remained the courthouse registration desk and voting near MPD headquarters. [ 12 ] The commission also encouraged citizens to consult an in-game election schedule at the courthouse, saying that short reminders would replace announcements of this length. The change made the capital itself a place to obtain current electoral information, as well as to register and vote. As of the September announcement, the October contests were prospective; their outcomes were not yet part of DC3's completed election history. [ 12 ] Municipal government Charter and executive offices Washington's municipal government operates through a charter and local legislation within the wider federal system. H.R. 41, D.C. Charter Revised, was recorded as passed by both houses of Congress and signed into law. Its text provided for a mayor, deputy mayor, council, local departments, and procedures for ordinances, nominations, succession, and charter amendments. Later council records contain further charter changes, so the revised charter represents a particular framework in the city's institutional history rather than an assumption that every provision remained unchanged. [ 4 ] [ 59 ] Under H.R. 41's framework, the mayor headed municipal government and was a non-voting member of the council with a right to be heard. The mayor and deputy mayor were elected together for three-month terms. The mayor nominated department heads for council confirmation, supervised municipal employees, enforced ordinances, and could issue administrative orders consistent with higher law. It advertised the first councilor election for the new Washington, with eligibility including membership in the United States group and a rank of Middle Class Citizen or higher. The appointment and election were distinct steps in organizing local government. [ 27 ] On 25 February, the announced council winners were AdamCarpenterJr, IBreakingNewsI, Robbyiscrazy, ADVlCE, Dariel_Powell, LilWill_OG, SevMacLeod, and DevGralius. A separate announcement that evening linked the Washington council's laws-and-codes board. The council thus had both elected membership and a public legislative record, providing an institutional counterpart to the city's development and service administration. [ 28 ] Another municipal election cycle used a dedicated D.C. Elections Center in July. Preliminary voting opened on 27 July; the following day, the preliminary stage closed ahead of schedule and final voting began. The final ballot included council candidates and five mayoral candidates. On 1 August, the election administrator announced eight council winners and certified TheySinned as the mayoral winner after disqualifying the initial winner on stated electoral-fraud grounds. The disqualification was the administrator's finding and announcement; the certified result placed TheySinned ahead of the remaining eligible candidates. [ 15 ] [ 29 ] Development continued alongside these elections. On 19 November 2018, Squareheaddude announced a large Washington update and directed citizens to the update log. On 24 November, he advertised a forthcoming lawful trucking-delivery system. The proposed system would add work outside government and law enforcement, although the announcement did not establish its eventual implementation date. City development was therefore concerned with both public institutions and activities available to ordinary citizens. [ 30 ] Banking was another area of change. On 3 April 2019, Squareheaddude sought a new banking company to replace Capital Bank, inviting established companies and proposals for a new bank. The notice connected a commercial institution to the operation of the capital. It did not identify a successful replacement or announce when a successor opened. [ 31 ] In June 2019, a Washington development survey invited citizens to comment on hypothetical changes. Respondents were required to supply their Roblox usernames, and the notice offered three cash prizes. It expressly described the questions as hypothetical, making the survey a consultation rather than a list of confirmed changes. The exercise nevertheless gave citizens a direct route to express views about the city's future. [ 32 ] Performance improvements accompanied the expansion of public use. A 6 September test invited citizens to try Washington with a 45-player cap. Its stated priorities were reducing vehicle flinging, introducing a menu for new players, and increasing stability for larger servers. Participants were offered unlimited test money and asked to play normally. The test addressed both the behavior of existing systems and the accessibility of the city to newcomers; the announced cap was a test setting rather than a measurement of ordinary attendance. [ 16 ] State of Columbia controversy Main articles: State of Columbia (nUSA) and In re Federal Government (nUSA) Washington's municipal status became central to a constitutional dispute in March 2019. Congress's S. 127, titled To restore municipal government , sought to unite Washington and Las Vegas as the State of Columbia. It provided for a provisional governor, the exercise of interim executive and legislative authority, the negotiation of a constitution, and associated agency and court arrangements. The new jurisdiction was publicly announced on 2 March. [ 33 ] On 3 March, the Supreme Court invalidated the principal merger provisions in In re Federal Government , heard with Kirkman v. State of Columbia . Neither city's legislature had consented. The Court required clear, public, and unambiguous municipal approval and held that notice to local authorities could not substitute for consent. It struck sections 101–104 and dependent sections 106–107, including arrangements that could not operate independently of the invalid union. [ 6 ] The Court also rejected an attempt to avoid the consent requirement by treating Las Vegas as already deprived of municipal status under H.R. 179. It did not decide the validity of H.R. 179 itself, and observed that its language continued to refer to Las Vegas as a municipality. For the proposed union, both cities remained municipalities whose legislatures had to agree. The judgment preserved Washington's separate municipal position and made its council consequential in the exercise of federal power over local government. [ 6 ] Public activity and municipal dissolution, 2020–2023 Washington continued to host government and community activity while other cities experienced changing levels of participation. On 16 April 2020, management described Las Vegas as less active and less fully operational than Washington, while retaining Las Vegas's official-city status. The comparison indicated Washington's greater activity at that time without establishing a permanent closure of Las Vegas or a complete end to its public services. [ 34 ] Local executive initiatives also shaped public life. On 8 February 2021, DirectorPoke announced Municipal Order 10-0001, Free Pizza Fridays, offering D.C. citizens a free slice each Friday. A second order extended municipal protection privileges to the mayor's cabinet and incoming mayoral leadership. Further notices on 11 and 19 February invited citizens to participate, and a 12 February account described a successful gathering and linked photographs. The program was a municipal policy and public event; the same account requested that developers add pizza slices, indicating that the event's civic organization and its in-game objects were separate matters. [ 35 ] On 27 June 2021, management announced that declining municipal participation, assessed through activity and voting statistics, would lead to the discontinuation of local government. The notice set 1 July at midnight Eastern Time as the effective point, made the City Council and mayor's office defunct, and directed team-bearing services into the federal government. It also asked Congress to supply an appropriate law and left open the possibility of a limited reopening if activity improved. A follow-up on 2 July confirmed that the D.C. government had been dissolved the preceding night. [ 7 ] The affected services included MPD, EMS, the Fire Department, and the United States State Police. Their proposed transfer concerned administration of the city services, not the disappearance of Washington as a game or the erasure of its capital role. The management notice also distinguished the dissolution decision from the legislative work needed to regularize agency arrangements. [ 7 ] In November 2022, Boulder County opened as another center of municipal activity. Federal preparations for its opening included agency and legal-service changes. Washington nevertheless continued to matter in protective-service policy. On 25 January 2023, President TacticalRock101 restored the Federal Protective Service to active status, citing increased activity in Washington and the unavailability of the MPD team. The order demonstrated the use of federal protection to address a gap in municipal coverage. [ 36 ] [ 37 ] On the same date, management discussed Boulder development and identified a new District of Columbia as a future project for the development team. The statement invited suggestions while work continued on Boulder's Dentsville and federal facilities. Washington's next generation was therefore part of a wider program of city development before the explicit DC2/DC3 roadmap of 2024. [ 38 ] Return of municipal services and DC2 renewal, 2024–2025 In January 2024, a renewed Washington administration drew on personnel from Boulder County. AIex announced an agreement with Boulder governor AlexReign on 17 January, providing municipal staff with lateral-transfer routes into D.C. departments. AlexReign was designated interim mayor pending council elections. MasonRockefeller was appointed MPD chief, with the Boulder County sheriff as deputy chief and the CPD chief as assistant chief. Police staffs were directed to merge into the MPD and arrange their rank transfers through its leadership. [ 8 ] The same transition addressed emergency services. Boulder deputy fire chief peep was designated to lead Washington's Fire Department because Boulder's fire chief, InfiniteOne, also served in management. Posiedon17 was appointed EMS chief; the announcement stated that Boulder had no equivalent EMS service. The arrangements supplied the capital with leadership and a transfer process across several services instead of treating each appointment as an isolated recruitment. [ 8 ] Rockefeller subsequently announced preparations for a new police command and its first class. Officers were instructed to wait while the department organized its operations, and a Metro academy would replace FLETC in that transition. This training arrangement belonged to the 2024 reorganization; the later DC3 program again assigned a central role to FLETC. [ 39 ] [ 40 ] The January management transition also proposed investment in D.C. development, advertising, and partnerships. Management wanted more national activity to occur inside Washington: its example was a citizen entering the game, driving to the courthouse, and attending a trial at the actual facility. The plan linked city development to the operation of public institutions, while leaving individual projects to be completed through subsequent work. [ 41 ] Developer recruitment on 8 March distinguished work on the existing city from the new capital. Benda587 supervised current D.C.; chexburger supervised new D.C. scripting; and Sheev_PalpatineTGR supervised new D.C. building. The announcement primarily sought builders and modelers for the new project, while allowing less experienced applicants to join the current-city team. These responsibilities were the announced arrangement at that time and did not constitute an exhaustive final credit list. [ 42 ] On 11 March, management asserted the City Council's role in representing citizens to developers and directing development requests through local government. An accompanying declaration that a revised charter was active was withdrawn later that day. The reversal preserved the council as an advisory intermediary while allowing deliberation over the charter. It also clarified that federal institutions could still legislate or request additions and renovations. The episode exposed the overlap between municipal representation, federal law, and management control of the game. [ 43 ] The April owner update formally described parallel work on DC2 and DC3. UKR41NIAN promised refinements and substantial new content for DC2, including a crime and private-business update, while targeting the first quarter of 2025 for DC3. On 11 May 2024, SupremeFedoraa announced that the crime update was live, describing it as the largest update since 2017 and saying it had been developed in thirteen days. The release confirmed a crime update to the existing city, although the announcement did not enumerate every previously proposed business feature. [ 3 ] [ 44 ] Local elections continued during the development period. On 23 February 2025, the Federal Election Commission declared PeepGPT mayor-elect with 35.89 percent of the vote and announced council winners for the coming term. The notice expressly distinguished election from taking office, stating that PeepGPT would remain mayor-elect until sworn in. It gave 19 May as the term's expiry. Later in 2025, municipal elections were included alongside congressional contests in the Winter Election Extravaganza . [ 45 ] [ 46 ] DC3 Development and building program DC3 was developed as the next generation of Washington while the existing city continued to receive attention. The April 2024 roadmap set a Q1 2025 launch target and connected the project to efforts to rebuild the development team, restore activity, and establish a clearer direction following changes in senior leadership. The later 2026 opening occurred beyond that initial target. Development of a new city and continued support for DC2 were concurrent commitments rather than a completed handover in April 2024. [ 3 ] [ 9 ] The building program sought contributions from the institutions expected to use the capital. On 20 February 2025, AcidRaps advertised a DC3 building quality-assurance team with approximately five participants from each major field: judicial and legislative processes, enforcement, transport and parks, the private sector, and the military. The notice specifically referred to courts and town halls, agency buildings, road details, public-service buildings, and parks. Participants were to check representation of their sectors and help establish consistent standards for colors, doors, and materials across the map. [ 47 ] This review process treated city design as a set of spaces for different kinds of public activity. The aim was to avoid large differences in building quality while accommodating the practical needs of agencies and civilian organizations. The recruitment described planned review responsibilities, not a certification that every proposed facility was finished. It nevertheless gave judicial, legislative, service, commercial, and military users a place in the development process. [ 47 ] Funding was also addressed publicly. On 12 April 2025, American_Online introduced an nUSA Sponsor Discord subscription as a way to contribute to the development program. The announcement stated that sponsor revenue would support DC3 and advertising for the current game and said ownership members had personally invested thousands in the project. The funding claims were ownership's account; no total development budget was specified. Subscription benefits included communication privileges and access to the political feed. [ 48 ] Sponsor participation extended to playtesting. On 13 May 2026, Bathamza reported touring the DC3 White House earlier that week during a sponsor playtest. He praised its building style and gun system and described sponsors participating as Secret Service personnel with standardized uniforms, accessories, and weapons. He thanked CIonk_Man, Jon_Ral, and the development team, and expressed an expectation of release in July. His account documented the tested setting and credited contributors while remaining a participant's assessment of the experience. [ 49 ] Release schedule and paid Early Access On 29 April 2026, nUSA announced that DC3 would arrive in July. The announcement promoted a living open world, new systems, detailed environments, and a more ambitious recreation of Washington. These were development aims and promotional assessments accompanying a release forecast. The first specific public-access date followed on 10 July, when nUSA announced Early Access for 24 July at 8 p.m. Eastern Time. [ 50 ] [ 9 ] The July announcement expressly described Early Access as a beta. Systems and builds were to be polished, expanded, and refined before a full release. The city was presented as an opportunity to begin using the world under construction, with further work expected after players entered. The announcement therefore separated opening access from completing the development program. [ 9 ] Early Access opened on 24 July. The opening notice confirmed paid admission and said the game would become free at full release. Some systems were intentionally disabled and would be introduced over time. Mobile gameplay was available but not yet fully supported. Ownership also stated that the current experience did not represent the city's final form and invited feedback to help determine subsequent development. [ 9 ] The asset associated with DC3, place 140564898391131, was created on 21 July. Its later city description offered participation in Congress, policing, defense of the capital, bank robbery, and the presidency. The description presented public office and street activity within the same Washington environment. Its asset history identifies the new place separately from the 2017 city, while the July announcement supplies the opening milestone. [ 14 ] [ 51 ] Free beta On 30 August, ownership announced that DC3 would become free to enter on 4 September. The announcement described a larger, more detailed Washington with new systems and a foundation for continued additions. It again identified the forthcoming opening as a beta. The change broadened access from the paid Early Access stage without declaring the city finished. [ 10 ] Publicity on 3 September specified a noon Eastern Time opening on the following day. The 4 September notice confirmed that DC3 was open to everyone in free beta and thanked the original paid-access participants. It warned of bugs, unfinished areas, balance changes, and evolving features, and requested feedback. The free opening was therefore a second access milestone within ongoing development. [ 52 ] [ 10 ] The change in access also made Washington available to citizens who had not participated in the paid period. Management encouraged both long-standing members and newcomers to enter the city. Subsequent thanks emphasized participation, exploration, and feedback. These statements expressed ownership's enthusiasm for the opening; they did not supply independently measured attendance or establish a completed development stage. [ 10 ] [ 53 ] Government readiness and law enforcement The approach of DC3 affected executive administration before the public beta. On 4 July 2026, President Jsjsjbsd announced an executive order establishing a Task Force on DC3 Readiness. He described declining agency activity and a disorganized structure as problems that required attention before new citizens arrived. The task force, led by UndeadsValor, was to review departments, address inactive leadership, and prepare the executive branch for the new city. [ 54 ] The President returned to these preparations in his July public statements. His 14 July State of the Union cited the readiness task force among the administration's measures, and his 16 July post-election address described DC3 as an opportunity to revise agency operations, consolidate where necessary, and change hiring practices. These were presidential policy commitments tied to the new capital's arrival, rather than evidence that all planned organizational changes had already been completed. [ 55 ] Law-enforcement training was another preparation. On 8 August, an application notice for a FLETC director described the center as the centralized authority for training, examining, and certifying law-enforcement officers in DC3. Recruits were to attend before entering an agency. The same notice assigned FLETC a conduct-enforcement role, including revocation of licenses when misconduct was proven. This program connected police employment to training and certification, with a disciplinary mechanism extending across agencies. [ 40 ] The 2026 arrangement differed from the Metro academy announced during Washington's 2024 police transition. Training institutions changed as the capital's departments were reorganized. Their functions should therefore be understood in their respective periods: the 2024 academy prepared the reorganized municipal police, while the August 2026 announcement described a centralized DC3 law-enforcement system. [ 39 ] [ 40 ] Employment and early public administration On 4 September, Jsjsjbsd addressed the press and public to commemorate DC3's opening. He stated that USAJOBS had handled more than 500 applications and that agencies were conducting a program of official events. These figures were the president's account of administrative activity. His address connected the city's launch with recruitment and efforts to prepare departments for new participation. [ 56 ] Employment subsequently made direct use of city facilities. On 19 September, the President reported using DC3's new jobs system to interview candidates on the spot and hire two people. He said his chief of staff was adapting USAJOBS to accommodate the in-game system for departments and agencies with a team. The account identified an implemented hiring interaction rather than only a promised future feature: candidates could be interviewed in the city and hired through its system. [ 11 ] The integration of employment with buildings and agency teams gave Washington a practical role in public administration. Earlier recruitment had often directed citizens to contact leaders or submit external applications; the September account described city facilities used in the interview and hiring process. The president's statement also indicated that integration remained in progress, so the initial use did not establish that every agency had completed its transition. [ 17 ] [ 25 ] [ 11 ] Economic plans accompanied the launch. The 4 September address promised a forthcoming nUSA Stock Exchange under the Department of Commerce and Labor. A cabinet account the next day likewise described the market as forthcoming and said the military was working on new maps. These statements concerned planned additions. They did not establish an operational stock exchange or a completed new military map at the free-beta opening. [ 56 ] [ 57 ] Election system Main articles: Elections in nUSA and Federal Election Code (nUSA) On 7 September 2026, the Federal Election Commission invited citizens to test elections in DC3. Candidate registration was located at the District Court building, and voting booths were near MPD headquarters. Both were marked by yellow checkmarks on the minimap. Participants were asked to register candidates, gather signatures, and cast votes so that problems could be identified before a real election. [ 58 ] The notice described a normal qualification of two hours of play within the preceding thirty days for candidate registration, support of a candidate, and voting in elections or referendums. During the test, the requirement was temporarily reduced to 0.1 hours, or six minutes. Candidates could not register in two simultaneous elections; changing contests required the commission to disqualify the candidate from the first. The test therefore assessed not only voting booths but also participation requirements and candidate management. [ 58 ] On 25 September, the commission announced the forthcoming Senate and House Class I elections as the first elections in DC3. Registration was scheduled for 5–8 October, with ten signatures required from non-incumbents. Voting was scheduled for 9–11 October. Seven representatives and five senators were to be elected, with terms beginning on 11 October. The announced locations remained the courthouse registration desk and voting near MPD headquarters. [ 12 ] The commission also encouraged citizens to consult an in-game election schedule at the courthouse, saying that short reminders would replace announcements of this length. The change made the capital itself a place to obtain current electoral information, as well as to register and vote. As of the September announcement, the October contests were prospective; their outcomes were not yet part of DC3's completed election history. [ 12 ] Municipal government Charter and executive offices Washington's municipal government operates through a charter and local legislation within the wider federal system. H.R. 41, D.C. Charter Revised, was recorded as passed by both houses of Congress and signed into law. Its text provided for a mayor, deputy mayor, council, local departments, and procedures for ordinances, nominations, succession, and charter amendments. Later council records contain further charter changes, so the revised charter represents a particular framework in the city's institutional history rather than an assumption that every provision remained unchanged. [ 4 ] [ 59 ] Under H.R. 41's framework, the mayor headed municipal government and was a non-voting member of the council with a right to be heard. The mayor and deputy mayor were elected together for three-month terms. The mayor nominated department heads for council confirmation, supervised municipal employees, enforced ordinances, and could issue administrative orders consistent with higher law. title: Winter 2025 Election Extravaganza (nUSA)
text: The Winter 2025 Election Extravaganza was a four-contest nUSA election cycle held in December 2025. The Federal Election Commission (FEC) scheduled elections for the Senate, House of Representatives, District of Columbia City Council, and mayor of the District of Columbia, with the elected officials' terms beginning on December 7. [ 1 ] It was a roleplay election cycle in the Roblox-based nUSA community, not a real United States election. Contests The FEC scheduled six Senate Class II seats, ten House seats, ten City Council seats, and the mayor and deputy mayor positions. The results document presents the congressional and municipal contests together. A separate House Class II election was set for January 2026 and was not part of the December results document. [ 2 ] Certified results The FEC's December 7 results listed chexburger as the leading City Council candidate, TonyyLewinsky as the leading House Class I candidate, cincyski as the leading Senate Class II candidate, and Emperorlol01 as mayor-elect. The certified mayoral tally was 59 votes for Emperorlol01 and 44 for warlockings. The results document lists the winning candidates in all four contests. [ 3 ] The results document reported 156 unique voters and 61 unique supporters across the cycle. It also gave separate valid and invalid ballot and supporter counts for each contest; those totals varied by race. title: Zeyad567
text: Zeyad567 5th President of nUSA In office 25 February 2014 – 30 July 2014 [ 1 ] Preceded by Lumidas Succeeded by Lumidas 11th President of nUSA In office 20 July 2015 – 7 January 2016 [ 1 ] Preceded by Lumidas Succeeded by SuddenRush12G NARA Presidential Records Zeyad567 was the fifth and eleventh president of the Roblox nUSA roleplay community. His first presidency followed Lumidas in February 2014 and ended when Lumidas returned to office that July. After serving again as vice president under Lumidas, he became president for a second time in July 2015. He left office before the end of that term, and Vice President SuddenRush12G completed the remainder. [ 2 ] Vice presidency and first term Zeyad567 served as Vice President to Lumidas from July to September 2014. During that tenure, the Senate impeached him and barred him from office. The Supreme Court overturned the impeachment and bar. The court later cited the 2015 case, Zeyad v. United States , as a precedent for judicial review of impeachment and described the removal as unconstitutional. [ 3 ] After the court's intervention, Zeyad567 later returned to the vice presidency under Lumidas. The archived vice-presidential chronology lists his service from 16 February to 20 July 2015. That succession placed him next in line when Lumidas's presidency ended, and Zeyad567 took office for a second time. [ 4 ] Second presidency Zeyad567's second term began on 20 July 2015. It was his 11th turn in the presidential succession. He resigned and was succeeded by SuddenRush12G, who completed the term. A retrospective chronology dates the change to 7 January 2016, although the resignation instrument itself has not been found. title: ZhangJingping
text: ZhangJingping (also rendered as “Zhang Jinping” in signed announcements) is a Roblox nUSA community archivist who was selected as Archivist of the United States in March 2025. The appointment post cited Zhang’s prior work maintaining the court system and its records. Later posts document archival publications, deputy appointments, and an additional National Elections Administrator (NEA) title; they do not supply a complete succession timeline or define the duration of each appointment. [ 1 ] Appointment and archival work The March 2025 announcement described Zhang as the sole custodian of the judiciary’s records after maintaining the court system for more than a year, and selected Zhang to lead NARA. It framed the appointment as part of an effort to streamline the agency and preserve nUSA history during preparation for a new gameplay experience. Those statements document the appointing announcement’s rationale, rather than an independent evaluation of the court records or a complete account of their custody. [ 2 ] On 28 April, Zhang posted a Deputy Archivist vacancy and described the position as supporting national records management. The posting required political abstention, specifically prohibiting campaigning, and requested an application including a résumé and references. This provides evidence of the role’s stated expectations during Zhang’s leadership. [ 3 ] In May 2025, Zhang signed a post announcing that NARA had prepared an accessible copy of the Constitution of the United States for use, including revisions enacted through a cited public law and Senate joint resolution. This was an archival publication and access measure; it does not by itself establish the full content or custody chain of the underlying constitution. [ 4 ] Deputy appointments and election administration In July 2025, Zhang announced bones as the new Deputy Archivist. In February 2026, a further post announced v0idedghost as “the next Deputy Archivist.” The source does not explain how the later selection related to bones’s appointment, so these are best treated as dated appointments rather than proof of uninterrupted or exclusive succession. [ 5 ] A staffing post dated 10 April 2026 announced gabezilla090909 as Deputy National Elections Administrator after 23 applications. Zhang signed that notice with both the Archivist of the United States and National Elections Administrator titles. This documents the two titles appearing together in that announcement; it does not establish that NARA and the FEC were a single agency or that Zhang held the NEA role throughout the preceding archival period. title: nUSA Wiki:Sources
text: Source guide explains the citations used in this local encyclopedia of the nUSA Roblox roleplay community. Discord exports The research archive contains two text exports, one from the #nusa-updates channel and one from #announcements . Article footnotes identify the channel, displayed date, and line number in the preserved export. The main research notes count lines using Python splitlines() ; the announcements document review also provides a crosswalk to ordinary LF line numbers. The exports do not contain Discord message IDs. Trello records and documents Trello citations link to the specific board or card. PDF citations identify the document and page. The local source archive preserves public JSON exports of NARA Hub and linked boards and copies of accessible PDFs. A board's current state can differ from its earlier state; article text should give dates where the record permits. Reading the evidence The records describe a fictional government and its institutions within the Roblox community, not the real United States government. A proposed bill, announcement, archived document, and later account may have different evidentiary weight. Allegations in community records are attributed to their sources; they are not treated as established findings merely because they appear in an archive.
